en: “Shoot!” said that arsehole of a lieutenant, and Canlan pulled the trigger, and put his bolt in the air, and straight away set to cranking his bow again.
bs: — Paljba! reče onaj poručnik kreten, a Canlan povuče obarač, posla strijelu u zrak i odmah iznova prionu na navijanje luka.

en: “Come on! Come on!” snapped that bastard beside him. Everyone had started growling, snarling, grunting, steeling themselves for the slow contact, and the tips of their pikes clicked against the tips of the enemy’s, and the shafts met, and scraped, and slid, closer and closer. A thicket of them, slipping and knocking against each other, and deadly metal on the end.
bs: — Ajmo! Ajmo! kresnuo je onaj gad pored njega. Svi su počeli režati, siktati, hroptati, čeličeći se za polagan sudar, a vrhovi njihovih pika zveckali su o vrhove neprijateljskih, i držači su se sudarali, strugali i klizili, sve bliže i bliže. Gustiš od njih, koji se klizao i udarao jedan o drugi, s ubojitim metalom na kraju.

en: He gave a snarl through his gritted teeth when it pricked him. Just a cold pinch, and then a biting, and a worse, and his snarl got higher and higher until it was a desperate, slobbering shriek, an impossible, unbearable pain cutting through his chest.
bs: Proizveo je režanje kroz stisnute zube kad ga je ubola. Bio je to tek hladan štipalj, a onda ugriz, pa još gori, a njegovo režanje postajalo je sve više dok se nije pretvorilo u očajnički, slinavi vrisak, u nemoguću, nepodnošljivu bol koja mu je sjekla prsa.

en: “Up we get,” grunted Scalla, pulling the wounded man off her and dumping him onto the stretcher. She’d almost complained when she first saw how rough he was with them. Like he was hefting sacks of coal. She’d soon learned that delicacy did no one any good. She stumbled to the foot of the stretcher, caught hold of the handles. Scalla had undone the buckle on the wounded man’s helmet and tossed it bouncing away, turned around to grab his handles and looked over his shoulder to meet her eye. “One,
bs: — Diži se, protisnu Scalla, zbacivši ranjenika sa sebe i istovarivši ga na nosila. Skoro se pobunila kad je prvi put vidjela koliko je grub prema njima. Kao da diže vreće ugljena. Ubrzo je naučila da nježnost nikome ne koristi. Posrnula je prema podnožju nosila, uhvatila se za ručke. Scalla je otkopčala kopču na kacigi ranjenika i hitnula je, a ona je odskočila u daljinu, okrenula se da dohvati svoje ručke i preko njegovog ramena susrela njezin pogled. — Jedan, dva…

en: Wanting to prove she was useful. Wanting to prove she was brave. She was the one always carried messages for Orso, so she’d carry this one. Realised her mistake soon as she ran from the town hall and into the madness in the street. She’d hated carrying Orso’s messages to that bitch Savine dan Glokta. Her affected elegance and her gaudy taste and her superior little smirks. But Hildi’s chances of getting killed carrying love letters had been very small.
bs: Želeći dokazati da je korisna. Želeći dokazati da je hrabra. Ona je uvijek nosila Orsove poruke, pa će ponijeti i ovu. Shvatila je svoju pogrešku čim je istrčala iz gradske vijećnice u ludilo na ulici. Mrzila je nositi Orsove poruke onoj kučki Savin dan Glokta. Njezinoj izvještačenoj eleganciji i kičastom ukusu te njezinim superiornim malim podsmjesima. No Hildine šanse da bude ubijena noseći ljubavna pisma bile su vrlo male.

en: She gave the corporal almost as hard a shove as he’d given her, then nearly tripped over a corpse just behind him. A Northman’s corpse, fur around his shoulders matted with blood. He wasn’t alone. Lots of bodies, left where they fell.
bs: Odgurnula je desetnika gotovo jednako snažno kao što je on nju, a onda se umalo spotaknula o leš koji je ležao neposredno iza njega. Sjevernjački leš, s krznom oko ramena zamršenim od krvi. Nije bio sam. Mnoštvo tijela, ostavljenih ondje gdje su pala.

en: Always thought he’d be one of the brave ones. Congratulated himself on it when he was doing his jacket up that morning. You’re one of the brave ones, Stillman!
bs: Uvijek je mislio da će biti jedan od hrabrih. Čestitao si je na tome dok je zakopčavao jaknu tog jutra. Ti si jedan od hrabrih, Stillmane!

en: They were like phrases in a foreign tongue. How could anyone be steady with red-handed murder rushing up the hill towards them? How could anyone be steady with the Northmen’s horrible yells, and the screams of dying comrades, and the endless clatter of metal, the thunder of the distant cannons echoing shrill in their ears?
bs: Zvučalo mu je to poput riječi na nekom stranom jeziku. Kako je ikad mogao ostati priseban dok im se krvavo ubojstvo žurilo uz brdo? Kako je tko mogao ostati miran uz strašne ratne pokliče Sjevernjaka, krikove umirućih suboraca i neprekidno zveckanje metala, uz grmljavinu dalekih topova što mu je prodorno odzvanjala u ušima?

en: “Die, bastard, fucking die, bastard,” every breath a flood of curses, and he hacked at a shield and put a great scar through the sun pattern on it, hacked at it again and knocked the man holding it over on his back, hacked at his leg and left his foot flopping off by a flap of gristle.
bs: — Crkni, gade, jebi se, crkni, gade, svaki mu je udah bio prepun psovki, usjekao se u štit i ostavio veliku ogrebotinu preko sunčeva motiva na njemu, udario ga ponovo i oborio čovjeka koji ga je držao na leđa, rasjekao mu nogu i ostavio stopalo da visi na komadu hrskavice.

en: “A cannon-stone must have clipped one of those lovely chimneys. A sad loss to posterity…” He brushed a few specks of plaster from his shoulder plate. Pauldron, was that the word? Or vambrace? He got them mixed up.
bs: — Topovsko đule moralo je okrznuti jedan od onih divnih dimnjaka. Tužan gubitak za potomstvo… — Otresao je nekoliko zrnaca žbuke s ramenog oklopa. Ramenjača, je li to bila riječ? Ili podlaktica? Miješao ih je.

en: “Damn it.” Orso would never forgive himself if anything happened to Hildi. “What about Lord Marshal Rucksted? Any sign?”
bs: — Prokletstvo. Orso si nikada ne bi oprostio da se Hildi nešto dogodilo. — Što je s lordom maršalom Ruckstedom? Ima li kakvih tragova?

en: Gurkish Fire had left a stinking black scar through the grass, shrouding the summit in smoke as the rain started to spit down. Below, she could see the troops of the Open Council slogging steadily up the hillside under drooping flags. They were battered by cannon fire, sodden from the river, exhausted from the climb. But they were coming, and in numbers.
bs: Gurkička vatra ostavila je smrdljiv, crn ožiljak na travi, obavivši vrh brda dimom dok je kiša počinjala rominjati. Dolje je mogla vidjeti postrojbe Otvorenoga vijeća kako se postojano penju uz padinu pod obješenim zastavama. Bile su izudarane topovskom vatrom, promočene od rijeke, iznurene usponom. Ali dolazile su, i to u gomili.

en: Savine stared, mouth open in disbelief as, with awful, nerve-shredding slowness, all her ambitions came apart at the seams.
bs: Savin je zapanjeno promatrala otvorenih usta dok su joj se, uz užasnu, živce parajuću sporost, sve ambicije raspadale po šavovima.

en: “I noticed,” said Leo, watching in helpless fury as the Open Council’s forces crumbled and fled for the river.
bs: — Primijetio sam, odvrati Leo, promatrajući s bespomoćnim gnjevom kako se snage Otvorenog vijeća rasipaju i bježe prema rijeci.

en: Leo could see exhausted men floundering from the river on the near bank. Across the water, the King’s Own cavalry surged and whirled like the starlings above the field the day before, harrying the panicked remnants of the Open Council’s forces. Corpses floated downstream, clogged into a great bobbing tangle in the boggy shallows.
bs: Leo je mogao vidjeti iscrpljene ljude kako se gegaju iz rijeke na bližoj obali. Preko vode, kraljeva osobna konjica navaljivala je i kovitlala se poput čvoraka iznad polja prethodnog dana, goneći uspaničene ostatke snaga Otvorenog vijeća. Leševi su plovili nizvodno, nakupljeni u veliku zapetljanu gomilu u močvarnim plićacima.

en: Now at a jolting canter, hooves drumming as the Young Lion’s cavalry charged into battle once again. A battle ill-suited to horsemen, though, it had to be admitted. Leo never seemed to learn where that was concerned.
bs: Sada u poskakujućem galopu, kopita su bubnjala dok je konjica Mlađeg Lava još jednom jurišala u bitku. Bitku posve neprikladnu za konjanike, doduše, moralo se priznati. Činilo se da Leo to nikako ne uspijeva naučiti.

en: The cavalry had thundered through and torn the lines apart. Ripped them into shreds of bitter fighting, tattered struggles to the death, writhing in the smoke. Broad saw the blobbed shapes of three men shaken loose. King’s men, he thought. Deserters, maybe. That was his best guess. In a battle, a guess is all you can afford. Time to let go, finally, and he felt the smile twist his face.
bs: Kroz sve to prohujala je konjica i rastrgala redove. Raznijela ih u dronjke ogorčena ratovanja, iskidane bitke na život i smrt, uz nemirno previjanje u dimu. Brod je ugledao zagasite obrise trojice ljudi koji su se odvojili od gomile. Kraljevi ljudi, pomislio je. Dezerteri, možda. To je bila njegova najbolja procjena. U bitci se drugo ne može ni tražiti. Krajnje je vrijeme da se konačno prepusti, i osjetio je kako mu osmijeh iskrivljuje lice.

en: Broad charged into the very midst of it, caught a man full in the side with his shoulder and dumped him sprawling, sword bouncing from his hand. He reeled into someone else, spear clattering against Broad’s back as he swung, too close for the hammer and Broad stabbed with his knife, overhand. It scraped on a breastplate, scratched down an armplate, found the joint between the two and punched deep into flesh. The man tried to twist away, fumbling at Broad’s shoulder, and Broad rammed the dagger t
bs: Brod je jurnuo u samu sredinu toga meteža, ramenom pokosio čovjeka u bok i bacio ga na tlo, dok mu je mač ispao iz ruke i odskočio. Posrnuo je na nekog drugog, Pajk mu je udarilo o leđa dok se okretao, preblizu za malj, pa je Brod ubo nožem, odozgo. Ostrugao je o prsni oklop, zarezao naramenicu, našao spoj između dvaju oklopa i duboko se zario u meso. Čovjek se pokušao izmaknuti, pipajući po Brodovu ramenu, a Brod mu je zabio bodež kroz otvor na kacigi, ostavivši ga ondje zabijenog do drške dok

en: Last stand wasn’t a phrase you ever wanted to use about your own side, but that was the look of it. Wounded men. Twisted faces. Desperate shouting. Someone coughed, leaning on a broken spear, coughing blood, and drooling blood, coughing again. The Northman, Jin, had a flatbow bolt in his thigh. He had Brock under the armpits even so, swearing in Northern as he struggled to drag him out from under his dead mount.
bs: Posljednji otpor nije bila fraza koju bi išta poželio upotrijebiti za svoju stranu, ali tako je izgledalo. Ranjeni ljudi. Izobličena lica. Očajničko vikanje. Netko se zakašljao, oslanjajući se na slomljeno Pajk, kašljući krv i balaveći krv, pa se ponovno zakašljao. Sjevernjak, Jin, imao je strelicu samostrela u bedru. Ipak je držao Broka ispod pazuha, psujući na sjevernjačkom dok se mučio izvući ga ispod njegovog mrtvog konja.

en: It was bad now. It was always bad, but it was real bad now. Everyone on the arrow-prickled, blood-smeared, mud-churned way was hurt. A Carl spluttered blood and bits of teeth into his hands. Another stared stupidly, hair clotted with blood. A Thrall clutched at the leaking stumps of two fingers, snarling curses. A Named Man sat, pale as milk, staring down at his hands as he tried to poke his guts back in through a great slit in his side. Clover caught his eye and gave him a nod. He was back to t
bs: Bilo je loše. Uvijek je bilo loše, ali sad je bilo zbilja loše. Svi na putu posijanom strijelama, uprljanom krvlju i razrovanom blatom bili su ozlijeđeni. Karl je ispljunuo krv i komadiće zuba u ruke. Dugi je tupo zurio, slijepljene kose natopljene krvlju. Tral je stiskao krvave patrljke dvaju prstiju režući psovke. Čovjek s Imenom sjedio je blijed poput krpe i zurio u vlastite ruke dok je pokušavao ugurati crijeva natrag kroz veliku rasjekotinu na boku. Klover ga pogleda u oči i kimne mu. Vrati

en: Downside’s eyes rolled slowly up, as if even that was too much effort, one turned bright red by a blow to the face and his cheek cut and his forehead scuffed raw and his brow opened up and weeping a dark streak.
bs: Daunsajdove se oči polako zakotrljaše prema gore, kao da je i to bilo previše truda; jedno mu je oko bilo jarkocrveno od udarca u lice, obraz rasječen, čelo izgrebano do krvi, a arkada rasklimana, pa je iz nje curio taman mlaz.

en: “’Course not,” said Clover. “But he might back off when it suits him, specially from another man’s fight. Wouldn’t be our victory. Won’t be our defeat.” He leaned close. “The Young Lion dug this fucking hole. He can be the one buried in it.”
bs: — Kako da ne, odvrati Klover. — Ali mogao bi se povući kad mu to odgovara, pogotovo iz tuđe bitke. To ne bi bila naša pobjeda. Neće biti ni naš poraz. Primače se posve blizu. — Mladi Lav je iskopao ovu jebenu rupu. Neka bude onaj koji će u njoj i završiti.

en: Leo used his sword like a crutch, weight all on his good leg, which an hour ago had been his bad leg. It hardly seemed to hurt at all now. Not compared to the other one, crushed by his horse. Not compared to his dangling arm, riddled with bits of steel from a cannon.
bs: Leo se oslonio na mač kao na štaku, sav se oslonivši na zdravu nogu — onu koja mu je još prije sat vremena bila ozlijeđena. Sada je jedva osjećao bol. Barem ne u usporedbi s drugom, koju mu je smrskao konj. Ni u usporedbi s visećom rukom, izbušenom komadićima čelika iz topa.

en: “Good, good. I hear Black Calder’s gone off to suck some cocks up in the High Valleys and left you holding the baby. That right?”
bs: — Dobro, dobro. Čujem da je Blek Kalder otišao pušiti kurce gore u Visoke doline i ostavio tebe da držiš ljestve. Je li tako?

en: She thought of the first time she saw a man killed. Those three she and Isern ran into in the woods the day Uffrith burned. Was it really only a year or two back? The cold shock as she let go the bowstring. The hurt look in that boy’s eyes. Still gave her a shiver. Then she thought of all the death she’d seen since. The murders and the battles and the duels. The last expressions, the last words, the last breaths, all blurred into one. The blood rolled off her now, like milk off a greased pan. Is
bs: Sjetila se prvoga puta kad je vidjela kako ubijaju čovjeka. Onu trojicu na koje su ona i Izern naišle u šumi onoga dana kad je Afrit izgorio. Je li doista prošlo tek godinu ili dvije? Hladan šok kad je otpustila tetivu. Povrijeđen pogled u očima toga dječaka. Od toga bi se još uvijek naježila. Zatim je pomislila na svu silu smrti kojoj je svjedočila od tada. Ubojstva, bitke i dvoboje. Posljednji izrazi lica, posljednje riječi, posljednji uzdasi, sve se to stopilo u jedno. Krv je sada klizila s n

en: “Some will be,” said Rikke. “But if King Orso took any notice of the letter I sent him, they’ll have a much harder fight than they were expecting. So Stour’ll come back with a lot fewer warriors than you were expecting. If he comes back at all.”
bs: — Neki hoće, reče Rike. — Ali ako je kralj Orso obratio ikakvu pažnju na pismo koje sam mu poslala, imat će mnogo težu borbu nego što su očekivali. Stoga će se Staur vratiti s mnogo manje ratnika nego što ti očekuješ. Ako se uopće vrati.

en: Shivers had his eye on Skarling’s Chair. “Trouble with being a strong man or a clever man with a big, bad name,” he said, and he ought to know, after all, “is that folk always have their best fight ready for you.”
bs: Šivers je motrio Skarlingovu stolicu. — problem s tim kad si snažan ili mudar čovjek s velikim, zlim imenom" – a on je to, zaboga, trebao znati – "jest u tome što narod uvijek čuva svoju najbolju borbu baš za tebe.

en: Rucksted frowned towards the rocky bluff, where yesterday’s cannons still poked from the hill like the prongs of an iron crown. “The world’s changing, that’s for damn sure. Now a man can put a spark to some powder and a thousand strides away another man’s blown limb from limb. There was a time you had to look in his eyes, at least.”
bs: Rucksted se namrštio prema stjenovitoj litici, s koje su jučerašnji topovi i dalje virili iz brda poput zubaca željezne kune. — Svijet se mijenja, to je prokleto sigurno. Sada čovjek može kresnuti iskru u malo baruta i tisuću koraka dalje drugom čovjeku raznijeti udove. Bilo je vrijeme kada si ga morao pogledati u oči, barem tada.

en: “Stour Nightfall himself is unaccounted for,” said Pike. “I fear we may not have heard his name for the last time.”
bs: — Sam Staur Najtfol još nije pronađen, primijeti Pajk. — Bojim se da njegovo ime nismo čuli posljednji put.

en: “This is all a misunderstanding, Your Majesty!” one young lordling spluttered, face pressed so hard against the bars they left livid marks in the flesh to either side. “All a terrible misunderstanding!”
bs: — Ovo je strašan nesporazum, Vaše Visočanstvo! procijedi mladi plemić prislonivši lice tako čvrsto uz rešetke da su na mesu ostali ljubičasti tragovi s objiju strana. — Sve je to strašan nesporazum!

en: Gorst lowered his eyes and trudged from the room, pulling the door shut. When Orso turned back, Brock had a pained grimace on his face.
bs: Brok je otvorio usta. Potom je uz bolnu grimasu slegnuo ramenima, ispustio jauk patnje i klonuo. — Je li to uopće važno?

en: Witty back and forth, as if they were discussing business on an ordinary day rather than hiding in a muddy hollow under the roots of a fallen tree, with everything in utter ruins. Savine wrapped her arms around herself, wrapped her arms around her baby and felt it move, thank the Fates. Her shoulder, her side, her neck were one great stiff throb where she must have hit the ground. She could easily have been dead.
bs: Duhovito nabacivanje riječima, kao da raspravljaju o poslu za obična dana, a ne se skrivaju u blatnjavoj udolini pod korijenjem oborenog stabla, dok je sve oko njih u potpunim ruševinama. Savin obgrli ruke oko sebe, obgrli ruke oko svog djeteta i osjeti kako se pomiče, hvala Sudbini. Rame, bok, vrat — sve ju je užasno, tupo boljelo ondje gdje je morala udariti o tlo. Lako je mogla biti mrtva.

en: “It’s my only chance to save myself. We have no supplies. The king’s forces are everywhere. My entourage is down to two and it’s two more than I deserve. We’ll never make it to the coast. Not with me the size of a house.”
bs: — To mi je jedina šansa da spasim sebe. Nemamo zaliha. Kraljeve snage su posvuda. Moja je pratnja spala na dvoje, a to je dvoje više nego što zaslužujem. Nikada nećemo stići do obale. Ne s mojim trbuhom velikim poput kuće.

en: She felt Zuri’s light hand on one shoulder. “My scripture teacher would no doubt have said…” She was frowning doubtfully out across the battered battlefield. “That regret is the gateway to salvation…”
bs: Vrata su zveckajući otklizala i ona se trznula tako naglo da joj je leđima prošao grč; umalo je povratila i ostala napola na nogama, oslanjajući se na stolicu jednom drhtavom rukom.

en: Savine swallowed. She had planned the best way to frame it, how to subtly shift the blame, each word picked out as carefully as an ensemble for the theatre, but now the excuses burbled out in a half-baked rush. “They were already planning it. Isher, and the rest. I had no choice. I could only—”
bs: Savin proguta knedlu. Bila je isplanirala najbolji način da to sroči, kako suptilno svaliti krivnju, svaka riječ odabrana brižljivo poput kostima za kazalište, ali sad su opravdanja navrla u brzopletomu, polupečenomu mlazu. — Oni su to već planirali. Išer i ostali. Nisam imala izbora. Mogla sam samo —

en: She could hardly stand. She sank down on her knees. “I’m begging you for mercy. For my husband. For myself. For our child.” Hands clasped, face wet with tears, nose clicking with snot. What a fucking cliché. “I know I don’t deserve it, but it’s all I can do now. Please, Orso.”
bs: Jedva se držala na nogama. Pala je na koljena. — Preklinjem te za milost. Zbog mog muža. Zbog sebe. Zbog našeg djeteta. Sklopljenih ruku, lica umrljanog suzama, nosa što joj šmrca. Kakav jebeni klišej. — Znam da to ne zaslužujem, ali to je sve što mi je preostalo. Molim te, Orso.

en: Men scurried about the ship as that distant light grew brighter and was joined to either side by the grey rumour of the coast. Wood clonked, rope hissed and salt spray flew as they brought in the sailcloth and leaned to the oars.
bs: Ljudi su se užurbano kretali po brodu dok je ono udaljeno svjetlo postajalo sve sjajnije, a s obje mu se strane pridružio sivi obris obale. Drvo je škripalo, konopi su šuštali, a slana je prskavica letjela dok su uvlačili jedro i naginjali se na vesla.

en: Greenway’s jaw hung open. “What—” And Downside’s axe split his head in half, spraying blood. Seemed Rikke had been right about him dying on the water, and not just him. All over the boat, Clover’s boys stabbed the men beside them, cut throats, smashed skulls, stuck blades in backs and fronts and sides. All done too close and too quiet and too sudden for swords. Just the way Clover always said it should be done. Far faster than when Stour killed Scale and his men. Far neater.
bs: Grinveju su se usta objesila. — Što–" I Daunsajdova mu je sjekira rascvjetala glavu na pola, špricajući krv. Činilo se da je Rike bila u pravu kad je govorila da će skončati na vodi, i to ne samo on. Posvuda po brodu Kloverovi su momci ubadali ljude do sebe, rezali grkljane, drobili lubanje, zabijali oštrice u leđa, prsa i bokove. Sve se odigralo preblizu, pretiho i prebrzo za mačeve. Baš onako kako je Klover uvijek govorio da treba. Puno brže nego kad je Staur pobio Skejla i njegove ljude. Puno

en: “You brought him, then,” he said as Clover clambered somewhat ungainly from the ship, wood of the wharf feeling unsteady under his sea legs.
bs: — Doveli ste ga, dakle, reče dok se Klover nekako nespretno ispeo s broda, a drvo gata činilo mu se nestabilnim pod njegovim mornarskim nogama.

en: “What’re you doing?” he squealed, twisting and struggling, but Downside had him under one arm now and the Nail under the other and he wasn’t going far with them two holding on.
bs: — Što radiš? zacvili, vrteći se i praćakajući, ali Daunsajd ga je već držao pod jednom rukom, a Čavao pod drugom, i nije mogao daleko s tom dvojicom na sebi.

en: He gave a whoop as his crutch slipped on the top step and spun from his hand. He clutched at nothing, then the side of his face banged hard into the platform. He heard a few gasps, a whimper from somewhere. Maybe him.
bs: Glasno je uzdahnuo kad mu se štaka okliznula na gornjoj stubi i izletjela mu iz ruke. Mahnuo je u prazno, a zatim se bočnom stranom lica snažno udario o platformu. Čuo je nekoliko uzdaha, nečiji prigušeni jecaj. Možda njegov vlastiti.

en: Was there dried blood on the rope? He felt vaguely affronted by that. For something so intimate, each person should surely get their own. Felt like dying in another man’s underwear. Though the underwear of those who’d gone ahead was no doubt in a far worse state. People pissed and shat and leaked every fluid when they were hanged, he knew. It had seemed quite a laugh when Antaup told them all about it over drinks. Didn’t seem much of a laugh now, needless to say.
bs: Je li na užetu bila suha krv? To ga je nekako vrijeđalo. Za nešto toliko intimno, svatko bi jamačno trebao dobiti svoje. Činilo se to kao umiranje u tuđem donjem rublju. Iako je donje rublje onih koji su prošli prije nesumnjivo bilo u puno gorem stanju. Ljudi pišaju, kake i puštaju svaku tekućinu kad ih vješaju, to je znao. Činilo se to prilično smiješnim kad im je Antaup sve to ispričao uz piće. Sad se to, nepotrebno je reći, više nije činilo tako smiješnim.

en: There were even different kinds of silence. An obstinate refusal to speak. A baffled inability to understand what was happening. A lip-trembling, stuttering, quivering fear.
bs: Postojale su čak i različite vrste tišine. Tvrdoglavo odbijanje govora. Zatečena nesposobnost shvaćanja onoga što se događa. Strah koji trese usne, izaziva mucanje i ledi krv u žilama.

en: Leo flinched as Mustred dropped with a clatter and a thud, and a set of crows that had gathered on the bare beams of a fallen roof flapped outraged into the sky.
bs: Leo se trgnuo kad je Mustred propao uz tresak i tupi udar, a jato vrana okupljenih na golim gredama srušena krova uzbuđeno i uzrujano prhnulo u nebo.

en: The next man swooned, knees giving and dropping to the platform. One of the executioners dragged him up, slapped his hooded face, stood him straight on his trapdoor. Clatter and thud as he dropped.
bs: Sljedeći se čovjek onesvijestio, koljena su mu klecnula te je pao na platformu. Jedan ga je dželat povukao gore, udario mu šamar po licu u kapuljači i uspravio ga ravno na njegovu trapulu. Tutnjava i prasak dok je propao.

en: And Leo felt the noose loosened, then slipped over his head. As if that had been the only thing holding him up, he slumped, crutch clattering down. The executioner was ready and caught him, lowered him to the platform.
bs: I Leo osjeti kako se omča opustila, a zatim skliznula preko njegove glave. Kao da mu je to bila jedina potpora, klonuo je, dok mu je štaka zveckajući pala na tlo. Dželat je bio spreman i uhvatio ga, spustivši ga na podest.

en: “I meant the prison camps of Angland. I have come to believe… that the heart of a society… is revealed in its prisons.” Pike rocked gently with the movement of his horse, eyes fixed up the empty street ahead. “I was not there nearly as long as you, but long enough to lose my face. Honestly, I was never a handsome man. I daresay I turn more heads now. Your scars may not show quite so clearly, but I never doubt you have them. So I believe I understand you.”
bs: — Mislio sam na logore Englenda. Uvjerio sam se… da se srce nekog društva… najbolje vidi u njegovim zatvorima. Pajk se lagano njihao u ritmu konjskog kretanja, upirući pogled u praznu ulicu pred sobom. — Nisam bio ondje ni približno dugo kao ti, ali dovoljno dugo da izgubim lice. Iskreno rečeno, nikad nisam bio naočit muškarac. Usudio bih se reći da sad privlačim više pogleda. Tvoji se ožiljci možda ne vide tako jasno, ali nijednog trenutka ne sumnjam da ih imaš. Stoga vjerujem da te razumijem.

en: “Fuck,” breathed Vick. Not often she was at a loss for words, but right then she had nothing better.
bs: — Jebi ga, prošaptala je Vik. Rijetko bi ostala bez riječi, ali u tom trenutku nije imala ništa pametnije.

en: “Three days ago,” said Risinau, rubbing his hands delightedly, “while King Orso was winning his great victory against the rebels. They wanted us to distract the king’s men for them. Instead, they distracted the king’s men for us!”
bs: — Prije tri dana, reče Risinau zadovoljno trljajući ruke, dok je kralj Orso izvojevao svoju veliku pobjedu nad pobunjenicima. Htjeli su im odvratiti kraljeve ljude. Umjesto toga, oni su odvratili kraljeve ljude za nas!

en: Vick thought of the long line of hanged men Pike had left outside the city, a few months before. She’d thought him ruthless then. Now it turned out they’d been his own people. A man who’ll waste no time hanging two hundred of his friends… what might he do to his enemies? Smoke was already pouring from the windows of the bank, giving every breath the familiar char and fury stink of Valbeck she so well remembered.
bs: Vik se sjetila se dugačkog niza obješenih ljudi koje je Pajk ostavio izvan grada nekoliko mjeseci prije. Smatrala ga je nemilosrdnim tada. Sada se pokazalo da su to bili njegovi vlastiti ljudi. Čovjek koji bez oklijevanja objesi dvjesto svojih prijatelja… što bi tek mogao učiniti svojim neprijateljima? Iz prozora banke već je kuljao dim, dajući svakom udahu onaj dobro znani miris paljevine i gnjeva Valbeka kojeg se tako dobro sjećala.

en: Colonel Forest—a hard-working officer with common origins and impressive scars, commanded the Crown Prince’s Division for Orso.
bs: Pukovnik Forest — marljivi časnik skromnog podrijetla i impresivnih ožiljaka, zapovijedao je Divizijom prijestolonasljednika za Orsa.

en: She pushed the spit-wet dowel out of her mouth with her tongue and croaked the one word she could think of. “Fuck.”
bs: Jezikom je izgurala drveni klin natopljen pljuvačkom iz usta i promuklo izustila jedinu riječ koja joj je pala na pamet: — Jebeno.

en: “I saw a wolf eat the sun. Then a lion ate the wolf. Then a lamb ate the lion. Then an owl ate the lamb.”
bs: — Vidjela sam vuka kako jede sunce. Onda je lav pojeo vuka. Onda je janje pojelo lava. Onda je sova pojela janje.

en: “There are few blessings without a curse hidden inside, nor curses without a whiff of blessing.” Isern carved a little piece of chagga from a dried-out chunk. “Like most things, it’s a matter of how you look at it.”
bs: — Malo je blagoslova bez prokletstva skrivenog u njima, niti prokletstava bez daška blagoslova. Izern je malim nožićem odrezala komadić čage sa suhog komada gljive. — Kao i većina stvari, sve je u načinu na koji gledaš na to.

en: Rikke spat chagga juice but messed it up and got most of it down her chin. “If you think I picked any part of this, you’re mad.”
bs: Rike ispljune sok od čage, ali se spetlja pa joj većina iste poteče niz bradu. — Ako misliš da sam ja išta od ovoga birala, luda si.

en: Isern strode on through the woods with that loping gait that, however fast Rikke walked, always left her an uncomfortable half-step behind. “You really think I’d be pissing my efforts away on you otherwise?”
bs: Izern je nastavila koračati šumom onim svojim dugim korakom zbog kojega bi Rike, ma koliko brzo išla, uvijek ostajala neugodan polukorak iza nje. — Stvarno misliš da bih inače tratila trud na tebe?

en: “Carelessness with a cook-fire would do it.” Isern’s eyes slid sideways. “Though up here in the North, I’d say war’s a more likely cause of cities aflame.”
bs: — Neopreznost s logorskom vatrom sasvim bi bila dovoljna. Izern odmjeri pogledom u stranu. — Mada, ovdje gore u Sjeveru, rekla bih da je rat vjerojatniji uzrok gradova u plamenu.

en: “Used to carry my da’s hammer, ’cause the smallest should take the heaviest load, but that day he was fighting with the hammer so I had his spear. This very one.” Its butt tapped the rhythm of their walking on the path. “My da knocked a man down, and he was trying to get up, and I stabbed him right up the arse.”
bs: — Nekad sam nosila očev čekić jer su najmlađi trebali nositi najteži teret, ali tog se dana on tukao čekićem, pa sam ja imala njegovo Pajk. Baš ovo. Donji je kraj koplja udarao ritam njihovu hodu po stazi. — Moj je otac oborio čovjeka, a on se pokušavao ustati, pa sam ga ubola ravno u guzicu.

en: Her father always said don’t point arrows at folk unless you mean to see ’em dead, so she drew her bow halfway and pointed it at the road.
bs: Otac joj je oduvijek govorio da ne cilja strijelom na Folk osim ako ih ne kani vidjeti mrtve, stoga je napela luk do pola i usmjerila ga prema putu.

en: “Stour Nightfall’s mark,” growled the big man, with a hint of pride, and Rikke saw he had a wolf on his shield, too, though his was scuffed almost back to the wood.
bs: — Znak Staura Najtfola, prozbori krupni čovjek s primjesom ponosa, a Rike primijeti da i on na štitu ima vuka, premda je njegov bio izlizan gotovo do gologa drva.

en: “She is bloody mad.” The big one stepped forwards. “Now drop the—” And he made this long wheeze, and his shirt stuck out, a glint of metal showing.
bs: — Ona je krvavo luda. Krupni čovjek iskorači naprijed. — A sad spusti… I tad ispuha dugi hropac, a košulja mu se napuhnu dok se ukazao bljesak metala.

en: As if to prove the point, he coughed some blood into his hand, and stared over it at Rikke. He looked a bit offended, like she’d said something hurtful.
bs: Kao da želi potvrditi te riječi, iskašlja malo krvi u ruku i preko nje zagleda u Rike. Izgledao je pomalo uvrijeđeno, kao da je rekla nešto ružno.

en: Rikke spat some chagga juice and wiped her chin, watching the blood work its way through the dirt about the lad’s nailed head. “Doubt my smile’s up to the task and I’m damn sure your words ain’t.”
bs: Rike ispljune malo soka od čage i obrisa bradu, promatrajući kako se krv probija kroz zemlju oko mladićeve glave prikovane za tlo. — Sumnjam da je moj osmijeh dostojan tog zadatka, a sasvim sam sigurna da tvoje riječi nisu.

en: “No,” whispered Rikke, the smell of fire getting stronger and her worry getting stronger with it. “No, no, no.”
bs: — Ne, prošapta Rike, dok je miris vatre postajao sve jači, a s njime i njezina tjeskoba. — Ne, ne, ne.

en: A lance shattered, a shard flying into Leo’s helmet with an echoing clang as he wrenched away. The world was a flickering slit of twisted faces, glinting steel, heaving bodies, half seen through the slot in his visor. Screams of men and mounts and metal mashed into one thought-crushing din.
bs: Pajk se rasprsnulo, a krhotina je s jekom udarila u Leovu kacigu dok se on trzao u stranu. Svijet je bio tek treperavi procjep iskrivljenih lica, blistavog čelika i uznemirenih tijela, poluproziran kroz vizir. Vriskovi Folk, životinja i metala stopili su se u zaglušujući tutanj koji je drobio misli.

en: Someone clutched at his leg. Curly hair. Freckles. Looked bloody terrified. Everyone did. Didn’t seem to have a weapon. Maybe surrendering. Leo smashed Freckles on the top of the head with the rim of his shield, gave his horse the spurs and trampled him into the mud.
bs: Netko ga je zgrabio za nogu. Kovrčava kosa. Pjegice. Izgledao je nasmrt prestrašeno. Svi su tako izgledali. Činilo se da nema oružje. Možda se predaje. Leo je udario Pjegavog po tjemenu rubom štita, potaknuo konja mamuzama i pregazio ga u blato.

en: Had they won? He stared around for more enemies. A few ragged figures bounded through the crops towards the distant trees. Running for their lives, weapons abandoned. That was all.
bs: Jesu li pobijedili? Zagledao se oko sebe tražeći još neprijatelja. Nekoliko izmučenih prilika trčalo je preko usjeva prema dalekim stablima. Bježali su glavom bez obzira, odbacivši oružje. To je bilo sve.

en: He felt drunk. He felt on fire. He felt like a king. He felt like a god. This was what he was made for!
bs: Osjećao se opijeno. Osjećao se kao da gori. Osjećao se kao kralj. Osjećao se poput boga. Za to je stvoren!

en: “We don’t need the king’s bloody help!” snapped Leo as soon as the flap dropped. “We can beat Black Calder’s dogs!” His voice sounded oddly weak in the tent, deadened by wet cloth. It didn’t carry anywhere near so nicely as it had on the battlefield.
bs: — Ne treba nam kraljeva krvava pomoć! kresnu Leo čim je šatorski pokrov pao. — Možemo mi pobijediti pse Black Kaldera! Glas mu je zvučao čudno slabašno u šatoru, zagušen mokrom tkaninom. Nije se širio ni približno tako lijepo kao na bojnom polju.

en: “Great leaders go where the fight’s hottest!” But he knew he sounded like the heroes in the badly written storybooks he used to love.
bs: — Great vođe idu tamo gdje je borba najžešća! No znao je da zvuči poput junaka iz loše napisanih zbirki priča koje je nekad volio.

en: “You can’t understand! You’re not…” He waved an impatient hand, failing, as always, to quite find the right words. “A man,” he finished lamely.
bs: — Ti to ne možeš razumjeti! Ti nisi… Zamaše nestrpljivom rukom, ne uspijevajući, kao obično, pronaći prave riječi. — Muškarac, dovrši mlako.

en: Leo swallowed, pride melting to leave ugly guilt behind as pristine snow melts to show the world rotten and bedraggled. “I should go and see him.” He turned towards the tent flap, nearly tripping on the loose strap of one of his greaves. “Is he… with the wounded?”
bs: Leo je progutao knedlu, a ponos mu se rastopio ostavljajući za sobom ružnu krivnju, poput netaknuta snijega koji se topi i otkriva svijet trulim i zapuštenim. — Trebao bih otići vidjeti ga." Okrenuo se prema šatorskom krilu, umalo se spotaknuvši o labavi remen svoje nazuvak-golenice. — Je li… s ranjenima?

en: “What good will a letter do?” He felt the stinging of tears at the back of his nose. “I’ll give them my house! In Ostenhorm!”
bs: — Kakvo će dobro pismo donijeti? Osjetio je žarenje suza u korijenu nosa. — Dat ću im svoju kuću! U Ostenhormu!

en: He trudged to the tent flap, shoulders drooping under armour that felt three times heavier than when he arrived. Ritter was gone, and never coming back, and had left his weak-chinned wife weeping at the fireside. Killed by his own loyalty, and Leo’s vanity, and Leo’s carelessness, and Leo’s arrogance.
bs: Oteščalim koracima zaputi se prema šatorskom krilu, spuštenih ramena pod oklopom koji se činio triput težim nego kad je stigao. Ritter je bio mrtav i nikad se više neće vratiti, ostavivši svoju ženu slabačke brade da plače pokraj ognjišta. Ubijen vlastitom vjernošću, i Leovom taštinom, i Leovom nepažnjom, i Leovom ohološću.

en: It grew louder as he raised that rag of a standard, and Antaup swaggered forwards, throwing up his arms for more noise. One of the men, no doubt drunk already, dragged down his trousers and showed his bare arse to the North, to widespread approval. Then he fell over, to widespread laughter. Glaward and Barniva caught Leo and bundled him high into the air on their shoulders while Jurand planted his hands on his hips and rolled his eyes.
bs: Graja postade još glasnija kad je podigao tu dronjavu zastavu, a Antaup istupi s ponosnim držanjem, šireći ruke tražeći još velebnu buku. Jedan od vojnika, nesumnjivo već pripit, spusti hlače i pokaza golu guzicu Sjeveru, naišavši na opće odobravanje. Zatim se sruši, izazvavši opći smijeh. Glavard i Barniva uhvatiše Lea i ponesoše ga visoko u zrak na svojim ramenima dok Džurand stavi ruke na bokove i prevrnu očima.

en: Rikke cursed as the clutching mud near sucked her boot right off. “We could make for some high ground, at least.”
bs: Rike opsova dok joj je ljepljivo blato zamalo istrgnulo čizmu s noge. — Mogle bismo se barem uputiti prema nekoj uzvisini.

en: She liked to think of herself as quite the rugged outdoorswoman, but in this company she was a towny oaf. Isern-i-Phail knew all the ways, that was the rumour. Even better’n her daddy had. Rikke had learned more from watching her the last couple of weeks than she had from that fool Union tutor in Ostenhorm in a year. How to build a shelter from ferns. How to set rabbit traps, even if they hadn’t worked. How to reckon your course from the way the moss grew on the tree trunks. How to tell a man fr
bs: Voljela je misliti o sebi kao o pravoj prekaljenoj gorštakinji, ali u ovom je društvu bila tek neuka gradska cura. Pričalo se da Izern-i-Fejl zna sve puteljke. Čak i bolje nego njezin stari. Rike je u posljednjih nekoliko tjedana naučila od nje više nego od onog bedastog Unionovog tutora u Ostenhormu u cijeloj godini. Kako sagraditi sklonište od paprati. Kako postaviti zamke za zečeve, čak i ako se nisu pokazale uspješnima. Kako odrediti smjer prema načinu na koji mahovina raste na stablima. Kak

en: Rikke knew what folk said about her, and maybe her head didn’t have the right parts in the right places, but she’d always had a sharp eye for things. So in spite of the gloom and Isern’s nimble fingers, Rikke saw the hillwoman only ate half as much as she handed over. She saw it, and was thankful for it, and wished she had the bones to insist on fair shares, but she was just so damn hungry. She stuffed her shred of dry meat down so quickly she swallowed her chagga pellet too without even noticin
bs: Rike je znala što folk govori o njoj, i možda joj Šef nije bila posve u redu, ali oduvijek je imao oštro oko za stvari. Stoga je, unatoč tami i Iserninu vještu prstima, primijetila da planinarka jede samo polovicu onoga što joj je dala. Vidjela je to, bila na tome zahvalna i poželjela imati hrabrosti inzistirati na poštenoj diobi, ali bila je jednostavno pregladna. Ugurala je onaj komadić suhog mesa u usta tako brzo da je progutala i svoju pilulu čage a da nije ni primijetila.

en: “Not sure I even made a choice.” Rikke picked at her sore fingernails as she picked at the memory, over and over. “Just fumbled the string. Just a stupid mistake.”
bs: — Nisam sigurna da sam uopće imala izbor. Rike je čupkala bolne nokte dok je iznova i iznova prebirala po sjećanju. — Samo mi je tetiva skliznula. Glupa pogreška.

en: She slapped Rikke’s thigh and gave a witchy cackle, and maybe there was some magic in it after all because Rikke cracked her first smile in a day or two, and that made her feel just a bit better. Your best shield is a smile, her father always said.
bs: Ona pljusne Rike po bedru i ispusti vještičji cerek, a možda je u tome doista bilo nešto čarobno jer Rike izmami svoj prvi osmijeh u posljednjih dan-dva, i zbog toga joj bude mrvicu lakše. Najbolji ti je štit osmijeh, uvijek je govorio njezin otac.

en: One of the six great sheds was her property. Two of the twelve looming chimneys. One in every six of the new machines spinning inside, of the coals in the great heaps shovelled in the yard, of the hundreds of twinkling panes of glass that faced the street. Not to mention one-sixth part of the ever-increasing profits. A flood of silver to put His Majesty’s mint to shame.
bs: Jedna od šest velikih hala bila je njezino vlasništvo. Dva od dvanaest prijetećih dimnjaka. Svaki šesti od novih strojeva što su se vrtjeli unutra, od ugljena u golemim hrpama naguranim u dvorištu, od stotina svjetlucavih staklenih okana okrenutih prema ulici. Da i ne spominjemo šestinu sve veće dobiti. Pravu poplavu srebra koja bi postidjela kovnicu Vaša Uzvišenosti.

en: There were others hoping to lighten purses by more direct means. Grubby little cutpurses weaving through the crowds. Footpads lurking in the darkness of the alleys. Thugs slouching on the corners, keen to collect on behalf of the district’s many moneylenders.
bs: Bilo je tu i drugih koji su se nadali olakšati tuđe džepove izravnijim metodama. Sitni, prljavi džepari provlačili su se kroz gomilu. Razbojnici su vrebali u tami uličica. Hulje su se lenjo vucarale po uglovima, nestrpljive da utjeraju dugove u ime brojnih gradskih zelenaša.

en: Savine gathered her skirts so she could squat beside him and look in his dirt-smeared face. She wondered if he sponged the muck on as artfully as her maids did her powder, to arouse just the right amount of sympathy. Clean children need no charity, after all.
bs: Savine je prikupila haljinu kako bi mogla čučnuti pokraj njega i zagledati mu se u lice zaprljano blatom. Upitala se nanosi li blato vješto poput njezinih sobarica koje su joj nanosile puder, kako bi pobudio taman pravu mjeru suosjećanja. Djeca čista lica ionako ne trebaju milostinju.

en: The grimy ale-hall fell silent as Savine swept in, as if some exotic jungle beast had wandered off the street.
bs: U prljavoj se krčmi umirilo onoga trena kad je Savine ušetala, kao da je neka egzotična džunglinska zvijer zalutala s ulice.

en: She planted one elbow on the stretch of counter Zuri had wiped so she could lean closer and draw out both syllables. “Savine.”
bs: Ona laktom nasloni ruku na onaj dio Shanka koji je Zuri obrisala kako bi se mogla primaknuti i otegnuti oba sloga. — Savine.

en: In low company, Savine could be low. These were bullies, so they needed to be bullied. It was the language they understood. Majir’s thick neck shifted as she swallowed. “Who would dare doubt it?” And she laid a flat leather pouch on the counter.
bs: U lošem društvu Savine je i sama mogla biti loša. Bili su to nasilnici, pa ih je trebalo pritisnuti. Bio je to jezik koji su razumjeli. Majirin se debeli vrat pomaknuo dok je gutala knedlu. — Tko bi se usudio posumnjati u to?" I spusti ravnu kožnu vrećicu na šank.

en: “Oh, come now. If something happened to me, your own forgiveness would be the least of your problems.”
bs: — Ma dajte, molim vas. Kad bi se meni nešto dogodilo, vaše vlastito oproštenje bilo bi vam najmanja briga.

en: She settled herself opposite while Zuri whisked off her hat. A lady of taste should appear to make no effort. The right things simply happen around her. “The opportunity for investment you mentioned at our last meeting,” she said.
bs: Smjestila se preko puta dok je Zuri spretno uklanjala njen šešir. Žena s ukusom treba izgledati kao da se uopće ne trudi. Prave se stvari jednostavno događaju oko nje. — Prilika za ulaganje koju ste spomenuli na našem posljednjem sastanku, reče.

en: To Savine, there was no more enticing invitation than a door slammed in her face. “One man’s mad is another’s perceptive,” she said, her smile not even dented. “Your canal takes a clever route and your bridge is a wonder. Truly, I congratulate you on it. In a few years, they’ll be building everything from iron. But it isn’t finished and you’ve run out of money.”
bs: Za Savine nije bilo primamljivijeg poziva od vrata zalupenih pred nosom. — Tuđe ludilo svačija je mudrost, dometnu ona, a osmijeh joj se ne okrznu. — Vaš kanal ima domišljat pravac, a most vam je pravo čudo. Doista vam čestitam na tome. Za nekoliko će godina sve graditi od željeza. No on još nije dovršen, a vama je ponestalo novca.

en: Kort was trapped halfway between anger and ambition. Savine rather liked him there. Most animals, after all, look better in a cage. “Extend my canal… into the Three Farms?”
bs: Kort je bio zaglavljen na pola puta između gnjeva i ambicije. Savine se prilično sviđao ondje. Većina životinja uostalom bolje izgleda u kavezu. — Produžiti moj kanal… do Tri Farme?

en: “A notary from the firm of Temple and Kahdia is already drawing up the papers. He will be in touch.” She turned towards the door.
bs: — Bilježnik iz odvjetničkog ureda Temple i Kahdia već sastavlja ugovore. Javit će vam se. Okrenula se prema vratima.

en: Lies, like everything that left his mouth, engineered to make him appear just a touch less detestable. He wondered who he was trying to fool. Hildi undoubtedly saw straight through it. The truth was, when it came to stopping this, as with so much else, he simply couldn’t be arsed. He took another pinch of pearl dust, his heavy snorts ringing out as the Inquisitor in charge stepped to the front of the scaffold and the crowd fell breathlessly silent.
bs: Laži, kao i sve što mu je napuštalo usta, smišljene tako da ga učine tek zericu manje odurnim. Zapitao se koga to pokušava prevariti. Hildi je nesumnjivo prozrela igru. Istina je bila da mu se, kad je bila riječ o zaustavljanju ovoga, kao i u toliko toga drugog, jednostavno nije dalo. Uzela je još jedan prstohvat bisernog praha, a njegovo teško frktanje odjeknulo je dok je glavni inkvizitor koračao prema prednjem dijelu vješala, a svjetina utihnula bez daha.

en: Yolk burst out laughing while swigging from his bottle and sprayed a reeking mist of spirits, which settled over the wig of a well-dressed old lady just in front.
bs: Žumanj prasnu u smijeh gutajući iz boce i ispljunu smrdljivu maglicu žestokog pića, koja se spustila na periku dotjerane stare gospođe neposredno Naprijed njih.

en: He took one more pinch for good measure. Peering down through watering eyes, he noticed the box was getting dangerously empty.
bs: Uzela je još jedan prstohvat za svaki slučaj. Gledajući dolje kroz suzne oči, primijetio je da je kutija opasno prazna.

en: “She’s a funny little thing, your errand girl,” warbled one of the whores, dragging too heavily on his arm.
bs: — Zabavno je to stvorenje, tvoja potrkuša, zapjeva jedna od kurvi, preteško se oslanjajući na njegovu ruku.

en: Rather than needing strong men or horses to haul up the condemned, some enterprising fellow had devised a system whereby prisoners could be dropped through the scaffold floor at a touch upon a lever. There was an invention to make everything more efficient these days, after all. Why would killing people be an exception?
bs: Umjesto da traže snažne momke ili konje za podizanje osuđenika, neki poduzetni domišljati duh osmislio je sustav prema kojem su zatvorenici mogli propasti kroz pod vješala jednim dodirom poluge. U današnje se vrijeme ionako nalazio izum za veću učinkovitost svega. Zašto bi ubijanje Folk bila iznimka?

en: “Please,” said the man beside her. There were tears streaking his dirty cheeks. “Take me but, please—”
bs: — Molim vas, prozborio je čovjek do nje. Suze su mu brazdale prljave obraze. — Uzmite mene, ali, molim vas —

en: But circumstances always conspired to stop him doing the right thing. He heard a soft, high voice in his ear. “Your Highness.”
bs: No okolnosti su se uvijek urotile da ga spriječe učiniti ispravnu stvar. Čuo je tihi, piskutav glas uz uho: — Uzvišenost.

en: “Any chance I can bring the whores with me?” asked Orso. “I’ve paid for the whole day.” It was his turn to face Gorst’s fish-eyed stare. He sighed. “Would you conduct the ladies to their residence, Tunny?”
bs: — Postoji li ikakva šansa da sa sobom povedem kurve? upita Orso. — Platio sam cijeli dan. Došao je red na njega da se suoči s Gorstovim pogledom ribljih očiju. Uzdahnuo je. — Bi li ispratio dame do njihova prebivališta, Tunnyju?

en: “Well, now that Styria is almost entirely controlled by our enemies, I get so little chance to practice.”
bs: — Pa, sad kad Stirijom gotovo potpuno vladaju naši neprijatelji, imam tako malo prilike za vježbanje.

en: “You are King Jappo’s mortal enemy and the rightful heir to all he and the thrice-damned Snake of Talins have stolen, and it is high time you took your position seriously! We have enemies everywhere. Inside our borders, too.”
bs: — Ti si smrtni neprijatelj kralja Jappa i zakoniti baštinik svega što su on i trostruko prokleta Zmija iz Talinsa ukrali, i krajnje je vrijeme da svoj položaj shvatiš ozbiljno! Svugdje imamo neprijatelje. I unutar naših granica.

en: “Don’t be facetious, Orso. Your sisters both did their dynastic duty. Do you suppose Cathil wanted to move to Starikland?”
bs: — Ne budi lakrdijaš, Orso. Obje su tvoje sestre izvršile svoju dinastičku dužnost. Misliš li da se Cathil htjela preseliti u Starikland?

en: “The Countess Istarine of Affoia is a proven politician, and would bring us valuable allies in Styria.”
bs: — Grofica Istarine od Affoie prekaljena je političarka i donijela bi nam dragocjene saveznike u Stiriji.

en: He almost wished he was back at the hanging. That, he could theoretically have stopped. Over his mother, he was utterly powerless. His only chance was to wait her out. There were a finite number of women in the Circle of the World, after all.
bs: Gotovo da je poželio vratiti se na vješanje. To je, teoretski, mogao zaustaviti. Protiv svoje majke bio je potpuno nemoćan. Jedina mu je nada bila nadživjeti je. U krugu svijeta ionako je postojao konačan broj žena.

en: “Money made through trade, and dealings, and investments.” The queen spat the words as though they were criminal enterprises. For all Orso knew, Savine’s dealings were criminal enterprises. He wouldn’t at all have put it past her.
bs: "Novac stečen trgovinom, i poslovima, i ulaganjima." Kraljica izgovori te riječi kao da je riječ o zločinačkim pothvatima. Što se Orsa ticalo, Savinini poslovi su možda i bili zločinački pothvati. Uopće ne bi posumnjao u to.

en: He crushed his face up, nearly swallowed his tongue, coughed and hissed one more desperate, “Fuck!” through gritted teeth, then sagged back with a whimper, kicked and sagged again, legs shuddering weakly with aching after-spasms.
bs: Skupio je lice, umalo progutao jezik, zakašljao se i prosiktao još jedan očajnički "Jebi ga!" kroz stisnute zube, a onda malaksao natrag uz jecaj, trgnuo se i ponovno klonuo, dok su mu noge slabašno podrhtavale u grčevitim naknadnim spazmima.

en: “I can only think of one reason,” she said, hitching her skirts up and wriggling onto the desk beside him.
bs: — Mogu se dosjetiti se samo jednog razloga, dometnula je, podignuvši suknje i migoljeći se na pisaći stol pokraj njega.

en: “Very fucking fancy,” sneered Grise. Vick hadn’t known her long, but she was already getting tired of her. “Daresay you’ve got a fucking ‘dan’ in your name, too, eh, your ladyship?”
bs: —"Jako jebeno pomodno", podsmjehnula se Grise. Vik ju nije poznavala dugo, ali već joj se slabila penjati na Kruna glave. — Kladim se da u imenu imaš i neko "dan, ha, visočanstvo?

en: “My father was innocent. Of what they accused him of, anyway. But once Old Sticks got started…” Vick slapped the table with a bang, Tallow jumping so high he nearly hit the ceiling. “He leaked confessions like a broken drain. High Treason. They sent him to Angland. To the camps right up North.” Vick didn’t feel much like it, but she grinned. “And no one likes to split up a happy family. So they sent my ma with him. My ma, and my brother, and my sisters, and me. The camps, Grise. That’s where I g
bs: — Otac mi je bio nevin. Barem za ono za što su ga teretili. No kad se Stari Štapić jednom primio posla… Vik udari dlanom o stol uz prasak, a Talou poskoči tako visoko da je zamalo udario u strop. — Iz njega su priznanja curila poput puknute cijevi. Veleizdaja. Poslali su ga u Englend. U logore sasvim na sjeveru. Vik mu nije bila previše po volji, ali se nasmiješila."A nitko ne voli rastavljati sretnu obitelj. Pa su s njim poslali i majku mi. Moju majku, mog brata, moje sestre i mene. Logore, Gri

en: “I care that your source is reliable. I care that it’s going to work. I care that it’s not going to pop too early and shower bits of us all over the Three Farms.”
bs: — Tiče me se je li izvor pouzdan. Tiče me se hoće li uopće djelovati. Tiče me se da ne pukne prerano i raznese nas u komadiće po cijelom imanju Tri Farme.

en: She looked at Tallow last. He couldn’t be older than fifteen himself, and might only have had three good meals in that whole stretch. Reminded her of her brother, a little. Those skinny wrists sticking from frayed sleeves just a touch too short. Trying to put a hard face on but beaming fears and doubts out like a lighthouse through those big damp eyes.
bs: Na kraju pogleda Taloua. Nije mogao imati više od petnaest godina, a u cijelom tom razdoblju valjda se pošteno najjeo jedva tri puta. Nekako ju je podsjećao na brata. Onako mršava zapešća provirivala su iz iznošenih rukava koji bijahu mrvicu premali. Trudio se poprimiti opasan izraz lica, ali strah i sumnje izbijali su iz njega poput svjetioničkog snopa kroz one velike, vlažne oči.

en: “In here, we’re together.” She jerked her head towards the warped door in the warped frame. “Out there…” Out there, everyone stood on their own.
bs: — Ovdje smo zajedno. Trgnula je glavom prema iskrivljenim vratima u iskrivljenu dovratniku. — Tamo vani… Tamo vani svatko je stajao za sebe.

en: A grin spread across his face. Seeing it made her smile. Her first in a while. Hardly felt like her mouth should bend that way.
bs: Osmijeh joj se razlio po licu. Ugledavši ga, i ona se osmjehnula. Prvi put nakon dugo vremena. Jedva da se sjećala kako se usta miču tako.

en: “I know,” he said, with a sad smile, like thinking about it was a fun game to play, but just a game. He flipped the book shut and tossed it back down on the boards. “Guess there comes a time you have to give up on what you want and make the best of what you’re given.”
bs: — Znam, reče sa sjetnim osmijehom, kao da mu je razmišljanje o tome zabavna igra, ali ipak samo igra. Zaklopio je knjigu jednim pokretom i bacio je natrag na daske. — Valjda dođe vrijeme kad čovjek mora odustati od onoga što želi i izvući najbolje od onoga što mu je dano.

en: “Shit!” she squawked, scrambling from her clammy cloak. A man had been hanged from the tree right above where she’d been sleeping. If she’d stood up tall, she could’ve touched his dangling feet. When she lay down, it’d been too dark to see her own hands, let alone a corpse hung overhead. But there was no missing him now.
bs: — Sranje! — graknula je istrgnuvši se iz vlažnog ogrtača. O drvetu točno iznad mjesta gdje je spavala bio je obješen čovjek. Da se uspravila, mogla je dotaknuti njegove noge koje su visjele. Kad je legla, bilo je previše mračno da vidi vlastite ruke, a kamoli leš obješen iznad glave. No sada ga se nije moglo previdjeti.

en: “How much more of this can we take?” And she knew her voice was getting shrill and cracked but couldn’t stop herself.
bs: — Koliko ovoga još možemo podnijeti? — I znala je da joj glas zvuči piskavo i napuklo, ali se nije mogla zaustaviti.

en: She thought of wandering comfortably drunk into her room, and her own warm cot with the blanket her mother made, and the pretty things she’d found placed nicely on the shelf, and the pretty clothes all dry and beautiful in the chest.
bs: Pomisli kako je u ugodnoj opijenosti lutala u svoju sobu, na vlastiti topli ležaj s pokrivačem što ga je majka izradila, i na lijepe stvari koje bi pronašla uredno posložene na polici te na prekrasnu, suhu i divnu odjeću u škrinji.

en: She felt Isern step close. Put a gentle hand on her shoulder. Take her chin, and tip it up, and speak in a softer voice than she’d ever heard her use before. “D’you know what my da would say, whenever I cried?”
bs: Osjetila je kako je Izern zakoračila bliže. Kako joj je položila nježnu ruku na rame. Uhvatila ju je za bradu, podignula joj lice i progovorila nježnijim glasom no što ga je ikada prije čula od nje. — Znaš li što bi moj tata rekao kad god bih zaplakala?

en: “You cunt!” screeched Rikke and punched Isern in the mouth. It was a decent punch, snapping her head back and sending specks of spit flying. Rikke had always reckoned herself weak. More a weeper than a fighter. Now a fury she never knew she had boiled up in her. It was a fine, strong feeling. The first flicker of warmth she’d felt in days.
bs: — Kuja si! vrisnu Rike i udari Izern šakom u usta. Bio je to pošten udarac, od kojega joj je Šef trznula unatrag, a komadići sline prsnuli u zrak. Rike je oduvijek smatrala sebe slabom. Više plakacicom nego borcem. Sada je bijes za koji nije ni znala da ga posjeduje proključao u njoj. Bio je to dobar, snažan osjećaj. Prvi titraj topline koji je osjetila danima.

en: “Aye,” agreed Jin in his thick Northern accent, lowering the glass and thoughtfully scratching at his beard. “They’re some bastards, all right.”
bs: — Tako je, složio se Jin debelim sjevernjačkim naglaskom, spustivši optičko pomagalo i zamišljeno se počešavši po bradi. — Prave su to gnjide, nema Što.

en: Leo frowned, wishing he had a scar of his own. “If war’s so terrible, why don’t you take up farming or something?”
bs: Leo se namrštio, priželjkujući da i sam ima pokoji ožiljak. — Kad je rat već tako strašan, zašto se ne ostaviš toga i ne počneš baviti zemljoradnjom ili nečim sličnim?

en: As handsome a crowd of young heroes as you could hope to find. What a painting they’d make! Maybe Leo would get one commissioned. Who’d know an artist? He found himself glancing sideways.
bs: Skupina mladih junaka, naočitih kakve se samo poželjeti može. Kakvu bi sliku tek tvorili! Možda bi Leo naručio jedan portret. Tko li poznaje kakva slikara? Uhvatio se kako kradomice pogledava u stranu.

en: Leo could usually rely on some cheering when the common soldiers saw him. A few shouts of, “The Young Lion!” so he could shake a fist and slap a back and bellow some nonsense about the king. Now the men struggled past in silence with their eyes on the mud, and with no help yet from Midderland, even Leo was a lot less inspired by royalty than he used to be. It seemed the days of warrior-kings like Harod the Great and Casamir the Steadfast were far in the past, and supplies of patriotic bluster we
bs: Leo se obično mogao osloniti na pokoji uzvik ohrabrenja kad bi ga obični vojnici ugledali. Nekoliko povika: — Juvens Lav!" kako bi mogao stisnuti šaku, potapsati nekoga po leđima i zagrmjeti pokoju glupost o kralju. Sada su vojnici prolazili u tišini uprtih očiju u blato, a bez ikakve pomoći s Miderlanda, čak je i Leo osjećao znatno manju inspiraciju kraljevskom krunom nego nekad. Činilo se da su dani ratničkih kraljeva poput Haroda Velikog i Kazimira Nepokolebljivog davno prošli, a zalihe domol

en: “Jurand’s right.” He slapped his sword back, forced his hand away from the hilt. “We don’t know what’s behind that ridge. And mother would kill me.”
bs: — Džurand je u pravu. Vratio je mač natrag, prisilio ruku da se odmakne od drške. — Ne znamo što je iza tog grebena. A majka bi me ubila.

en: “I wouldn’t want them to miss the show.” His mother nodded towards the straggling column, thrown into even more disarray by a puddle in the track. “I put our shabbiest men in this valley with orders to march as badly as they could.”
bs: — Ne bih htjela da propuste predstavu. Majka je kimnula prema razvučenoj koloni koju je lokva na putu učinila još neurednijom. — Smjestila sam naše najjadnije ljude u ovu dolinu sa zapovijedima da marširaju što traljavije mogu.

en: “Did you never read that Verturio I gave you? Not fighting is what war’s all about.” And taking the last word, as ever, she trotted off westwards with her retinue following.
bs: "Nisi li nikada pročitao tog Verturija što sam ti ga dala? Ne boriti se jest ono o čemu se u ratu radi." I uzevši posljednju riječ, kao obično, otandrkala je zapadno sa svojom pratnjom u stopu.

en: Leo stooped and plucked them up before the boy could bend, gripped them in his teeth while he shrugged off his cloak and offered it out. “I’ll swap you.”
bs: Leo se sagne i pokupi ih prije negoli se dječak mogao sagnuti, ugura ih u zube dok je svlačio ogrtač i ponudi ga. — Mijenjat ću se s tobom.

en: “I’ll try to remember how to play,” he called over his shoulder, “if you lot can remember how to march!”
bs: — Pokušat ću se prisjetiti kako se svira, dobacio je preko ramena, ako se vi momci sjetite kako se maršira!

en: “Tart,” he said, baring his teeth, “but tolerable. Like life, eh, lads? Like life.” They stared at him blankly. He heaved a weary sigh. “Back to it, then.”
bs: — Kiselkasto, prozbori otkrivajući zube, ali podnošljivo. Baš kao život, ha, momci? Baš kao život. Oni su ga tupo promatrali. On ispušta Trdak uzdah. — Natrag na posao, dakle.

en: “Out there in the sun?” Clover chuckled to himself. “I didn’t become a bloody teacher so I could get up and do it my bloody self.”
bs: — Ovdje na suncu? Klover se nasmija u sebi. — Nisam postao jebeni učitelj zato da ustajem i radim to sam, u pičku materinu.

en: Clover took a slow breath in and slowly blew it out. “First of all, it’s about deciding when to, and when not to. In the end… the only thing a man can really do… is pick his moment. Watch for the opening, and recognise it when it comes, and seize it.” And Clover snatched at a handful o’ nothing and shook his fist. “Picking your moment. That’s the secret. You understand?”
bs: Klover duboko udahnu pa polako izdahnu."Kao prvo, sve je u tome da odlučiš kada ćeš udariti, a kada ne. Na koncu… jedino što čovjek doista može jest… odabrati svoj trenutak. Paziti na otvor, prepoznati ga čim se ukaže i zgrabiti ga." I Klover zgrabi pregršt ničega pa stisnu šaku. — Odabrati svoj trenutak. U tome je tajna. Shvaćate li?

en: Calder worked his mouth even more sourly. He was a sour sort these days, given how much life had given him, or how much he’d managed to claw from it, leastways. Time was he’d had a fine sense of humour, but the more men get, the sourer they tend to turn, and Black Calder had almost the whole North. His brother Scale might wear the king’s chain, but everyone knew Black Calder made the king’s choices.
bs: Kalder još kiselije izvijesni usne. U posljednje vrijeme bio je nekako kiselog raspoloženja, s obzirom na to koliko mu je život pružio ili koliko je uspio izmusti iz njega, naposljetku. Bilo je vrijeme kad je imao istančan smisao za humor, ali što Folk više dobivaju, to obično postaju kiseliji, a Black Kalder je držao gotovo cijeli Sjever. Njegov brat Ljuska možda je nosio kraljevski lanac, ali svatko je znao da Black Kalder donosi kraljevske odluke.

en: “Those…” Clover considered denying any acquaintance with them, but doubted he’d get away with it. “Are my pupils.”
bs: — Oni… Klover je razmislio o tome da zaniječe bilo kakvu povezanost s njima, ali sumnjao je da bi se izvukao. — Moji su učenici.

en: “My father used to say you point three Northmen the same way they’ll be killing each other before you can order the charge. I’ve got Gregun Hollowhead and his boys from the West Valleys as like to join the Dogman as fight against him. How do I make them take my say-so when my own blood won’t? If Stour weren’t my son, I’d be forced to say the boy’s a fucking prick.”
bs: — Moj otac je znao reći da trojicu Sjevernjaka okreneš u istom smjeru i već će početi ubijati jedni druge prije nego što stigneš izdati zapovijed za juriš. Imam Greguna Holouheda i njegove momke iz Zapadnih dolina koji će se prije pridružiti Dogmanu nego se boriti protiv njega. Kako da natjeram njih da poslušaju moju riječ kad moja vlastita krv neće? Da Staur nije moj Filio, bio bih prisiljen reći da je taj dečko jebeni kreten.

en: “Reckon that’s all any of us can do, in the end. You’re a straight edge, Clover. You’ve always been loyal.”
bs: — Smatram da je to sve što bilo tko od nas može učiniti, na kraju. Ti si čvrst oslonac, Klover. Uvijek si bio odan.

en: “Oh, me too.” And he patted his belly. “The body of a hero lies just below this carefully nurtured layer of fat.”
bs: — Oh, i ja isto. I potapšao se po trbuhu. — Tijelo heroja leži tik ispod ovog brižno njegovanog sloja sala.

en: Clover thought he’d caught that old burning-building whiff on the breeze. “Why fight for something if all you do is burn it?”
bs: Klover pomisli kako je osjetio onaj stari vonj spaljenih zgrada na povjetarcu. — Zašto se boriti za nešto ako ćeš sve ionako spaliti?

en: Stour Nightfall fixed Clover with that wet, cold, hollow stare, quick hand sitting loose on the pommel of his sword, and his grin was full of good teeth and bad threats.
bs: Staur Najtfol uperi u Klovera onaj vlažan, hladan, šuplji Oko, dok mu je brza ruka ležala opušteno na dršku mača, a osmijeh mu bijaše pun dobrih zuba i loših prijetnji.

en: “Never scratch your eyebrows with a sword.” Clover grinned. No one else did, but that was their lookout. “Best to just leave ’em in the scabbard whenever possible, I’d say. Drawn swords are bloody dangerous, that’s a fact.”
bs: — Nikada ne češi obrve mačem. Klover se nasmiješi. Nitko drugi nije, ali to je bio njihov Trobli. — Rekao bih da ih je najbolje jednostavno ostaviti u koricama kad god je to moguće. Izvučeni mačevi opasno su krvavi, to je živa istina.

en: “Shit,” came a voice, so loud it seemed in Rikke’s ear, and she startled, might’ve splashed from the bank on an instinct if Isern’s hand hadn’t clamped tight about her numb arm under the water.
bs: — Sranje, dopro je glas, toliko glasan da joj se učinio u samom Rikinu uhu, te se trgnula i umalo instinktivno prsnula iz vode s obale da joj Izern nije čvrsto stisnula umrtvljenu ruku pod vodom.

en: “Union are pulling back as fast as they can. Some skirmishes but there’s no real fight in ’em. No sign o’ the Dogman’s boys. Running, I reckon.”
bs: — Unija se povlači brže nego što mogu. Bilo je manjih čarki, ali u njima nema prave borbe. Ni traga od Psa Čovjekova momaka. Bježe, rekla bih.

en: “Chief!” someone roared up on the road. “Nightfall! The king-in-waiting!” And there was an approving clatter of weapons on shields.
bs: — Glavaru! zaurlao je netko gore na cesti. — Najtfol! Kralj u čekanju! I prolomio se odobravajući zveket oružja o štitove.

en: A snorting chuckle from the enthusiastic pisser. “Well, who wouldn’t want a girl out in the woods?” There was a silence, like the jest had miscarried. Certainly Rikke wasn’t fucking laughing. “How do we tell this girl from another?”
bs: Frktavi smijeh onog zagrijanog kretena. — Pa, tko ne bi želio djevojku u šumi?" Nastala je tišina, kao da šala nije sjela. Rike se Sejf nije smijala. — Po čemu ćemo razlikovati ovu djevojku od drugih?

en: “But that’s for later.” And Nightfall gave a disappointed sigh. “Can’t cook what you haven’t caught, can you? My father’s offering a big gild for her, that’s sure. Whoever brings her in’ll be a wealthy man.”
bs: — Ali to je za kasnije. I Najtfol uzdahne razočarano. — Ne možeš skuhati ono što nisi uhvatio, zar ne? Moj otac nudi veliko zlato za nju, to je Sejf. Tko god je dovede, bit će imućan čovjek.

en: Rikke could only agree. She thought she saw a hint of their reflections, dancing among the black branches in the water.
bs: Rike se mogla samo složiti. Učinilo joj se da nazire njihove odbljeske kako plešu među crnim granama u vodi.

en: When he saw the house, huddled among those bare trees, lamplight showing around the shutters, he had this strange urge to walk on. This strange thought he didn’t belong there any more. Not with what he’d seen. Not with what he’d done. What if he trod it in with him?
bs: Ugledavši kuću stisnutu među golim stablima, dok se svjetlost svjetiljke probijala oko šurki, obuzeo ga je čudan poriv da produži dalje. Čudna pomisao kako više ne pripada ondje. Ne nakon svega što je vidio. Ne nakon svega što je učinio. Što ako sve to unese sa sobom?

en: Liddy stepped forward and he shrank away, hunched and hurting, arms up as if to fend her off. Like she was made of glass and might shatter in his hands. She caught him even so. Thin arms, but a hold he couldn’t break, and though she was a head shorter than him, she held his face against her chest, and kissed his head, and whispered, “Shhhh, now. Shhhhh.”
bs: Lidi iskorači naprijed, a on se trgne natrag, pogrbljen i shrvan, podigavši ruke kao da se želi obraniti. Kao da je od stakla i da bi se mogla rasprsnuti u njegovim rukama. Ipak ga je uhvatila. Tanke ruke, ali stisak koji nije mogao razbiti, i premda je bila glavu niža od njega, privukla mu je lice na svoja prsa, poljubila ga u glavu i prošaptala: — Šššš, sad. Šššš.

en: When he left, she’d been boyish, quiet, awkward. As if her skin didn’t fit her. She was bony still, but there was a quick strength in the way she moved. She’d grown up fast. She’d had to. Another thunk and two more neat pieces of wood went tumbling.
bs: Kad je otišao, bila je dječakobana, tiha, nespretna. Kao da joj koža nije pristajala. Još je bila koščata, ali u njezinim je pokretima tutnjala hitra snaga. Brzo je odrasla. Morala je. Još jedan udarac i dva uredna komada drveta otkotrljala su se na zemlju.

en: “Well…” All that time spent dreaming of her face and now she was looking right at him, it was hard to meet her eye. “It was bad.”
bs: — Pa… Nakon sveg tog vremena provedenog u sanjarenju o njezinu licu, sada kad ga je gledala ravno u oči, bilo mu je teško susresti njezin Oko. — Bilo je loše.

en: May blinked over at her mother, and Liddy gave an odd kind of grimace, and Broad felt that dread pressing on him all the heavier. “What is it?”
bs: Mej je trepnula prema majci, Lidi je napravila čudnu grimasu, a Brod je osjetio kako ga strava pritišće još jače. — Što je?

en: “None o’ this works without a flock!” His father had raised sheep, and his grandfather, and his grandfather’s grandfather. Felt like the whole world had come unravelled. “What’ll we do?” He found he’d clenched his fists again. He was shouting but he couldn’t stop. “What’ll we do?”
bs: — Ništa od ovoga nema smisla bez stada! Njegov je otac uzgajao ovce, i njegov djed, i djedova djeda. Činilo se kao da se cijeli svijet raspao. — Što ćemo sad? Otkrio je da je ponovno stisnuo šake. Vikao je, ali nije se mogao zaustaviti. "Što ćemo učiniti?"

en: There were three men coming up it. Coming slow, like they had all day to get there. One on a big chestnut. Two on a wagon with a creaky wheel. Gunnar recognised the driver. Lennart Seldom, the miller’s younger brother. Broad had always reckoned him a coward and there was nothing in his shifty squint now to change his opinion.
bs: Dolazila su trojica muškaraca. Dolazili su sporo, kao da imaju cijeli dan na raspolaganju. Jedan na velikom doratu. Dvojica na kolima sa škripavim kotačem. Gunar je prepoznao kočijaša. Lennarta Seldoma, mlađega mlinarovog brata. Brod ga je oduvijek smatrao kukavicom i ni u njegovu se mutnom pogledu nije naziralo išta što bi promijenilo to mišljenje.

en: “Even bigger,” said the bearded one, barely giving Broad a glance as he settled his hat back on. “Evidently.”
bs: — Još veći, dometnu bradonja, jedva pogledavši Broda dok je namještao šešir natrag na glavu. — Očito.

en: Seldom sneaked another shifty glance at Liddy. “Just wanted to give her some more time, ’cause we all know each other and—”
bs: Seldom kradomice baci još jedan prikriveni Oko na Lidi. — Samo smo joj htjeli dati još malo vremena jer se svi znamo i — "

en: Broad caught his boot and flung him out of his saddle. Marsh gave a shocked grunt, flailed at the air as he went tumbling down.
bs: Brod ga je uhvatio za čizmu i izbacio iz sedla. Marsh je ispustio zgranut prigušeni uzvik, mlatarajući rukama dok se strmoglavljivao dolje.

en: He managed to swing the bow but Broad brushed it away with his forearm, caught Able by the front of his jacket. He gave a little hoot as Broad jerked him into the air and rammed him head first into the old gatepost, blood speckling the side of the wagon. He flopped down with one arm wedged through that creaky wheel, smashed skull bent all the way backwards.
bs: Uspio je zamahnuti lukom, ali ga je Brod otresao podlakticom, uhvativši Ablea za predio prsa na jakni. Able je ispustio tihi hropac dok ga je Brod trzajem povukao u zrak i zabio glavačke u stari stup od ograde, dok je krv prskala po stranici kola. Skliznuo je dolje s jednom rukom zaglavljenom kroz onaj škripavi kotač, razlupane lubanje savijene skroz unatrag.

en: “With thanks to our distinguished patrons—the Lady Ardee, and her daughter Lady Savine dan Glokta!” Curnsbick gestured towards Savine’s box and she smiled over her fan as though her delicate feelings could hardly stand the attention. There were whoops, and calls of, “Hear, hear.” From members who particularly wanted her money, she imagined.
bs: — Uz zahvalnost našim uvaženim pokroviteljima — gospođi Ardi i njezinoj kćeri, gospođici Savine dan Glokta! Kurnsbik je mahnuo prema Savininoj loži, a ona se osmjehnula iza lepeze kao da njezini nježni osjećaji jedva podnose toliku pozornost. Iz publike su se začuli povici i uzvici odobravanja: — Tako je, tako je! Od članova koji su ponajviše željeli njezin novac, moglo bi se reći.

en: A considerable crowd had already gathered beneath the three great chandeliers, buzzing with excited chatter, seething with prospects and proposals. Knots of soberly dressed gentlemen broke and re-formed, drawn into dizzying swirls and eddies, ladies’ dresses bright dots of colour bobbing on the flood. Here and there, one could even spot the fabulous robes of some relic of the old merchant guilds. Savine’s practised eye picked out those with money or connections, those without sucked spinning aft
bs: Golemo se mnoštvo već okupilo pod trima velikim lusterima, zujeći od uzbuđena čavrljanja, uzavrelo od izgleda i prijedloga. Skupine staloženo odjevenih gospoda raspadale su se i ponovno okupljale, uvučene u vrtoglave kovitlace i vrtloge, dok su ženske haljine bile svijetle točkice boje što su poskakivale na toj matici. Tu i tamo moglo se opaziti čak i bajne odore kakva relikvija iz starih trgovačkih cehova. Savinino vježbano oko izdvojilo je one s novcem ili vezama, dok su oni bez njih bili uvuč

en: “I only need to convince the owner of the land, a relative of Lord Isher, and I know you are a close confidante of his sister…”
bs: — Samo trebam uvjeriti vlasnika zemljišta, rođaka lorda Išera, a znam da ste bliska povjerenica njegove sestre…

en: “Lady Savine?” A woman, young, red-wigged, freckle-shouldered, with a way of peeking over her gaudy fan that was meant to be winsome but to Savine looked merely sly. “I am—forgive me—a tremendous admirer of yours.”
bs: — Lady Savine? Žena, mlada, crvenokosa, pjegavih ramena, s navikom da proviruje iznad svoje kičaste lepeze, što je trebalo djelovati umiljato, ali je na Savine djelovalo tek lukavo. "Ja sam – oprostite mi – golema vaša obožavateljica."

en: “Certainly not in beauty.” He was unremarkable, it was true, apart from his bright eyes. They were different colours, one blue, one green. “My name is Yoru Sulfur.”
bs: — Zasigurno ne u ljepoti. Bio je neupadljiv, istina, osim po svojim sjajnim očima. Bile su različitih boja, jedna plava, jedna zelena. — Zovem se Joru Salfur.

en: “There was a time, in the days of Euz and his sons, when magic was the best way to do it. But that time is long past. These days…” And Sulfur glanced about the heaving foyer and leaned close as if to share a secret. “I begin to think this is better.”
bs: — Bilo je vrijeme, u danima Euza i njegovih sinova, kada je Umijeće bila najbolji način za to. Ali to je vrijeme davno prošlo. Ovih dana… Salfur baci Oko po užurbanom predvorju i nagne se blizu kao da želi podijeliti tajnu. — Počinjem misliti da je ovo bolje.

en: “Curnsbick, you old dog!” It was Arinhorm, the deliverer of the first address, blundering into their conversation like a hog into a rose garden.
bs: — Kurnsbik, stari moj vuče! Bio je to Arinhorm, govornik s početka, koji se upleo u njihov razgovor poput vepra u ružičnjak.

en: There was sense in what he said, but Savine detested the way he said it. “My thanks, but it is not iron that interests me at the moment, but soap.”
bs: U njegovim je riječima bilo smisla, ali Savine je mrzila način na koji ih je izgovarao. — Zahvaljujem, ali mene u ovom trenutku ne zanima željezo, već sapun.

en: “Master Arinhorm looks rather angry,” murmured Curnsbick as they moved away through the crowd. “You might find, in the long run, that a little generosity can repay itself five-fold. Goodwill can be the best of investments—”
bs: — Majstor Arinhorm djeluje prilično ljutito, promrmlja Kurnsbik dok su se probijali kroz gomilu. — Možda ćeš dugoročno otkriti da se malo darežljivosti može peterostruko isplatiti. Dobra volja može biti najbolja investicija…

en: “I suppose so,” she grudgingly admitted, putting the distasteful union of Arinhorm and Heugen from her mind. “As long as they’re paying me rent.”
bs: — Valjda, nevoljko prizna, izbacujući iz glave neugodan Unija Arinhorma i Heugen. — Sve dok mi plaćaju najamninu.

en: “Especially not kings, Your Majesty,” said Savine, sinking into an even deeper curtsy. One of the royal party issued a choked splutter at her insolence, but no risk, no profit.
bs: — Pogotovo ne kraljeve, Vaša Uzvišenosti, reče Savine, spuštajući se u još dublji naklon. Jedan iz kraljeve pratnje prigušeno se zakašlja na njezinu drskost, no bez rizika nema ni dobitka.

en: “My apologies, Lady Savine. My apologies, everyone! I am needed at the Agriont.” The gilt edge of His Majesty’s cloak snapped as he spun on one highly polished heel, his retinue crowding after like a gaggle of self-important ducklings behind their mother, not a smile among them.
bs: — Ispričavam se, lady Savine. Ispričavam se svima! Potreban sam u Agriontu. Pozlaćeni rub plašta Vašeg Veličanstva škljocnuo je dok se okrenuo na jednoj visokoj, uglačanoj peti, a njegova ga je pratnja slijedila poput jata umišljenih pačića za svojom majkom, bez ijednog osmijeha na licima.

en: “—can be as inconsistent as he damn well pleases.” Orso’s fumbling hand closed about the handle of a jug and he lifted it and took a swig, realised too late there was stale ale in it rather than water, and spat it over the wall in a mist.
bs: — može biti nedosljedan koliko mu se prokletom Bogu svidi. Orsova ruka napipa dršku vrča, on ga podigne i otpije gutljaj, prekasno shvativši da je u njemu usidjelo pivo, a ne voda, te ga u obliku maglice ispljune preko zida.

en: “Sorry!” said Orso. “Terribly sorry, but… Northmen! Invaded! Lions and wolves and whatever!” He grabbed his little box and took a pinch of pearl dust up each nostril.
