bs: Rijeka je srkala prolazeći, ljubičasta, narančasta i zelena od golemih mrlja neprirodnih boja iz tvornica boja uzvodno, poskakujući na otpacima, uzburkana u smrdljivu pjenu desecima udarajućih vodenih kotača. Na lijevoj obali nalazila se neka vrsta žala, išaranog tragovima plime i mrtve smeđe trave, posutog gradskim otpacima, krpama, kožama, slomljenim stolcima, krhotinama stakla, zahrđalom žicom i stvarima previše istrulim da bi se prepoznale, sve to izbljuvano iz napaćenih voda, što su kljucal

en: She wanted nothing more, right then, than to burrow into the refuse and hide. But they would be coming for her. They knew who she was. Who her father was. They would have broken down the office door by now, found the loose board. They would be following her bloody trail, through the machines, past the wheel. Any moment now, they would find her.
bs: Nije željela ništa više u tom trenutku nego se zagnjuriti u otpad i sakriti se. No oni će krenuti za njom. Znali su tko je. Tko joj je otac. Do sada su već razvalili vrata ureda, pronašli pomičnu dasku. Pratili su njezin krvavi trag, kroz strojeve, pokraj kotača. Svakog će je trenutka pronaći.

en: Lisbit practised her sitting-up-straight. She wasn’t sure how Lady Savine made her neck look the way she did. She couldn’t have more bones in it than anyone else. But Lisbit had been studying her, every spare moment, and she’d get the trick of it. You had to work your shoulder blades back till it felt like they’d touch, then not lift your chin exactly, but sort of lift your whole throat…
bs: Lisbit je vježbala uspravno sjedenje. Nije bila sigurna kako je gospođa Savine uspjela postići da joj vrat izgleda tako kako je izgledao. Sejf nije imala više kralježaka od bilo koga drugoga. No Lisbit ju je promatrala u svakom slobodnom trenutku i dokučit će tu vještinu. Morala je povući lopatice unatrag dok joj se ne bi učinilo da će se dodirnuti, a onda ne podignuti bradu, nego nekako podignuti cijelo grlo…

en: At that moment, two of the others came out dragging Vallimir between them, his clothes torn and his face bloody and his eyes barely open. One of the lads spat on him. “Fucking bastard!” growled another.
bs: Utom dvojica iziđoše vukući Valimira između sebe, poderane odjeće, krvava lica i jedva otvorenih očiju. Jedan ga momak popljunu. — Jebeni kopilan!" zaurla drugi.

en: Kurbman turned back to the workers, his voice cracking. “We’ve a chance to make a better world, brothers! A better world, you understand? But we have to do it right.”
bs: Kurbman se okrenu natrag radnicima, napuklim glasom: — Imamo priliku stvoriti bolji svijet, braćo! Bolji svijet, razumijete li? Ali moramo to učiniti ispravno.

en: They had dragged him from behind his desk. “Damn you!” Dragged him across his own deck. The factory floor, that was, pelted with rubbish by his own employees, who were working with more vigour than they ever had before, destroying the machines he had hired them to operate! “Curse you all!” After everything he had done for these men, for this city. They had manacled him to this damn chain, shackled to two dozen other helpless unfortunates like slaves in bloody Gurkhul. “How dare you?”
bs: Izvukli su ga iza njegova stola. — Prokleti bili!" Vukli su ga preko vlastite palube. Bio je to pogon tvornice, zasut smećem od strane njegovih vlastitih radnika, koji su radili s više žara nego ikad prije, uništavajući strojeve koje im je platio da opslužuju! — Prokleti bili svi redom!" Nakon svega što je učinio za te ljude, za ovaj grad. Okovali su ga za ovaj prokleti lanac, privezani uz dvadesetak drugih bespomoćnih nesretnika poput robova u krvavom Gurkhulu."Kako se usuđujete?"

en: “These bastards!” he snarled at the nearest guard. The nearest Breaker. The nearest traitor. The nearest animal. “I am Karlric dan Resling, and I’ll see you all—”
bs: "Ovi gadovi!" zanjeskao je najbližem stražaru. Najbližem Rušitelju. Najbližem izdajici. Najbližoj životinji. — Ja sam Karlric dan Resling i pobit ću vas sve —"

en: Her father had always been so impatient when she cried. “Toughen up, girl.” Furious, as though her tears were an unfair attack on him. Sometimes he had cuffed her around the head, but the blows seemed to have made her less tough, not more. Her husband had opted for a kind of benign neglect instead. The idea of his being interested enough to hit her was absurd. Being shackled to a chain was the most attention anyone had paid her in years.
bs: Otac joj je uvijek bio tako nestrpljiv kad god bi plakala. — Odrasti, curice." Bijesan, kao da su njezine suze predstavljale nepravedan napad na njega. Ponekad ju je ošamario po glavi, no činilo se da su je ti udarci učinili manje otpornom, a ne otpornijom. Njezin je muž umjesto toga izabrao neku vrstu dobroćudnog zanemarivanja. Sama pomisao da bi mogao biti dovoljno zainteresiran da je udari zvučala je apsurdno. Biti okovana lancem predstavljalo je najveću količinu pažnje koju joj je bilo tko p

en: They passed three hunched shapes on the ground. Red jackets ripped, stained dark. Soldiers. If the army couldn’t stop this madness, what hope for the rest of them?
bs: Prošli su pored tri pogurena tijela na tlu. Crvene jakne poderane, tamno umrljane. Vojnici. Ako vojska nije mogla zaustaviti ovo Ludilo, kakva je nada preostala ostalima?

en: “Wait,” said the Breaker in charge o’ the chain, and the column staggered to a halt on the bridge. Strange thing was, Colton knew him. Lock was his name, he thought. He’d been a weaver, way back when. Remembered him and Colton’s old man laughing together at a meeting o’ the guild, before his old man died and the guild got broke up. He was a grim-looking bastard now. But a lot of weavers were. Mostly on account of Masrud’s weaving engine.
bs: — Čekajte, reče Trdak zadužen za lanac i kolona se zateturala te stala na mostu. Čudno je bilo što ga je Colton poznavao. Zvao se Lock, činilo mu se. Nekad davno bio je tkalac. Sjećao se kako su se on i Coltonov stari zajedno smijali na sastanku esnafa prije nego što mu je stari umro, a esnaf se raspao. Sad je bio sumoran gad. No, mnogi su tkalci bili takvi. Najviše zbog Masrudova stroja za tkanje.

en: A few men bleeding and a few women blubbing but Lock felt no pity. Didn’t feel anything. Hadn’t felt anything for a long time.
bs: Nekoliko je muškaraca krvarilo, a nekoliko žena je šmrcalo, ali Lock nije osjećao sažaljenje. Nije osjećao ništa. Već jako dugo nije osjećao ništa.

en: She dared not go up onto the bridge, where she would be hemmed in and helpless. She had only followed the prisoners because she hardly knew what else to do. At least with them ahead, it felt as if she was not quite alone. But she could not help them. They could not help her. There was no help for anyone.
bs: Nije se usudila kročiti na most, gdje bi bila stiješnjena i bespomoćna. Kretala se za zatvorenicima samo zato što jedva da je znala što bi drugo mogla učiniti. Barem joj se uz njih činilo da nije sasvim sama. No nije im mogla pomoći. Niti oni njoj. Spasa nije bilo ni za koga.

en: A murk even more hellish than usual had descended on the city as the sun sank and smoke from burning buildings billowed into the streets. Shapes loomed and vanished, phantoms in the soupy gloom. Savine was utterly lost. Valbeck was become a maze of horrors from which there was no escape. Could this be the same world as the one in which she presided over meetings of the Solar Society, changing lives with a flick of her fan?
bs: Sumrak još pakleniji nego inače spustio se na grad dok je sunce tonulo, a dim od zapaljenih zgrada kuljao ulicama. Obisi su se nazirali i nestajali, utvare u juhi magle. Savine se potpuno izgubila. Valbek se prometnuo u labirint strahota iz kojega nije bilo izlaza. Je li to doista bio isti svijet onome u kojem je predsjedala sastancima Sunčanog društva, mijenjajući živote jednim zamahom lepeze?

en: Like a poem. Like a prayer. She used to laugh when Zuri spoke of God. How could someone so clever believe something so silly? Now she tried to believe herself. Wished she could believe.
bs: Poput pjesme. Poput molitve. Nekad se smijala kad bi Zuri govorila o Bogu. Kako netko tako pametan može vjerovati u nešto tako glupo? Sada je pokušavala vjerovati sama. Željela je moći vjerovati.

en: Sparks was scared of nothing. The more he said it, to everyone else and to himself, the more true it became. Acres had been scared of everything. Had hidden crying in the cupboard when men came to visit his mother. Sparks hated that weak little cringing bastard, scared of everything. So he’d shrugged him off like a snake sheds its skin. Sparks was scared of nothing.
bs: Sparks se nije bojao ničega. Što je više to ponavljao, svima drugima i sebi samome, to je to bivalo istinitije. Acres se bojao svega. Skrivao se plačući u ormaru kad bi muškarci dolazili u posjet njegovoj majci. Sparks je mrzio tog slabog, prepredenog malog kopileta, ustrašenog od svega. Pa ga je otresao sa sebe poput zmije koja presvlači kožu. Sparks se nije bojao ničega.

en: And he scrubbed the bastard’s hanging head with his hand and then, ’cause his hair was all full of wine and blood, had to wipe it on his bloody shirt front. Then he hopped down, and grabbed the bottle out of Framer’s hand, and took a pull. The spirits helped him feel brave. Helped him feel like Acres was far away, and the cupboard, too, and Judge even.
bs: I protrlja gadovu obešenu glavu rukom, a onda ju je, budući da mu je kosa bila puna vina i krvi, morao obrisati o prednji dio svoje krvave košulje. Zatim skoči dolje, ugrabi bocu iz Framerove ruke i otpije gutljaj. Žestoko piće pomoglo mu je da se osjeti hrabrim. Pomoglo mu je da osjeti kako su Acres daleko, i ormar također, pa čak i Džadž.

en: He had wondered if it was a questionable neighbourhood in which to lease an office. But to be taken seriously, an engineer needs an office, and the rents in the better parts of Valbeck were out of all compass. They had said the Breakers were entirely under control. Had been taught harsh lessons. That the Burners were just a rumour spread by pessimistic moaners intent on talking down the city. They had pointed out the brand-new and thoroughly modern branch of Valint and Balk, and talked of gentri
bs: Pitao se je li unajmio ured u sumnjivoj četvrti. No da bi ga se shvatilo ozbiljno, inženjeru je potreban ured, a najamnine u boljim dijelovima Valbeka bile su potpuno nedostupne. Govorili su mu da su Lomljači pod potpunom kontrolom. Da su naučili gorke lekcije. Da su Palioci samo glasine što ih šire pesimistični cmizdravci s namjerom da podcjenjuju grad. Pokazali su mu potpuno novu i modernu podružnicu Valint i Balka te naširoko govorili o gentrifikaciji.

en: A woman ripped down her dress and another poured wine over her bared breasts and a man shoved his face between them like a pig into a trough, all shrieking with desperate laughter, as if the world would end tomorrow. Perhaps it had ended already. The fiddle-player capered past, sawing discordant music, broken strings dangling from the neck of his instrument.
bs: Žena je rastrgala svoju haljinu, druga je prosula vino preko svojih obnaženih grudi, a muškarac je zario lice među njih poput svinje u korito, dok su svi vrištali od očajničkog smijeha, kao da će svijet skončati sutra. Možda je već i skončao. Svirkač na violini poskakivao je u prolazu, proizvodeći raštimanu glazbu, dok su potrgane žice visjele s vrata njegovog glazbala.

en: Mally wanted to be free. Who doesn’t? In principle. It’s a pretty dream, to go running through the flower garden with your hair down. But she didn’t want to be free of getting paid. She’d tried that, and it hurt like you wouldn’t believe. That’s how she’d ended up whoring in the first place. No one had forced her to it, exactly. It was just that a choice between whoring and hunger weren’t no choice at all.
bs: Mally je željela biti slobodna. Tko ne bi? U načelu. Divan je to san, trčkaraš kroz cvjetnjak raspuštene kose. No nije željela biti slobodna od primanja plaće. Bila je to već probala, i boljelo je kao suvišno i pomisliti. Zbog toga je i završila u kupleraju. Nitko ju na to nije natjerao, barem ne doslovno. Jednostavno je izbor između kurvanja i gladi bio posve izlišan.

en: She saw Sparks watching her. Felt like she had to do something cruel, show she was one of them. The naked lawyer blundered past and she stuck out a boot and tripped him. He tumbled over, rolling in the dirt, and she pointed at him and howled with forced laughter.
bs: Vidjela je kako je Sparks promatra. Osjećala je da mora učiniti nešto okrutno, pokazati da je jedna od njih. Goli odvjetnik protetura pokraj nje, a ona podmetnu čizmu i spotaknu ga. On se sruši, kotrljajući se po prašini, na što ona uperi prst u nj i grohotom se nasmija iznuđenim smijehom.

en: He had spent his life’s work on that firm. Built it up with his own hands. Well, his and Zalev’s and Crun’s, he supposed, but mostly his, since Zalev had died and Crun was concentrating on patents.
bs: Cijeli je životni vijek uložio u tu firmu. Izgradio ju je vlastitim rukama. Dobro, svojim, Zalevljevim i Crunovim, pretpostavljao je, no ponajviše svojim, budući da je Zalev preminuo, a Crun se usredotočio na patente.

en: “Dance, you fat shit!” And he kicked the lawyer in the jaw as he tried to stagger up and knocked him on his back, threw the whip down and snatched up a hammer in both hands, started beating at the statue again.
bs: — Pleši, debelo govno! I udario je odvjetnika nogom u čeljust dok se pokušavao uspraviti te ga oborio na leđa, bacio bič i objema rukama grabio čekić, počeo ponovno udarati po kipu.

en: He wobbled with her shaking, but he did not wake. One of his eyes was a little open, just a slit of white showing. But he did not wake.
bs: Zaljuljao se od njezina treskanja, ali se nije probudio. Jedno mu je oko bilo napola otvoreno, tek se bjelina nazirala u procjepu. Ali se nije probudio.

en: The priests said if she prayed every morning and every night and was pure within then good things would happen. She had prayed every night and every morning. Had she done it wrong? Was she rotten inside, that God should punish her?
bs: Svećenici su govorili da će se, ako se moli svako jutro i svaku večer i bude čista srca, dogoditi lijepe stvari. Molila se svake večeri i svakog jutra. Je li to činila pogrešno? Je li bila trula iznutra kad ju je Bog trebao kazniti?

en: “Please!” shouted Hessel, grabbing at her bare arm. “Please! Please!” She started to scream it, louder and louder, she could not stop herself. She was not even sure if she was saying it in the Union tongue or the Kantic.
bs: — Molim te! povikala je Hesel hvatajući je za golu ruku. — Molim te! Molim te! Počela je to vikati, sve glasnije i glasnije, nije se mogla zaustaviti. Nije bila ni sigurna govori li to jezikom Unije ili kantijskim.

en: She fled, forcing her trembling legs to another effort, ducked down a side street, slid in filth, went over in the gutter and scrambled up again. She plunged past a staring old woman, through a court crammed between tiny houses, a great heap of ash and dung and bones piled in the midst, crawling with vermin.
bs: Pobjegla je, prisiljavajući svoje drhtave noge na novi napor, skrenula u sporednu ulicu, skliznula u prljavštinu, pala u jarak i ponovno se uspentrala. Projurila je pokraj zapanjene starice, kroz Sud stiješnjen između malenih kuća, usred kojega se uzdizala velika gomila pepela, gnojiva i kostiju, prepuna gamadi.

en: “None of your business.” Savine tried to make her voice effortlessly confident, the way it used to be. Sound in command, you’re halfway to being there. It came out a quavering croak. But her accent was plain, even so.
bs: — Nije to tvoja briga. Savine je pokušala namjestiti glas da zvuči samouvjereno, onako kako je nekad zvučao. Ako zvučiš moćno, već si na pola puta. Izletjelo je u obliku drhtavog graktanja. Ali naglasak joj je svejedno bio jasan.

en: The one with the cap reeled away and Savine darted forward, slashing him across the back of the thigh. She fumbled the sword and it caught him with the flat, didn’t even cut through his ragged trousers, but it was enough to make him stumble and he sprawled in the gutter.
bs: Onaj s kapom se zanese unatrag i Savine jurišajući izleti naprijed, posjekavši ga preko stražnje strane bedra. Spretno zahvati mačem i udari ga plosnatom stranom, nije mu čak ni prerezala otrcane hlače, ali bilo je dovoljno da se spotakne i sruši u jarak.

en: He hoisted her effortlessly up beside him. She saw torch flames bobbing, could hardly breathe for fear, hardly move for it. She shrank down trembling behind a broken chest of drawers, clung to a chair leg.
bs: On ju je bez napora podigao pored sebe. Vidjela je plamene baklje kako plutaju, jedva je disala od straha, jedva se pomicala. Skupila se drhteći iza razbijene komode, priljubivši se uz nogu stolice.

en: The big man pushed his folded lenses into Savine’s limp hand and gently curled her fingers shut around them. He sounded almost sad. “Believe me, there’s naught here you want.”
bs: Krupni čovjek gurnuo je sklopljene naočale u Savininu mlohavu ruku i nježno joj savio prste oko njih. Zvučao je gotovo tužno. — Vjeruj mi, ovdje nema ničega što želiš.

en: The big man looked up at Tall Hat’s companions, brushing a few embers from his shoulder. They stood in a shocked half-circle. Five men, but none of them had moved the whole time.
bs: Krupni čovjek pogleda prema Hatovim drugovima, otresajući nekoliko žeravica s ramena. Stajali su u zapanjenom polukrugu. Petorica Folk, ali nijedan se nije pomaknuo sve to vrijeme.

en: Bull was an apt name for the big man. He frowned at Savine, and she cringed away until her back hit a wall. “Well,” he said, wincing as he rubbed at his knuckles, “you know what happens to plans when the fighting starts.”
bs: Bull je bio prikladan nadimak za krupnog muškarca. Namrštio se na Savine, a ona se stisnula uz zid. — Pa, reče, trljajući zglobove uz bolnu grimasu, znaš kako je s planovima kad počne borba.

en: “Ardee,” she whispered. Her mother’s name was the first she could think of, and she felt a burning pain building at the back of her nose, and gave a great snotty sob, and started to cry. She couldn’t remember the last time she cried. She wasn’t sure she ever had. “Thank you,” she blubbered. “Thank you—”
bs: — Ardi, prošapta. Prvo čega se sjetila se bilo je majčino ime, a u korijenu nosa osjeti žareću bol, ispusti glasan, šmrcavi jecaj i briznu u plač. Nije se mogla sjetiti se kad je posljednji put plakala. Nije bila sigurna je li ikad i suzu pustila. — Hvala vam, mucala je. — Hvala vam —

en: There was a rousing rattle of arms and armour as the men spun towards Orso, stomped down their left heels and saluted in perfect unison. Five hundred soldiers, moving as one, sun glinting from their freshly forged equipment. A mere tenth part of his newly raised expeditionary force, fully prepared to sail north and give Stour Nightfall a resounding kick up the arse.
bs: Zazvečalo je oružje i oklop dok su se vojnici okrenuli prema Orsu, tresnuli lijevim petama o tlo i salutirali u savršenom skladu. Pet stotina vojnika kretalo se kao jedan, a sunce se presijavalo na njihovoj svježe skovanoj opremi. Tek deseti dio njegove novoosnovane ekspedicijske snage, potpuno pripremljen zaploviti na Sjever i dati Stauru Najtfolu pošten udarac nogom u tur.

en: “A fine body of men, Your Highness.” Orso had to stop himself wincing. However often one heard that piping voice, one never quite got comfortable with it. “You are to be congratulated.”
bs: — Valjan odred Folk, Uzvišenost. Orso se morao suzdržati da se ne trzne. Koliko god puta čovjek čuo taj piskavi glas, nikada se posve ne privikne na nj. — Treba vam čestitati.

en: The two of them had formed a winning partnership, so far. Forest provided the experience, judgement, warmth, discipline, courage, facial scarring and, of course, superb moustache. Orso supplied the sparkle, the… Well, his facial hair had always been wretched and he had no noticeable scars, so honestly the sparkle was about all. Perhaps that was what the historians would call him. The King of Sparkle. He gave a helpless snort of laughter. People could have called him worse, he supposed. Indeed, t
bs: Njih dvojica dotad su činili pobjedničku kombinaciju. Forest je osiguravao iskustvo, prosuđivanje, toplinu, disciplinu, hrabrost, ožiljke na licu i, dakako, vrhunske brkove. Orso je donosio blistavost, ono… Pa, dlake na njegovu licu oduvijek su bile jadne i nije imao primjetnih ožiljaka, tako da je ta blistavost doista bila otprilike sve što je imao. Možda bi ga povjesničari tako prozvali. Kralj Blistavosti. Otpuhnuo je prigušeni hihot. Folk su ga mogli zvati i gore, pretpostavljao je. Doista, č

en: “It’s who you couple with, Orso, as you very well know. I’d much rather you were getting married.” She sat back, giving him a thorough examination, tapping at the arm of her folding chair with one exquisitely manicured fingernail. “But if you must play soldiers in the meantime, I will admit…” And she allowed the corner of her mouth to bend by an infinitesimal fraction. “I am impressed.”
bs: "Stvar je u tome s kim se paraš, Orso, kao što dobro znaš. Puno bih radije da se ženiš." Naslonila se odmjerivši ga od glave do pete, kuckajući jednim iznimno urešenim noktom po naslonu svoje sklopive stolice."No, ako se u međuvremenu moraš igrati vojnika, priznat ću…" I dopustila je da joj se kut usana pomakne za neznatan dio milimetra."Impresionirana jesam."

en: Tunny glanced over at Forest, face reddening beneath that fine fur hat as he bellowed orders at the men. “That bloody hat of his looks like a quim.”
bs: Tani baci Oko na Foresta, čije se lice rumenjelo pod onom finom krznenom kapom dok je drao grlo izdajući zapovijedi ljudima. — Ta njegova prokleta Hat izgleda kao pička.

en: Tunny leaned in to mutter, “You’ve made glory wait twenty years. Daresay another hour won’t make the difference.”
bs: Tani se primače da prošapuće: — Dow si slavi da čeka Dvadesetero godina. Usudio bih se reći da još jedan Straža neće promijeniti stvar.

en: Orso swallowed. “Uprising?” The word was a decidedly ugly one to use before someone of royal blood. Could Pike not have gone for something a bit more neutral, like incident? Even riot would have been preferable. Then he realised the fact that the Superior was using it, in front of a king, a crown prince and their Arch Lector, might be a good guide to the severity of the situation.
bs: Orso proguta knedlu. — Pobuna?" Ta je riječ zvučala krajnje ružno kad bi se izgovorila pred nekim kraljevske krvi. Zar Pajk nije mogao odabrati nešto malo neutralnije, poput incidenta? Čak bi i izgred bio poželjniji. Potom shvati kako bi sama činjenica da Superior doista rabi taj izraz, i to pred kraljem, prijestolnasljednikom i njihovim Lektorom, mogla poslužiti kao dobar pokazatelj težine novonastale situacije.

en: Orso swallowed again. It felt as if there was a lump in his throat he could not force down. “I take it their opinion of me is less than glowing?”
bs: Orso ponovno proguta knedlu. Osjećao je kao da mu u grlu zapinje gruda koju nikako ne uspijeva progutati. — Pretpostavljam da o meni nemaju osobito visoko mišljenje?

en: Glokta sagged into his chair. “She was in Valbeck. Visiting one of her manufactories.” His grey lips peeled back from his ruined teeth. “I have not heard from her. I do not know if she is free, or a prisoner. I do not know if she is alive, or—”
bs: Glokta se sruši u stolac. — Bila je u Valbeku. U posjetu jednoj od svojih manufaktura." Sive su mu usne ogolile uništene zube. — Nisam čuo ništa od nje. Ne znam je li slobodna ili zatočena. Ne znam je li živa ili…

en: If his mother could’ve packed his head in a box but left the rest of him available, it would’ve suited Rikke just fine, but he probably didn’t want to hear that.
bs: Da mu je majka mogla spakirati glavu u kutiju, a ostatak tijela ostaviti dostupnim, Rike bi to sasvim odgovaralo, no vjerojatno to nije htjela čuti.

en: “Well, not on his own.” Rikke tried to pick the sleep out of her eyes. “My father says he’s bringing five thousand men with him.”
bs: — Pa, ne sam. Rike pokuša protrljati san iz očiju. — Moj otac kaže da sa sobom vodi pet tisuća Folk.

en: Rikke had never been able to understand why you’d care a shit who someone you’d never even met lay with. How few problems do you need to have before you count that among ’em? “Would’ve thought you’d understand. You spend most o’ your time with men.”
bs: Rike nikada nije mogla shvatiti zašto bi se itko zamarao time s kim liježe netko koga nikada u životu nije ni vidio. Koliko malo problema moraš imati u životu da ti to bude među njima? — Mislila bih da ćeš ti to razumjeti. Ti provodiš većinu vremena s muškarcima.

en: The memory floated up, as it did at least once a day, of hiding under that riverbank while Stour Nightfall laughed about what he’d do to her. She thought of Uffrith in flames, and all the good folk hurt or killed, and she clenched her fists at the usual rush of fury. No one wanted that bastard dead more than she did, but even she saw they had to be patient. Whether you waited for all the help you could get seemed like no kind of question at all.
bs: Sjećanje je isplivalo, kao što se to događalo barem jednom dnevno, na skrivanje ispod one obale rijeke dok se Staur Najtfol smijao zbog toga što će joj napraviti. Mislila je na Afrit u plamenu i na sve one dobre ljude koji su bili ozlijeđeni ili ubijeni te je stisnula šake pred uobičajenim valom bijesa. Nitko nije želio tog kopiladi mrtvog više od nje, ali čak je i ona vidjela da moraju biti strpljivi. Čekati svu moguću pomoć činilo se kao pitanje o kojem uopće nema rasprave.

en: “Grand,” grunted Rikke, upending her boot and shaking it till the chagga pellet fell out, then wedging it behind her lip.
bs: — Baš sjajno, progunđa Rike, preokrenuvši čizmu i tresući je dok kuglica čagge ne ispadne, a zatim je zaglavi iza usne.

en: He glanced across, surprised. “Actually, I do.” And he offered her his elbow so she could stop hopping. “You’re hard not to like.”
bs: On je pogleda, iznenađen. — Zapravo, volim." I ponudi joj lakat da prestane poskakivati na jednoj nozi. — Teško te je ne voljeti.

en: The forge was stuffed with people, warm and damp from their nervous breath. Leo’s mother had her gloved fists planted on a table spread with maps, a litter of anxious officers clustered about her. Lords Mustred and Clensher were among ’em, two dour old noblemen of Angland who’d brought some reinforcements in the day before. Rikke wasn’t sure which was which, but one had a thick grey moustache, the other whiskers all around his jaw but his top lip shaved. Like they only had one whole beard betwee
bs: Kovačnica je bila krcata ljudima, topla i zagušljiva od njihovih uznemirenih uzdaha. Leova majka držala je šake s rukavicama oslonjene na stol prekriven kartama, dok se roj zabrinutih časnika okupio oko nje. Lords Mustred i Clensher bili su među njima, dvojica namrgođenih starih plemića iz Englenda koji su dan prije doveli pojačanje. Rike nije bila sigurna tko je tko, ali jedan je imao guste sive brkove, a drugi zaliske oko cijele čeljusti, dok mu je gornja usna bila obrijana. Kao da su dijelili

en: Silence, then, as Finree dan Brock broke the great red seal and began to read, stony face giving nothing away. Rikke knew her letters. Had learned the bastards at great personal pain during her horrible year in Ostenhorm. But she couldn’t make a thing out of these ones, the writing was so flourished and flounced.
bs: Nastala je tišina dok je Finri dan Brok lomila Great crveni pečat i počela čitati, kamena lica koje nije odavalo ništa. Rike je poznavala slova. Naučila je te gadosti uz mnogo muke tijekom svoje užasne godine u Ostenhormu. No, iz ovih nije mogla razabrati ništa; rukopis je bio toliko nakinđuren i isprepleten.

en: There was silence in the little forge then, but for the patter of a new shower on the roof, the plop and trickle of a leak into a bucket. Silence, while each man or woman chewed over the implications. Then everyone started shouting at once.
bs: U maloj kovačnici zavladala je tišina, prekidana tek pljuskanjem nove kiše po krovu, kapanjem i curenjem vode u kantu. Tišina, dok je svatko od prisutnih razmišljao o posljedicama. A onda su svi počeli vikati u isti glas.

en: “He’ll be along, Master Sulfur,” said Calder, laying a humble hand on the tabletop between them. “You can depend on it.”
bs: — Doći će on, majstore Salfure, reče Kalder spuštajući poniznu ruku na površinu stola između njih. — Možete računati na to.

en: The old king and his old cunts glowered at the young heir and his young cunts, naught praiseworthy on either side but all jealous of what the others had even so. Matching groups, in many ways; Clover could almost see each warrior squaring up to his counterpart. The mean one, the handsome one, the one who hardly spoke, the one who spoke too much.
bs: Stari kralj i njegove stare drame mrko su gledali mladog nasljednika i njegove mlade drame, ničega hvalevrijednog ni s jedne strane, ali svejedno ljubomornih na ono što su drugi imali. Slične skupine, na mnogo načina; Klover je gotovo mogao vidjeti kako se svaki ratnik odmjerava sa svojim parnjakom. Onaj opak, onaj zgodan, onaj koji jedva progovara, onaj koji govori previše.

en: “Maybe two,” said Wonderful. “He could empty one while his servants filled the other. The poor girls would never have to stop pouring.”
bs: — Možda dva, rekla je Vonderful. — Mogao bi isprazniti jedan dok mu služavke pune drugi. Jadne djevojke nikad ne bi morale prestati točiti.

en: “Aye,” said Clover, “and every telling makes Stour a bigger hero. Soon he’ll be beating a thousand barbarians with his hands behind his back and his sword tied to his cock.”
bs: — Da, reče Klover, a svakim pričanjem Staur postaje sve veći junak. Uskoro će pobjeđivati tisuću barbara s rukama na leđima i mačem svezanim za kurac.

en: “Calling a wolf a cow will not make him give milk. The same could be said of calling chaos order.” Sulfur put aside his cup and stood, looking down at Calder. “My master appreciates that we must sometimes have a little chaos if a better order is to emerge. There can be no progress without pain, no creation without destruction. That is why he has indulged this little war of yours.” He looked up as Scale roared with laughter at some new flourish of Stour’s, and the warriors about them competed wit
bs: — Nazoveš li vuka kravom, neće ti dati mlijeka. Isto se može reći i za nazivanje kaosa redom. Salfur je odložio čašu i ustao, gledajući Kaldera odozgo. — Moj gospodar cijeni to što ponekad moramo imati malo kaosa kako bi se pojavio bolji red. Nema napretka bez boli, nema stvaranja bez uništenja. Zato je dopustio ovaj vaš mali rat. Pogledao je gore dok se Ljuska glasno smijao nekom novom Staurovom hvalisanju, a ratnici oko njih natjecali su se tko će proizvesti najpljuvačkije salve veselja. — Moj

en: “And at this rate, these two heroes will be blundering right into it.” Calder frowned harder than ever at his son. “How did he end up with so little of me in him?”
bs: — A ovim tempom ova dva heroja uletjet će u nju glavom bez obzira. Kalder se još mrko zagleda u sina. — Kako je moguće da je u njemu tako malo mene?

en: Scale was frowning down into the firepit now. “My father was betrayed. My father was struck down! His kingdom torn up like meat between greedy dogs.” His dewy eyes rolled up, and he pointed to Stour with his good hand. “But we’ll put right the wrongs of the past. We’ll finish the Dogman’s fucking Protectorate! We’ll drive the bloody Union out of the North! Stour Nightfall, my nephew and my heir, will rule supreme from the Whiteflow to the Crinna and beyond!” And he held up his cup, ale slopping
bs: Ljuska se sada namrštio gledajući u ognjište. — Mog oca su izdali. Mog oca su srušili! Njegovo kraljevstvo raskomadali su poput mesa između pohlepnih pasa." Njegove suzne oči zakolutale su prema gore, a zdravom rukom pokazao je na Staura. — Ali mi ćemo ispraviti nepravde iz prošlosti. Dokrajčit ćemo jeben Protektorat onog Psa Čovjeka! Istjerat ćemo krvavu Unija iz Sjevera! Staur Najtfol, moj nećak i moj nasljednik, vladat će suvjereno od Whiteflowa do Crinne i dalje!" Podigao je vrč, pivo se pre

en: Savine looked across the little room at May, light from outside the ill-fitting window catching her clenched jaw, head turned away from her parents’ voices as if to pretend she could not hear them.
bs: Savine pogleda preko malene sobe u Mej; svjetlost s ulice kroz loše postavljen prozor obasjala joj je stisnutu čeljust, dok je glavu okrenula od roditeljskih glasova kao da se pretvara da ih ne čuje.

en: There was no weakness in Liddy’s voice. Her strength amazed Savine, the way she kept going, working, smiling, making the best of this nightmare. “It’s a fine line, Gunnar, between helping people and hurting ’em. You’re prone to wander all over it.”
bs: U Lidinu glasu nije bilo slabosti. Njezina ju je snaga zadivljivala – način na koji je nastavila dalje, radila, smiješila se i izvlačila najbolje iz ove noćne more. — Tanka je linija, Gunar, između pomaganja ljudima i nanošenja bola. A ti imaš običaj lutati preko nje.

en: She had thought of trying to get out of the city, but the truth was she scarcely had the courage to look out of the window, let alone to risk the streets again. She found she had a great deal less courage altogether than she had smugly supposed while blackmailing investors, or choosing a wig, or pronouncing social death sentences in the salons of Adua. She had always reckoned herself such a gambler. No more audacious woman in the Union. Now she realised the games had always been rigged in her fa
bs: Pomišljala je na bijeg iz grada, no istina bijaše ta da se jedva odvažila pogledati kroz prozor, a kamoli ponovno kročiti na opasne ulice. Shvatila je da ima znatno manje hrabrosti nego što je tašte pretpostavljala dok je ucjenjivala ulagače, birala periku ili dijelila društvene smrtne presude u salonima Adue. Uvijek je sebe smatrala takvom hazarderkom. Nije bilo odvažnije žene u Uniji. Sada je shvatila da su te igre oduvijek bile namještene u njezinu korist. Nikada prije nije morala kockati se

en: “You were in Colonel Vallimir’s house,” said May. Savine stared at her, caught off balance and failing to hide it, the constant nagging ache of fear turned suddenly, terribly sharp.
bs: — Bili ste u kući pukovnika Valimira, reče Mej. Savine je zagledala u nju, zatečena i nesposobna da to sakrije, dok se stalna, pritajena bol straha odjednom prometnula u strahovitu oštricu.

en: “Little too honest for my own good, I expect. Always been a problem of mine. You stood up for me, though. I listened at the keyhole, and you stood up for me.”
bs: — Malo previše iskrena za vlastito dobro, pretpostavljam. Oduvijek moj Trobli. Ipak si stala u moju obranu. Slušala sam preko ključanice i stala si u moju obranu.

en: “Don’t think they’d go with my ensemble.” May’s eyes flicked down to her own threadbare dress, then back up to Savine. “You keep ’em.”
bs: — Ne vjerujem da bi išle uz moju modnu kombinaciju. Mayin Oko skliznu niz vlastitu dronjavu haljinu, a zatim se vrati na Savine. — Zadrži ih.

en: Vick only broke a silence when she knew she could improve on it. Risinau was the sort of man who’d soon answer his own questions.
bs: Vik je prekinula šutnju tek kad je znala da je može učiniti smislenijom. Risinau je bio čovjek koji bi ubrzo sam odgovorio na svoja pitanja.

en: Vick wondered how many workers would be dying for Risinau’s vainglory. No small number was her guess. Casting down a king two centuries dead was one thing. The one currently on the throne might raise stiffer objections. She was starting to think the ex-Superior was at least half-mad. But then sanity was a rare commodity in Valbeck lately, and didn’t look to be coming back into fashion any time soon.
bs: Vik se upitala koliko će radnika poginuti za Risinauovu taštinu. Njezina je procjena bila da taj broj neće biti mali. Rušenje kralja mrtvog već dva stoljeća jedno je. Onaj koji je trenutno na prijestolju mogao bi staviti ozbiljnije prigovore. Počela je misliti da je bivši Praktik bio barem upola lud. No zdrav razum ionako je posljednjih dana bio rijetka roba u Valbeku, a nije se činilo ni da će se tako skoro vratiti u modi.

en: “The mind needs nourishment, too, brother.” Risinau waved away a fly, the only things prospering in the stifling city, then grinned at Vick. “No doubt Sibalt told you that.”
bs: — I umu je potrebna hrana, brate. — Risinau je otjerao muhu, jedino stvorenje koje je napredovalo u tom zagušljivom gradu, a zatim se nasmiješio Vik. — Sibalt ti je to zasigurno rekao.

en: “A title I borrowed from a better man,” mused Risinau, before his fickle attention was snatched away. “We should draw up a manifesto, don’t you think? Demand a workers’ representative on the Closed Council!” He had that gleam in his eye again, as though he was gazing off towards a better tomorrow. “Sibalt would have loved that idea…”
bs: — Titula koju sam posudio od boljeg čovjeka, zamislio se Risinau prije negoli mu je nestalna pažnja odlutala. — Trebali bismo sastaviti manifest, zar ne misliš? Zahtijevati radničkog predstavnika u Zatvorenom Vijeću! Opet mu je zasjao onaj sjaj u oku, kao da motri negdje prema boljoj sutrašnjici. — Sibalt bi obožavao tu ideju…

en: “It would appear she slipped through our fingers. The day of the uprising was rather chaotic, as I say, even more so than expected…”
bs: — Izgleda da nam je izmakla iz ruku. Dan ustanka bio je prilično kaotičan, kao što rekoh, čak i luđi no što se očekivalo…

en: “Well… they’re unpredictable people. Fiery. That’s why they call them Burners, I suppose!” He snorted up another a little titter, then, when he saw Vick had never looked less like laughing, cleared his throat and went on. “I suppose I could ask for her prisoners…”
bs: — Pa… to su nepredvidljivi Folk. Vatreni. Zato ih i zovu Palioci, pretpostavljam! — Ponovno ispusti onaj svoj sitni hihot, a onda, ugledavši Vickino lice na kojem nije bilo ni traga smijehu, pročisti grlo i nastavi. — Valjda bih mogao zatražiti njezine zatvorenike…

en: There were houses plundered, their broken doors dangling from twisted hinges. There were houses burned out, their windows yawning empty, the fire-blackened brickwork of a fallen chimney stack left in pieces across the sun-baked mud of the roadway. Rubble and glass were scattered, torn clothes and broken furniture flung around as if a great wind had ripped through the neighbourhood. The place stank, worse the further they went. Stank of rot and piss and charred wood and stale smoke, all cooking i
bs: Kuće su bile opljačkane, a njihova slomljena vrata visjela su s iskrivljenih šarki. Neke su kuće izgorjele do temelja, prozori su im zjapili prazni, a čađava opeka srušena dimnjaka ležala je u komadima razbacana po suncem spečenome blatu ceste. Ruševine i staklo bili su posvuda, razbacana odjeća i slomljeni namještaj letjeli su uokolo kao da je silan vjetar protutnjao susjedstvom. Mjesto je zaudaralo, a smrad se širio što su dublje zalazili. Zaudarao je na trulež i mokraću, na nagorjelo drvo i u

en: All felt far too quiet. He saw a figure lurking in an alleyway, a face at a window quickly vanished, a couple fighting over a bone who scurried away as they came close. Someone had been busy with a paintbrush, there were slogans smeared and spattered everywhere. Painted across whole terraces in letters three strides high. Scrawled across front doors in letters tiny as in a book.
bs: Sve se činilo pretjerano tiho. Spazio je priliku koja se prikradala u uličici, lice na prozoru koje je ubrzo nestalo, par likova koji su se borili oko kosti i razbježali čim su se primaknuli. Netko se pošteno zabavljao kistom, parole su bile razmazane i ispisane na sve strane. Oslikane preko cijelih nizova kuća slovima visokim tri koraka. Nažvrljane na ulaznim vratima sitnim slovima kao u knjizi.

en: “Someone tried to hold ’em off here,” he said as they eased up the steps. The doors were battered, one half-torn from its hinges and hanging loose.
bs: — Netko ih je ovdje pokušao zadržati — prozborio je dok su se penjali stubama. Vrata su bila razbijena, a jedno je visjelo s polomljenih šarki.

en: “Ricter dan Vallimir!” sneered Judge. “Quite apart from anything else, you stand accused of having a fucking ‘dan’ in your name—”
bs: — Ricter dan Valimir! podsmjehnu se Džadž. — Osim svega ostalog, optužen si da imaš prokleti "dan" u imenu —

en: Judge shook her ring-covered fist at him. “We have the authority of the fist! We have the authority of sharpened metal! We have the authority of force, you blubbing cunt, which is the only real authority there is.” Some light cheering from the few members of the audience still conscious. “You should know that. You were a soldier. Counsel for the defence? Where’s that fucker Randock?”
bs: Džadž zaprijeti stisnutom šakom punom prstenja. — Mi imamo ovlast šake! Mi imamo ovlast naoštrenog čelika! Mi imamo ovlast sile, ti pizdo balava, što je jedina stvarna ovlast koja postoji." Slabo navijanje nekoliko prisutnih u publici koji su još bili pri svijesti. — Trebao si to znati. Bio si vojnik. Branitelj? Gdje je taj jebeni Randock?

en: “Should I be scared?” The Burners were waking up to the new arrivals now, staring blearily over, hands creeping towards weapons.
bs: — Trebam li se bojati? Palioci su se sada budili zbog pridošlica, mutnih pogleda buljili u njih, dok im ruka nehotice ne kliznu prema oružju.

en: “I get it.” Vick stepped forward. “You want to see someone pay. No doubt there’s plenty to pay for.” Broad didn’t know how she could stay so cool with all this sweltering madness around her. “No one wants to see them pay more than me. But we’ve a city full of people to think about. We need something to bargain with.”
bs: — Kužim. Vik iskorači. — Želiš vidjeti kako netko plaća. Nema sumnje da ima podosta onoga što treba platiti. Brod nije shvaćao kako može ostati tako hladnokrvna uz sve ovo sparno ludilo oko sebe. — Nitko ne želi da plate više od mene. No moramo misliti na grad pun Folk. Treba nam nešto za pogodbu.

en: “Ooooooooh.” Judge’s throaty voice had gone all purry-soft, and even though she was just a sparkly blur now, Broad knew she was staring straight at him. “You I like. You’ve got a devil in you. Takes one to know one, eh?”
bs: — Ooooooooh. Judgein glas, duboko grlno, postao je svilenkasto mek, iako je sada bila samo sjajna mrlja, Brod je znao da ga gleda ravno u oči. "Tebe volim. Imaš demona u sebi. Zna se, zar ne?"

en: “Used to settle the disputes among the whores, down on the docks in Keln. Judge who had the right of it. Judge what was fair. Those girls can dispute fucking anything, believe me. And in that game, well, sometimes you’ve got to find a compromise. We’re all on the same side, aren’t we, after all? All seeking a better world? A world where we’re all equal?”
bs: — Rješavala sam sporove među kurvama dolje u kelnskim dokovima. Sudila tko je u pravu. Sudila što je pravedno. Te cure, vjeruj mi, mogu raspravljati o najebrenijoj svačemu. A u toj igri, pa, ponekad moraš pronaći kompromis. Svi smo mi na istoj strani, zar ne, naposljetku? Svi težimo boljem svijetu? Svijetu u kojem smo svi jednaki?

en: Broad stood staring at her a moment longer, pulse still thudding in his skull, then let Vick steer him after the warden’s hairy buttocks and out of the courtroom. The jeers of the jury followed him but they were half-hearted. It seemed, for now, the Burners had drunk their fill of justice.
bs: Brod je još trenutak stajao zagledan u nju, s pulsom što mu je i dalje bubnjao u lubanji, a onda dopustio Vik da ga povede za upraviteljevim dlakavim stražnjim dijelom i izvede iz sudnice. Podrugljivi smijeh porote pratio ga je, ali bio je mlak. Činilo se da su se Palioci za sada napili pravde.

en: “Prince Orso isn’t coming,” said Leo, stomping up the crumbling stairway after his mother with the Dogman behind him. “We have to fight.”
bs: —— Princ Orso neće doći, reče Leo, penjući se uz trošno stepenište za majkom, dok mu je Pas Covjek bio za petama."Moramo se boriti."

en: The Dogman snorted. “Your mother was a prisoner of Black Dow, and faced him down, and didn’t only talk her own way free but saved sixty men besides. I’ll hear her given no lessons in courage, boy. There’s a world o’ difference between being scared to fight and waiting till you can win.”
bs: Pas Covjek frknu. — Tvoja je majka bila zarobljenica Blacka Dowja, suočila se s njim, i ne samo što se uspjela izvući riječima nego je još i spasila šezdeset Folk. Ne želim slušati kako joj držiš lekcije o hrabrosti, momče. Velika je razlika između straha od borbe i čekanja pravog trenutka za pobjedu.

en: “Ground’s good.” He considered the steep-sided trough of a valley with its grey thread of a river, its brown thread of a road, the rocky hills to either side. “Could be very good, if luck’s with us.”
bs: — Teren je dobar. Odmjeri strme stranice udoline sa sivom niti rijeke, smeđom niti ceste i kamenim brežuljcima s obje strane. — Mogao bi biti vrlo dobar, posluži li nas sreća.

en: “I like it,” said the Dogman. “If there’s one thing you can rely on, it’s young men’s folly. I’ll send word for Uffrith’s warriors to gather here and be ready for a battle.” He paused, wind stirring the grey hair about his craggy face. “Lady Finree… I’ve fought beside great warriors. Great War Chiefs. Against some, too. But I rarely saw an army better handled than by you. Might be men who think there’s something weak in what you’ve done, the last few weeks.” He curled his tongue and spat over th
bs: — Sviđa mi se, reče Pas Covjek Čovjek. — Ako se u nešto možeš pouzdati, to je Ludilo mladih Folk. Poslat ću glasnika da okupi Afritove ratnike ovdje i pripremi ih za bitku. Zastade, a vjetar mu zamrsi sivu kosu oko ispijenog lica. — Gospođo Finri… Borio sam se uz bok velikim ratnicima. Velikim ratnim poglavicama. I protiv nekih, također. Ali rijetko sam vidio vojsku kojom se bolje upravljalo nego što ti to činiš. Možda ima Folk koji misle da je nešto slabašno u ovome što si učinila posljednjih t

en: “With the reserves?” He waved a hand towards the valley. Towards the glory. Towards the songs. “Finally we fight and you leave me with the baggage?”
bs: — S pričuvom? Mahnu rukom prema dolini. Prema slavi. Prema pjesmama. — Napokon se borimo, a ti me ostavljaš s prtljagom?

en: “Then fucking act like it!” she snarled, with such violence he shrank back a little. “This isn’t a negotiation! You’ll stay with the reserves, and that’s the end of it! Your father’s dead! He’s dead, and I can’t lose you, too, do you understand?” She turned her back on him to look into the valley. “I can’t lose you, too.”
bs: — Onda se, do vraga, ponašaj tako! odbrusi s toliko žestine da se on malo trgnu. — Ovo nije pregovaranje! Ostat ćeš s pričuvom i to je kraj priče! Tvoj otac je mrtav! Mrtav je, a ne mogu izgubiti i tebe, razumiješ li? Okrenula mu je leđa kako bi pogledala u dolinu. — Ne mogu izgubiti i tebe.

en: She stood hunched, up to her knees in the river, soaked dress rolled and tucked into a belt made from knotted rope, all thought of propriety long gone. All thought of propriety had gone the moment she staggered from this sewer of a river the first time, shivering in her drawers.
bs: Stajala je pognuta, do koljena u rijeci, navlažene haljine podfrknute i zataknute za pojas načinjen od usukanog užeta, a svaka je pomisao na pristojnost davno iščezla. Svaka je pomisao na pristojnost nestala onoga trena kad se prvi put zanjihala i izašla iz ove pogane rijeke, drhteći u donjem rublju.

en: The clatter of the handle, the gurgle of water as it filled, the slop and trickle as she passed it to May, her legs, her arms, her shoulders trembling with the effort. Was it the cold, or the exhaustion, or the fear that made her shake so? What was the difference?
bs: Zveket ručke, klokot vode dok se punilo, pljuskanje i cijeđenje dok ga je dodavala Mej, a noge, ruke i ramena drhtali joj od napora. Je li je tresla hladnoća, iscrpljenost ili strah? U čemu je uopće bila razlika?

en: “It’s out over here,” she whispered, staring across to the great blaze still raging on the far bank.
bs: — Ovdje se ugasilo, prošaptala je gledajući u veliku buktinju koja je još bjesnjela na suprotnoj obali.

en: May ran her tongue around the inside of her mouth and spat. “They say the crown prince is coming with five thousand soldiers. Rumour is they’ll be outside the city tomorrow.”
bs: Mej prevrne jezikom po ustima i pljune. — Pričaju da krunski princ dolazi s pet tisuća vojnika. Glasine kažu da će sutra biti pred gradom.

en: Crown Prince Orso was riding to her rescue. Perhaps she should have laughed at that. Perhaps she should have wept at it. But she had no laughter and no tears left. She was a husk.
bs: Kraljević Orso jahao joj je u spas. Možda se trebala nasmijati tomu. Možda se trebala zaplakati nad time. No nije joj ostalo ni smijeha ni suza. Bila je samo ljuska.

en: “Attacking the city with an army would be like eating peas with a sword,” he said. “Messy, frustrating and you’ve a good chance of stabbing yourself in the face. We need to be measured. Calm. The firm but necessary hand of authority. We need to be the grown-ups.” For once in his life.
bs: — Napasti grad vojskom bilo bi poput jedenja graška mačem, reče. — Neuredno, frustrirajuće i imate dobre šanse da se sami ubadate u lice. Moramo biti odmjereni. Smireni. Čvrsta, ali nužna ruka autoriteta. Moramo biti odrasli. Barem jednom u životu.

en: “I was just now struggling to put out a fire in the North when the unmistakable tang of the Union in flames reached my nose.” Sulfur smiled wider. “Never any peace, eh? Never the slightest peace.”
bs: — Upravo sam se mučio gasiti Veliko Gorenje u Sjeveru kad mi je u nos dopro neoborivi zadah gorućeg Unije. Salfur se šire nasmiješi. — Nema nikad mira, jelda? Niti najmanjeg mira.

en: “Risinau, the Superior of the Inquisition. Called himself the Weaver. Seemed like he was leading them, but he talked like a madman. Then there was a woman called Judge.” He gave a little shiver. “But she seemed even madder’n Risinau. Then there was an old fellow. Mulmer. Molmer. Something like that. He seemed… decent, I reckon.”
bs: — Risinau, šef Inkvizicije. Nazvao se Tkačem. Činilo se kao da ih vodi, ali pričao je kao lud čovjek. Onda je bila i neka žena po imenu Džadž. On se blago zatresé. — Ali činila se još luđom od Risinaua. Onda je tu bio i jedan stari momak. Malmer. Molmer. Tako nekako. Činio se… pristojan, reklo bi se.

en: Orso stood frowning towards the city as they walked away, one hand on his stomach. “Hildi?” he called.
bs: Orso je stajao mršteći se prema gradu dok su se udaljavali, držeći jednu ruku na trbuhu. — Hildi?" pozva on.

en: Pike raised one brow. Or looked as if he would have, had he any to raise. Then he gave the faintest nod, perhaps even a nod of approval, and faded back to confer with Sulfur.
bs: Pajk je podignuo obrvu. Ili je barem izgledalo kao da bi to učinio, da je imao koju za podignuti. Zatim je jedva primjetno kimnuo, možda čak i u znak odobravanja, te se povukao kako bi se posavjetovao sa Salfurom.

en: She stuck two fingers in a pouch and started smearing something on the pink and puckered skin. It was Rikke’s turn to wrinkle her nose. The smell of it was quite impossible to describe. “By the dead,” trying to hold her breath, “what is that?”
bs: Zavukla je dva prsta u torbicu i počela mazati nešto po ružičastoj, naboranoj koži. Sada je bio red na Rike da nabere nos. Miris je bio posve neopisiv. — Mrtvih mi, reče pokušavajući zadržati dah, što je to?

en: The silence stretched. The silence, and the nerves, and somewhere someone started up a song in a deep bass. That one about the Battle in the High Places, where her father laid Bethod low. Old battles. Old victories. She wondered whether some time in the future, folk would sing songs about the Battle of Red Hill, and if they did, who’d be the winners and who the losers.
bs: Tišina se razvukla. Tišina, nervoza i negdje u daljini netko je započeo pjesmu dubokim basom. Onu o bitci na Visovima, gdje je njezin otac srušio Bethod. Stare bitke. Stare pobjede. Pitala se hoće li u budućnosti folk pjevati pjesme o bitci kod Red Hilla, i ako hoće, tko će biti pobjednici, a tko gubitnici.

en: “Patience is the parent of success,” murmured Jurand, with so gentle a touch on Leo’s shoulder he only just felt it. “Stolicus.”
bs: — Strpljenje je roditelj uspjeha, prozbori Džurand, s toliko blagim dodirom na Leovu ramenu da ga je jedva osjetio. — Stolicus.

en: Jurand heaved out a sigh, and Barniva drew his blanket tight about his shoulders, and they went back to watching the sausages sizzle.
bs: Džurand ispusti Trdak uzdah, Barniva navuče deku čvrsto oko ramena te se vratiše promatranju cvrčanja kobasica.

en: “She said sit tight.” Antaup leaned on Jin’s shoulder, made him turn, then reached around his blind side and nimbly stole the fork from his plate. “She said she’d let you know if anything changed.” And he stretched over to fork one of the sausages from the pan.
bs: — Rekla je da sjedimo mirno. Antaup se naslonio na Jinovo rame, okrenuo ga, a zatim posegnuo s njegove slijepe strane i spretno mu ukrao vilicu s tanjura. — Rekla je da će ti javiti ako se što promijeni. I nagnuo se kako bi vilicom uzeo jednu kobasicu iz tave.

en: Magweer bristled. Always the ones quickest to insults got the thinnest skin, for some reason. “You spend more time on your blisters than your weapons.”
bs: Magvir se narogušio. Iz nekog su razloga oni koji najbrže hvataju uvrede uvijek imali najtanju kožu. — Više vremena trošiš na žuljeve nego na oružje.

en: “If you say there’s no sign,” she said, “I daresay there isn’t any. You’re the War Chief. I’m… I don’t know, a seer, maybe?” Sounded like a bloody presumptuous title. “Just… a really shit one.”
bs: — Ako ti kažeš da nema ničega, odvrati ona, usudila bih se reći da i nema. Ti si Vojskovođa. Ja sam… štajaznam, neka proročica? Zvučalo je prokleto pretenciozno. — Samo… jako loša.

en: Isern had set her bony arse on the heap of crumbled masonry that was once the north wall of the fortress, spear across her knees, giving the blade a few licks with the whetstone.
bs: Izern je spustila svoju koščatu stražnjicu na hrpu urušenog kamenja, nekadašnji Northern zid utvrde, s kopljem preko koljena, oštreći oštricu brusom.

en: A few Carls scrambled onto the crumbling wall, staring down. Oxel was one. Rikke was waiting for him to roar out for more men, but all he did was turn his shifty sneer from the trees to her and spit.
bs: Nekoliko se Carlsa popelo na urušeni zid, zureći dolje. Oksel je bio jedan od njih. Rike je čekala da zaurla i pozove ostale, no on je samo okrenuo svoj sumnjičavi podsmjeh s drveća prema njoj i pljunuo.

en: Rikke was sick again. Just a little string of drool this time, and she spat and wiped her mouth. “Thought he… was way off north.”
bs: Rike je opet pozlilo. Ovoga puta samo malo sline, pa je pljunula i obrisala usta. — Mislila sam da je… daleko na Sjeveru.

en: “I must confess, I did not. But your daughter did.” She slapped a heavy hand down on Rikke’s shoulder. “The moon has smiled upon us all and blessed her with the rare gift o’ the Long Eye. We should make ready for blood.”
bs: — Moram priznati, nisam. Ali tvoja kći jest. Opalila je teškom šakom Rike po ramenu. — Mjesec nam se osmjehnuo i blagoslovio je rijetkim darom Dugog oka. Trebali bismo se pripremiti za krv.

en: “A long, lean, pale bastard with an axe and a sword, sort of hunched over, all elbows. Ugh.” And she had to bend over herself, hands on her knees, head spinning.
bs: — Dug, mršav, blijed gad sjekirom i mačem, nekako pogrbljen, sam lakat i koljeno. Uf. I morala se sama sagnuti, ruku na koljenima, dok joj se vrtjelo u glavi.

en: She was kneeling in the bracken just beyond the summit, an eyeglass trained on the valley, a whispering group of scouts and officers around her.
bs: Ona je klečala u paprati tik iznad vrha, s dalekozorom uperenim u dolinu, okružena šapućućom skupinom izvidnika i časnika.

en: “Yes.” His mother pulled her eyeglass from his limp grip and set it to her own eye again. “And this time, I’ve no doubt, the Great Wolf is here in person.”
bs: — Tako je. Mati mu je istrgnula monokl iz mlitava stiska i ponovno ga primaknula oku. — A ovog puta, nemam nimalo sumnje, Great je Vuk osobno ovdje.

en: The man glanced over at Greenway, somewhat sheepish, and scratched his head. Seemed that was exactly what he’d been planning.
bs: Čovjek netremice pogleda Grinveja, pomalo posramljen, pa se počeša po glavi. Činilo se da mu je uistinu to bila namjera.

en: Stour’s eyes were sharper, and thoughtfully narrowed in its direction. “You reckon that’s Leo dan Brock’s standard down there?”
bs: Staurove su oči bile oštrije, a Oko mu se zamišljeno suzio u tom smjeru. — Misliš li da je ono tamo standard Lea dan Broka?

en: He kept his face blank as fresh snow, counting on the short attention span common to famous warriors and, indeed, soon enough, the Great Wolf forgot all about it, fully occupied glowering down the valley, towards that bridge. Towards that standard. He gave a great sniff. “Let’s have a poke at those bastards.”
bs: Lice mu je ostalo mirno poput svježe pala snijega, uzdajući se u kratak raspon pažnje svojstven slavnim ratnicima i, doista, Great Vuk ubrzo sve to zaboravi, potpuno zaokupljen mrkim pogledom usmjerenim niz dolinu, prema onom mostu. Prema onom barjaku. Glasno potegne nosom. — Idemo malo bocnuti tu kopilad.

en: Rikke crouched on the roof of the broken tower, twitching, chewing, fretting, even more nervous than before. Almost too nervous to bear.
bs: Rike je čučala na krovu srušene kule, trzajući se, žvačući i grizući usne, još živčanija nego prije. Gotovo previše živčana da izdrži.

en: Rikke’s father stood up tall at the crumbling battlements, bellowing down into the yard. “Man the walls! Black Calder’s coming from the North!”
bs: Rikkien je otac uspravno stajao na trošnim grudobranima, urličući dolje u dvorište. — Na Tell! Black Kalder dolazi sa Sjevera!

en: Leo heard the calls of the officers spreading out across the back of the hill. The great scrape and rattle as the men stood, took up their weapons, began to form ranks.
bs: Leo je čuo pozive časnika koji su se širili stražnjom stranom brda. Golemo struganje i zveket dok su Folk ustajali, hvatali oružje i počeli se svrstavati u redove.

en: It rang out over the valley, piercingly loud, and there was an almighty clattering as several thousand armoured men began to march.
bs: Ona odjeknu nad dolinom, prodorno glasno, i zaori se silan tresak dok je nekoliko tisuća oklopljenih Folk počelo marširati.

en: Wonderful looked stunned, and well she might’ve. “You’re playing their bloody game!” she said. “It’s a fucking trap!”
bs: Vonderful je djelovala ošamućeno, a i imala je zašto. — Igraš njihovu prokletu igru!, reče. — To je jebena zamka!

en: She saw a boy with curly hair just staring, taking a step one way, then the other way, face white and pale and his jaw hanging open, not knowing what to do. Rikke wondered if he was going to die here. Wondered if she was going to die here.
bs: Vidjela je dječaka kovrčave kose kako samo zuri, korača čas na jednu, čas na drugu stranu, lica bijela i blijeda, čeljusti obješene, ne znajući što učiniti. Rike se zapitala hoće li ovdje umrijeti. Zapitala se hoće li ona ovdje umrijeti.

en: She saw a man sitting on the ground, cursing as he fiddled with his bloody sleeve, blood in his beard, axe dangling from one wrist. She saw a man stomping on someone’s head, spots of blood across his mad snarl as he lifted his boot and rammed it down, lifted it and rammed it down. “Can you save my leg?” A lad with yellow hair turned dark by the drizzle and the rags of his trousers all oozing black. Another man gibbered, mail pulled up to show a little slit that welled blood and when the healer w
bs: Vidjela je čovjeka kako sjedi na tlu i psuje dok si namješta krvavi rukav, s krvi u bradi i sjekirom koja mu visi s jednog zgloba. Vidjela je čovjeka kako gazi nečiju glavu, s kapljicama krvi na suludom ciničnom osmijehu dok je dizao čizmu i spuštao je, dizao je i spuštao. — Možeš li mi spasiti nogu?" upitao je mladić žute kose koju je rosulja zamračila, dok su mu krpe od hlača curile od crnila. Drugi je čovjek neartikulirano mumljao, a krzno mu je bilo podignuto kako bi se vidio mali prorez iz

en: That wedge of Black Calder’s men was choked off, and hemmed in, and cut down one by one, stabbed with spears, shoved over with shields, stomped on the ground. One huge warrior was left, wearing battered plates of armour, swinging a great axe around in heedless circles, rattling and clattering against the spears that stabbed at him.
bs: Taj klin Folk Black Kaldera bio je zagušen, opkoljen i isječen jedan po jedan, izboden kopljima, oboren štitovima, izgažen po tlu. Ostao je jedan golemi ratnik, u izudaranim oklopnim pločama, koji je bezumno mlatarao velikom sjekirom ukrug, zveckajući i udarajući o koplja koja su badala po njemu.

en: It was the greatest battle he’d ever seen. The greatest the North had seen since the Battle of Osrung, where his mother loved to say he’d been conceived.
bs: Bila je to najveća bitka koju je ikad vidio. Najveća koju je Sjever vidio još od bitke kod Osrunga, za koju je njegova majka voljela govoriti da je u njoj začet.

en: They could all see it. Some of Nightfall’s Thralls were still dribbling onto the battlefield. If the Dogman didn’t come soon, they might get around the flank and the Union line would crumble.
bs: Svi su to vidjeli. Neki od Najtfolovih tralla još su se uvijek vukli na bojište. Ako se Pas Covjek Čovjek uskoro ne pojavi, mogli bi im zaobići bok i linija Unije će se raspasti.

en: “We have to send in the reserves.” He stepped close to his mother. No whining now, no wheedling. Just the simple truth. “There’s no choice. We’re committed.”
bs: — Moramo poslati rezerve. Priđe bliže majci. Bez cviljenja sada, bez umiljavanja. Samo gola istina. — Nema izbora. Vezani smo.

en: It was all quite the mess now. Stour’s Carls had only just held the Union at the foot of that red hill, their shield wall twisting back on itself and threatening to burst. But they’d held them, and now there was a mad fight all along the valley, the bridge at one end the fiercest spot, Leo dan Brock’s golden standard fluttering above the carnage. It was a temptation Stour couldn’t ignore
bs: Sada je sve već bila prava kaša. Čete Staurove vojske jedva su zadržale Unija u podnožju tog crvenog brda, dok im se zid od štitova savijao i prijetio pucanjem. No ipak su ih zadržali, i sada se vodila luda borba duž cijele doline, pri čemu je most na jednom kraju bio najžešća točka, a zlatni barjak Lea dan Broka lepršao je visoko iznad pokolja. Bila je to napast koju Staur nije mogao ignorirati.

en: “A coward’s just a man with the proper respect for sharp metal,” said Clover, waving him down. “A battle’s no place for a warrior.”
bs: — Kukavica je samo čovjek koji gaji dužno poštovanje prema oštrom čeliku, rekao je Klover, odmahujući rukom. — Bitka nije mjesto za ratnika.

en: Up the muddy road he struggled, away from the bridge where the fight was going harder than ever, away from the great shield wall that was stretching up the valley, past frowning Carls flooding the other way. More flatbow bolts flickered down from the high ground, peppered the grass.
bs: Mučnim se usponom vukao blatnjavim putem, dalje od mosta na kojem se borba rasplamsavala žešće nego ikad, dalje od golemih bedema štitova koji su se pružali uz dolinu, mimo mrkih Carls koji su hitali u suprotnom smjeru. Još je strijela iz teških samostrela zujalo s uzvisina i sipalo po travi.

en: The healer didn’t answer. Busy tending to the next man in line, who’d a nasty-looking gash out of his shoulder, blood welling down his limp arm in streaks.
bs: Liječnica mu nije odgovorila. Bila je zauzeta previjanjem sljedećeg čovjeka u redu, koji je imao gadnu ranu na ramenu, dok mu se krv u potocima cijedila niz mlohavu ruku.

en: First at a walk, down the rutted track from the village, rain-pricked puddles shattered by his horse’s hooves. Barniva came level, and through the open face of his helmet Leo could see his eager smile, that fashionable war-weariness burned away in the fire of action. Leo smiled with him and urged his horse on. On, to the very point of the spear, where a leader belonged.
bs: Najprije u koraku, niz izlokani put iz sela, dok su kopita njegova konja razbijala lokve načete kišom. Barniva se izjednači s njim, a kroz otvor na kacigi Leo je mogao vidjeti njegov željni osmijeh, onaj pomodni ratni umor izgorio je u vatri akcije. Leo mu uzvrati osmijehom i potjera konja dalje. Naprijed, do samog vrha koplja, gdje je vođi i bilo mjesto.

en: Leo pounded heedless past the scattering Anglanders, fixed on one of the pursuing Northmen. As he saw Leo bearing down, his yellow grin became a circle of surprise. He turned, slipping and falling, hunter become prey. He was still scrambling up when Leo’s axe caught him between the shoulders and flung him on his face.
bs: Leo je bezglavo jurio pokraj razbježanih Anglanđana, usredotočen na jednog od sjevernjačkih progonitelja. Kad je vidio da mu Leo juri u susret, njegov se žuti osmijeh pretvorio u Round iznenađenja. Okrenuo se, poskliznuo i pao – Zamkač je postao plijen. Još se pokušavao uspeti kad ga je Leova Hachette pogodila između lopatica i bacila ničice na tlo.

en: Leo twisted the other way, his helmet hot with his own breath as he snarled and spat and swore. He hacked at a shield, knocked it clear, hacked at the man who held it, ripped his shoulder open and hurled him from his saddle, blood and mail rings flying, hacked at the leg left caught in the stirrups and chopped a great gash in it.
bs: Leo se okrenuo na drugu stranu; kaciga mu je bila vruća od vlastita daha dok je režao, pljuvao i psovao. Sjekao je po štitu, razbio ga, udario čovjeka koji ga je držao, raskomadao mu rame i izbacio ga iz sedla dok su krv i kolutići verižnjače letjeli na sve strane, te je odsjekao nogu zaglavljenu u stremenu, zarivši u nju duboku ranu.

en: Suddenly his wrist tore free and he almost stumbled over backwards. The rider with the silver in his beard was lying just next to him, mace in his hand, one leg caught under his horse.
bs: Zapešće mu se odjednom oslobodilo i umalo je pao unatrag. Jahač sa srebrnim brkom ležao je tik do njega, s buzdovanom u ruci, prikliještene noge pod konjem.

en: The chill wind hit his sweaty face like a slap and the world rushed at him, the roar of battle furiously loud.
bs: Hladan vjetar ošinuo mu je znojno lice poput pljuska, a svijet je navalio na nj, uz tutnjavu bitke koja je bjesnila svuda uokolo.

en: “Leo!” Barniva grabbed him, dragged him down, shield across his face. Something rattled from it. An arrow. Another bounced from Barniva’s armoured shoulder, more flickered into the grass. Someone fell, hands clapped to his throat. Leo peered over the rim of his shield, saw the archers, kneeling in a long row before the bridge, nocking arrows.
bs: — Leo! — Barniva ga je uhvatio, povukao dolje, štit preko lica. Nešto je zazvečalo o njega. Strelica. Još jedna odskočila je od Barnivina oklopljenog ramena, više ih je zazujalo u travu. Netko je pao, ruke pritisnute na grlo. Leo je provirio preko ruba svog štita, vidio strijelce, klečeće u dugom redu Naprijed mosta, koji su napinjali strelice.

en: “Fuckers!” he screeched, spraying spit. “Fuckers!” He caught his foot and went sliding on his face, took a mouthful of grass, near stabbing himself with his own blade. He scrambled up and charged on, throwing his stolen shield away and lifting his sword in both hands.
bs: — Jebeni gadovi! — vrisnuo je, prskajući pljuvačkom. — Jebeni gadovi! — Zapleo se nogom i kliznuo licem, zagrizao travu, zamalo se probo vlastitim mačem. Skaknuo je i napao dalje, bacivši ukradeni štit i podižući mač objema rukama.

en: There were Carls here, desperately trying to organise a shield wall. A Named Man with a fox-fur around his shoulders pointed with a thick finger. Leo didn’t so much charge at him as fall onto him, his weary swing clattering harmlessly off the Named Man’s shield. He caught his chin on the rim, mouth filling with the salt taste of blood.
bs: Ovdje su bili Carls, očajnički pokušavajući organizirati zid od štitova. Čovjek s imenom ogrnut lisičjim krznom pokazao je debelim prstom. Leo nije toliko jurnuo na njega koliko je pao na nj, a njegov umorni zamah bezazleno se odbio od štit čovjeka s imenom. Udario je bradom o rub štita, a usta su mu se napunila slankastim okusom krvi.

en: “Have… to pull back.” It was Jurand, with hardly the breath to talk. Helmet off and his face spotted with blood. He hugged Leo, half holding him up, half leaning on him. “Get you to safety.”
bs: — Moramo… se povući. Bio je to Džurand, jedva hvatajući dah za govor. Kaciga mu je bila skinuta, a lice poprskano krvlju. Zagrlio je Lea, upola ga držeći, upola se oslanjajući na njega. — Izvući te na Sejf.

en: “Stour Nightfall!” Leo roared back, spit flying from his bared teeth. He tried to drag himself forward but Jurand held him back, or maybe held him up, it was only fury stopped Leo’s knees from buckling.
bs: — Staur Najtfol! uzvratio je Leo rikom, dok mu je slina prskala s ogoljenih zubi. Pokušao se odvući naprijed, ali ga je Džurand zadržao, ili ga je možda samo držao da ne padne, jer samo ga je gnjev spriječio da mu kleknu koljena.

en: “Good,” murmured Orso. “Good.” He expressed the exact opposite of his feelings so often, one might have hoped he would be better at it. In fact, the thought of the Breakers’ arrival left him desperately wanting a drink. But dawn was probably considered too early at a peace negotiation, even for a small beer or something. He puffed out a worried sigh.
bs: — Dobro, promrmlja Orso. — Dobro. Svoje je osjećaje tako često izražavao suprotno od onoga što je zapravo mislio da bi se moglo pomisliti kako će u tome s vremenom postati vještiji. Zapravo, sama pomisao na dolazak Lomljača u njemu je budila očajničku želju za pićem. No, zora se vjerojatno smatrala preranim dobom za mirovne pregovore, čak i za obično pivo ili nešto slično. Ispustio je zabrinut uzdah.

en: “Welcome!” He aimed at a balance between warm indulgence and effortless authority, but no doubt ended up with prickly weakness. “I am Crown Prince Orso, this is Colonel Forest, commander of the four regiments currently encircling Valbeck, and this—”
bs: — Dobro došli! Ciljao je na ravnotežu između tople popustljivosti i nenametljivog autoriteta, no nesumnjivo je završio zvučeći poput trnaste slabosti. — Ja sam prijestolonasljednik Orso, ovo je pukovnik Forest, zapovjednik četiriju pukovnija koje trenutočno okružuju Valbek, a ovo je —

en: “Please!” Orso held up a calming hand and made Pike sit back like a hound called off. “No one will die because of a defect of etiquette. It is my ardent hope that no one will die at all. I understand… hostages have been taken?”
bs: — Molim vas! Orso podigne ruku u znak smirivanja i natjera Pajka da se vrati natrag u sjedalo poput lovačkog psa kojeg su opozvali. — Nitko neće poginuti zbog propusta u bontonu. Moja je žarka želja da nitko uopće ne pogine. Shvaćam… uzeti su taoci?

en: His satisfaction was quickly cut off as Teufel flung a folded paper so it spun across the polished table and into his lap. He winced as he unfolded it, expecting insults scrawled in blood.
bs: Zadovoljstvo mu naglo splasne kad Tojfel baci presavijeni papir koji klizne preko uglačanog stola i padne mu u krilo. Trznuo se dok ga je rasklapao, očekujući uvrede nažvrljane krvlju.

en: Malmer knows he has little left to bargain with. Offer him too much and he will become suspicious. He feared you would attack at once. Now he fears you will surround the city and starve the Breakers out. He expects you to be an arrogant liar. My advice is to treat him with honesty and respect. To seek a peaceful solution and avoid bluster. But to firmly refuse any demands and make him aware that you know time is on your side. If you were to offer amnesty for the Breakers, I believe he could be p
bs: Malmer zna da mu je preostalo malo toga za cjenkanje. Ponudite li mu previše, postat će sumnjičav. Strahovao je da ćete odmah napasti. Sada strahuje da ćete opkoliti grad i izgladnjeti Lomljače. Očekuje da ćete biti bahati lažljivac. Moj je Vijeće da se prema njemu ophodite s iskrenošću i poštovanjem, da tražite mirno rješenje i izbjegavate prijetnje, ali i da odlučno odbijete sve zahtjeve te mu date do znanja da ste svjesni kako je vrijeme na vašoj strani. Ako biste ponudili amnestiju za Lomlja

en: “The very last thing we want is further bloodshed, Colonel Forest,” said Orso, giving him the calming palm now. He had enough calming palm for everyone. “We are all citizens of the Union. We are all subjects of my father. I refuse to believe we cannot find a peaceful solution.”
bs: Posljednja stvar koju želimo jest novo prolivanje krvi, pukovniče Foreste, reče Orso, smirujuće podignuvši dlan. Imao je on dovoljno smirujućih gesta za svakoga. — Svi smo mi građani Unije. Svi smo mi podanici mog oca. Odbijam povjerovati da ne možemo pronaći mirno rješenje.

en: Orso silenced him with that raised hand, without taking his eyes from Malmer’s. “I fear the alternative is that I order Colonel Forest to surround the city and let nothing in or out. I have quite cleared my calendar and can wait as long as it takes. When you surrender, which you surely must, it will not be to me, but to Superior Pike.”
bs: Orso ga utiša podignutom rukom, ne mičući Oko s Malmerovih očiju. — Bojim se da je alternativa ta da naredim pukovniku Forestu da okruži grad i ne dopusti ništa unutra ni vani. Potpuno sam oslobodio svoj raspored i mogu čekati koliko god treba. Kada se predate, što Sejf morate, to nećete učiniti meni, već Superioru Pajku.

en: “You’ll have it.” Malmer considered him a moment longer. “Your Highness.” He strode weightily from the room, his twitchy friend at his back. Teufel’s chair screeched on the tiled floor as she stood, gave Orso one last blast of scorn, then turned her back on the meeting. The door clicked shut.
bs: — Imat ćete ga. Malmer ga promatraše još tren. — Vaša visosti. Teško otetura iz sobe, a njegov mu je nervozni prijatelj bio za petama. Teufelina stolica zaškripje po pločicama dok je ustajala, baci Orsu posljednji Oko pun prezira, pa okrenu leđa sastanku. Vrata se kliknuvši zatvoriše.

en: She wondered how many were laid out in that glade. Maybe a hundred. Maybe more. Hunched and bloodstained healers moved among them, stitching, bandaging, setting, giving food and water and what comfort they could. It wasn’t much.
bs: Pitala se koliko ih je polegnuto po toj čistini. Možda stotinu. Možda i više. Pogrbljeni i krvlju umrljani iscjelitelji kretali su se među njima, šivajući, previjajući, namještajući kosti, nudeći hranu, vodu i svaku utjehu koju su mogli pružiti. Nije to bilo mnogo.

en: Isern gave Rikke a significant look from under her brows. “A great healer, like a great leader, must make of her heart a stone.”
bs: Izern značajno pogleda Rike ispod obrva. — Velik iscjelitelj, baš kao i velik vođa, mora od svoga srca načiniti kamen.

en: Isern shook her head, lips pressed into a hard line as she nimbly worked that needle. “All the effort it takes to make a person but it’s the killers they sing about. When did you last hear a man sing a woman’s name? Unless he was singing for his mummy when the Great Leveller had a hand on him.”
bs: Izern odmahne glavom, usana stisnutih u tanku crtu dok je spretno radila iglom. — Koliko je truda potrebno da se čovjek stvori, a ipak se pjesme pjevaju o ubojicama. Kada si posljednji put čula muškarca da pjeva žensko ime? Osim ako nije pjevao majci dok ga Veliki Izravnavatelj nije uzeo pod svoje.

en: “Sorry. You’ll have to find someone else to hold it soon. I’ve been called to a meeting at dawn.” Rikke puffed herself up. “By Lady Governor Brock, in fact.”
bs: — Oprosti. Ubrzo ćeš morati pronaći nekoga drugog da je drži. Pozvana sam na sastanak u zoru. Rike se napuše. — I to od guvernerice Brok osobno.

en: Rikke’s mood was by no means helped by the knight herald standing motionless in the middle of the tent, a letter from His August Majesty held out in one gauntleted fist. When she’d slipped through the flap and seen him standing there, she’d wondered where they found all these tall bastards. Then she’d wondered why everyone else was ignoring him. Then, during a particularly impassioned rant, the lady governor had walked right through him and back the other way, and Rikke had realised her left eye
bs: Rikkeino raspoloženje nipošto nije popravljao heraldički Ritter koji je nepomično stajao sred šatora, držeći u oklopljenoj šaci pismo od Vašeg Veličanstva. Kad se provukla kroz šator i ugledala ga ondje, zapitala se gdje pronalaze sve te visoke kopilane. Potom se zapitala zašto ga svi ostali ignoriraju. Zatim je, usred osobito vatrena ispada, gospa upraviteljica prošla ravno kroz njega pa natrag, a Rike je shvatila da joj je lijevo Oko užareno i da on zapravo nije ondje. Ili možda još nije.

en: “Has it occurred to either of you that I might bloody win?” Leo angrily bunched one scabbed fist. “We’re fought out! We’ve no help coming and Scale Ironhand has fresh men ready! This might be our only chance to take back Uffrith. To keep the Protectorate alive!”
bs: "Je li ikome od vas palo na pamet da bih mogao krvavo pobijediti?" Leo gnjevno stisnu krastavu šaku. — Iscrpljeni smo! Nemamo nikakve pomoći, a Ljuska Željezna Ruka spreman je sa svježim ljudima! Možda nam je ovo jedina prilika da vratimo Afrit. Da održimo Protektorat na životu!

en: But somewhere at the back of her mind, in a dark corner she’d hardly known she had, she found she wanted to see Leo fight Stour Nightfall. To see him spill that evil bastard’s blood in front of the whole North. To take her share of vengeance, for her father, for those wounded in the glade, for the dead already in the mud, for the shit she’d gone through out in the cold woods.
bs: No negdje u dubini uma, u mračnom kutku za koji jedva da je znala da postoji, osjeti kako zapravo želi vidjeti Lea kako se bori protiv Staura Najtfola. Vidjeti ga kako prolijeva krv tog zlobnog gadstva pred licem cijelog Sjevera. Uzeti svoj dio osvete, za oca, za ranjene na čistini, za mrtve koji već leže u blatu, za sva sranja kroz koja je prošla vani u hladnoj šumi.

en: There was a breathless stillness in the tent as Leo took the scroll and slowly unrolled it. He read the first few lines and looked up, eyes wide.
bs: U šatoru zavlada tišina od koje zastaje dah dok je Leo uzeo svitak i polako ga odmotao. Pročitao je prvih nekoliko redaka i podigao Oko, širom otvorenih očiju.

en: “It feels like yesterday I was feeding him, and dressing him, and wiping his arse.” She looked at Rikke, voice turning harsh. “He’s a bloody idiot who knows nothing about anything, but he was born with a cock, so he gets to decide for all of us!”
bs: — Čini mi se kao da sam ga jučer hranila, odijevala i brisala mu dupe. Pogledala je Rike, a glas joj postade grub. — On je prokleti idiot koji ne zna ništa ni o čemu, ali rođen je s kurcem, pa zato odlučuje u ime svih nas!

en: King Scale was drinking. What else would he be doing? He was drinking, and laughing lustily at stories of the battle, already bloating out with lies like so much watered beer. His nephew, the mighty Stour Nightfall, decorated with a few fresh cuts and bruises, grinned to hear of his own exploits, even more at the falsehoods than the facts. About these two heroes, old warriors and young basked in the sunny radiance of a victory they hadn’t won yet.
