But she was every bit as sleek and dignified as the day they met. Not rattled by the long drop beyond the short parapet at her back, or their whirlwind courtship, or her delicate condition. Apparently impossible to rattle at all. His first thought was what a portrait they’d make together.
bs: Savine je stajala na parapetu, a Agriont se prostirao pod njom kao da ga posjeduje. Nekako je očekivao da će postati majčinski nastrojena, rumenih obraza, natečena od djeteta. No bila je jednako vitka i dostojanstvena kao onog dana kad su se upoznali. Nije je uznemirio ni duboki ponor iza niskog parapeta za njezinim leđima, ni njihovo vrtoglavo udvaranje, ni njezino delikatno stanje. Očigledno ju je nemoguće uznemiriti. Njegova prva pomisao bila je kakav bi portret njih dvoje činili zajedno.

en: “I can only apologise for the ambush,” she said, turning to look at the view. The statues standing proud on either side of the Kingsway, the wide expanse of the Square of Marshals, the glinting dome of the Lords’ Round. “If it’s any consolation, they did the same to me. I was somewhat… surprised at first.”
bs: — Mogu se samo ispričati zbog zasjede, rekla je okrećući se prema pogledu. Kipovi koji su ponosno stajali s obje strane Kingswaya, široko prostranstvo Trga Maršala, svjetlucava kupola Lords Rounda. — Ako ti je za utjehu, i meni su priredili isto. Bila sam pomalo… iznenađena isprva.

en: “My father doesn’t own me. Not even a percentage. If we marry, my loyalty will be to you. But you should know I am my own woman and do things my own way. I do not plan for that to change.”
bs: — Moj otac me ne posjeduje. Niti jedan posto. Ako se vjenčamo, moja će odanost biti tebi. Ali trebaš znati da sam svoja žena i da stvari radim na svoj način. Ne planiram promijeniti se.

en: She didn’t seem to take anything so tasteless as steps, but still she drifted closer. He enjoyed watching her move. So graceful. So precise. So regal, even. He liked a woman with pride, and Savine dripped with it. With her on his arm, he’d be the envy of the world.
bs: Nije se doimala kao netko tko pravi tako prozaične korake, ali se svejedno primakla bliže. Uživao je promatrajući je kako se kreće. Tako graciozna. Tako precizna. Čak i tako kraljevski dostojanstvena. Sviđala mu se žena s ponosom, a Savine je pucala od njega. S njom pod rukom, bio bi predmet zavisti cijeloga svijeta.

en: “Let’s.” He caught Savine’s free hand and slid his mother’s ring onto her finger. It proved too tight to go over the knuckle, but he didn’t care a shit.
bs: — Hajdemo. Uhvatio je Savinu za slobodnu ruku i navukao joj majčin prsten na prst. Pokazao se pretijesnim da bi prešao preko zgloba, ali njega nije bilo briga ni za što.

en: Vick shrugged again. “I asked myself what I’d have tried, if I’d been in Vitari’s place. Anyone could’ve done it.”
bs: Vik ponovno slegne ramenima. — Pitala sam se što bih ja pokušala da sam na mjestu Vitari. Svatko je to mogao učiniti.

en: “The swamps will run out of flies,” said Shudra, “before politicians run out of arguments. They are already splitting into new factions over the latest issue.”
bs: — Močvare će ostati bez muha, reče Šudra, prije nego što političari ostanu bez argumenata. Već se dijele u nove frakcije oko najnovijeg pitanja.

en: “The Union is far from perfect. We have our rivalries, our greed and our ambition. That is why we need honest, upright, passionate people. People like you.”
bs: — Unija je daleko od savršenstva. Imamo svoja nadmetanja, svoju pohlepu i ambiciju. Zato su nam potrebni pošteni, čestiti, strastveni Folk. Folk poput vas.

en: “Well, you convinced Shudra.” Vick slipped the purse from her pocket, weighed it in her hand, silver clinking. “He was the only audience that counted.”
bs: — Pa, uvjerio si Šudru. Vik izvuče vrećicu iz džepa, odmjeri je u ruci uz zveckanje srebra. — On je bio jedina publika koja je bila važna.

en: “Who says there even is a real Shenkt? People like things that are simple. Black and white. Good and evil. They want to make a choice and tell themselves they were right. But as His Eminence is fond of saying, the real world is painted in greys. The truth is complicated, full of mixed emotions and blurred outcomes and each-way bets. The truth… is a hard sell.”
bs: "Tko kaže da uopće postoji stvarni Šenkt? Folk vole proste stvari. Crno i bijelo. Dobro i zlo. Žele donijeti odluku i utješiti se kako su bili u pravu. No, kako Eminencija voli reći, stvarni je svijet naslikan u nijansama siva. Istina je zamršena, puna oprečnih osjećaja, mutnih ishoda i ograda na sve strane. Istina… slabo se prodaje."

en: She saw boots through the blur. Well-worn old work boots. Then something was over her face. Darkness and her own booming breath. Hands tied behind her. Scrape of her toes as she was dragged along under the armpits. Hiss over the cobbles. Clack, clack, clack over the boards of a wharf.
bs: Kroz maglu ugleda čizme. Dobro iznošene stare radne čizme. Zatim joj se nešto nađe preko lica. Tmina i vlastiti tutnjajući dah. Ruke svezane na leđima. Struganje prstiju dok su je vukli ispod pazuha. Šuškanje po oblucima. Kljac, kljac, kljac preko dasaka gata.

en: “Know who I am?” she asked. A Styrian accent, but she spoke common well. Like someone who’d spent a lot of time in the Union.
bs: — Znaš li tko sam? upita ona. Stirijski naglasak, ali dobro je govorila općim jezikom. Poput nekoga tko je proveo mnogo vremena u Uniji.

en: Styria’s most infamous killer, if it really was him, gave Vick a watery, slightly apologetic smile. Few men had ever looked so ordinary. Gaunt and colourless, with dark rings around his eyes. But then awesome looks put people on their guard, and that’s the last thing a killer wants. He leaned back against the wall and pulled something from a pocket. A piece of wood, roughly carved. He began to whittle it with a little curved knife, blade flashing, white shavings scattering about his worn boots.
bs: Najozloglašeniji ubojica u Stiriji, ako je doista bio on, udijelio je Vik vodenast, pomalo ispričavajući osmijeh. Malo je kojih muškaraca izgledalo toliko obično. Mršav i bezbojan, s tamnim kolutovima oko očiju. No zastrašujući izgled privlači previše pažnje i tjera ljude na oprez, a to je posljednje što ubojica želi. Naslonio se leđima na zid i izvukao nešto iz džepa. Komad drveta, grubo izrezbaren. Počeo ga je strugati malim zakrivljenim nožićem; oštrica je bljeskala, a bijele strugotine rasip

en: “But you weren’t there to kill him. You were there to pretend we’d tried, so you could pretend to save him. I watched the whole thing with a growing sense of annoyance, then a growing sense of admiration. It was very neat, wasn’t it?”
bs: — Ali nisi ga bio došao ubiti. Bio si ondje da odglumiš kako smo pokušali, ne bi li mogao odglumiti kako ga spašavaš. Promatrala sam sve to uz sve veći osjećaj iritacije, a potom i sve veće divljenje. Bilo je vrlo uredno, zar ne?

en: Thump, thump, thump went the pulse in Vick’s head and the blood tickled at her scalp and it occurred to her this might be one of those turning points. Like in the mine, when she chose to run. Or in the camps, when she chose to tell. Or in Valbeck, when she chose to stay. Her mouth felt very dry all of a sudden.
bs: Tup, tup, tup – udarao je puls u Vickinoj glavi, a krv joj je škakljala tjeme te joj sinu kako bi ovo mogao biti jedan od onih prijelomnih trenutaka. Poput onoga u rudniku, kad je izabrala pobjeći. Ili u logorima, kad je izabrala progovoriti. Ili u Valbeku, kad je izabrala ostati. Usta joj odjednom postaše posve suha.

en: “The First of the Magi?” The idea of that self-satisfied old bastard pulling anyone’s strings seemed hard to credit.
bs: — Prvi među Magi? Pomisao da taj samodopadni stari gad vuče ikakve konce činila se teško vjerojatnom.

en: Tallow made a high-pitched squeak into his gag. Vitari gave a long sigh. Shenkt issued that indifferent grunt one more time. Vick bared her teeth, back prickling, expecting the blade. Any moment now. The brittle silence stretched, almost unbearable.
bs: Talou ispusti visok, piskav zvuk u svoj uvez. Vitari duboko udahnu. Šenkt još jednom ispusti onaj ravnodušan grleni glas. Vik ogoli zube, a koža joj se naježi, očekujući oštricu. Svakog trenutka. Krhka tišina se razvuče, gotovo neizdrživa.

en: “For now.” Vitari drew the bolt and opened the door. Shenkt slipped away that little curved knife, pulled up his hood and walked out, humming faintly to himself, leaving nothing but a scattering of pale shavings on the boards.
bs: — Za sada. Vitari je pomaknula zasun i otvorila vrata. Šenkt je spremio onaj mali zakrivljeni nož, navukao kapuljaču i izašao tiho sebi u bradu pjevušeći, ne ostavljajući za sobom ništa osim rasutih svijetlih strugotina po podu.

en: “Can’t lose you, Rikke.” The grey stubble on his grey cheek shifted as he clenched his jaw. “Can’t do it.”
bs: — Ne smijem te izgubiti, Rike. Sijeda čekinja na njegovu sijedu obrazu pomaknula se dok je stiskao čeljust. — Ne mogu to podnijeti.

en: “When I was a boy, my brother called me pig fat, I cried so easy. Then I forgot how. All I wanted was to be feared. But you never feared me.”
bs: — Kad sam bio dječak, brat me zvao svinjskom masti, plakao sam tako lako. Onda sam zaboravio kako. Sve što sam želio bilo je da me se boje. Ali ti me se nikad nisi bojala.

en: “I always behave,” said Isern, frowning at those two flatheads with her grip tight on the dark haft of her spear. Far as Shanka have expressions beyond just a lot of teeth, these ones seemed to frown back. “Let’s go, then.”
bs: — Ja se uvijek lijepo ponašam, reče Izern, namrštivši se na tu dvojicu ravnoglavaca čvrsto stežući tamno drško svog koplja. Koliko su Shanka uopće imali izraze lica osim silnih zuba, činilo se da joj ovi uzvraćaju mrštenje. — Idemo onda.

en: Night, and firelight danced on the gathered faces. Withered old faces and fresh young ones. Faces pricked with the swirling tattoos of the hillmen. Faces that weren’t there yet, maybe, or had been there long ago. Rikke could hardly tell today from yesterday from tomorrow any longer. Meat spat and sizzled. The cold, crisp air of the hills on the back of Rikke’s head but the warmth of the fire on her face and she grinned at the simple pleasure of it, snuggled into a smelly old fur.
bs: Noć, a odsjaj vatre plesao je po okupljenim licima. Izbrazdanim starim licima i svježim mladim licima. Licima ispresijecanim kovrčavim tetovažama gorštaka. Licima kojih možda još nije bilo tu, ili su tu bila davno prije. Rike više jedva da je razlikovala danas od jučer ili sutra. Meso je cvrčalo i prštalo. Hladan, Trdak planinski zrak ležao je Rike na zatiljku, dok joj je toplina vatre grijala lice te se široko osmjehnula na to jednostavno zadovoljstvo, ušuljavši se u smrdljivo staro krzno.

en: Scenn looked over at Rikke, then. Small, dark eyes he had, but she saw the sharpness in them. Beware of clever men, her father told her once. But beware most of clever men who look like fools. “What do you say, girl?” And he spat a bit of gristle into the fire and pointed at her with the stripped-bare bone. “If you can see the future, tell me mine.”
bs: Skenn je tada bacio Oko na Rike. Sitne, tamne oči je imao, ali ona je u njima opazila oštrinu. Čuvaj se pametnih Folk, govorio joj je otac jednom. Ali najviše se čuvaj pametnih Folk koji izgledaju poput budala. — Što ti kažeš, djevojko?" I ispljunuo je komadić hrskavice u vatru te pokazao na nju ogoljenom kosti. — Ako možeš vidjeti budućnost, reci mi moju.

en: Isern spat ale in the fire and made it hiss. “What would you know about it, Scenn-i-Phail, who carries our father’s hammer?”
bs: Izern ispljune pivo u vatru, koja zagrcnuto zacvrči. — Što ti znaš o tome, Skenn-i-Fejl, koji nosiš očev čekić?

en: “My brother Scenn knows the way. He is a turd in the shape of a man, but he’ll help. We’ll head to his village first, which is a turd in the shape of a village. Slorfa, they call it, at the head of the valley four valleys on.”
bs: — Moj brat Skenn zna put. On je govno u obliku čovjeka, ali pomoći će. Prvo ćemo poći do njegova sela, koje je govno u obliku sela. Slorfa, zovu ga, na začelju doline četiri doline odavde.

en: “Let’s make some footprints,” grunted Isern, turning back to the steeply climbing trail. “The forbidden lake won’t be coming to us, will it?”
bs: — Hajdemo ostavljati tragove, prosikta Izern okrećući se natrag prema stazi koja se strmo uspinjala. — Zabranjeno jezero neće samo doći k nama, zar ne?

en: He was pretty, Rikke thought, even if he wasn’t the cleverest. And he had an odd manner and talked strange. But being brought up in the Union would do that to a boy, maybe, and for pretty you could forgive a lot.
bs: Bio je zgodan, pomisli Rike, čak i ako nije bio najbistriji. A i čudno se ponašao i govorio nekako neobično. No odrastanje u Uniji moglo bi to učiniti dječaku, možda, a čovjek mu je zbog lijepog lica mogao oprostiti mnogo toga.

en: “My turn to hide!” shouted Leo, and he dashed off, slipped and fell, rolled in a shower of hay dust, then scrambled up and disappeared through the barn door. Made Rikke sad, for some reason, to see him go. So sad.
bs: — Moja je red da se sakrijem!, viknuo je Leo, a zatim je krenuo u trk, skliznuo i pao, kotrljao se u oblaku slamenog prašine, pa se naglo podigao i nestao kroz vrata štale. Rike je bilo tužno, iz nekog razloga, gledati kako odlazi. Toliko tužno.

en: “That and slicing cheese,” said Sholla, lifting her knife towards her mouth with furious concentration, a cheese-shaving so fine it was almost see-through clinging to the flat. A spring gust came through the courtyard just as it was getting to her lips and blew it away like thistledown, left her clutching helpless at the air.
bs: — I za rezanje sira, reče Šola, podižući nož prema ustima s bijesnom koncentracijom, dok se na ravnom dijelu oštrice nalijepila sirna pločica toliko tanka da je bila gotovo prozirna. U dvorište je upravo uletio proljetni povjetarac upravo kad joj je to trebalo do usana i odnio ga kao pletivu, ostavivši je da nesposobno hvata zrak.

en: “I fucking hate this prick,” murmured Sholla as she tried to shave an even thinner slice from the edge of the cheese block, then clicked her tongue in disgust as it crumbled.
bs: — Mrzim ga, kurva, promrmlja Šola dok je pokušavala ogrebati još tanji komadić s ruba sira, a zatim je jezikom udarila o zube od gađenja kad se srušio.

en: “That’s the way of things, lad, we all end up stinking. And yes, I’m sure. It’s not for my benefit, I can tell you that.”
bs: — Takav je život, momče, svi na kraju zaudaramo. I da, siguran sam. Nisam to za svoju korist, to ti mogu reći.

en: “You should be kneeling,” growled Greenway as they stopped in the midst of that wide stone floor in front of Stour.
bs: — Trebali biste klečati, zagruntao je Grinvej dok su se zaustavili u sredini tog širokog kamenog poda Naprijed Staura.

en: “Men are greedy, aren’t they? No gratitude. They don’t think about what they’ve already got from you, only about what they can get next.”
bs: — Muškarci su pohlepniji, zar ne? Bez zahvalnosti. Ne razmišljaju o onome što su već dobili od vas, već samo o onome što mogu dobiti sljedeće.

en: Clover had his doubts as he watched that cage gently turn. Hollowhead was a popular man. Lot of friends and family all over those valleys on the border with Uffrith. Lot of hard fighters who’d be less than happy about that man being in a cage. Black Calder had spent years stitching the ripped-up North together with threats and whispers and debts and favours. Can’t do it just with fear alone. But it was hardly Clover’s job to say so.
bs: Klover je bio u dvojbi, promatrajući kako se taj kavez lagano okreće. Šupljoglav je bio omiljen čovjek. Mnogo prijatelja i obitelji posvuda po onim dolinama na granici s Afritom. Mnogo opasnih boraca koji ne bi bili pretjerano sretni što je taj čovjek u kaveznoj tamnici. Black Kalder je proveo godine krpajući raskomadani Sjever prijetnjama, šaptima, dugovima i uslugama. To se ne može postići samo strahom. No, jedva da je Kloverov posao bio to naglasiti.

en: “Little present for you.” Clover took the bag from Flick and upended it, and the Shanka heads bounced and rolled out across the floor. He wished those had been the first scattered across Skarling’s Hall, but he’d a sorry sense severed heads had been quite a frequent decoration down the years.
bs: — Mali dar za vas. Klover uze torbu od Flika i preokrenu je, a glave Shanka poskočiše i otkotrljaše se preko poda. Poželio je da su to bile prve glave razasute po Skarlings Hallu, ali imao je žalostan osjećaj da su odsječene glave tijekom godina bile prilično uobičajen ukras.

en: “No, no, no.” Which was something of a relief, as Clover couldn’t say he’d much enjoyed their last war with the Union. “Gave my word in the Circle, didn’t I? Swore a solemn oath to the Young Lion! Think I’d break my word?”
bs: — Ne, ne, ne. Što je bilo pravo olakšanje, jer Klover nije mogao reći da je pretjerano uživao u njihovom posljednjem ratu s Unijom. — Dow sam riječ u Krugu, zar ne? Položio sam svečanu prisegu Mladom Lavu! Misliš li da bih pogazio svoju riječ?

en: Then Stour grinned bigger’n ever. And he squatted down on his haunches, that beautiful wolfskin cloak dragging in the mess the heads had left. He took the biggest one in his hands and set it right-side up, its great spiked helmet still on and its great long bloated tongue hanging from its oversized jaws.
bs: Tada se Staur nasmiješi šire nego ikad. Čučnuo je na pete, a onaj prekrasni ogrtač od vučje kože vukao se po neredu koji su glave ostavile za sobom. Uzeo je najveću među njima u ruke i postavio je uspravno, s velikom šiljatom kacigom još uvijek na glavi i dugačkim, natečenim jezikom koji je visio iz prevelikih čeljusti.

en: “Chilly as winter’s arse,” she gasped as she wobbled up next to the woman. From the side she looked about normal. Old and deep-lined, cool blue eyes fixed on the horizon.
bs: — Hladno kao u zimskoj guzici, zadihano je dobacila dok se ljuljala pokraj žene. S boka je izgledala posve normalno. Stara i duboko izbrazdana lica, hladnih plavih očiju uprtih u horizont.

en: Rikke had grown up in the North where a man with no scars was no man at all, but she never before saw a scar the like of this. She looked down at the water, already settling around her own sharp shin bones and holding a dark reflection of herself. “What happened to you?”
bs: Rike je odrasla na Sjeveru, gdje čovjek bez ožiljaka nije bio pravi muškarac, ali nikada prije nije vidjela ožiljak poput ovoga. Pogledala je dolje u vodu, koja se već smirivala oko njezinih oštrih goljeničnih kostiju i zadržavala njezin tamni odraz. — Što ti se dogodilo?

en: “I’m guessing…” Rikke winced as she tried to shift her foot on the slippery lake bed and caught her toe on a pointed rock. “We’re not actually talking about pots now? Or are we talking about pots now?”
bs: — Pretpostavljam… Rike se zgrize dok je pokušavala pomaknuti stopalo na skliskom jezerskom dnu i zapela prstom za oštri kamen. — Sada zapravo ne govorimo o loncima? Ili ipak govorimo o loncima?

en: “Ah!” Caurib smiled, and the great scar through her top lip stretched about the wire in a way Rikke found most unsettling. “Breakfast.”
bs: — Ah! Caurib se nasmiješi, a Great ožiljak kroz njezinu gornju usnu rastegnu se oko žice na način koji je Rike smatrao krajnje uznemirujućim. — Doručak.

en: “The Shanka don’t like baths and they’ve no sense of humour at all, but they understand the meeting betwixt flesh and metal. They learned that much from the Master Maker.” And the Shanka bent down, crooked lips pursed, and coaxed a flame into life with its breath.
bs: — Shanka ne voli kupanje i nema nimalo smisla za humor, ali razumije susret mesa i metala. To su naučili od Majstora graditelja. Shanka se sagnuo, iskrivljenih usana stisnutih u usku liniju, i svojim dahom potaknuo plamen na život.

en: Gave Rikke a worried feeling, the way Caurib said it. Like there was an unpleasant surprise coming. Pleasant surprises seemed to get rarer as you got older. “Aye, well… I feel better now.” Rikke put her palm a little nervously to her left eye. Cool and clammy, just like the other. Just like anyone’s. “Whatever you did worked.”
bs: Način na koji je to Caurib izgovorila izazvao je u Rike nelagodu. Kao da slijedi neko neugodno iznenađenje. Činilo se da su ugodna iznenađenja postajala sve rjeđa kako je čovjek stario. — Da, pa… sad se osjećam bolje." Rike je pomalo nervozno prislonila dlan na svoje lijevo oko. Hladno i vlažno, baš kao i ono drugo. Baš kao i u svakoga. — Što god da si učinila, djelovalo je.

en: Rikke brushed her cheek with her fingertips as she watched the smoke from the cook-fire drift across the lake. She thought of the hillmen, and the hillwomen, and those bastards from past the Crinna she’d seen sometimes with their blue painted faces. She gave one of those sorry sighs made her lips flap. “There’s just no going back from tattoos on your face, is there?”
bs: Rike je vrhovima prstiju dotaknula obraz dok je promatrala dim s vatre za kuhanje kako lebdi iznad jezera. Razmišljala je o brđanima i brđankama te onim kopiladima nasuprot tome Crinna koje je ponekad viđala s licima obojenim u plavo. Ispustila je onaj jadni uzdah od kojeg su joj usne zalepršale. — Jednostavno nema povratka kad jednom istetoviraš lice, zar ne?

en: “Look about you, girl. If I had all the answers, do you think I would be standing in a freezing lake with my head stitched together?”
bs: — Pogledaj oko sebe, djevojko. Da imam sve odgovore, misliš li da bih stajala u ledenome jezeru sa zašivenom glavom?

en: Open disdain for not one but two kings felt a mite disloyal to Leo, especially here at the heart of government, attending a trial where a man’s life would hang in the balance. His mother would’ve been most displeased to hear it. But then, sooner or later, a man has to stop making everything about pleasing his mother.
bs: Otvoreno preziranje ne jednog, nego dvojice kraljeva činilo se pomalo nelojalnim Leu, pogotovo ovdje, u samom srcu vlasti, gdje prisustvuje suđenju u kojem ovisi čovjekov život. Njegova majka bila bi silno nezadovoljna da to čuje. No, prije ili kasnije, čovjek mora prestati sve podređivati ugađanju majci.

en: “But… why?” asked Leo, struggling to find a position on the hard bench where his leg didn’t nag at him.
bs: — Ali… zašto? upita Leo, boreći se da na tvrdoj klupi pronađe položaj u kojem ga noga neće toliko mučiti.

en: The vast doors were heaved open, the crack of light down the middle gradually widening. Orso set his shoulders in what he hoped was a regal bearing, plastered on a smile, realised that was utterly inappropriate to the occasion, swapped it for a solemn frown and stepped through.
bs: Masivna vrata su se uz škripu otvorila, a procjep svjetlosti po sredini se postupno širio. Orso je isprsio ramena u ono za što se nadao da je kraljevsko držanje, nabacio osmijeh, shvatio da je to potpuno neprimjereno za tu prigodu, zamijenio ga ozbiljnim namrštenim izrazom i zakoračio unutra.

en: He flinched as he felt hands reaching around his neck, but it was only Gorst, unfastening the golden clasp and whisking the royal vestment away, while one of his legion of footmen did the same with the crown. Orso wasn’t even sure he knew the man’s name. He wasn’t even sure he had a name.
bs: Trznuo se kad je osjetio ruke kako mu posežu oko vrata, ali bio je to samo Gorst, koji je otkopčao zlatnu kopču i odnio kraljevsku odoru, dok je jedan iz njegove legije poslužitelja učinio isto s krunom. Orso nije bio siguran zna li uopće ime tog čovjeka. Nije bio siguran ni je li taj čovjek uopće imao ime.

en: “I call this meeting of the Open Council of the Union…” The announcer let it hang there as the noise gradually faded into weighty silence. “To order!”
bs: — Proglašavam ovaj sastanak Otvorenog vijeća Unije… Najavljivač je ostavio rečenicu da visi u zraku dok se buka postupno stišavala u tešku tišinu. — …otvorenim!

en: “I wish to congratulate one of the most celebrated of our number, His Grace Leonault dan Brock, the Lord Governor—and, if I may say, the undoubted saviour—of Angland… on his forthcoming marriage!”
bs: — Želim čestitati jednom od naših najslavnijih članova, Njegovoj Milosti Leonaultu dan Broku, lordu guverneru – i, ako smijem dodati, neupitnom spasitelju – Englenda… na njegovu nadolazećem vjenčanju!

en: The whole chamber was filled with thunderous applause. The high justice was leaning across him to congratulate the Arch Lector. Orso became aware he was clapping himself. A limp-wristed flapping that made almost no noise at all. Clapping at his own funeral. Down on the front row, lords had clustered around an awkward-looking Leo dan Brock to slap him on the back.
bs: Cijela je dvorana odjekivala gromoglasnim pljeskom. Visoki Džadž nagnuo se preko njega kako bi čestitao Lektoru. Orso postade svjestan da i sam plješće. Mlohavo mahanje rukama koje nije proizvodilo gotovo nikakav zvuk. Pljeskanje na vlastitom pogrebu. Dolje prvenstveno, Lords su se okupili oko neugodnog Lea dan Broka kako bi ga potapšali po leđima.

en: But she did not care at all for the manner of the announcement. She had supposed that her engagement would be a matter of supreme indifference to Orso, but the intensity of the look he had given her told a different story. She wished she could somehow have let him know about it sooner. And she could not have trusted the self-appointed announcer less. Lord Isher was entirely too pleased with himself, too friendly with her husband-to-be and too willing to share the glory of his wedding with them.
bs: No, nimalo joj se nije svidio način na koji je objava izvedena. Pretpostavljala je da će njezine zaruke biti stvar potpune ravnodušnosti za Orsa, ali intenzitet pogleda koji joj je uputio govorio je drukčiju priču. Voljela bi da mu je nekako mogla ranije dati do znanja. A samoprozvanom najavljivaču nije mogla manje vjerovati. Lord Išer bio je previše zadovoljan samim sobom, previše prijateljski nastrojen prema njezinu budućem suprugu i previše voljan dijeliti slavu njihova vjenčanja s njima. Dok

en: A side door was flung open with an echoing bang. There was a rustling as lords and proxies twisted to see, people in both public galleries leaning out dangerously far in their eagerness to glimpse the prisoner. The hall fell quiet. There was a scraping, tapping, clinking sound, and Fedor dan Wetterlant emerged from the darkness.
bs: Bočna su se vrata otvorila uz odjekujući tresak. Začulo se šuškanje dok su se Lords i zastupnici okretali ne bi li vidjeli, a Folk na objema javnim galerijama naginjali se opasno daleko u svojoj žudnji da ugledaju zatvorenika. Dvorana utihnu. Začuo se zvuk struganja, kuckanja i zveckanja, a Fedor dan Wetterlant izroni iz tame.

en: “Order, my lords! Order!” bellowed the announcer. If the atmosphere had been hostile when Orso arrived, it was rapidly swinging towards outright rebellion. He had an unpleasant sensation that the wheels were already coming off his plan as it careered down a steep slope at high speed, and by no means towards a better politics. But he could hardly disembark now.
bs: — Red, gospodo! Red! zagrmi najavljivač. Ako je ozračje bilo neprijateljsko kad je Orso stigao, sada je naglo skretalo prema otvorenoj pobuni. Obuzeo ga je neugodan osjećaj da su kotači već otpadali s njegova plana dok je jurio niz strminu velikom brzinom, i to nipošto prema boljoj politici. No, teško da je sada mogao odustati.

en: In one moment, Orso’s carefully laid plans went up in flames and his hopes for a better politics sank into the depths. Now he realised why his father had always despised this place.
bs: U jednom trenutku, Orsovi pomno razrađeni planovi pretvoriše se u pepeo, a njegove nade u bolju politiku potonuše u dubine. Sada shvati zašto je njegov otac oduvijek prezirao ovo mjesto.

en: “Waste our time?” shouted Leo, lurching to his feet. Damn it, his leg hurt. It was as if he were being stabbed again and he almost fell, had to clutch the back of the bench to steady himself as the announcer struck his staff on the floor for order.
bs: — Gubiti naše vrijeme? zagrmi Leo, naglo ustajući. Kvragu, noga ga je boljela. Kao da ga ponovno bodu, zamalo se srušio, morao se uhvatiti za naslon klupe kako bi se stabilizirao dok je najavljivač udarao štapom o pod tražeći red.

en: “My father,” he bellowed, in an ever angrier and more broken voice, “always told me Union justice was the envy of the world!”
bs: — Moj otac, zagrmio je, sve ljućim i slomljenijim glasom, uvijek mi je govorio da je pravda Unije predmet zavisti cijeloga svijeta!

en: “Sit down, you bloody fool,” Savine forced through gritted teeth, gripping the rail of the gallery. But the Young Lion would not sit down.
bs: — Sjedni, prokleta budalo, procijedila je Savine kroz stisnute zube, stežući ogradu galerije. Ali Juvens Lav nije htio sjesti.

en: “Colonel Gorst,” he managed to choke out, his throat so tight he could hardly form the words. “Remove Lord Brock from the chamber.”
bs: — Pukovniče Gorst, uspio je procijediti, grla toliko stegnutog da je jedva izgovarao riječi. — Izbacite lorda Broka iz dvorane.

en: But he might as well have complained to the tide. Gorst showed no emotion as he bundled Leo from the hall, across the antechamber, then out of the Lords’ Round into the daylight. He finally set Leo down with exaggerated care beside a statue of Casamir the Steadfast, feeling much the same sense of awe and relief as he had when the sea finally washed him up on that beach near Uffrith as a boy, but with an added helping of crippling embarrassment.
bs: No mogao se žaliti i plimi, bilo bi isto. Gorst nije pokazivao emocije dok je izbacivao Lea iz dvorane, preko predvorja, pa van iz Rounda na dnevnu svjetlost. Naposljetku je Lea spustio s pretjeranom pažnjom pokraj kipa Kazimira Steadfasta, osjećajući istu onu mješavinu strahopoštovanja i olakšanja koju je osjetio kada ga je more kao dječaka izbacilo na onu plažu blizu Afrita, ali uz dodatak paralizirajuće neugode.

en: “The members of this exalted body must be exemplars,” snapped Orso, glowering at the silent lords, “held to higher standards, not lower, and subject to the same justice as any other man. The king’s justice. My justice.” And he stabbed at his chest with a finger. “There is no question in my mind of your guilt. I have given you every chance to show remorse and you have slapped my hand away. I therefore sentence you to death by hanging. Take him down.”
bs: — Članovi ovog uzvišenog tijela moraju biti uzori, odbrusi Orso, mrko gledajući šutljive lordove, "podložni višim standardima, a ne nižim, i podložni istoj pravdi kao i svaki drugi čovjek. Kraljevoj pravdi. Mojoj pravdi." I zabode prst u vlastita prsa. — Nemam nikakve dvojbe o vašoj krivnji. Pružio sam vam svaku priliku da pokažete kajanje, a vi ste mi odbili ruku. Stoga vas osuđujem na smrt vješanjem. Odvedite ga.

en: He flung the crown angrily over his shoulder and left one of his footmen juggling the damn thing, stomped out into the daylight and off towards the palace, shocked bystanders scraping out of his way, his entourage clattering after.
bs: Bijesno je prebacio krunu preko ramena i prepustio jednom od svojih sluga da žonglira tom prokletom stvari, pa odbauljao na dnevno svjetlo prema palači, dok su šokirani prolaznici uzmicali pred njim, a njegova ga je pratnja bučno slijedila.

en: “What the hell were you thinking, you thick shit?” was what she was burning to ask, but instead she stuffed her voice with concern. “Are you hurt?”
bs: — Što ti je, do vraga, bilo na umu, glupane jedan? to je ono što je gorjela od želje upitati, no umjesto toga glas joj je ispunila zabrinutošću. — Jesi li ozlijeđen?

en: “That is why you have me.” She took his elbow, one hand draped on top while the other held it firmly underneath, so she could hold him up while it looked as if she were leaning upon him, and steer him away from the Square of Marshals towards the quieter ways while it looked as if he were steering her. “This is politics.” She smiled at passers-by as if this was the most wonderful afternoon of her life. “You have to be subtle. There is a way to do things.”
bs: — Zato imaš mene. Uhvatila ga je za lakat, jednom rukom položenom odozgo, dok ga je drugom čvrsto pridržavala odozdo, kako bi ga mogla podupirati dok se činilo da se ona oslanja na njega, te ga usmjerila dalje od Trga maršala prema mirnijim prolazima, dok se činilo da on usmjerava nju. — Ovo je politika. Nasmiješila se prolaznicima kao da je ovo najljepše poslijepodne njezina života. — Moraš biti suptilan. Postoji način kako se stvari rade.

en: She smiled as they walked. The Union’s most admired couple, so very well matched and so much in love. She had smiled through far worse, after all. She kept her eyes ahead, but she was conscious that he was looking at her all the way.
bs: Smiješila se dok su hodali. Najcjenjeniji par u Uniji, tako skladni i tako zaljubljeni. Uostalom, smiješila se ona i kroz puno gore stvari. Gledala je ravno Naprijed sebe, no bila je svjesna da je on cijelim putem promatra.

en: Pain stabbed through her head and Rikke screamed, screamed so hard her voice cracked and became a breathy wheeze. A long-drawn rattle. A laugh. Stour Nightfall’s laugh, wet eyes on her as he grinned at the audience, dancing, mocking, and a golden snake was coiled around him.
bs: Bol joj probode glavu i Rike vrisne, vrisne toliko snažno da joj glas pukne i pretvori se u hrapavo šištanje. Dugo, isprekidano krkljanje. Smijeh. Smijeh Staura Najtfola, vlažnih očiju uprtih u nju dok se cerio publici, plešući, izrugujući se, a zlatna zmija bila je omotana oko njega.

en: Something pressed across her chest. Pressed so hard she could scarcely breathe, iron fingers tight across her forehead, pinprick lights burning at her. Bright lights like blazing stars in a midnight sky.
bs: Nešto joj pritisnu prsa. Pritisnu toliko snažno da je jedva disala, željezni prsti stisnuti preko njezina čela, sitne točkice svjetlosti što su je pekle. Svijetla svjetla poput plamtećih zvijezda na ponoćnom nebu.

en: “An arrow,” croaked Rikke, stirring her thick tongue in her thick lips. “From its making to its end. When it flew, I pushed it away with my finger. And a sword. And a crack in the sky.”
bs: — Strijelu, promuklo reče Rike, pomičući zadebljali jezik po zadebljalim usnama. — Od njezina nastanka do kraja. Kad je poletjela, odgurnula sam je prstom. I mač. I pukotinu na nebu.

en: She saw people at the top of a high tower beneath a bloody sunset. A line of them. A queue of them. One by one they fell. One by one they hit the ground beneath, tap, tap, tap.
bs: Vidjela je ljude na vrhu visoke kule pod krvavim zalaskom sunca. Niz njih. Povorka njih. jedan po jedan padali su. jedan po jedan udarali su o tlo ispod, tap, tap, tap.

en: “Scores have to be settled,” said Shivers, grey hair plastered to his scarred face with the rain. “But don’t expect it to feel good.” And he charged towards a gate, and men charged after him, their boots hammering on a wooden bridge, tap, tap, tap.
bs: — Dugovi se moraju naplatiti, rekao je Šivers, sijeda kosa slijepljena kišom uz njegovo ožiljcima prekriveno lice. — Ali ne očekuj da će biti ugodno. I jurnuo je prema vratima, a Folk su jurnuli za njim; njihove su čizme udarale po drvenom mostu, tap, tap, tap.

en: Hiss of more herbs on the brazier and her face stung and sweated and stung and she was so thirsty, so thirsty, her eye burned. A wolf ate the sun and a lion ate the wolf and a lamb ate the lion and an owl ate the lamb.
bs: Siktalo je još bilja na žeravniku, lice ju je peklo, znojilo se i peklo, a bila je tako žedna, tako žedna, njezino ju je Oko peklo. Vuk je pojeo sunce, a lav je pojeo vuka, i janje je pojelo lava, i sova je pojela janje.

en: Savine studied her face in the mirrors from every angle, no fewer than nine maids fluttering nervously about her: Freid with powder and brush, Metello with comb and scissors, Liddy with a mouthful of pins, May with four different colours of thread woven around her fingers. Aside from a wrinkle or two about the eyes—and unless great Euz could turn back time for her there was no help for that—she saw no opportunity for improvement.
bs: Savine je proučavala svoje lice u zrcalima iz svakog kuta, dok je oko nje nervozno lepršalo najmanje Nine sluškinja: Freid s puderom i kistom, Metelo s češljem i škarama, Lidi s ustima punim pribadača, Mej s četiri različite boje konca omotane oko prstiju. Osim pokoje borice oko očiju – a osim ako Great Euz nije mogao vratiti vrijeme unatrag, tu nije bilo pomoći – nije vidjela prostora za poboljšanje.

en: “I… never saw such a dress,” she murmured as Liddy stooped to make some tiny adjustment to Savine’s train.
bs: — Ja… nikada nisam vidjela takvu haljinu, promrmljala je dok se Lidi sagnula kako bi sitno popravila Savinin šlep.

en: “You’re so lucky. I have hardly any family left. My uncle died before I was born, on campaign in the North, then my father last year, and my mother a few months after. I never had any siblings.” Leaving her, no doubt, with quite the inheritance. Savine began to divine what made her so irresistible to Lord Isher. “I only wish one of them had lived to see this…”
bs: Savine nije bila nimalo sigurna da je odvažnost osobina koju netko najviše traži kod mladenke. Uhvatila je Isold za njezine mlohave ručice. — Ponašaj se kao da sve ide točno prema tvojim planovima. Kao da si najsamouvjerenija osoba na svijetu. Kao da nikada u životu nisi imala ni trunke sumnje." Savine je prisilno povukla ramena unatrag, podigla bradu i okrenula se prema vratima. — Meni to uspijeva.

en: And none of them were invited anyway. There had been no time to send for them. Leo had come to Adua to attend Lord Isher’s wedding and make new friends. Not to make an enemy of the king and get bloody married himself.
bs: A ionako nitko od njih nije bio pozvan. Nije bilo vremena poslati po njih. Leo je došao u Aduu kako bi prisustvovao vjenčanju lorda Išera i stekao nove prijatelje. Ne kako bi stvorio neprijatelja od kralja i sam se, kvragu, oženio.

en: No one could. The future Lady Isher was a simpering little girl by comparison, the blushing maid beside the peerless empress. Savine was doing her best not to outpace her, to hold her hand, to show her off to best advantage, but poor Isold was utterly upstaged at her own wedding.
bs: Nitko nije mogao. Buduća lady Išer bila je tek uplašena djevojčica u usporedbi s njom, rumena mladenka pored neusporedive carice. Savine se trudila ne preteći je, držati je za ruku, pokazati je u najboljem svjetlu, ali jadna Isold bila je potpuno u sjeni na vlastitoj svadbi.

en: Lady Finree dan Brock and Lady Ardee dan Glokta, mothers to one of the happy couples, glided about the gathering arm in arm, an all-conquering double act, the one imposing military precision on the serving staff, the other administering risqué anecdotes to every guest. So many different styles of laughter. Hearty guffaws and bubbling chuckles from the gentlemen. Silvery giggles and tinkling titters from the ladies.
bs: Lady Finri dan Brok i lady Ardi dan Glokta, majke jednog od sretnih parova, klizile su kroz okupljene ruku pod ruku, nepobjediv dvojac; jedna je nametala vojnu preciznost poslužnom osoblju, a druga dijelila pikantne anegdote svakom gostu. Toliko različitih stilova smijeha. Srdačni grohoti i prigušeni smijeh gospode. Srebrnasti kikot i zvonki smijeh dama.

en: Orso had spent a great deal of time pointlessly rehearsing the events of that day and, though he could prove nothing, he strongly suspected Isher had orchestrated the whole thing. To Lady Wetterlant, he blamed Orso; to Orso, he blamed Lady Wetterlant; then he teased out Leo dan Brock’s little performance and imagined he would come through greatly empowered and still everybody’s friend.
bs: Orso je proveo silno vrijeme besmisleno premlevajući događaje toga dana i, iako nije mogao dokazati ništa, snažno je sumnjao da je Išer režirao cijelu stvar. Lady Vetelant je krivio Orsa; Orsu je krivio lady Vetelant; zatim je isprovocirao malu predstavu Lea dan Broka i zamišljao da će iz svega izaći znatno osnažen, a i dalje svačiji prijatelj.

en: Their glasses chinked pleasantly together, and Orso thought about how much he would have loved to smash his in Isher’s face and grind the jagged remnant into his groin.
bs: Čaše su im se ugodno sudarile, a Orso je pomislio koliko bi volio razbiti svoju o Išerovo lice i nazubljene ostatke mu zabiti u međunožje.

en: For what her father the Arch Lector had spent on the wine today, maybe he could’ve built some better houses in Valbeck, and folk wouldn’t have been stuck in rotten cellars, and the Breakers wouldn’t have risen up, and two hundred good people wouldn’t have been hanged.
bs: Za ono što je njezin otac, Lektor, danas potrošio na vino, možda je mogao izgraditi pristojnije kuće u Valbeku, pa Folk ne bi zaglavili u trulim podrumima, Lomljači se ne bi pobunili, a dvjesto dobrih duša ne bi završilo na vješalima.

en: “All worth it, eh?” said Liddy. She was talking about the nights she’d spent stitching by candlelight, he reckoned, not the nights he’d spent beating men by lamplight.
bs: — Sve je to vrijedilo, je li tako?, reče Lidi. Mislio je da govori o noćima provedenim u šivanju uz svijeću, a ne o noćima koje je on proveo premlaćujući ljude uz svjetlost svjetiljki.

en: “Oh, Bayaz could have locked me in the House of the Maker and I’d still have found a way to attend!” She tapped him on the chest with her fan. “That’s two wonderful shows you’ve put on in the Lords’ Round.”
bs: "Oh, Bajaz me mogao zaključati u Kuću Tvorca i ja bih svejedno pronašla način da dođem!" Ljuskom lepeze lagano ga je udarila po prsima. "To su vam dva prekrasna spektakla koja ste priredili u Lords’ Roundu."

en: She left him sitting, watching his wife dance, whirl, twist, smile, flitting effortlessly from one partner to another. The sight no longer filled him with quite the same delight.
bs: Ostavila ga je da sjedi i promatra svoju ženu kako pleše, vrti se, okreće, smiješi i bez napora lebdi iz jednog partnera u drugi. Taj prizor više u njemu nije budio onako snažnu radost.

en: Savine shut the doors and leaned back against them, taking a moment to breathe. Her cheeks burned from the dancing, and the compliments, and the endless smiling, and the ever-greater quantities of pearl dust. She could hardly feel her face any more. She simply had to get some air.
bs: Savine je zatvorila vrata i naslonila se leđima na njih, uzimajući trenutak da udahne. Obrazi su joj gorjeli od plesa, komplimenata, beskrajnog osmijeha i sve veće količine bisernog praha. Jedva je više osjećala lice. Jednostavno je morala udahnuti malo svježeg zraka.

en: A silence, and she saw the side of his face twitch in the warm light from the party, and he reached up and wiped a streak of wet from his leaking left eye. “Well. A life without regrets is not a life at all. It is in the past now. I know I cast a long shadow, Savine. I am glad you are ready to step out from under it. Just… be careful.”
bs: Tišina, a ona opazi kako mu se profil trza na toplom svjetlu zabave, dok on podiže ruku i obrisa trag vlage iz svoga suznog lijevog oka. — Pa. Život bez žaljenja nije život. Sada je to prošlost. Znam da bacam dugu sjenu, Savine. Drago mi je što si spremna izaći iz nje. Samo… budi oprezna.

en: Savine raised one brow. “Valbeck may be better in the years to come. But being there while it burned was far from pleasant.”
bs: Savine podigne obrvu. — Valbek će možda biti bolji u godinama koje dolaze. No biti ondje dok je gorio bilo je daleko od ugodna iskustva.

en: But it had to be done. He was a leader, and a husband, soon to be a father. He had responsibilities. He was starting to see that humiliations came with the territory.
bs: Ali to se moralo učiniti. Bio je vođa, suprug, uskoro i otac. Imao je odgovornosti. Počeo je shvaćati da poniženja idu u paketu s tim položajem.

en: Leo felt angry colour rising to his cheeks as he limped over. “The whorehouse?” All the effort he’d put into his apology and the arrogant bastard couldn’t even be bothered to hear it?
bs: Leo osjeti kako mu gnjev navire u obraze dok je hramao prema njima. — U javnoj kući?" Sav trud koji je uložio u ispriku, a arogantni gad se nije udostojio ni saslušati ga?

en: Heugen gave a huff of upset. Barezin’s jowls wobbled in denial. Isher firmly shook his white head. “We would be acting in the king’s best interest. In the country’s best interest.”
bs: Heugen je izdao razočarani uzdah. Barezinovi obrazi zanjihali su se u znak poricanja. Išer je odlučno potresao bijelom glavom. "Mi bismo djelovali u najboljem kraljevom interesu. U interesu Countryja."

en: “Loyalists,” mused Leo, taking another drink and feeling its heat spreading. He’d always been fiercely loyal. No man more of a patriot. But what was he loyal to? A coven of greedy bureaucrats who’d sent him no help in war and only outrageous demands for tax in peace? A libertine king who’d had him thrown from the Lords’ Round and, it seemed, fucked his wife?
bs: — Lojalista, razmišljao je Leo, ispivši još jedan gutljaj i osjećajući kako mu se toplina širi po tijelu. Uvijek je bio žestoko odan. Nijedan čovjek nije bio veći domoljub od njega. Ali čemu je točno bio odan? Skupu gramzivih birokrata koji mu nisu poslali nikakvu pomoć u ratu, već samo nečuvene zahtjeve za porezom u miru? Bludnom kralju koji ga je Dow izbaciti iz Lords Rounda i, čini se, ogrebao mu ženu?

en: “He may be my father-in-law,” said Leo, “but I’m no friendlier with Old Sticks than you are. Less, if anything.”
bs: — Možda mi jest tast — odvrati Leo —, ali s Starim Štapom nisam ništa u boljim odnosima nego vi. Ni u kakvima, ako se iskreno izrazim.

en: “Good to hear.” Isher tapped at his glass with one well-shaped fingernail. “But we do not want it to come to that. Even with the Open Council and the army of Angland united, we could not be sure of victory.”
bs: — Drago mi je to čuti — reče Išer, kucnuvši prstom po čaši lijepo oblikovanim noktom. — No ne bismo željeli da do toga dođe. Čak ni s Otvorenim Vijećem i vojskom Englenda ujedinjenima, ne bismo mogli biti sigurni u pobjedu.

en: “But you could keep him on the leash!” Barezin clapped Leo on the shoulder. “And how many warriors could he call upon?”
bs: "Ali ti bi mogao držati ga na uzici!" Barezin mu stisnuo rame. "A koliko bi ratnika on mogao pozvati?"

en: “Lord Marshal Kroy?” He’d commanded the Union army at the Battle of Osrung, and died when Leo was small. He only remembered the man from stories, really. But there was undoubtedly a hint of Leo’s mother about his withering frown. “Couldn’t find one of my other grandfather?”
bs: — Lord maršal Kroy? Zapovijedao je vojskom Unije u bitci kod Osrunga i umro je kad je Leo bio dijete. Sjećao se ga samo iz priča. Ali nesumnjivo je bilo nešto od njegove majke u onom iscrpljenom mrštenju. — Nisi mogla naći nekog drugog djeda?

en: “Ah, the great minds of the Open Council.” Her total calmness was only making him angrier. It was how his mother would’ve behaved, but with more of an edge. “What did they have to discuss?”
bs: — Ah, Great umovi Otvorenog Vijeća. Njezina ga je potpuna smirenost samo još više ljutila. Tako bi se ponašala njegova majka, samo s više oštrine. — O čemu su imali raspravljati?

en: There was a long pause. Savine didn’t so much as twitch. A woman made from porcelain could have given more away. “And what did you say?”
bs: Nastala je duga stanka. Savine nije ni trepnula. Žena od porculana ne bi odala više. — A što si ti rekao?

en: Leo caught it by the wrist. “Shush.” Shock had turned to excitement, and excitement to a thrill that reached every part of him. Very slowly, very deliberately, he lifted her hand up, and let go of it.
bs: Leo joj uhvati zapešće. "Ššš." Šok se pretvorio u uzbuđenje, a uzbuđenje u trzaj koji ga je prožimao od glave do pete. Vrlo polako, vrlo namjerno, podigao joj je ruku i pustio je.

en: “You fucking worthless shit,” she hissed, ripping Leo’s trousers down around his ankles. He gave a dumb moan of excitement with every breath, shivering, trembling, wriggling up onto his elbows. He could see the whorl in her hair at the crown of her shaved head as it bobbed up and down, lapping, slurping.
bs: — Jebeni beskorisni smrdljivi kurac, zarežala je, savijajući Leove hlače oko gležnjeva. On je ispuštao glupe zvukove uzbuđenja sa svakim udahom, tresući se, drhteći, vukući se na laktove. Vidio je zavoj u njezinoj kosi na kruni obrijane glave kako se ljulja naprijed-natrag, lížući, šmrcajući.

en: “Stay…” she breathed, lips twisted around gritted teeth, “there.” She worked her hips in circles, she giving a little growl and he a little sob each time she pushed lower. Her face inched closer until her open mouth pressed against his open mouth.
bs: — Ostani… prozviždala je, usne stisnute u grimasu, tamo. Kretala je kukovima u krugovima, ona s malim ržnjavim zvukom, a on s malim jecanjem svaki put kad se spustila niže. Njezino lice se približavalo sve više, sve dok joj se otvorena usta nisu prislonila na njegova otvorena usta.

en: “Can’t see that changing,” said Yolk, filling up everyone’s glasses again. Orso really should’ve told him not to, but he was too drunk to bother.
bs: — Ne vidim da bi se to moglo promijeniti — reče Žumanj, ponovno napunivši svima čaše. Orso mu je doista trebao reći da to ne čini, ali bio je previše pijan da bi se zamarao.

en: “Daresay there are worse jobs.” Tunny gripped his pipe between his yellowed teeth as he shuffled. “Less marching than in the standard-bearing game, at least. More fighting, mind you, but at least there’s the chance of making people happy. Sure you won’t join us, Colonel Gorst?”
bs: — Rekao bih da ima i goreg posla. — Tani stisne lulu među požutjelim zubima dok je miješao karte. — Manje marširanja nego u poslu s nošenjem zastave, u svakom slučaju. Više borbe, pazi molim te, ali barem postoji prilika da učiniš ljude sretnima. Siguran si da nam se nećeš pridružiti, pukovniče Gorst?

en: “I tried to manage a compromise in which he’d get life in prison, probably to worm his way out when nobody was looking.”
bs: — Pokušao sam pronaći kompromis u kojem bi dobio doživotnu robiju, s izgledima da se izvuče kad nitko ne gleda.

en: “He’s pretty,” said Hildi, twisting her old soldier’s cap off so her blonde curls popped out in a mop, then twisting it back on.
bs: — Zgodan je — reče Hildi, skinuvši svoju staru vojničku kapu tako da joj se plave kovrče razbaruše poput čuperka, a zatim je ponovno nataknu na glavu.

en: “My Closed Council, my Open Council, the boy who empties my bloody chamber pot, too, I shouldn’t wonder, they all think I’m a fucking—”
bs: — Moje Zatvoreno vijeće, moje Otvoreno vijeće, čak i onaj dječak što mi prazni prokletu noćnu posudu, ne bih se čudio, svi misle da sam jebeni —

en: “I’ll talk to the lord chancellor and have you written into the budget, how’s that?” As the knights tramped down the stairs to leave, Orso leaned close to Tunny. “Thank you for that, Corporal.”
bs: — Razgovarat ću s lordom kancelarom i uvrstiti te u proračun, što kažeš na to? Dok su vitezovi marširali niz stube odlazeći, Orso se nagne blizu Tunnyja. — Hvala ti na tome, kaplaru.

en: “Where I can help you put them in order.” And people might care less about appearances and Zuri would not have to haul quite so savagely on the laces. “Probably best that we leave before Wetterlant’s hanging.”
bs: "Gdje ću pomoći tebi da ih središ." A Folk će možda manje mariti za pojavnosti i Zuri se neće morati toliko divljački mučiti s vezicama. — Vjerojatno je najbolje da otputujemo prije nego što Vetelant bude obješen.

en: “Angland will just have to get used to them. Haroon and Rabik are Zuri’s brothers, and they’re some of the most diligent, conscientious, trustworthy people I know. Haroon used to be an officer in the emperor’s army, I believe, and Rabik’s an absolute magus with horses. As for Zuri…” She was Savine’s closest friend, and the very thought of her being unwelcome somewhere made her want to grind that place under her heel. “She is indispensable. My business interests would suffer more without her than
bs: — Englend će se jednostavno morati naviknuti na njih. Harun i Rabik Zuričina su braća i među najmarljivijim su, najsavjesnijim i najpouzdanijim ljudima koje poznajem. Harun je, čini mi se, bio časnik u carevoj vojsci, a Rabik je pravi čarobnjak s konjima. Što se tiče Zuri… Bila je Savinina najbliža prijateljica, i sama pomisao na to da je negdje nepoželjna u njoj je budila nagon da to mjesto smrvi pod petom. — Ona je nezamjenjiva. Moji bi poslovni interesi bez nje patili više nego bez mene. Povj

en: “Wild and packed with danger. I have tales to tell which the pampered citizens of Adua will scarcely credit!” Savine certainly would not credit them, for she had it on good authority that he rarely strayed far from the harbour at Rostod and paid a scout to wear his clothes while riding across the plains so they would have an authentically adventured-in appearance on his return.
bs: "Divlja i nabijena opasnošću. Imam priča koje razmaženi građani Adue jedva da će povjerovati!" Savine im zasigurno ne bi povjerovala jer je iz pouzdanih izvora znala da rijetko napušta pristanište u Rostodu i da unajmljuje izviđača da nosi njegovu odjeću dok jaše ravnicama kako bi po povratku djelovao autentično proživljeno.

en: Leo paused with fork halfway to his mouth. “I’m twenty-two years old. I hope I’ve a few achievements still to come.”
bs: Leo zastade s vilicom na pola puta do usta. — Imam Dvadesetero dvije godine. Nadam se da me još čeka pokoji uspjeh.

en: “I am all in the subtext.” Sworbreck sat back, considering the trees in the garden as though their branches were laden with weighty revelations. “It would help if we could find our way to a place of honesty. I hope you will not think me indelicate if I suggest we might… make use of your experiences during the uprising in Valbeck?”
bs: "Ja sam sav u podtekstu." Svorbrik se zavali, promatrajući stabla u vrtu kao da im grane obiluju važnim spoznajama. "Pomoglo bi kad bismo uspjeli pronaći mjesto iskrenosti. Nadam se da nećeš pomisliti kako sam nedoličan ako predložim da bismo… mogli iskoristiti tvoja iskustva tijekom ustanka u Valbeku?"

en: “Indeed. A few etchings can truly make a pamphlet sing. Words are powerful, but an image can shortcut the reason and speak directly in the language of the heart.”
bs: — Doista. Nekoliko bakropisa doista može svaku brošuru učiniti pamtljivom. Riječi su moćne, ali slika može preskočiti razum i progovoriti izravno jezikom srca.

en: “And so we pass into the Three Farms.” Sworbreck spoke in an urgent whisper, scribbling away in his notebook. “Perhaps the most infamous of Adua’s districts, once largely burned then brutally occupied by the savage Gurkish, now rendered into an endless night… no, a perpetual dusk by the smoke of the manufactories, and a moral murk even more complete in which… what? In which the light of hope is extinguished for its thousands of wretched inhabitants. Can I find a place for the word crepuscular, d
bs: — I tako prolazimo u Tri Farme. Svorbrik progovori hitrim šapatom, žurno šarajući po bilježnici."Možda najozloglašeniji okrug Aduje, nekoć uvelike spaljen, a potom brutalno okupiran od divljih Gurkisha, sada sveden na vječnu noć… ne, u neprekidan suton dimom iz tvornica, i moralni mrak još potpuniji u kojemu… što? U kojemu je svjetlo nade ugašeno za tisuće njegovih jadnih stanovnika. Mogu li pronaći mjesto za riječ sumračan, što mislite?"

en: “No doubt. That’s a Ladderman’s tattoo on his hand, you know. First men onto the walls in a siege. Most deadly duty in the whole army. And four stars means he did it four times.” Leo glanced sideways at Broad. “That… is a dangerous man.”
bs: — Nema sumnje. Znaš, to mu je tetovaža ljestvara na ruci. Prvi Folk na zidinama pri opsadi. Najsmrtonosnija dužnost u cijeloj vojsci. A četiri zvjezdice znače da je to učinio četiri puta. Leo poprijeko pogleda Broda."To… opasan je čovjek."

en: Savine did understand it. But if she truly went to a place of honesty, all she really felt was glad she was no longer one of these wretched ghosts. All she really wanted was to get back to her palatial rooms and her conscientious servants as soon as possible. That familiar smell of sweat, piss, damp and rot, mixed with the acrid scratch of the furnaces, was hard to ignore as they worked their way deeper into the gloomy maze of streets. Strange, how smells can bring memories back so sharply. She
bs: Savine je to razumjela. No, kad bi bila posve iskrena prema sebi, osjećala je tek olakšanje što više nije jedna od tih bijednih utvara. Jedino što je željela bilo je vratiti se u svoje raskošne odaje i k svojim savjesnim slugama što je prije moguće. Poznati miris znoja, mokraće, vlage i truleži, pomiješan s oštrim, nadražujućim dimom iz peći, bilo je teško ignorirati dok su prodirali dublje u mračni labirint ulica. Čudno kako mirisi mogu tako oštro prizvati sjećanja. Shvatila je da u ruci drži k

en: They had made it to the very heart of the slum, an unpaved square with stagnant water gathered in puddles, thick with scum and blooms of multicoloured oil. A strange building stood at one side, an ancient low house with a sagging, moss-covered roof.
bs: Stigli su do samog srca sirotinjske četvrti, nepopločanog trga s lokvama ustajale vode, guste od prljavštine i šarenih mrlja ulja. s jedne strane stajala je neobična građevina, drevna niska kuća s obješenim krovom prekrivenim mahovinom.

en: “As Lady Brock moves through those darkened streets, it is as if a lamp shines. No, a beacon! Lighting the way to a better life for these neglected unfortunates. As if the sun breaks through the smoke of the manufactories. She gives out bread, yes, she gives out comfort, surely, she gives out silver with an open hand, but more valuable than all, she gives out hope.”
bs: "Dok se lady Brok kreće tim mračnim ulicama, kao da svjetiljka sja. Ne, svjetionik! Osvjetljava put prema boljem životu ovim zapuštenim nesretnicima. Kao da sunce probija dim manufaktura. Ona dijeli Hardbred, da, ona dijeli utjehu, doista, ona dijeli srebro otvorene ruke, ali vrjednije od svega, ona dijeli nadu."

en: “Who, on account of her charity… no, selflessness… on account of her remarkable charity and selflessness, has become known among the common folk of Adua, as, hmmmm…”
bs: "Tko je, na račun svoje dobrotvornosti… ne, nesebičnosti… na račun svoje iznimne dobrotvornosti i nesebičnosti, među običnim pukom Adua postala poznata kao, hmmmm…"

en: “Oh, my dear.” Sworbreck looked up wide-eyed from Carmee’s paper to Savine, holding up his hands as though framing a painting with her as its subject, that desperate orphan clinging to her feet. “You should be a writer!”
bs: "O, draga moja." Svorbrik je raširenih očiju podignuo Oko s Carmeeing papira prema Savini, podigavši ruke kao da uokviruje sliku čiji je ona motiv, dok joj se ono očajno siroče držalo za stopala. — Trebala bi biti spisateljica!

en: A scruffy little girl with a scruffy little dog gawped as she passed. The dog couldn’t take its shocked eyes off her, either. “People can get used to pretty much anything,” said Rikke.
bs: Neredna djevojčica s nerednim psićem zurela je u nju dok je prolazila. Pas Covjek također nije mogao skinuti šokirane oči s nje. — Folk se mogu naviknuti na gotovo sve, rekla je Rike.

en: There were a lot of people gathered in front of her father’s hall. There were always folk wanting something from him. Always wanting more than he had to give, whether it was silver, or men, or reassurance, or favour. They’d drained him dry of all of them, down the years.
bs: Pred dvoranom njenog oca okupilo se mnoštvo Folk. Uvijek bi bilo svetine koja bi nešto od njega tražila. Uvijek bi htjeli više nego što je mogao dati — bilo da je riječ o srebru, ljudima, utjehi ili naklonosti. S godinama su ga iscrpili do kraja.

en: “Oh, no.” Everyone watching her, silent, slipping out of her way as she walked up, like you might from someone had the plague. She stopped by the table, looking down at her father. Seemed he had the ghost of a smile about his mouth.
bs: — O, ne. — Svi su je promatrali u tišini, mičući joj se s puta dok je prolazila, kao da ima kugu. Zastala je pored stola i zagledala se u oca. Činilo se kao da mu oko usana titra sjenka osmijeha.

en: “Good point, Clover, good point.” Stour grinned his wolf grin and with a snapping of cloth pulled his wolf cloak around his shoulders. “Let’s take nothing for granted. We’ll head straight into Uffrith, pay our respects. Or the lack of ’em. Then we can talk to Oxel. See how things stand.”
bs: — Dobro zboriš, Klover, dobro zboriš. Staur se iscerio vučjim osmijehom te uz glasan prasak tkanine prebacio vučji ogrtač preko ramena. — Nemojmo ništa prepustiti slučaju. Upravit ćemo ravno u Afrit, odati počast. Ili njezin manjak. Onda možemo popričati s Okselom. Vidjeti kakvo je stanje.

en: Lots of weapons in that hall, lots of sorrow and lots of anger, and Clover made sure he knew where all the doors were. When a great man dies, those left over always take a moment working out where their loyalties are most fruitfully laid, and there’s a high risk of bloodshed in the meantime. He’d seen one funeral turn into several often enough.
bs: Mnoštvo oružja u toj dvorani, mnoštvo tuge i mnoštvo gnjeva, a Klover se pobrinuo da zna gdje su sva vrata. Kad Great čovjek umre, oni koji preostanu uvijek uzmu malo vremena da dokuče gdje će im lojalnost biti najplodonosnija, a u međuvremenu postoji visok rizik od krvoprolića. Dovoljno se puta nagledao kako se jedan sprovod pretvori u njih nekoliko.

en: Rumour was the Dogman’s daughter was a witch. That she had the Long Eye. Clover hadn’t taken it too seriously. Now it was hard to doubt. She’d turned so lean her face was like a skull, skin so stretched you fancied you could see through it, scabbed and angry around her left eye, across her forehead, her cheek, the bridge of her nose. Clover wondered if, of the two of ’em, her father looked the healthier.
bs: Glasine su govorile da je kći Psa Covjeka vještica. Da posjeduje Dugi Oko. Klover to nije preozbiljno shvaćao. Sada je bilo teško u to posumnjati. Toliko je smršavjela da joj je lice nalikovalo lubanji, koža joj je bila toliko napeta da se činilo kako se može prozreti kroz nju, izgrebana i Red oko lijevog oka, preko čela, obraza i korijena nosa. Klover se zapitao je li, od njih dvoje, njezin otac izgledao zdravije.

en: Isern-i-Phail, no doubt used to being the weirdest in just about any company, was of a sudden looking workaday by comparison. “I didn’t paddle,” she said, and spat some chagga juice across the floor.
bs: Izern-i-Fejl, zasigurno naviknuta na to da bude najčudnija u gotovo svakom društvu, odjednom je djelovala posve obično u usporedbi s njom. "Ja nisam gacala po vodi, reče i pljune malo soka od čage preko poda.

en: “Not me,” muttered Greenway, who should’ve been called Whiteway he’d turned so pale. He blundered to the door, and saw a bucket there put under a leak, and he shrank away from it, then scrambled out into the daylight. The rest of Stour’s big men weren’t far behind him. Seemed this hadn’t turned out quite the fun he’d promised.
bs: — Ja neću, promrmlja Grinvej, kojega su trebali zvati Whiteway, toliko je poblijedio. Odrinta do vrata, pa ugleda kantu podmetnutu pod mjesto gdje je curilo, trgnu se od nje, a potom odrnda van na dnevno svjetlo. Ostali Staurovi krupni Folk nisu zaostajali za njim. Činilo se da ovo nije ispalo onako zabavno kako je obećao.

en: “D’you know? I wish I could.” And it was true. He’d rather have stayed with the witches and the dead than gone back out to Stour and his bastards. “But I am what I am.” Nightfall had the power. More even than before, with the Dogman back to the mud. And Clover was done with losing sides. So he nodded to Isern-i-Phail, and nodded to Rikke, too. Then he turned for the door.
bs: — Znaš što? Volio bih da mogu. I to je bila istina. Radije bi ostao s vješticama i mrtvima nego se vratio van, Stauru i njegovim kopiladima. — Ali ja sam ono što jesam. Najtfol je imala moć. Čak i veću nego prije, sada kad se Pas Covjek vratio u blato. A Klover je završio s gubljenjem strana. Stoga kimne Izern-i-Fejl, a kimne i Rike. Zatim se okrene prema vratima.

en: They said he’d been the best of his kind. The last straight edge. Closest friend to the Bloody-Nine, worst enemy to Black Dow, who’d fought for Bethod and fought against him, across the North and back. Red Hat shouted out a story about the fight in the High Places. Oxel barked one about the Siege of Adua. Hardbread talked of the Battle of Osrung, folk murmuring with every famous name—Curnden Craw and Whirrun of Bligh and Cairm Ironhead and Glama Golden. He started at a creaky murmur, white hair
bs: Govorili su da je bio najbolji među svojima. Posljednji pravi čovjek. Najbliži prijatelj Krvavom Nineu, najgoriji neprijatelj Black Dowu, koji se borio za Bethod i protiv njega, od kraja do kraja Sjevera. Red Hat glasno je ispričao priču o borbi u Visokim Mjestima. Oksel je zagrmio o opsadi Aduje. Hardbred je pričao o bitci kod Osrunga, dok je okupljeni Folk šaputao na svako slavno ime — Curnden Craw, Virun iz Bligha, Cairm Željezna Šef i Glama Zlatna. Počeo je promuklim mrmljanjem, bijela kosa

en: “Shit,” she croaked, shaking her head at that heap of ground. She’d helped to pile it on him. There it was, dark in the grain of her hands, black under her fingernails. Still she couldn’t believe he was under there, and wouldn’t step smiling from the crowd to give the last, best word. “Fucking shit.” She took a long, salty sniff, and rubbed the wet from the blind side of her face.
bs: — Sranje, zaždala je promuklo i odmahnula glavom prema onoj hrpi zemlje. Pomogla ju je nabaciti na nju. Eto je, tamna u naborima njenih dlanova, Black ispod noktiju. Ipak nije mogla vjerovati da leži ondje, da se neće nasmijan pojaviti iz gomile i reći posljednju, najbolju riječ. — Jebeno sranje. Duboko je udahnula slankast zrak i obrisala vlagu s slijepe strane lica.

en: “By the dead, I was proud to be his daughter,” she said. “Folk can talk a lot of shit at a funeral, but even his enemies thought he was the best man in the North.” She took a damp breath and blew it out hard, her lip trembling. “That’s all I got.”
bs: — Tako mi mrtvih, ponosna sam što sam mu kći, reče. — Svatko se može nadrobiti svašta na pogrebu, ali čak su i njegovi neprijatelji smatrali da je najbolji čovjek u Sjeveru. Udahnula je vlažan zrak i snažno ga izdahnula, a usna joj je zatreperila. — To je sve što imam.

en: “Don’t take the Long Eye to see that.” Red Hat had come from the ebbing crowd to stand frowning on one side of the grave. “Stour fucking Nightfall ain’t fit to rule a shit-pit.”
bs: — Ne treba mi Dugo Oko da to vidim. Red Hat je došao iz osipajuće gomile i stao namršten s jedne strane groba. — Jebeni Staur Noćni Dausaid nije ni za što nego da vlada u septičkoj jami.

en: “My point is, you can’t lead. But there’s some who’ll listen to you, still. Out o’ respect for your father—”
bs: "Poanta je u tome što ti ne možeš voditi. Ali ima onih koji će te još uvijek slušati. Iz poštovanja prema tvom ocu —"

en: “I’m sorry about your father,” said Red Hat. “I stood second to him most of my life. I couldn’t be sorrier. But tears’ll wash no one clean, my ma used to say. The Protectorate was never going to outlive him. Oxel’s right about one thing. Folk’ll listen to you. You’d best decide which side o’ this you’re on.”
bs: — Žao mi je zbog tvoga oca, reče Hat. — Bio sam mu drugi čovjek gotovo cijeli život. Nisam mogao žaliti više. Ali suze nikoga neće oprati, govorila je moja majka. Protektorat ga nikad ne bi nadživio. Oksel je u pravu u jednom. Folk će te slušati. Najbolje bi bilo da odlučiš na kojoj si strani.

en: “Picky Rikke, eh? Ain’t long since I was choosing an eye, and now I’ve got to choose a side?” She squinted up at the sky, where the rain was slacking off. “I’ll let the earth settle on my father, then I’ll get the garden tidied, then I’ll have a little think. The moment I’ve made my choice, I’ll let you know, how’s that?”
bs: — Izbirljiva Rike, ha? Nije prošlo tako davno otkad sam birala Oko, a sad moram birati stranu? Prižmirila je prema nebu, gdje je kiša slabjela. — Pustit ću da se Country slegne na mog oca, onda ću urediti vrt, a zatim malo promisliti. Čim donesem odluku, javit ću vam, kako vam to zvuči?

en: A good question. Rikke pressed at the raw skin around her eye with her dirty fingertips. Things would be different now. Everything would be different, and her especially. She was nowhere near getting used to losing her face, and now she’d lost her father, and it looked like her home might get took away as well. “My da said you have to be realistic. My da said you want things right, you have to put ’em right yourself. My da said Uffrith would need my bones and my brains when he was gone.”
bs: — Dobar je to upit. Rike pritisne prljavim jagodicama prstiju oguljenu kožu oko svog Oka. Sada bi stvari bile drugačije. Sve bi bilo drugačije, a ponajviše ona. Ni izbliza se nije naviknula na to da je izgubila lice, a sada je izgubila i oca, dok se činilo da bi joj i dom mogao biti oduzet. — Moj je tata govorio da čovjek mora biti realan. Moj je tata govorio da, želiš li da stvari budu kako treba, moraš ih sam takvima napraviti. Moj je tata govorio da će Afrit trebati moje kosti i moju pamet ka

en: The ship’s timbers grated against the wharf and Leo took a deep breath of that good Angland air. Felt pure after the smogs of Adua. Felt honest.
bs: Brodski je trup zažezao o drvenu građu mula, a Leo udahnu duboko onaj dobri anglandski zrak. Činio se čistim nakon aduanskih magli. Činio se poštenim.

en: “You must be Lord Clensher.” She slipped gracefully forward to offer her hand. “I do like your boots, are those new?”
bs: — Vi morate biti lord Clensher. Ona graciozno istupi pružajući ruku. — Baš su vam lijepe čizme, jesu li te nove?

en: “And Lord Mustred—what a magnificent moustache—I brought you a newly printed volume on the heraldry of Angland and Starikland, do you have that one?”
bs: — I Lord Mustred — kakvih li veličanstvenih brkova — donijela sam vam novotiskani svezak o heraldici Englenda i Stariklanda, imate li već taj?

en: “I own a stake in the armoury here in Ostenhorm,” Savine was saying, “but I have never had the chance to visit. Perhaps one of you two magnates might be kind enough to show me the way?”
bs: — Posjedujem udio u ovdašnjoj oružarnici u Ostenhormu, govorila je Savine, ali nikada nisam imala priliku posjetiti je. Možda bi netko od vas dvojice velikaša bio toliko ljubazan da mi pokaže put?

en: The leg was still sore, but he was learning how to manage it. He’d strapped a belt around it under his trousers, just above the knee. Made it stiffer, but a lot more solid. Jurand tried to circle but Leo watched, waited, forced him to circle back the other way. He’d had to change his style. Far less aggression. Much more patience.
bs: Noga ga je još boljela, ali učio se nositi s tim. Svezao je remen oko nje ispod hlača, neposredno iznad koljena. Ukočilo ju je, ali učinilo mnogo čvršćom. Džurand je pokušao kružiti, no Leo je motrio, čekao i prisilio ga da se vrati u suprotnom smjeru. Morao je promijeniti stil. Mnogo manje agresije. Puno više strpljenja.

en: They all laughed, but they’d no idea how right they were. Leo thought Savine might’ve loosened one of his teeth last night.
bs: Svi su se nasmijali, ali nisu imali pojma koliko su u pravu. Leo pomisli kako mu je Savine sinoć možda olabavila jedan zub.

en: “Next time you will be,” said Leo, putting a hand on his shoulder. “We can’t let the bastards get away with it. There comes a point when talking about a better world just isn’t enough. When good men have to bloody stand up and fight for it!”
bs: — Sljedeći put hoćeš, reče Leo, spustivši mu ruku na rame. "Ne možemo dopustiti da se kopiladi to izvuče. Dođe trenutak kada pričanje o boljem svijetu jednostavno nije dovoljno. Kada dobri Folk moraju jebeno ustati i boriti se za nj!"

en: “They brought the fight to us!” snapped Leo, and Antaup gave a grunt of agreement. “They left us to die in their war.” And Jin gave a growl of support. “They made us pay for their war.” Glaward nodded along harder with each point. “They’re bleeding us white with their taxes.” As Leo convinced them, he convinced himself. “They’re hanging our friends. They’re shitting on our most solemn principles!”
bs: — Oni su donijeli borbu nama! odbrusi Leo, a Antaup ispusti gunđanje odobravanja. — Ostavili su nas da umremo u njihovom ratu. I Jin prozuji u znak potpore. "Natjerali su nas da platimo njihov rat." Glavard je klimao glavom uz svaku točku sve snažnije. — Cjede nas do gole kože svojim porezima. Dok ih je Leo uvjeravao, uvjeravao je i samog sebe. — Vješaju naše prijatelje. Sere im se na naša najsvetija načela!

en: Savine walked down the echoing hallway, shaking her head. “This building. It feels more like a prison than a palace.”
bs: Savine je koračala odzvanjajućim hodnikom i odmahnula glavom. — Ova zgrada. Više sliči na zatvor nego na palaču.

en: Nowhere was that more obvious than in the so-called governing council. It might better have been called the grumbling council, since the old men around the monstrous table in the cavernous hall treated every point of business as a problem to be avoided in the most tedious way imaginable.
bs: Nigdje to nije bilo očiglednije nego u takozvanom upravnom vijeću. Primjerenije bi bilo nazvati ga vijećem gunđala, budući da su starci oko monstruoznog stola u prostranoj dvorani svaku točku dnevnog reda tretirali kao Trobli koji treba izbjeći na najdosadniji mogući način.

en: Leo bashed the table with his fist, making everyone flinch. “I’ve made my decision! I didn’t ask for your advice, Mother.”
bs: Leo je šakom udario po stolu, natjeravši sve da se trgnu. — Donio sam odluku! Nisam tražio vaš Vijeće, majko.

en: “With your kind permission, I would meet with some interested parties—owners of land, mines and mills, operators of penal colonies—with a view to raising more taxes.” She gave Leo’s shoulder the gentlest of reassuring touches. “I am confident you will be pleasantly surprised.”
bs: — Uz vaše ljubazno dopuštenje, sastala bih se s nekim zainteresiranim strankama – vlasnicima zemljišta, rudnika i mlinova, upraviteljima kažljeničkih kolonija – s namjerom da prikupimo više poreza. Ona nježno dotaknu Leovo rame u znak ohrabrenja. — Uvjerena sam da ćete biti ugodno iznenađeni.

en: “You and your investors in the coal, iron and copper mines of Angland are making great profits,” said Savine. “I know because Selest dan Heugen never stops boasting about it.”
bs: — Ti i tvoji ulagači u rudnike ugljena, željeza i bakra u Englendu ostvaruju velike dobiti, dometnu Savine. — Znam to jer Selest dan Heugen ne prestaje se hvaliti time.

en: “Token amounts, as we both know,” said Savine. “We have gone over the books, Master Arinhorm. I get the feeling that the worthy old gentlemen who have been in charge of Angland’s government do not fully understand the books. But we do. And we see all kinds of ways to make things more… equitable. Ways for the industries of the province to contribute to the common good.”
bs: — Simbolične iznose, kao što oboje znamo, reče Savine. — Pregledali smo knjige, majstore Arinhorme. Stekla sam dojam da ti časni stari gospodinji koji su upravljali Englendovom vlasti ne razumiju posve te knjige. Ali mi ih razumijemo. I vidimo svakojake načine da stvari učinimo… pravednijima. Načine na koje industrije ove provincije mogu pridonijeti općem dobru.

en: “There,” said Savine. “Doesn’t that sound better? Something we can all take pride in. You will also fit your pumps to my mines at your own expense. Then we can allow you to operate.”
bs: — Eto, reče Savine. — Zar to ne zvuči bolje? Nešto na što svi možemo biti ponosni. O svom ćete trošku također ugraditi pumpe u moje rudnike. Tek vam tada možemo dopustiti rad.

en: Arinhorm wobbled to his feet, but he had nothing to say. Savine had made sure of that. All he could do was turn on his heel and stalk from the room.
bs: Arinhorm se teturajući pridigne na noge, ali nije imao što reći. Savine se pobrinula za to. Jedino što je mogao učiniti jest okrenuti se na peti i izmarširati iz prostorije.

en: He slumped ever more sourly into his gilded chair. “I doomed us to this when I looked for a compromise. When I tried to do the right thing.”
bs: Još se mrzovoljnije otkotrljao u svoju pozlaćenu stolicu. — Osudio sam nas na ovo kad sam tražio kompromis. Kad sam pokušao postupiti ispravno.

en: She gripped his wrist with a sudden strength, immaculately manicured nails digging into him. “You are my son, too! So smile. And contemplate your revenge.”
bs: Stegnula mu je zglob iznenadnom snagom, a pomno uređeni nokti zarezali su mu se u meso."I ti si moj Filio! Zato se nasmiješi. I razmišljaj o osveti."

en: Something hit one of the executioners in the face and he stumbled back, catching the lever with his elbow. The trapdoor fell open but Wetterlant wasn’t quite in position. He gave a muffled cry as one of his legs dropped, but his other foot stayed on the scaffold and he ended up halfway through, twisting and jerking with his knee trapped under his chin and the rope almost but not quite taut.
bs: Nešto je pogodilo jednog od krvnika u lice te je posrnuo unatrag i laktom zakačio polugu. Vrata su se otvorila, ali Vetelant nije bio posve na mjestu. Prigušeno je jecnuo kad mu je jedna noga propala, ali mu je drugo stopalo ostalo na vješalima te je završio napola propao, koprcajući se i trzajući s koljenom priklještenim pod bradom i užetom koje je bilo gotovo, ali ne sasvim zategnuto.

en: People were throwing things at the nobles’ enclosure now. Not only fruit but coins. Stones. Orso heard a bottle shatter. He saw someone stumbling from their seat with blood on their face.
bs: Folk su sada počeli bacati stvari na plemićku ložu. Ne samo voće nego i kovanice. Kamenje. Orso je čuo kako se razbila boca. Vidio je nekoga kako tetura sa sjedala, lica oblivenog krvlju.

en: He definitely heard a scream of, “Fuck the Young Lamb!” Black-clothed Practicals were shoving through the press, laying about them with sticks and fists, dragging struggling figures from the chaos. Orso saw a group of men break through the line of soldiers and go sprawling at the foot of the scaffold, punching and wrestling. Gorst loomed up, shielding Orso and his mother with his armoured body.
bs: Definitivno je čuo vrisak: — Jebo Mlađahnog Janjca!" Praktičari odjeveni u crno probijali su se kroz tjesnac, mlatarajući štapovima i šakama te vukući izbezumljene prilike iz općeg kaosa. Orso je ugledao skupinu muškaraca kako se probija kroz vojni kordon i ruši u podnožje vješala, udarajući i rvući se. Gorst se nadvio nad njima, štiteći Orsa i njegovu majku svojim oklopljenim tijelom.

en: “And up till now it’s been little choices for me.” Rikke tossed her scissors down and crossed her legs. “What song to sing or how short to trim my toenails or which eye to have pricked out o’ my head.”
bs: — I sve do sada za mene su to bili mali izbori. Rike baci škare na pod i prekrsti noge. — Pjesmu koju treba zapjevati, ili koliko podrezati nokte na nogama, ili koje mi oko valja iščupati iz glave.

en: “Time-tested traditions!” Rikke wagged a finger at the old men like they’d strayed from the pasture and she was there to play shepherd. “My father always used to say, you want things right, you have to put ’em right yourself. No better way to settle a difference of opinion…” And she made a ring with her finger and thumb and peered at ’em through it with the one eye that still could. “Than in the Circle!”
bs: — Tradicije provjerene vremenom!
