Rike zaprijeti prstom starcima kao da su zalutali s pašnjaka, a ona je tu da glumi pastira. — Moj otac je uvijek govorio, želiš li da stvari budu kako treba, moraš ih sam postaviti na svoje mjesto. Nema boljeg načina da se riješi razlika u mišljenju… I napravi prsten od kažiprsta i palca te ih promotri kroz njega onim jedinim okom koje je još moglo. — Negoli u krugu!

en: No one disagreed with that. How could they? Hardbread wearily sagged. “I reckon. If neither o’ you twain back down.”
bs: Nitko se nije usprotivio tome. Kako bi i mogao? Hardbred klonu u svom sjedištu. — mislim da. Ako se nijedan od vas dvojice ne povuče.

en: “Shields for the rest o’ you, then!” cried Isern, clapping her hands. “And into the Circle with our two grey champions!”
bs: — A vi ostali primite se štitova! povika Izern plješćući rukama. — I u Round s našim dvama sijedim divovima!

en: She pulled the old sheepskin tight around her shoulders. Still smelled like him, somehow. She wished for a moment he could be woken, and thought of him striding in to see what all the fuss was about. Thought of him smiling at her the way he used to, like she was the most precious thing he had. The most precious thing there was. Then she wondered if he would smile, when he saw her blinded eye and the runes on her face. Wondered if he’d have stared, fearful and queasy like everyone else. The thoug
bs: Čvrsto je ogrnula staru ovčju kožu oko ramena. Nekako je još uvijek mirisala po njemu. Poželjela je na tren probuditi ga, zamišljajući kako korača unutra da vidi oko čega se diže tolika guka. Sjetila se kako bi joj se osmjehnuo onako kako je znao, kao da je najdragocjenija stvar koju ima. Najdragocjenija stvar na svijetu. Zatim se zapitala bi li joj se osmjehnuo kad bi ugledao njezino slijepo oko i rune na njezinu licu. Zapitala se bi li zreno u nju, uplašen i zgrčen poput svih ostalih. Zbog te

en: Oxel’s men sent up a great cheer. Red Hat’s drooped, sullen and silent. Rikke had always liked Red Hat. He’d laughed at her jokes when she was a girl. He’d talked with her father into the night, firelight on their lined faces. And out of joining the Union or joining the North, she reckoned his had been much the better idea. But someone had to steer Uffrith now, and it couldn’t be him.
bs: Okselovi Folk provalili su u silan kliktaj. Hatovi su klonuli, potišteni i nijemi. Rike je oduvijek voljela Hata. Smijao se njezinim šalama dok je bila djevojčica. Razgovarao je s njezinim ocem do kasno u noć, dok je svjetlost vatre obasjavala njihova izborana lica. I između pridruživanja Uniji ili pridruživanja Sjeveru, držala je da je njegova ideja bila puno bolja. No netko je sada morao voditi Afrit, a to nije mogao biti on.

en: A mutter went through the watching men. Oxel’s men, and Red Hat’s, and Hardbread’s, and the rest. Fear, and anger, and excitement, too. The Bloody-Nine was the worst man in the world to find yourself in the Circle with. But Caul Shivers came a close second.
bs: Mrmljanje prostruji među promatračima. Okselovim ljudima, i Hatovima, i Hardbredovima, i svima ostalima. Strah, bijes, a bogme i uzbuđenje. Krvava Devetka bio je najgori čovjek s kojim se možeš naći u krugu. No Caul Šivers bio je odmah iza njega.

en: Oxel came on, feinted low but swung high. Rikke gasped, sure he’d caught Shivers in the face, knowing the future of Uffrith, not to mention her own, was hanging by a thread. But Shivers whipped back from the waist at the last moment, let the blade whistle past his nose, let Oxel stumble after it.
bs: Oksel navali, izvede nisku varku, ali zamahnu visoko. Rike uzdahnu, uvjerena da mu je uhvatio lice, znajući da budućnost Afrita, da njezinu i ne spominjemo, visi o koncu. No Šivers se u posljednji tren izvi u struku, pustivši oštricu da mu prozuji pokraj nosa, dopustivši Okselu da posrne za njom.

en: Shivers’ sword pinged as it took Oxel’s head off and sent it bouncing across the circle. One of Red Hat’s shield-carriers jumped out of the way to let it roll past. Shivers turned to Oxel’s men as their chief’s body flopped sideways. He didn’t roar in triumph or throw his arms up in victory or bellow insults. Just looked at ’em, like he was making an offer, and wasn’t much bothered either way whether anyone took him up on it.
bs: Šiversov mač zazveketnu dok mu je odsjekao glavu i poslao je da poskakuje preko kruga. Jedna od štitonoša Red Hat odskočila je u stranu kako bi propustila glavu da se otkotrlja. Šivers se okrenuo prema Okselovim ljudima dok se tijelo njihovog poglavara stropoštalo u stranu. Nije rizao od trijumfa, niti je bacao ruke u pobjedi, niti je urlao uvrede. Samo ih je promatrao, kao da daje ponudu, a bilo mu je posve svejedno hoće li je tko prihvatiti.

en: “What happens now?” muttered Hardbread, staring at the two corpses and clutching at his sparse white hair.
bs: — Što će se sad dogoditi? promrmlja Hardbred, zagledan u dva leša dok se hvatao za rijetku bijelu kosu.

en: “The Magus Radierus, at your service!” No doubt he sounded the part, making quite the meal from every “r” passed through his mouth, and he looked the part, too. Robe with all sorts of gold thread in it, and a big long beard forked and streaked with white, and a twisted staff with a sort of crystal on the end.
bs: —— Magus Radierus, na usluzi! Zvučao je i više nego uvjerljivo, naglašavajući svako slovo "r" koje bi mu prevrnuo preko usana, a tako je i izgledao. Odora protkana zlatnim nitima sa svih strana, duga, račvasta brada išarana bijelim pramenovima i zavinut Sticks s nekakvim kristalom na vrhu.

en: Stour, it seemed, did not agree. He narrowed his eyes the way he did when someone was about to get hurt, which wasn’t rarely. “I heard tell you could disappear.”
bs: Staur se, kako se činilo, nije slagao s tim. Suzio je oči onako kako bi to činio kad je netko trebao nastradati, što se događalo prilično često. — Čuo sam da možeš nestati.

en: Black Calder gave a great scornful snort as Radierus was dragged out, making Stour frown over. “Something tickling you, Father?”
bs: Black Kalder prezrivo i glasno udahnu kroz nos dok su Radierusa vukli van, natjeravši Staura da se namršti prema njemu. — Je li te nešto zagolicalo, Oče?

en: Greenway was marching the next magician in, and she looked a lot less promising than the last. A sturdy woman with a ragged dress and dirty bare feet who couldn’t tear her big round eyes away from the cage in the corner. Gregun Hollowhead wasn’t in it any more. His head was rotting on a spike over the gates of Carleon. But one of his Named Men had come to complain about it so the cage had a new guest, starved and battered, one scabbed leg dangling from the bottom and nearly scraping the sticky s
bs: Grinvej je uvodio sljedeću čarobnicu, a ona je izgledala mnogo beznadnije od prethodne. Krupan stas, poderana haljina i prljava bosa stopala, a krupne okrugle oči nije mogla odvojiti od kaveza u kutu. Gregun Šupljoglav više nije bio u njemu. Šef mu je trulila na kolcu iznad gradskih vrata Carleona. No jedan od njegovih prisegaćenih ratnika došao se žaliti na to, pa je kavez dobio novu stanarku, izgladnjelu i izmlaćenu, s jednom krastavom nogom koja je visjela s dna i umalo grepstila ljepljivo ka

en: “The Dogman’s daughter?” Seff from up near Yaws nervously licked her lips. “I heard she’s got the Long Eye. Got it real and true, like back in the Old Time. Heard she can see what a man’s thinking. Heard she can stay dry in the rain ’cause she knows where all the drops’ll fall. Heard she’s got everything that’ll happen written in a golden book and all she has to do is look it up so—”
bs: — Kći Psa Čovjeka? Seff iz kraja kod Javsa nervozno oblaže usne. — Čula sam da ima Dugo Oko. Baš pravo, zbilja, kao u Staro vrijeme. Čula sam da može vidjeti što čovjek misli. Čula sam da može ostati suha na kiši jer zna kamo će svaka kap pasti. Čula sam da ima zapisano sve što će se dogoditi u nekoj zlatnoj knjizi i samo treba potražiti pa —

en: “Give this girl a coin and send her back to her children, eh?” Stour patted her face and wiped some of the tears away with his thumb. “You tried, didn’t you? That’s all I can ask. You see anything, you let me know, eh?”
bs: — Daj ovoj curi novčić i pošalji je natrag djeci, ha? Staur joj pomilova lice pa palcem obrisa pokoju suzu. — Trudila si se, zar ne? To je sve što mogu tražiti. Bilo što vidiš, javi mi, ha?

en: “Rikke tricked him into it!” squealed Dancer. Before Clover saw her with the runes on her face, he would’ve laughed at that. But he wasn’t laughing now. No one was. Specially not Dancer. “Well, she tricked him and Red Hat into it, then Oxel killed Red Hat, then Shivers killed—”
bs: — Rike ga je prevarila! zacvilio je Danser. Prije negoli ju je Klover ugledao s runama na licu, tomu bi se nasmijao. No sada se nije smijao. Nitko nije. Ponajmanje Danser."Pa, prevarila je njega i Red Hat, onda je Oksel ubio Red Hat, onda je Šivers ubioj — "

en: Snakes have no friends. It made Savine wonder what Isher was really up to. Most of Angland’s serious business was done here in the Lady’s Chamber these days, between Savine and a few chosen people, on its carefully curated furniture in the light of its new, thoroughly modern windows. But just this once she would much rather have been on the other side of the connecting door, in the panelled gloom of the Lord’s Chamber, puzzling out how exactly Isold’s husband meant to take advantage of hers. She
bs: Zmije nemaju prijatelje. Zbog toga se Savine zapitala što Išer zapravo smjera. Većina ozbiljnih poslova u Englendu obavljala se ovih dana ovdje, u Gospodinoj odaji, između Savine i nekoliko odabranih Folk, na brižno odabranom namještaju pod svjetlom njezinih novih, posve modernih prozora. No, barem ovog puta radije bi bila nasuprot tome veznih vrata, u obloženoj tami Gospodareve odaje, razbijajući glavu oko toga kako točno Isoldin muž namjerava iskoristiti njezina. Nikada nije vidjela Lea tako u

en: “Really?” Isold was tepid but Savine had hoped to pick up some more gossip. She had relished the challenge of taking charge in Ostenhorm, but now she was undisputed mistress here she was teetering on the edge of boredom. She missed being at the heart of things. She missed the rush of the gamble and the thrill of the win. She missed her friends, her acquaintances, even her enemies. Her enemies most of all, perhaps. “It’s barely even dusk.”
bs: — Stvarno? Isold je bila mlaka, ali Savine se nadala doznati još pokoji trač. Uživala je u izazovu preuzimanja uzda u Ostenhormu, no sada kad je ovdje bila neprikosnovena gospa, ljuljala se na rubu dosade. Nedostajalo joj je biti u središtu zbivanja. Nedostajali su joj navala kocke i uzbuđenje pobjede. Nedostajali su joj prijatelji, poznanici, čak i neprijatelji. Neprijatelji možda ponajviše. — Jedva da se smračilo.

en: “Fifteen of us committed now,” came Isher’s voice, “but we must move with the utmost care. There are laws restricting the raising of private armies, and we cannot risk making Old Sticks suspicious.”
bs: — Petnaestorica su nam se sada obvezala, dopre Išerov glas, "ali moramo postupati krajnje oprezno. Postoje zakoni koji ograničavaju podizanje privatnih vojski, a ne smijemo riskirati da probudimo sumnju starog Hat-a.

en: Do nothing? Retire to bed like Isold and pretend she never heard? Sit back like the good wife and let Leo manage their affairs?
bs: Ne učiniti ništa? Povući se u krevet poput Isold i praviti se da ništa nije čula? Pustiti mozak na pašu poput poslušne supruge i prepustiti Leu da upravlja njihovim životima?

en: It was a risk. An awful risk. Yet she could not help but think of all there might be to gain. No less than everything, if she played her hand well… The Closed Council had made many enemies, within the Union’s borders and without. Had her father not often listed them, discussed with her their fears and desires, their strengths and weaknesses? If they all could be brought together, pushed in the same direction at the same moment… It would take a delicate touch. Something Leo by no means had.
bs: Bio je to rizik. Strašan rizik. Ipak, nije mogla pobjeći od pomisli na sve što bi se moglo dobiti. Ništa manje nego sve, ako odigra svoje karte kako treba… Zatvoreno Vijeće stvorilo je mnoge neprijatelje, unutar granica Unije i izvan njih. Zar ih njezin otac nije često nabrajao, raspravljao s njom o njihovim strahovima i željama, njihovim prednostima i manama? Kad bi se svi oni mogli okupiti i pogurnuti u istom smjeru u isto vrijeme… Za to bi bila potrebna suptilna ruka. Nešto čime Leo definitiv

en: “The two of you plan to risk everything you have. Therefore, you plan to risk everything I have. My future. The future of my child. It is clear you have already taken several steps along this path. Too far to turn back without considerable danger. Perhaps too far to turn back at all. So. It seems you have left me no choice but to commit myself to this project and do everything possible to make sure it succeeds.” She raised her chin. “But if you think I would ever do so without voicing my opinion
bs: "Vas dvojica planirate riskirati sve što imate. Samim tim, planirate riskirati sve što ja imam. Moju budućnost. Budućnost mog djeteta. Jasno je da ste već poduzeli nekoliko koraka na tom putu. Predaleko da biste se vratili bez znatne opasnosti. Možda predaleko da se uopće vratite. Dakle. izgleda da mi niste ostavili drugog izbora nego da se posvetim ovom projektu i učinim sve što je moguće kako bih osigurala njegov uspjeh." Podigla je bradu. — No, ako mislite da bih ikada učinila tako što bez iz

en: “He’s no politician, either. Only see what happened at Wetterlant’s trial.” Isher gave a disgusted sneer. “The man’s a fool.”
bs: — Nije ni političar. Samo pogledaj što se dogodilo na Vetelantovu suđenju. Išer prezrivo savije usne u gađenju. — Čovjek je budala.

en: “The Breakers?” Leo looked almost as astonished as the stuffed stag’s head over his shoulder. “They’re traitors!”
bs: — Lomljači? Leo je izgledao gotovo jednako zapanjeno kao i prepunjena jelenja Šef iznad njegova ramena. — Oni su izdajnici!

en: “No. But I understand King Jappo is keen to step from his mother’s shadow… I might be able to arrange a meeting with him directly.”
bs: — Ne. Ali shvaćam da je kralj Džapo željan iskoračiti iz majčine sjene… Možda uspijem dogovoriti sastanak s njim osobno.

en: “If looking unpatriotic worries you, then consider how being hanged for treason looks.” Savine put some iron into her voice. “This is not a game. We must be utterly committed. Fail and we are doomed.”
bs: — Ako te brine to što djelujemo nepatriotički, razmisli samo kako izgleda kad te objese zbog veleizdaje. Savine unese čvrstinu u glas."Ovo nije igra. Moramo biti posve posvećeni. Podbacimo li, propast nam ne gine."

en: “Who do you imagine will be king when this is over?” Savine arranged herself again in her chair and coolly met his eye.
bs: — Tko po tvom mišljenju treba biti kralj kad sve ovo završi? Savine se ponovno namjesti u stolici i hladno ga pogleda u oči.

en: “Even so. In the army of Angland, we supply the best and most experienced soldiers you could hope for. In Stour Nightfall, we bring a decisive ally. Would you agree?”
bs: — Pa ipak. U vojsci Englenda osiguravamo najbolje i najiskusnije vojnike koje možete poželjeti. Sa Staurom Najtfolom dovodimo odlučujućeg saveznika. Slažeš li se?

en: Lord Isher narrowed his eyes at his glass, swirled the spirit around in it, then looked up at her. She had taken him on quite a journey that evening. From scornful, to thoughtful, to impressed, through admiration, suspicion and, finally, to acceptance. An acquaintance, romance and estrangement all in one sitting. “Your terms are acceptable.”
bs: Lord Išer suzi oči prema svojoj čaši, promoči žestoko piće u njoj, a potom pogleda u nju. Te ga je večeri povela na prilično putovanje. Od prezira, preko zamišljenosti i impresioniranosti, do divljenja, sumnjičavosti i naposljetku prihvaćanja. Poznanstvo, romansa i udaljavanje u jednoj jedinoj večeri. — Vaši su uvjeti prihvatljivi.

en: “Might we talk for a moment?” she asked, like they were two old friends who never got the chance to catch up. She had that glow about her, now, that women can get when they’re expecting. Broad remembered that glow on Liddy, when she was pregnant with May. Long time ago, when he had all his hopes intact.
bs: — Biste li mogli na trenutak porazgovarati? upita ona, kao da su dvoje starih prijatelja koji se nikako ne stignu ispričati. Obasjavao ju je onaj poseban sjaj koji žene znaju imati kada su trudne. Brod se prisjetio tog sjaja na Lidi dok je bila trudna s Mej. Davno prije, dok su sve njegove nade još bile čitave.

en: “Of course you did. Is there any possibility, do you think…” And she looked up at him from under her eyelashes. “That you could get in touch with them again?”
bs: — da jesi. Misliš li da postoji ikakva mogućnost… Podigla je Oko prema njemu ispod trepavica. — Da nekako ponovo stupiš u kontakt s njima?

en: May watched him from the doorway, one hand fiddling with the silver necklace she wore these days. “It’s nothing dangerous, is it?”
bs: Mej ga je promatrala s vrata, a jednom se rukom igrala srebrne ogrlice koju je tih dana nosila. — Nije to ništa opasno, zar ne?

en: “I’m doing my bloody best,” said Leo. She rode well. What didn’t she do well? Perched elegantly side-saddle with her whip-hand resting on the slight swell of her belly, steering her horse with the same effortless confidence she steered everything else. But he still worried. “Sure you don’t want to go in the carriage, though?”
bs: — Dajem sve od sebe, prokletstvo, reče Leo. Jahala je odlično. Što ona to nije radila odlično? Sjedjela je elegantno bočno, s rukom u kojoj je držala bič oslonjenom na jedva primjetnu oblinu trbuha, upravljajući konjem s istim onim ležernim samopouzdanjem s kojim je upravljala svime ostalim. Ipak, on se i dalje brinuo. — Pa ipak, sigurna si da ne želiš u kočiju?

en: He felt hugely excited, of course. They were on a grand adventure, of course. And doing the right thing, of course. It was just that he also, sometimes, in quiet moments, felt strangely horrified. But there was no way back now. He’d look an utter fool. And once Savine got her teeth into a thing, it was happening, and that was all there was to it.
bs: Osjećao se silno uzbuđeno. Bili su u velikoj pustolovini. I radili su pravu stvar. Samo što bi ga ponekad, u tihim trenucima, obuzeo i čudan osjećaj užasa. No sada više nije bilo povratka. Ispao bi običan idiot. A jednom kad bi Savine zabila zube u nešto, to se i ostvarilo i tu nije bilo pomoći.

en: “And then I begged for her help and loaded her down with enough work on the new tax system to keep five clever people busy. What your mother wants second most in the world is to feel useful.”
bs: "A onda sam je zamolila za pomoć i natovarila je s dovoljno posla oko novog poreznog sustava da zaposlim petoricu pametnih Folk. Ono što tvoja majka želi drugo po važnosti na svijetu jest osjećati se korisnom."

en: “Good old Uffrith!” He took a long breath of that familiar air. Sheep, dung, woodsmoke and sea salt, but sweet with happy memories for him. “I spent the best years of my childhood here. I know every alley of the place!”
bs: — Stari dobri Afrit! Duboko udahnu onaj poznati zrak. Ovce, gnoj, miris paljevine i morske soli, ali prožet dragim uspomenama koje su mu grijale srce. — Ovdje sam proveo najbolje godine djetinjstva. Poznajem svaki kutak ovoga mjesta!

en: “Leo! Savine! I’ve missed you.” And Rikke swaggered from the shadows, arms spread wide, dangling with bracelets and thongs and charms, into the shaft of light from the smoke-hole.
bs: — Leo! Savine! Nedostajali ste mi. I Rike samouvjereno istupi iz sjene raširenih ruku, ovješena narukvicama, remenjem i amajlijama, ravno u snop svjetlosti što je dopirao iz otvora za dim.

en: “Could I look closer?” asked Savine, stepping towards her, not put off in the least. “I have seen a very great number of painted faces, but never such fine work.” And she put a finger under Rikke’s chin and tipped her face gently into the light. “I think it’s beautiful.” And she traced the lines of the tattoo with her fingertips. “It could not be more… you.”
bs: — Mogu li pogledati bliže? upita Savine, koračajući prema njoj, nimalo posramljena. — Vidjela sam jako velik broj našaranih lica, ali nikad ovako finog rada. I stavi prst pod Rikinu bradu te joj nježno nagne lice prema svjetlu. — Mislim da je predivno. I prstima prijeđe preko linija tetovaže. — Ne bi moglo biti više… ti.

en: “Is it?” Rikke narrowed her eyes, then slid them, sly as a cat, towards Savine. “Sure you aren’t hers?”
bs: — Je li? Rike suzi oči, a zatim ih, lukava poput mačke, okrenu prema Savine. — Sigurna da nisi ti njezina?

en: Leo tried to smile, but it wasn’t easy. Every time he saw a hint of that gangly girl he’d played hide and seek with in this very hall, she’d flash that sly smile, and turn that strange left eye on him, and he’d feel as if she was looking right into him. Right through him. The woman he’d known was vanished, sure as her father, and he was shocked at how much he missed them.
bs: Leo se pokuša nasmiješiti, ali nije išlo. Svaki put kad bi spazio i natruhu one mršave djevojke s kojom se igrao skrivača upravo u ovoj dvorani, ona bi ga počastila onim lukavim osmijehom, okrenula prema njemu svoje čudno lijevo oko i u njemu bi se rodio osjećaj kao da mu se zavlači pod kožu. Kao da gleda kroz njega. Žena koju je poznavao iščezla je, pouzdano baš poput njezina oca, a on je bio zaprepašten koliko su mu nedostajali.

en: “Naught my father wouldn’t have done for an old friend. And we go way back, eh? Used to wrestle on this very floor, didn’t we? What do you need?”
bs: — Ništa što moj otac ne bi učinio za starog prijatelja. A nas dvoje vučemo dugu povijest, zar ne? Znali smo se rvati na ovom istom podu, zar ne? Što trebaš?

en: “To beg for the Great Wolf’s help.” Rikke bared her teeth and snarled at him with sudden, shocking fury. “The man who burned half this city on a whim? Who promised to send my guts to my father in a box? Who killed my friends and yours? Who’d have killed you, if my Long Eye hadn’t seen it coming? Break what they love, he said. You’d have me link arms with my worst enemy?”
bs: — Moliti Velikoga Vuka za pomoć? Rike ogoli zube i zaurla na nj s iznenadnim, potresnim bijesom. — Čovjeka koji je zapalio pola ovoga grada iz hire? Koji je obećao poslati moje utrobe mom ocu u kutiji? Koji je pobio moje i tvoje prijatelje? Koji bi ubio tebe da moje Oko nije vidjelo što se sprema? Slomi ono što vole, govorio je. Zar bi htjela da se ruku pod ruku združim sa svojim najgorim neprijateljem?

en: He held up his hands before things got any worse. “We’re friends! I risked my life for you. For Uffrith.” He grimaced as he shifted his leg. “I’ve got the scars. But I’d do the same again. I helped you against your enemies. I’m asking you to help me against mine.”
bs: Podignu ruke prije nego što stvari postanu još gore. — Mi smo prijatelji! Riskirao sam život radi tebe. Radi Afrita." Namrgodi se pomaknuvši nogu. — Nosim ožiljke. Ali učinio bih isto ponovno. Pomogao sam ti protiv tvojih neprijatelja. Sad ja tražim od tebe da pomogneš meni protiv mojih.

en: She still wasn’t used to sleeping in her father’s bed, but it made her feel close to him, even though he was gone. And when you’re left the best bed in the North, what should you do, sleep on the floor?
bs: Još se nije naviknula spavati u očevu krevetu, ali zbog njega se osjećala bliskom s njim, premda je otišao. A kad ti ostave najbolji krevet na Sjeveru, što bi trebala učiniti, spavati na podu?

en: Savine considered her, eyes narrowed against the low sun, then she took Rikke’s hand and guided it to her stomach.
bs: Savine ju je odmjerila pogledom, suzivši oči pred niskim suncem, a onda uzela Rikinu ruku i navela je na svoj trbuh.

en: “Aye.” And Rikke frowned towards her father’s grave, half-hidden by the overgrown bushes. She was making even less progress on the gardening than he had. “He’s always had a big heart, Leo.”
bs: — Da. Rike natmureno pogleda prema očevu grobu, napola skrivenom bujnim raslinjem. Čak joj je i uređivanje vrta išlo slabije nego njemu. — Leo je oduvijek imao veliko srce.

en: “You haven’t killed each other, then?” Leo had stepped out into the sun, a worried look on his face. There was no disguise in him at all. He couldn’t have hidden a tree in a forest.
bs: "Znači, vi niste posušile jedna drugu?" Leo je istupio na sunce sa zabrinutim izrazom lica. U njemu nije bilo nikakve pretvaranja. Niti stabalce u šumi ne bi mogao sakriti.

en: Leo frowned at Savine. “I don’t want the crown. A new Closed Council and an honest government and I’ll be satisfied.”
bs: Leo se namrštio na Savine. — Ne želim Krunu. Novo Zatvoreno Vijeće i poštena vlada, i bit ću zadovoljan.

en: They packed to leave soon after, which was quite the operation as Savine needed six big boxes with brass corners just to get out the door. The dead knew what she had in ’em. Secrets and lies, maybe.
bs: Ubrzo nakon toga stali su se pakirati za polazak, što je bio pravi pothvat budući da je Savine trebalo šest velikih sanduka s mjedenim okovima samo da bi izašla kroz vrata. Mrtvi su znali što je u njima držala. Tajne i laži, možda.

en: “’Course…” hummed Isern, dragging that one word out into a whole story, then folding her arms tight. “I trust that woman less than the weather. She is the fanciest thing I ever saw.”
bs: — ’Course… promrmlja Izern, razvlačeći tu jedinu riječ u cijelu priču, a zatim čvrsto prekriži ruke. — Manje vjerujem toj ženi nego vremenskoj prognozi. Ona je najizvještačenija stvar koju sam ikad vidjela.

en: Rikke shaded her good eye with her hand. He was very tall. Taller than Shivers, even, but with a stoop, elbows stuck out and chin stuck forward, white-blond hair sprouting in tufts. “Unless I’m much mistook, I believe that’s the Nail.”
bs: Rike zaštiti dobro oko dlanom. Bio je jako visok. Čak viši od Šiversa, ali pogrbljen, laktova isturenih u stranu i brade gurnute prema naprijed, s pramenovima bijeloplave kose koji su stršili na sve strane. — Osim ako se grdno varam, vjerujem da je to Najl.

en: “Can’t think o’ higher praise. Saw you in the battle, too, and at the duel after. Before all this, though.” And he waved towards the left side of his face, his pale eyes still on her, taking it all in.
bs: — Ne mogu se sjetiti se veće pohvale. Vidio sam i tebe u bitci, a i u dvoboju poslije. Iako, prije svega ovoga. Zatim mahnu prema lijevoj strani lica, a blijede mu oči ostanu uprte u nju, upijajući svaki detalj.

en: “I heard you’re a bad enemy to have. I know Stour fears you. Thought maybe, with my sword and your eye, the odds would be shorter. Uffrith and the West Valleys together. That’d be a thing no one could dismiss.”
bs: — Čuo sam da je tebe opasno imati za neprijatelja. Znam da te Staur seže. Pomislio sam, uz moj mač i tvoje Oko, da bi izgledi mogli biti povoljniji. Afrit i Zapadne doline zajedno. To bi bilo nešto što nitko ne bi mogao zanemariti.

en: “I tend somewhat to agree. No reason you and I can’t be good neighbours, though. Why don’t you come inside? I’ll toss a fresh log on the firepit and crack a keg of my father’s ale.”
bs: — Donekle se slažem. No to ne znači da ti i ja ne možemo biti dobri susjedi. Zašto ne uđeš unutra? Ubacit ću svježu cjepanicu u ognjište i natočiti keg očeva alea.

en: He twisted the circlet gently from his head and held it up, looking through it towards the gleaming track. Towards the expectant crowd. He gave a little giggle.
bs: Nježno skine krunu s glave, podigne je i zagleda se kroz nju prema blistavoj pruzi. Prema očekivanju u gomili. Tiho se zahihota.

en: Honrig Curnsbick, the great machinist himself, stood near his creation with tall hat and riotous side whiskers, surrounded by cheering well-wishers, shaking a fistful of drawings at his oil-blackened engineers. One of them shovelled coal furiously into the glowing maw of the machine. Another weighed a giant wrench while frowning towards the royal box with an intensity bordering on hatred. Sadly, there was nothing remarkable in that. Orso regarded anything warmer than strong dislike from one of h
bs: Honrig Kurnsbik, Great mehaničar glavom i bradom, stajao je blizu svog izuma s visokim šeširom i bujnim zaliscima, okružen kličućim simpatizerima, mašući snopom nacrta pred svojim inženjerima pocrnjelima od ulja. Jedan od njih bijesno je ubacivao ugljen u užarenu čeljust stroja. Drugi je vagao divovski francuski ključ mršteći se prema kraljevskoj lozi s intenzitetom koji je graničio s mržnjom. Nažalost, u tome nije bilo ničeg neuobičajenog. Orso je svako lice toplije od snažne odbojnosti koje bi

en: “Far better to tour with a wife, then you could introduce her to the people and get started on producing an heir at the same time.”
bs: "Mnogo je bolje krenuti na turneju sa suprugom, tada bi mogao predstaviti nju narodu i usput započeti rađanje nasljednika."

en: “There is not so wide a gulf between science and magic as some suppose.” Sulfur nodded towards the city, where the House of the Maker was still the tallest spike on the horizon. “Was not Kanedias himself the first and greatest of engineers? And did not Juvens say that knowledge is the root of power? Lord Bayaz delights in nothing more than ideas, innovations, new ways of thinking.” He turned his bright eyes towards Curnsbick’s steam-wreathed engine. “Imagine a network of these track-roads. Iron
bs: — Nije jaz između znanosti i magije tako Brod kao što neki misle. Salfur kimnu prema gradu, gdje je Dom Stvoritelja i dalje bio najviši šiljak na obzorju. — Nije li sam Kanedias bio prvi i najveći inženjer? I nije li Juvens kazao da je znanje korijen moći? Lord Bajaz ne veseli se ničemu više nego idejama, inovacijama, novim načinima razmišljanja. Okrenu svoje bistro oko prema Kurnsbikovu parom ovijenom stroju. — Zamislite mrežu takvih tračnih cesta. Željezne spone koje čvršće no ikad povezuju Un

en: “We have made astonishing progress in a few brief years, my friends!” Depending on who you asked, of course, Orso still heard plenty of complaints. “With the right techniques and machinery, one man can now do the work that once took ten! Took twenty!” Though what became of the other nineteen was not made clear.
bs: — Ostvarili smo zapanjujući Naprijed u svega nekoliko kratkih godina, prijatelji moji! Ovisno o tome koga ste pitali, Orso je još uvijek slušao pregršt žalopojki. — Uz prave tehnike i strojeve, jedan čovjek sada može obaviti posao za koji je nekada trebalo desetoricu! Dvadesetero! Mada nije bilo najjasnije što se dogodilo s preostalih devetnaest.

en: It always worried Orso when someone wanted to involve him in a decision, however superficially. But decisions still had to be made. However superficially. “Carry us into the future, Master Curnsbick!” he called, grinning to the crowd.
bs: Orsa je uvijek brinulo kada bi ga netko htio uplesti u neku odluku, ma koliko površno to bilo. No odluke su se ipak morale donositi. Ma koliko površno. — Povedite nas u budućnost, Majstore Kurnsbik!" doviknu, široko se osmijehnuvši mnoštvu.

en: “I firmly believe that this, my latest invention…” And Curnsbick gestured towards his smouldering engine with the presence of a great actor upon the stage. Such a powerful man, those strong hands. Such a generous man, those impressive side whiskers. Such a visionary, piercing eyes behind his flashing lenses. The spirit of the age! “Will carry all of us… into the future!”
bs: — Čvrsto vjerujem da će ovaj moj najnoviji izum… I Kurnsbik pokretom ruke pokaže na svoj dimni stroj s držanjem velikog glumca na pozornici. Tako moćan čovjek, te snažne ruke. Tako velikodušan čovjek, ti dojmljivi zalizci. Takav vizionar, prodorne oči iza blistavih stakala. Duh vremena! "Odvesti sve nas… u budućnost!"

en: “We have made astonishing progress in a few brief years, my friends!” It was true the Union was much changed in the two decades since Muslan arrived but mostly, in his opinion, for the worse. He felt the stares when he walked the streets in his own neighbourhood. He felt the stares now. Less curiosity than there once had been, and more fear. More dislike. Insults were sometimes thrown. Objects, too, on occasion. A very pleasant young man of his acquaintance had been hit by a slate thrown from a
bs: — Ostvarili smo zapanjujući Naprijed za samo nekoliko kratkih godina, prijatelji moji! Istina je da se Unija silno promijenio u Dvadesetero godina otkad je Muslan stigao, ali uglavnom, po njegovu mišljenju, na gore. Osjećao je poglede kad bi prolazio ulicama vlastite četvrti. Osjećao ih je i sada. Bilo je tu manje znatiželje nego nekada, a više straha. Više odbojnosti. Ponekad su padale i uvrede. Ponekad i predmeti. Jednog iznimno ugodnog mladića iz njegova poznanstva pogodio je komad škriljevca

en: We all are carried into the future, always. What greets us when we arrive, that is the pressing question. When the Prophet vanished, Muslan and those of his mind—the thinkers, philosophers, engineers—had hoped for a new age of reason. Instead had come an age of madness. The priests had said his work was against the laws of God. Ignorant cowards. Who made the minds of men, if not God? What was the desire to create, if not a humble imitation of His example? What was the grand idea, the great visio
bs: Svi mi hrlimo u budućnost, neprekidno. Što nas dočekuje kad stignemo, to je goruće pitanje. Kada je Poslanik nestao, Muslan i oni slična uma – mislioci, filozofi, inženjeri – nadali su se novom dobu razuma. Umjesto toga stiglo je doba ludila. Svećenici su govorili da je njegov rad protivan Božjim zakonima. Neuki kukavice. Tko je stvorio ljudske umove, ako ne Bog? Što je bila želja za stvaranjem, ako ne skromna imitacija Njegova primjera? Što je bila grandiozna ideja, Great vizija, duboka objava,

en: Morilee frowned at that Gurkish bastard. Was that the future of the Union? Overrun by brown bastards, not even with the decency to come with drum and flag and sword so they could be properly fought and beaten, but just welcomed in at the back door by treacherous fucks wanting to sell their country for a few marks.
bs: Morilee se namrštila na tu gurkiskog kopiladi. Je li to bila budućnost Unije? Pregaženi od smeđih kopiladi, koji čak nisu imali ni toliko pristojnosti da dođu uz bubnjeve, zastave i mačeve kako bi se s njima moglo pošteno potući i pobijediti ih, nego su ih kroz stražnja vrata uveli izdajnički gadovi koji su htjeli prodati svoj Country za šaku maraka.

en: Blah, blah, progress, invention. High Justice Bruckel was hardly listening. He was thinking about that case yesterday. Terrible case. Regrettable business. The way the woman wept in the dock. Bruckel had wanted to weep himself. You cry so easily, his father used to say, you have to present a hard front. What would become of the children, though? It felt as if every verdict took a piece of him. Every sentence bled him. But his hands had been tied, as always. Arch Lector Glokta would demand harsh
bs: Bla, bla, Naprijed, izumi. Visoki Džadž Bruckel jedva je slušao. Razmišljao je o jučerašnjem slučaju. Strašan slučaj. Žaljenja vrijedna rabota. Način na koji je žena plakala na optuženičkoj klupi. Bruckel je i sam htio zaplakati. Tako lako zaplačeš, znao mu je reći otac, moraš pokazati čvrsto lice. Što će im tek biti s djecom? Osjećao se kao da mu svaka presuda otkida komadić duše. Svaka mu je kazna isisavala krv. Ali ruke su mu bile vezane, kao i uvijek. Vrhovni Lektor Glokta zahtijevao je oštr

en: “It will carry all of us…” screeched Curnsbick, a pygmy pretending to be a giant, the sort of man who passed for a hero in this petty age, “into the future!”
bs: "Odvest će sve nas…" zacvrči Kurnsbik, patuljak koji se pretvara da je div, onakav čovjek koji prolazi kao junak u ovom bijednom dobu, u budućnost!

en: “Carry us into the future, Master Curnsbick!” shouted Orso, with that infinitely good-humoured smile Terez’s own mouth always longed to imitate.
bs: — Povedi nas u budućnost, majstore Kurnsbik! povikao je Orso s onim beskrajno dobronamjernim osmijehom koji su Terezine usne uvijek priželjkivale oponašati.

en: She tried to stand, but the over-bright world tipped crazily and slapped her in the side. Dust and splinters. Boots shuffled. She saw someone staring at her. One of Curnsbick’s friends, blowing bloody bubbles out of his nose. It looked as if there might be an iron rivet embedded in the side of his neck. She realised they were both lying on the floor.
bs: Pokušala se uspraviti, ali zasljepljujuće sjajan svijet divlje se zanio i udario je sa strane. Prašina i iverje. Čizme su se vukle po podu. Ugledala je nekoga kako je blijedo promatra. Jedan od Kurnsbikovih prijatelja, s krvavim mjehurima koji su mu izbijali iz nosa. Činilo se kao da mu je željezna zakovica zabodena u vrat. Shvatila je da oboje leže na podu.

en: There were people coming through the bodies. Not helping. Stepping over the corpses. People in dark clothes, with dark masks over their faces. One held a hatchet. One a long knife. One pointed towards the royal box with a sword. Where was Orso? By the Fates, where was Orso?
bs: Među tijelima su prolazili Folk. Nisu pomagali. Prekoračivali su leševe. Folk u tamnoj odjeći, s tamnim maskama na licima. Jedan je držao sjekiru. Drugi dugačak nož. Treći je mačem pokazivao prema kraljevskoj loži. Gdje je bio Orso? Zaboga, gdje je bio Orso?

en: Someone shoved her, near knocked her over. One of the other Burners, desperate to begin the killing. Wasn’t that what she came for? All she’d wanted, for so long. To kill them. Tear them with her bare hands. Bite them with her teeth. Now she wondered who “them” was. Whose enemy was the little boy with a fluttering pamphlet stuck across his face and his guts hanging out? She felt sick.
bs: Netko ju je gurnuo, umalo je oborivši. Jedan od ostalih Palitelja, očajan da počne s ubijanjem. Nije li to ono za čim je došao? Sve što je željela, i to tako dugo. Ubiti ih. Rastrgati ih golim rukama. Izgristi ih zubima. Sada se pitala tko su to "oni. Čiji je neprijatelj dječak s lepršavim letkom zalijepljenim preko lica i prosušenim utrobama? Pozlilo joj je.

en: Curnsbick’s terror, when he struggled up with his hat blown off, was not for his own safety, but that he might be responsible. Or, at any rate, that he might be blamed.
bs: Kurnsbikov strah, dok se uspinjao s klobukom otpalim s glave, nije bio zbog vlastite sigurnosti, nego da ne bi snosio odgovornost. Ili, u svakom slučaju, da ne bi bio optužen.

en: “If I may, Your Majesty?” That man Sulfur. He was brushing the king aside. Went smiling towards a dozen well-armed fanatics as they mounted the steps. What the hell was he about?
bs: — Ako dopustite, Vaša Uzvišenosti? Onaj čovjek, Salfur. Odgurnuo je kralja u stranu. Nasmiješen je krenuo ususret desetorici naoružanih fanatika dok su se penjali stubama. Kakvu je to igru igrao?

en: The lecture theatres of the University’s grand new buildings had contained only dry whispers and dated ideas. The inspiring speeches were given in the teahouses and jerry shops on the borders of the poor districts, where the intellectuals would spring onto the tables to hold forth on the injustice of the current system, lay out bold fantasies for what could replace it, compete with each other to make the most outrageous pronouncements on behalf of the noble and oppressed commoner. The commoners
bs: Predavaonice novih velelepanih sveučilišnih zgrada nudile su samo suhoparne šapute i zastarjele ideje. Nadahnuti govori držali su se po čajnonicama i sklepanim krčmama na rubovima siromašnih četvrti, kamo bi intelektualci skakali na stolove kako bi naširoko propovijedali o nepravdi postojećeg sustava, iznosili odvažne tlapnje o tomu što bi ga moglo zamijeniti te se natjecali tko će izreći odvažnije izjave u ime plemenita i potlačenog pučanstva. Sami pučani, podrazumijevalo se samo po sebi, jedva

en: Except someone stepped in front of the king as Gus laboured to the top of the steps. No armoured Knight of the Body, just a nondescript, curly haired fellow in plain clothes, with a strange, bland smile which did not quite touch his eyes. If this fool thought he could stop the changing of an epoch, rob the people, steal this moment, he was mistaken! Gus was the instrument of history! He was a torrent that could not be dammed!
bs: Samo što mu je netko stao na put pred kraljem dok se Gus penjao stubama. Nije to bio oklopljeni Ritter tjelesne straže, nego tek običan, kovrčavi momak u civilu, čudnog, blagog osmijeha koji mu nije dopirao do očiju. Ako je taj luđak mislio da može zaustaviti promjenu epohe, opljačkati Folk, ukrasti ovaj trenutak, prevario se! Gus je bio instrument povijesti! Bio je bujica koja se nije dala zaustaviti!

en: No one up here would be much use in a fight. Curnsbick had his hands pressed to his horrified face. Kort had scrambled for the rear. Funny, when death’s on the table, how vitally important it seems that one be killed last.
bs: Nitko ovdje gore ne bi bio od velike koristi u borbi. Kurnsbik je dlanovima prekrio prestrašeno lice. Kort je otpuzao prema začelju. Čudno je kako se, kad je smrt na stolu, čini životno važnim da čovjek pogine posljednji.

en: “If I may, Your Majesty?” It was Sulfur, brushing past and carefully, almost daintily, stepping over High Justice Bruckel’s corpse. Orso had forgotten the magus was even there.
bs: — Dopuštate li, Vaša Uzvišenosti? Bio je to Salfur, koji se provukao pokraj njega i pažljivo, gotovo nježno prekoraknuo leš vrhovnog suca Bruckela. Orso je posve zaboravio da je magus uopće ondje.

en: Orso was not sure whether he was trying to shield his mother or cling to her for support. In the space of a breath, maybe two, Sulfur reduced half a dozen assassins to flying meat. Corpses turned inside out, twisted into corkscrews, popped open or crushed in on themselves. Worse than anything the exploding engine had done to the people down near the tracks.
bs: Orso nije bio siguran pokušava li štititi majku ili se hvatati za nju kako bi se održao na nogama. U tren oka, možda u dva, Salfur je polovicu od desetak atentatora pretvorio u leteće meso. Trupla su bila izvrnuta iznutra prema van, uvrnuta poput vadičepa, raskomadana ili zdrobljena u samima sebi. Bilo je to gore od svega što je eksplozivni stroj učinio ljudima dolje kod tračnica.

en: “Regarding the funding for new track-roads, Your Majesty. Under the auspices of the Banking House of Valint and Balk.”
bs: — Što se tiče financiranja novih tračnih cesta, Vaša Uzvišenosti. Pod pokroviteljstvom Bankarske kuće Valint i Balk.

en: “Weren’t we fighting that Union bastard a few months back? Fitting welcome for him would be an axe in the head.”
bs: — Zar se nismo do jučer tukli s tim unijskim kopaletom? Prilična dobrodošlica za njega bila bi Hachette u glavi.

en: Clover heard Downside give a disgusted grunt and shot an arm out in front of him ’fore he exposed Greenway’s skull for real.
bs: Klover ču kako je Dausaid zgroženo prozujao kroz zube i ispruži ruku Naprijed sebe prije nego što on doista ogoli Greenwayevu lubanju.

en: “I never been much for waiting,” grunted Downside, glaring daggers across at Greenway, who was complaining at some Named Man whose cloak-buckle wasn’t to his liking. “Time comes you have to stand up, Chief.”
bs: — Nikad nisam previše mario za čekanje, prozbori Dausaid strijeljajući pogledom Grinveja, koji se žalio nekakvom Imenovanom čovjeku čija mu kopča na ogrtaču nije bila po volji. — Dođe vrijeme kad čovjek mora ustati, Šefe.

en: The doors were swung open, and there was a rustle and a jingle as men shifted to see the Young Lion make his entrance. He looked quite the hero—breastplate, boots and teeth all buffed to a pretty sheen—but it was the woman beside him that really drew the eyes. She seemed to Clover to be an exception to the rule that men get more excited about a woman the less clothes she’s got on. Her dress might’ve been spun from sunlight, glittering as she moved. Jewels on her long fingers, and jewels at her l
bs: Vrata se širom otvoriše, a prostorijom prostruja šuškanje i zveckanje dok su se Folk pomicali ne bi li vidjeli kako Juvens Lav stupa na scenu. Izgledao je poput pravog heroja — oklop, čizme i zubi, sve je blistalo savršenim sjajem — no žena koja je koračala uz njega privlačila je sve poglede. Kloveru se učinila izuzetkom od pravila po kojem se muškarci tim više pale na ženu što ona ima manje odjeće na sebi. Haljina joj je bila kao da je satkana od Sunčevih zraka, blistajući pri svakom pokretu. D

en: Brock rendered it into the Union tongue for his wife, and she gave a laugh as glittering as her dress. Clover wondered how long she’d practised to get it just right but still felt greatly pleased with himself that he’d been the cause of it, then greatly disappointed when she walked on. Downside stared after her like a fox at an open chicken coop.
bs: Brok to prevede na jezik Unije svojoj ženi, a ona se nasmija jednako blistavo kao što joj je haljina sjajila. Klover se zapitao koliko je vježbala da joj smijeh zvuči posve prirodno, no i dalje je bio silno zadovoljan sobom što ga je on izazvao, a zatim silno razočaran kad je produžila dalje. Dausaid je blenuo za njom poput lisice u kokošinjac širom otvorenih vrata.

en: “So, you see…” Leo stumbled on, “the Closed Council have to be stopped. Before they do more damage. We need good men in charge. Honest men. Patriots.”
bs: —— Dakle, vidiš… nastavi Leo mucajući, zatvoreno Vijeće mora biti zaustavljeno. Prije nego što načine još štete. Trebamo poštene ljude na čelu. Čestite ljude. Patrijote.

en: He felt Savine’s gentle touch on his arm. “You fought the man and won,” she murmured in his ear. “Surely you can talk to him?”
bs: Osjeti nježan Savinin dodir na ruci. "Borio si se s čovjekom i pobijedio, prošapta mu na uho. — Zar doista ne možeš razgovarati s njim?

en: “And even better to learn the ways of his friends. I have been trying to garner some words of Northern, but I fear I am a poor study.”
bs: — A još je bolje naučiti običaje svojih prijatelja. Pokušavam pohvatati poneku riječ sjevernjačkog, no bojim se da sam loš učenik.

en: Savine gave Leo a wink as she took Black Calder’s bony hand and let the old man lead her from the dais. “Black Dow fought the Bloody-Nine right there,” he was saying.
bs: Savine namignu Leu dok je prihvaćala koščatu ruku Black Kaldera i dopuštala starcu da je povede s uzdignuta podija. — Black Dow se borio protiv Krvava Devetka upravo tamo, govorio je.

en: “So… you’re asking for warriors of the North… to sail to Midderland in their thousands… and fight against the big king in Adua?”
bs: — Dakle… tražiš ratnike sa Sjevera… da otplove u Miderland na tisuće… i bore se protiv velikog kralja u Adui?

en: “But I’m not a woman,” said Stour, “and my father might be quite the carper, but he knows a thing or two. So the question keeps drifting past—what’s in it for me? You offering a piece of Midderland?”
bs: — Ali ja nisam žena, dometnu Staur, "a moj otac možda jest cjepidlaka, ali zna on ponešto. Pa mi se pitanje stalno mota po glavi — što je tu za mene? Nudiš li mi komad Miderlanda?

en: “Steepfield?” Leo frowned. “The one who held the pass at Grey Breaks? The one who killed Cairm Ironhead?”
bs: — Stipfild? Leo se namršti. — Onaj koji je držao klance kod Sivih Pukotina? Onaj koji je smaknuo Cairma Ironheada?

en: When she agreed to marry him, she had expected to quickly become bored. To spend time on long trips. Maybe take a lover, in due course. But there was a lot to like about the Young Lion. Honesty, loyalty, courage, passion. Old-fashioned virtues, perhaps. The virtues of a really excellent dog. But virtues she was starting to appreciate. Even to admire. He was a decent man, in several ways that actually counted. Enough to make her feel almost decent when she was beside him. And that was a pleasant
bs: Tako zvani Great vuk skočio je sikćući na jednog od svojih sparing-partnera, tako iznenadno i divljački da je Savine instinktivno stavila zaštitničku ruku na trbuh. Morala se prisiliti da se ne trzne unazad dok je Staur sjekao po štitu i bacao iverje na sve strane, sagnuo se pod štapom i prošao ispod njega, gurnuvši čovjeka ramenom u zid i natjeravši ga da prozuji od bola. Staur je uhvatio rub štita, udario čovjeka koljenom u trbuh, a zatim mu okrutno zadao udarac plosnatom stranom mača po nozi

en: “Well,” he whispered, narrowing those horrible wet eyes at her. “We’re known more for our swords than our cities up here.” He dodged a swing of the stick without even looking, caught it with his free hand, slipped around the shield and clubbed the straw-strapped warrior in the face with the pommel of his sword.
bs: — Pa, prošaptao je, suzivši one grozne vlažne oči na nju. — Ovdje gore poznatiji smo po svojim mačevima nego po gradovima. Izbjegao je zamah štapa a da ga nije ni pogledao, uhvatio ga slobodnom rukom, provukao se pokraj štita i udario ratnika s remenjem od slame drškom mača po licu.

en: They called him the Great Wolf and Savine did not doubt he was well named. She could hear his growling breath. Smell his sour sweat. A wild dog indeed. And you cannot show a dog your fear. Her skin crawled, her heart thudded, but she forced herself to stand still, forced herself to meet his eye as the cold point tickled at her throat, then along her shoulder, caught something just inside her collar and eased it out.
bs: Zvali su ga Great Wolf, a Savine nije sumnjala da s razlogom nosi to ime. Čula je njegov režavi dah. Osjetila njegov kiseli znoj. Pravi divlji Pas Covjek. A psu se ne smije pokazati strah. Koža joj se naježi, srce joj zatreperi, ali prisili se ostati na mjestu, prisili se susresti s njegovim okom dok joj je hladni Kruna golicao grlo, zatim klizio niz rame, zahvatio nešto tik ispod njezine ovratnice i izvukao to van.

en: “Afterwards, you will be lord from the Whiteflow to the Crinna and beyond. A true King of the Northmen.” She sank down, and took his sword gently by the blade, and offered the hilt to him as she stood. “All of them. Something I understand your father could never quite manage.”
bs: — Nakon svega, bit ćeš gospodar od Whiteflowa do Crinne i dalje. Pravi kralj Sjevernjaka. Ona se spusti, nježno uhvati njegov mač za sječivo i ponudi mu dršku dok je ustajala. "Svi oni. Nešto što, kako shvaćam, tvoj otac nikada nije posve uspio."

en: The bruises on his face and the cut above his eye were faded. Probably happened when they blew up Curnsbick’s engine. But the hand was more recent.
bs: Modrice na licu i posjekotina iznad oka bile su izblijedjele. Vjerojatno su nastale kad su digli u zrak Kurnsbikov stroj. No ruka je stradala nedavno.

en: “Never met him.” He shrugged as if lifting his shoulders took all the strength he had. “That’s what they told me.”
bs: — Nikad ga nisam upoznao. Slegnu ramenima kao da mu je dizanje ramena oduzelo svu preostalu snagu. — Tako su mi rekli.

en: She remembered what Shenkt had done to those two Practicals, on the quay in Westport. Big men, tossed like dolls.
bs: Sjetila se što je Šenkt učinio onoj dvojici Praktičara na doku u Vestportu. Krupni Folk, odbačeni poput lutaka.

en: She thought about smashing her fist down on that mess of a hand while she screamed the questions in his face. But he had no answers. None that helped her, anyway. She got up and left him ranting, as mad as any of the cut-price prophets in Westport’s Temple Square.
bs: Pomislila je kako će spustiti šaku na onu razbijenu ruku dok mu bude vikala pitanja u lice. Ali on nije imao odgovora. Barem ne onih koji bi joj pomogli. Ustala je i ostavila ga da galami, luđeg od bilo kojeg niskobudžetnog proroka na Trgu hrama u Vestportu.

en: “Inquisitor Teufel!” It was only the bloody king. “I never got the chance to thank you for your help in Valbeck. You made me look good, and that takes some damn doing. That note of yours saved my arse, not to mention several thousand others.” His smile faded somewhat. “Shame it couldn’t save everyone’s, really. And now I hear you pulled our feet out of the fire in Westport, too!”
bs: — Inkvizitor Tojfel! Bio je to samo prokleti kralj."Nikad nisam dobio priliku zahvaliti vam na pomoći u Valbeku. Učinili ste da ja izgledam dobro, a za to se bogami valja potruditi. Ona vaša poruka spasila mi je stražnjicu, da i ne spominjem nekoliko tisuća drugih." Osmijeh mu je pomalo izblijedio. — Šteta zapravo što nije mogla spasiti svačiju. A sad čujem da ste nam i u Vestportu izvadili kestene iz vatre!

en: “We have never met,” said Sulfur, “though I, too, am a great admirer of your work in Valbeck.” He gave her a neat little bow. “I was once apprentice to the First of the Magi.”
bs: — Nikada se nismo susreli, odvrati Salfur, iako sam i ja Great obožavatelj vašeg rada u Valbeku. Udvorito joj se naklonio. — Nekoć sam bio štićenik Prvog među Magima.

en: Vick swallowed, her skin unpleasantly prickling. A plot. The Open Council. Allies in the North and Styria. A traitor in the Closed Council. This could be a threat to make the uprising in Valbeck look like a village dance.
bs: Vik proguta knedlu, a koža joj se neugodno naježi. Urota. Otvoreno vijeće. Saveznici u Sjeveru i Stiriji. Izdajica u Zatvorenom vijeću. To bi mogla biti prijetnja uz koju bi se buna u Valbeku činila poput seoskog plesa.

en: The Arch Lector was looking even more pale than usual. “Isher and Brock were married together…” One of them to his own daughter, as they were no doubt all well aware.
bs: Vrhovni lektor izgledao je još bljeđe nego inače. — Išer i Brok su se orodili…" Jedan od njih s vlastitom kćerkom, čega su, kao što su nesumnjivo svi dobro znali, bili i te kako svjesni.

en: “In the meantime, we take the advice of our anonymous friend and prepare,” said Orso. “We raise our own forces, we gather every ally we can find.”
bs: — u međuvremenu, poslušajmo Vijeće našega anonimnog prijatelja i pripremimo se, reče Orso. — Podignimo vlastite snage, okupimo svakog saveznika kojega možemo pronaći.

en: “By generous,” said Glokta, wiping a long tear from his cheek as his eyelid flickered, “I assume you mean further loans at even more crippling rates of interest?”
bs: "Pod velikodušnošću", reče Glokta, brišući dugu suzu s obraza dok mu je kapak treperio, pretpostavljam da mislite na nove zajmove uz još pogubnije kamatne stope?

en: Glokta sat forward, hands clasped. “Inquisitor Teufel, I would like you to observe the other members of the Closed Council. Subtly, of course. If one of them is disloyal, we have to know. Employ only people you trust. Outsiders, if possible.”
bs: Glokta se nagnuo naprijed, sklopivši ruke. — Inkvizitore Tojfel, volio bih motriti na ostale članove Zatvorenog Vijeća. Diskretno, dakako. Ako je netko od njih nevjeran, to moramo znati. Angažirajte samo ljude kojima vjerujete. Po mogućnosti strance.

en: She shook herself, trying to shake free of the fear. That was all long ago. That girl was gone, not trapped inside her, screaming to get out.
bs: Treseći se, pokušala se osloboditi straha. Sve je to bilo davno. Ta je djevojka nestala, nije bila zarobljena u njoj, vrišteći da izađe.

en: “It has been mentioned. But fear is a poor reason to limit your options.” He looked her discerningly up and down, like a tailor guessing a client’s measurements. “Tough day?”
bs: — Spomenuli su mi to već. No strah je loš razlog za sužavanje izbora. Odmjerio ju je prodornim pogledom od glave do pete, poput krojača koji pogađa klijentove mjere. — Trdak dan?

en: He held up his finger and thumb and peered at her through the tiny space between. “A little. But with a subtlety and class you don’t often get in Adua. Shylo Vitari doesn’t like being embarrassed, but she likes people who can manage to do it. She works on the principle that it’s your worst enemies that make the best friends. Have you come to take up her offer of employment?”
bs: Podigao je kažiprst i Palioc te ju promotrio kroz taj sićušni prorez među njima. — Malo. Ali sa suptilnošću i stilom kakvi se rijetko viđaju u Adui. Šajlo Vitari ne voli kad ju se sramoti, ali voli ljude kojima to polazi za rukom. Vodi se načelom da nam najgori neprijatelji postaju najbolji prijatelji. Jesi li došla prihvatiti njezinu ponudu za posao?

en: Some flinched away. Some shook their heads. Some barely even seemed to hear him, lost in their own misery.
bs: Neki su se trznuli. Neki su odmahnuli glavama. Neki su se činili kao da ga jedva čuju, izgubljeni u vlastitoj bijedi.

en: Broad stood aside to watch the mourners pass. Wanted to give ’em something. The way they’d all chipped in when he lived on a street like this, even when they had next to nothing to give. He wanted to give ’em something but he set his jaw against it. You can’t make every problem your problem, Liddy was always telling him. And she was right.
bs: Brod se pomaknuo u stranu kako bi ispratio ožalošćene pogledom. Htio im je nešto dati. Sjetio se kako su svi oni pripomogli kad je živio u ovakvoj ulici, čak i kad nisu imali gotovo ništa za dati. Htio im je nešto dati, ali je stisnuo čeljust i uskratio si to. Ne možeš svaki Trobli učiniti svojim problemom, to mu je Lidi stalno govorila. I bila je u pravu.

en: “Gunnar Broad, back from the dead.” Sarlby’s voice had a throaty crackle to it. Seemed he’d aged ten years in the ten months since they last spoke. “Heard you were looking for me.”
bs: — Gunar Brod, vratio se iz mrtvih. Sarlbyjev glas zvučao je promuklo i krhko. Činilo se kao da je ostario deset godina u onih deset mjeseci otkako su posljednji put razgovarali. — Čuo sam da me tražiš.

en: “No.” Broad thought about lying. But he owed Sarlby the truth, didn’t he? Owed him that much. “Been working for Savine dan Brock.”
bs: — Ne. Brod pomisli da slaže. No dugovao je Sarlbyju istinu, zar ne? Dugovao mu je toliko. — Radim za Savine dan Brok.

en: “I tried it your way.” He settled his lenses back on his sweaty nose, made himself breathe slow. “Look where it got us.”
bs: — Pokušao sam na vaš način. Vratio je naočale na znojni nos i prisilio se disati polako. — Pogledaj kamo nas je to dovelo.

en: Sarlby barked out a joyless laugh. “No. No one accused you o’ that.” There was silence as he slowly tore off a piece of bread, and slowly swept it around in the gravy on his plate till he’d soaked up every drop. “But I got to warn you, the cool heads all died wi’ Malmer. Feelings are running hot.”
bs: Sarlbi se kiselo nasmija. — Ne. Nitko te za to nije optužio." Nastade tišina dok je polako kidao komad kruha i polako njime upijao umak s tanjura sve dok nije pokupio svaku kap. — Ali moram te upozoriti, hladne glave su izginule s Malmerom. Strasti su uzavrele.

en: “Like a palace,” grunted Leo, frowning at two carved cherubs among the gilded moulding. He supposed he was the Lord Governor of Angland and should demand the best of everything. His wife always did. But in truth, luxury made him nervous. Couldn’t help thinking what the Dogman might’ve made of it. Shook his head and murmured, “State o’ this,” and given a little grunt of a laugh, most likely. Leo was carved from the same wood. Always felt happier sleeping in hay than on silk, eating with his hands
bs: — Poput palače, progunđao je Leo mršteći se na dva urezana kerubina među pozlaćenim letvicama. Pretpostavljao je da je on Lord Guverner Englenda i da bi trebao zahtijevati najbolje od svega. Njegova supruga je uvijek to činila. No istini za volju, luksuz ga je uznemiravao. Nije mogao prestati razmišljati o tome što bi Pas Covjek Čovjek rekao na sve ovo. Odmahnuo je glavom i promrmljao: — Kakvo stanje, uz vjerojatno jedva primjetan prigušeni smijeh. Leo je bio skrojen od istoga drveta. Uvijek se

en: Antaup sat up. “Rubs me the wrong way, making nice with one of the Union’s worst enemies.” And he punched a pillow as if it was King Jappo’s face.
bs: Antaup se uspravio. — Žuč mi se diže na pomisao da se ulagujemo jednom od najvećih neprijatelja Unije." I udario je jastuk šakom kao da je to lice kralja Jappa.

en: “Glanhorm doesn’t cover any of that shit.” Antaup set his brows waggling. “Just the brothels. And Cardotti’s House of Leisure is first on the fuck list.”
bs: — Glanhorm ne piše o takvim sranjima. Antaup razigra obrvama. — Samo o bordelima. A Kardottijeva Kuća užitaka prva je na popisu za jebanje.

en: “I know you don’t think much of Styria, but even you can’t deny…” And Jurand planted his hands on the pitted parapet and looked out at the sunset. “It’s a hell of a romantic setting.”
bs: — Znam da nemaš visoko mišljenje o Stiriji, ali čak ni ti ne možeš poreći… Džurand spusti ruke na izlokani parapet i zagleda se u zalazak sunca. — Ovo je pakleni, romantični prizor.

en: A silence, then, while the violin played on, and a pleasure-barge drifted down the grey-green canal below them, masked merrymakers lazing in each other’s arms on the upper deck. One of those moments you hope might last for ever.
bs: Potom nastupi tišina dok je violina svirala dalje, a brodica za razonodu klizila niz sivozeleni kanal pod njima, s maskiranim veseljacima koji su ljenčarili zagrljeni na gornjoj palubi. Jedan od onih trenutaka za koje se nadaš da bi mogli trajati vječno.

en: “Here you go!” Antaup blundered out through the window, wedged a glass into Leo’s hand, another into Jurand’s, spattering wine on the balcony, making them both take an awkward little step apart. “Our boy’s all grown up!” And he planted a slobbery kiss on Leo’s cheek, and ruffled Jurand’s already ruffled hair, and ducked back inside.
bs: — Evo vas! Antaup bučno izleti kroz prozor, ugura čašu Leu u ruku, drugu Džurandu, prosuvši vino po balkonu i natjeravši ih da obojica naprave nespretan korak unatrag. — Naš je dječak odrastao! I opaliti slinavi poljubac Leu po obrazu, pa razbarušiti Džurandovu već razbarušenu kosu, pa se strmoglaviti natrag unutra.

en: “Well, I’m not him.” Though he feared in fact he might be. “It’s brought out the responsible servant of the people in me.”
bs: — Pa, ja nisam on. Premda se strašio da bi zapravo mogao biti. — U meni je probudilo onog odgovornog slugu naroda.

en: “Couldn’t you have got pregnant or something?” murmured Orso from the corner of his mouth. “That would have been a perfect diversion.”
bs: — Zar nisi mogla zatrudnjeti ili nešto? promrmlja Orso iz kuta usana. — To bi bila savršena diverzija.

en: “Not that.” He thought about it. “Well, yes, that, but I was referring more to the demands of power.”
bs: — Ne s tim. Zamislio se. — Dobro, da, i s tim, ali više sam mislio na zahtjeve koje vlast postavlja.

en: He gathered his courage, then puffed out his chest and met her raised chin with his own. “Mother. For the time being, I want you to stay in Sipani.”
bs: Skupio je hrabrost, zatim napuhao prsa i suprotstavio joj bradu. — Majko. Za sada želim da ostaneš u Sipani.

en: He noticed there were grey streaks in her hair. Wrinkles around her eyes, at the corners of her mouth. When had she started to look old? It made him feel deeply uneasy. He had always supposed she was indestructible.
bs: Primijetio je sijede pramenove u njezinoj kosi. Bore oko očiju, u kutovima usana. Kada se to ona počela doimati starom? Zbog toga ga obuze duboka nelagoda. Uvijek je držao da je ona neuništiva.

en: “You know as well as I do that they make the best women in the world here. Speaking of which, has our guest arrived?”
bs: — Znaš dobro kao i ja da su ovdje najbolje žene na svijetu. Kad smo već kod toga, je li stigla naša gostća?

en: “Well,” said Carlot, making for the door and jerking her head significantly towards it. “I have some… things to do.”
bs: — Pa, reče Carlot krenuvši prema vratima i značajno kimajući glavom u tom smjeru, imam nekakvih… poslova.

en: Women glided about the hallway with high shoes and hungry smiles, with hair piled and twisted, with clinging clothes of shimmering pearl-white and glistening oil-black. Clothes that gave tricking glimpses of thigh and shoulder through slits and slashes, showed the laces and buckles of elaborate underwear.
bs: Žene su klizile hodnikom u cipelama s visokim potpeticama i gladnih osmijeha, s uzdignutom i upletenom kosom, u pripijenoj odjeći biserno bijelog sjaja i blistave uljne crne boje. Odjeći koja je kroz procjepe i proreze mamila poglede na bedra i ramena te otkrivala vezice i kopče složenoga donjeg rublja.

en: “King Jappo is most keen to speak with you but… otherwise engaged just now. The entertainments of Cardotti’s stand entirely at your disposal in the meantime.”
bs: "Kralj Džapo silno želi razgovarati s vama, ali… trenutno je zauzet. Zabavni sadržaji Kardottija stoje vam u međuvremenu potpuno na raspolaganju."

en: “You need to live a little!” Glaward swept two drinks from the tray of a waitress with a mask like a golden octopus and started to swill one back while holding out the other.
bs: — Moraš malo uživati u životu! Glavard zgrabi dva pića s pladnja konobarice s maskom nalik na zlatnu hobotnicu i poče iskapljati jedno držeći drugo ispruženo.

en: “Don’t worry.” Jurand, slipping up close to speak softly. Knowing Leo’s feelings without a word said, like always. He guided Leo over to the dice table. It was the right height to lean on, at least, and take the weight off his throbbing leg without showing any weakness. “You’re the Young Lion! You convinced Rikke and Stour to join you. United two bitter enemies under your banner! Just be honest, and strong, and generous. Just be you.” Jurand leaned closer, grinning. “Only a bit more ruthless. Th
bs: — Ne brini. Džurand se prišuljao blizu kako bi progovorio tiho, znajući Leove osjećaje i bez izgovorene riječi, kao i uvijek. povio je Lea prema stolu za kocku. Bio je barem prave visine da se nasloni na nj i skine teret s bolne noge a da ne pokaže nikakvu slabost."Ti si Juvens Lav! Uvjerio si Rike i Staura da ti se pridruže. Ujedinio si dva ogorčena neprijatelja pod svojim barjakom! Samo budi iskren, snažan i velikodušan. Samo budi svoj." Džurand se primakao još bliže, šeretski se smiješeći. —

en: “Your Majesty,” she said, dropping into a deep and graceful curtsy. Almost as deep and graceful as the ones Savine used to perform, though her skirts had never split all the way to her hips in quite so mesmerising a way.
bs: — Vaša Uzvišenosti, reče spuštajući se u dubok i elegantan naklon. Skoro jednako dubok i elegantan kakve je Savine znala izvoditi, premda joj se haljina nikad nije rasporila sve do kukova na tako očaravajući način.

en: “All of them.” The greeter led them into a dark-panelled hall where games of skill, chance and ruination were being played. Groups of men sat talking, laughing, smoking, drinking. Girls cooed and crooned and fluttered fans between them. Coloured light gleamed on fine glassware and soft skin, filtered through amber drinks and curling smoke. Rarely if ever had such a tableau of high-class debauchery been assembled in one place, and Orso had arranged quite a few himself, in his misspent youth. And
bs: "Sve." Domaćin ih uvede u dvoranu tamnih drvenih obloga u kojoj su se igrale igre vještine, sreće i propasti. Skupine muškaraca sjedile su razgovarajući, smijući se, pušeći i pijući. Djevojke su gugutale, prele i mahale lepezama. Šareno svjetlo blistalo je na finom staklu i mekoj koži, probijajući se kroz jantarna pića i kovitlac dima. Rijetko kad, ako ikad, takav je prizor visokoklasnog razvrata bio okupljen na jednome mjestu, a Orso ih je i sam priredio podosta u svojoj promašenoj mladosti. A

en: “It’s a House of Leisure,” said the whale, spreading his hands in good-natured apology. “Shouldn’t we all be drunk?”
bs: — Ovo je Kuća dokolice, reče kit, šireći ruke u dobrodušnoj isprici. — Zar ne bismo svi trebali biti pijani?

en: “I suppose it all depends on finding the right woman.” Orso gave a long sigh. “Thought I had her. But she slipped through my fingers somehow.”
bs: — Moje sve ovisi o tome da nađeš pravu ženu. Orso otpusti dug uzdah. — Mislio sam da ju imam. Ali nekako mi je izmaknula iz ruku.

en: Jappo mon Rogont Murcatto—Grand Duke of Ospria and Visserine, Protector of Puranti, Nicante, Borletta and Affoia, not to mention King of Styria—sprawled on a velvet chaise in front of a mural of winged women floating naked from a sunset sky and looked very pleased about it. His Suljuk silk gown trailed open to show his muscular stomach, complete with a streak of thick black hair.
bs: Džapo mon Rogont Murkato — Great vojvoda Osprije i Viserin, zaštitnik Purantija, Nicantea, Borlette i Afoije, da i ne spominjemo kralja Stirije — izvalio se na baršunastom ležaju Naprijed murala s krilatim ženama koje golišave plutaju s neba u sutonu te je izgledao vrlo zadovoljno time. Njegova svilena odora iz Suljuka vukla se otvorena pokazujući mu mišićav trbuh, ukrašen prugom guste crne kose.

en: “Alas, I have not met your wife, but by all accounts she’s a very shrewd woman.” Jappo shook his fist. “Very tough.” He stroked his shining gown. “Very beautiful. I love to surround myself with beautiful things. But women?” He held up a wobbling hand and made a sound like nyeh. “Mixed feelings. Hope you’re enjoying Cardotti’s.”
bs: — Nažalost, nisam upoznao tvoju ženu, ali prema svemu sudeći, izuzetno je pronicljiva žena. Džapo je stisnuo šaku. — Vrlo čvrsta. Pomilovao je svoju sjajnu haljinu. — Vrlo lijepa. Volim se okruživati lijepim stvarima. No, žene? Podignuo je drhtavu ruku i ispustio zvuk poput njee. — Podijeljeni osjećaji. Nadam se da uživaš u Kardottijevima.

en: “Well…” Leo struggled to force his mind back onto the script. “The only real dispute we have is King Orso’s claim on Talins. His false claim, that is—”
bs: — Pa… Leo se namučio vratiti misli na scenarij. — Jedini stvarni spor koji imamo jest pravo kralja Orsa na Talins. Njegovo lažno pravo, naime…

en: “Our quarrel’s not with King Orso, but with his Closed Council. Their arrogance. Their corruption. They’re dragging the nation into the sewer!”
bs: — Naša se svađa ne vodi s kraljem Orsom, nego s njegovim Užim vijećem. S njihovom bahatošću. S njihovom korupcijom. Guraju naciju u kanalizaciju!

en: “He doesn’t suspect a thing.” Leo was trying so hard not to look at Jappo’s bare stomach, he ended up constantly glancing at it. “A member of his Closed Council is in our pocket, warning us of every move he makes.”
bs: — Nema pojma o svemu tome. Leo se toliko trudio da ne gleda Jappov goli trbuh da je na kraju neprestano krajičkom oka buljio u nj. — Netko iz njegovog Užeg vijeća nam je u džepu i upozorava nas na svaki njegov potez.

en: Leo paused. They’d all agreed to offer Westport, if they had to. A superstitious slum, Savine had said. A paltry price to pay for Angland, Starikland and Midderland. He’d reluctantly agreed at the time, but now his leg was aching, and perhaps it was the chagga smoke, but he was feeling out of sorts, hot in the face and slightly dizzy. He hated Styria, hated Sipani, hated Cardotti’s, hated this degenerate excuse for a king most of all. He raised his chin, trying to look haughtily down his nose, b
bs: Leo zastade. Svi su se složili ponuditi Vestport, ako bude nužno. Praznovjerna prčvarnica, rekla je Savine. Sitna cijena za Englend, Starikland i Miderland. Tada je nevoljko pristao, ali sada ga je noga boljela, a možda je to bio i dim čage, no osjećao se loše, lice mu je gorjelo i bio je blago ošamućen. Mrzio je Stiriju, mrzio Sipani, mrzio Kardottijevu palaču, a najviše od svega mrzio je ovu izopačenu ispriku od kralja. Podignuo je bradu, pokušavajući se ponosito držati s visoka, ali oči su mu

en: Leo ground his teeth as he pulled the door shut. He would’ve liked to fling the bastard thing closed and snarl some ugly curses after it, but the greeter was in the hallway, guiding someone else towards Jappo’s door. It was that smug idiot from downstairs with a gilded sun for a mask.
bs: Leo zaškrguta zupcima dok je privlačio vrata. Rado bi tresnuo tim gadnim vratima i ispalio nekoliko ružnih psovki za njima, ali domar je bio u hodniku, vodeći nekog drugog prema Jappovim vratima. Bio je to onaj umišljeni idiot iz prizemlja s pozlaćenim suncem umjesto maske.

en: “We both owe our mothers a debt, then. Mine gave me a whole kingdom.” And Jappo plucked his mask off and dropped it beside Orso’s. His face was not at all what Orso had imagined. Handsome, but in a strong-boned, broad-jawed sort of way. Surprisingly pale, too, in spite of his dark curls. He looked more like a Northman than a Styrian.
bs: — Onda obojica dugujemo zahvalnost majkama. Moja mi je dala čitavo kraljevstvo. I Džapo skine svoju masku pa je spusti pokraj Orsove. Lice mu nije bilo ni nalik onomu što je Orso zamišljao. Zgodno, ali na onako grubu, široku čeljust. Zapanjujuće blijedo, štoviše, unatoč tamnim kovrčama. Više je nalikovao na Northmana nego na Stirijca.

en: “Honestly, I’d rather put it all behind me. What’s the point in having new generations if all we do is pick up the feuds of the old one?”
bs: — Iskreno, radije bih sve to ostavio iza sebe. Kakva je svrha novih naraštaja ako samo nastavljamo poduzimati stare zavade?

en: Jappo shrugged. “Here in Styria we had the Years of Blood, then the Years of Fire. There in the Union you had two wars with the Gurkish and two wars against the North. Then, to cap it off, we fought three wars against each other. Half a century of destruction. No one is asking me, but if they were, I would say that we could probably take a breath. Build something! Make the world better!” He seemed to remember himself and sat back. “And, you know, fuck. Make music.”
bs: Džapo slegnu ramenima."Ovdje u Stiriji imali smo Godine krvi, a potom Godine vatre. Tamo u Uniji imali ste dva rata protiv Gurkisha i dva rata protiv Sjevera. A onda, šećer na kraju, vodili smo tri rata međusobno. Pola stoljeća razaranja. Nitko me ne pita, ali kad bi pitao, rekao bih da bismo mogli malo udahnuti. Izgraditi nešto! Učiniti svijet boljim!" Činilo se kao da se sjetio se samoga sebe pa se zavalio. — I, znaš, jebati. Stvarati glazbu.

en: The woman gave him a towering sneer, then a disgusted hiss, and turned back to the cracked mirror, touching up the paint on her mouth with furious concentration.
bs: Žena mu uputi silan prezir, potom zgađeni hropac te se okrete natrag napuknutom zrcalu, popravljajući boju na usnama s bijesnom koncentracijom.

en: The thought gave him some fleeting satisfaction, but it was soon driven off by the pain in his thigh. He leaned against the wall to grip it, knead it, breathing hard through clenched teeth. He wished he’d brought his cane now, but he refused to look like a cripple. A band was tuning up somewhere, a flurry of screeching notes.
bs: Ta mu je pomisao pružila trenutno zadovoljstvo, ali ga ubrzo istisnu bol u bedru. Naslonio se na zid kako bi ga uhvatio i izmasirao, teško dišući stisnutih zuba. Žalio je što nije ponio Sticks, ali odbijao je izgledati poput bogalja. Negdje se u daljini ugađao orkestar, uz nalet kreštavih tonova.

en: “I’m afraid… I expect she’s probably working.” Leo cleared his throat, not knowing what the hell to do with her and deciding nothing was his best bet. Somewhere a female voice screeched furiously in Styrian, an endless flow of sing-song curses. “Do you know where the gaming hall is?”
bs: — Bojim se… pretpostavljam da vjerojatno radi. Leo pročisti grlo, ne znajući što bi zaboga mogao s njom te zaključivši kako mu je najbolje ne činiti ništa. Negdje u daljini ženski glas bijesno vrisnu na stirskom, ispaljujući beskrajnu bujicu pjevnih psovki. — Znaš li gdje je kockarnica?

en: “Treason,” said Orso, simply. “I may be facing a rather serious rebellion, and these rebels may be seeking your help. I want to convince you not to give it.”
bs: — Izdaja, odgovori Orso jednostavno. — Možda se suočavam s prilično ozbiljnom pobunom, a ti bi pobunjenici mogli tražiti vašu pomoć. Želim vas uvjeriti da im je ne pružite.

en: Orso gave a long sigh. “If I was willing to stab my own sister in the back, how could you possibly trust me? How could anyone? I could lie and say yes, then later renege, but I think we’ve all had enough of that sort of behaviour. I would rather be honest and say the best you’ll get from me is that things stay comfortably familiar. I will give up my claims on Talins. I’ve only ever seen the place in paintings. Take it with my blessing. Perhaps in time we can even join hands across the Circle Sea
bs: Orso teško uzdahnu. — Ako sam spreman zabiti vlastitoj sestri nož u leđa, kako bi meni uopće mogao vjerovati? Kako bi itko mogao? Mogao bih slagati i reći da pristajem, a onda kasnije prekršiti riječ, ali mislim da nam je svima dosta takvog ponašanja. Radije ću biti pošten i reći da je najbolje što od mene možeš dobiti to da stvari ugodno ostanu poznate. Odreći ću se svojih potraživanja na Talins. Taj sam grad vidio samo na slikama. Uzmi ga s mojim blagoslovom. Možda s vremenom uspijemo pružiti

en: “My mother would want me to promise you yes.” Jappo grinned very wide. “Then stab you in the back at the first opportunity.”
bs: — Moja bi majka htjela da ti obećam da hoću. Džapo se široko osmjehnu. — A onda da ti zabijem nož u leđa prvom prilikom.

en: Antaup started giggling, which didn’t help. He’d been giggling all the way from bloody Cardotti’s. “Pour me a drink, eh—”
bs: Antaup je počeo hrišati, što nije pomoglo. Hrišao je cijelim putem od prokletog Kardottija. — Nalij mi pića, Ain —

en: “Leo!” Jurand’s voice echoed at him from behind and Leo flinched, kept lurching on, didn’t look back.
bs: — Leo! — Džurandov mu se glas odjekivao izstraga, a Leo se trznuo, nastavio se kretati naprijed, nije se okrenuo.

en: He’d been hoping for Risinau. That would’ve been worrying enough. Judge was ten times worse. Worse ’cause she was far more clever and far more dangerous. Worse ’cause if she was in charge, reason was out the window and running for the hills. Worse ’cause the moment he saw her, he felt that guilty tickle, deep inside. The same one he got when he felt violence coming.
bs: Nadao se Risinauu. I to bi bilo dovoljno zabrinjavajuće. Džadž je bila deset puta gora. Gora jer je bila daleko pametnija i daleko opasnija. Gora jer je, ako je ona vodila glavnu riječ, razum bio izbačen kroz prozor i pobjegao glavom bez obzira. Gora jer je onog trena kad ju je ugledao osjetio onaj potmuli, grijehom natopljeni žmarac duboko u sebi. Isti onaj koji bi ga obuzeo kad god bi osjetio da se sprema nasilje.

en: Broad watched, caught somewhere between terrified and fascinated as she reached down, took the hem of her tattered skirts and pulled it up, up to show the writing tattooed around and around her thigh, long-winded quotes from some political treatise or other, and she slipped that leg over his and straddled him, knives and chains scraping against her breastplate as she perched herself on his lap.
bs: Brod ju je promatrao, razapet između užasa i opčinjenosti, dok se ona saginjala, hvatala rub svojih dronjavih suknji i podizala ga, podizala sve više kako bi otkrila natpis istetoviran ukrug po njezinim bedrima, dugačke citate iz nekakva političkog spisa, pa prebacila tu nogu preko njegove i zajahala ga, dok su joj noževi i Chains strugali o oklop namještajući se na njegovu krilu.

en: Judge smiled. Or at any rate showed her teeth. “Don’t try and trick a trickster. Or at least try a bit harder. The owners chisel our pay every unjust way they can and call it an honest wage. The Closed Council drafts a set of rules that make the rich richer and drive the poor to starve and call it an equality law. You know what they named the most low-lying, smog-choking, shit-stinking alley of rotten cellars in all of Valbeck?” She leaned a little closer to whisper it. “Primrose Heights. Callin
bs: Džadž se nasmiješila. Ili je barem pokazala zube. — Ne pokušavaj prevariti prevaranta. Ili se barem malo jače potrudi. Vlasnici nam režu plaću na svaki nepravedan način i nazivaju to poštenom nadnicom. Closed Council piše set pravila koja bogate čine još bogatijima, a siromašne tjeraju u glad te to nazivaju zakonom o jednakosti.
