Znaš li kako su nazvali najnižu, dimom zagušenu, smrdljivu uličicu trulih podruma u cijelom Valbeku?" Nagnula se malo bliže da to prošapće. — Primrose Heights. Nazvati n

en: “It is.” Broad’s voice had a scared squeak to it. Or was it an excited one? He had to keep a grip on himself. “The whole army of Angland. On the last day of summer, they’ll land on the coast of Midderland. Thousands of Stour Nightfall’s warriors, too. They’ll join up with the noblemen and they’ll march on Adua.”
bs: — Jest. Brodov je glas imao uplašeni cilik. Ili je bio uzbuđen? Morao se sabrati. — Cijela vojska Englenda. Posljednjeg dana ljeta iskrcat će se na obali Miderlanda. Tisuće ratnika Staura također. Pridružit će se plemićima i krenuti na Adua.

en: “You’ll get a say in how things are done. Might not be a Great Change, but it’ll be a change for the better. The Brocks have done some good up in Angland. Limits on workers’ hours. Rules to keep gears and driveshafts safe. Controls on truck shops and overseers’ penalties. All sorts o’ things the Breakers been after for years.”
bs: — Imat ćete pravo glasa u tome kako se stvari vode. Možda to neće biti Velika Promjena, ali bit će promjena nabolje. Obitelj Brok učinila je dosta toga dobroga gore u Englendu. Ograničenja radnih sati radnika. Pravila za sigurnost zupčanika i pogonskih osovina. Inspektorat nad tvorničkim dućanima i kaznama nadstojnika. Sve ono za čim Lomljači vape već godinama.

en: Swords glittered inside. A neat row of brand-new swords, all the same, with a long, straight, single-edged blade and a dull steel grip, fresh oiled from the foundry.
bs: Unutra su blistali mačevi. Uredan niz potpuno novih mačeva, posve jednakih, s dugačkom, ravnom, jednostrano naoštrenom oštricom i tupom čeličnom drškom, svježe nauljenih iz ljevaonice.

en: “Then there’s this.” Broad ripped the top from the biggest case, dragging a fistful of wood-shavings out of the way. Dull metal shone underneath. A great dark, tapering tube three strides long, and stamped into it: Armoury of Ostenhorm, 606.
bs: — Onda je tu i ovo. Brod razvali poklopac najvećeg sanduka, odgurnuvši u stranu pregršt strugotina drveta. Ispod njih zasja tup metal. Velika, tamna, sužena cijev dugačka tri koraka, na kojoj je bio utisnut natpis: Oružarnica Ostenhorma, 606.

en: “I tell the Brocks we’ve got a deal, there’s a full shipload waiting on the docks in Ostenhorm. Enough to arm a whole rebellion. And all they want is for you to speak to the Weaver, get the Breakers and Burners to do what they want to do anyway. Rise up, all at once. On the last day of summer. Throw up the barricades and fix the King’s Own where they are. Make sure they can’t come to help His Majesty. The Young Lion will do the rest.”
bs: — Kažem Brocksima da smo sklopili dogovor, cijeli brod tereta čeka na dokovima u Ostenhormu. Dovoljno da naoruža cijelu pobunu. A sve što oni žele jest da prozboriš s Weaverom, da navedeš Lomljače i Palitelje da učine ono što ionako žele učiniti. Da se dignu, svi odreda. Posljednjeg dana ljeta. Da podignu barikade i prikovanu ostanu Kraljevu gardu. Da se pobrinu da ne mogu priskočiti u pomoć Vašem Veličanstvu. Juvens Lav učinit će ostalo.

en: “It seems our letter-writer may have been a friend after all,” said Orso. “Or at least an honest enemy. King Jappo confirmed it all.”
bs: —— Čini se da nam je pisac pisma ipak bio prijatelj, reče Orso. — Ili barem pošten neprijatelj. Kralj Džapo potvrdio je sve.

en: “Superior Pike!” shrieked Glokta, so piercingly Orso was obliged to narrow his eyes as Pike walked in, black coat flapping.
bs: — Superior Pajk! zacvilje Glokta toliko prodorno da je Orso bio primoran zaškiljiti dok je Pajk ulazio, a Black mu se kaput nadimao.

en: Glokta’s brows went up, as though the question had never occurred before. “Move to the country? Pin butterflies to a board? Argue with my wife? I always wanted to write a book about fencing.”
bs: Glokta je podignuo obrve, kao da mu to pitanje još nikad nije palo na pamet. — Preseliti se u Country? Pribadati leptire na ploču? Svađati se sa ženom? Oduvijek sam htio napisati knjigu o mačevanju.

en: Arch Lector Pike stepped behind the desk. There was no chair now, of course, and so he stood, spreading his burned hands out on the leather top and frowning down at the ring on his finger. It seemed Glokta had found the one man even more monstrous than he as his replacement. But these were desperate times. And in desperate times, one must sometimes call upon the services of monsters.
bs: Glavni lektor Pajk zakoračio je iza pisaćeg stola. Stolice više nije bilo, stoga je ostao stajati, raširivši spržene ruke po kožnoj površini stola i mršteći se nad prstenom na svom prstu. Činilo se da je Glokta kao svoju zamjenu pronašao čovjeka koji je bio još monstruozniji od njega samog. No ovo su bila očajnička vremena. A u očajničkim vremenima čovjek ponekad mora zatražiti usluge čudovišta.

en: “Some in disused barracks outside the city. Some camped in woods and valleys. Some still at their old jobs, waiting for the call. But they can be gathered quickly.”
bs: — Nešto u napuštenim vojarnama izvan grada. Nešto u logorima po šumama i dolinama. Neki su još na svojim starim dužnostima i čekaju Poziv. No mogu se brzo okupiti.

en: The newly minted general glanced cautiously about, but there were few prying ears. Those without rebellions to crush were still in bed. “I can, Your Majesty, if you can gather more money.”
bs: Novopečeni general oprezno se osvrne oko sebe, ali radoznalih ušiju jedva da je bilo. Oni bez pobuna koje je trebalo ugušiti još su bili u krevetu. — Mogu, Vaša Uzvišenosti, ako vi možete skupiti više novca.

en: “The only real skill a king needs is to pick the best men to serve him. You may like to paint yourself as the least dependable man in the Union, but… I rather suspect it’s all a front. When it comes to it, I’m not sure there’s a man in the Circle of the World I trust more.”
bs: — Jedina stvarna Umijeće koja treba jednom kralju jest odabir najboljih Folk koji će mu služiti. Možda voliš prikazivati sebe kao najneodgovornijeg čovjeka u Uniji, ali… prilično sam sklon sumnjati da je sve to samo paravan. Kada dođe stisni do kapi, nisam siguran postoji li u Krugu svijeta čovjek kojem više vjerujem.

en: Brock’s treachery left the room even more stunned than Glokta’s resignation. Gorodets was tugging so hard at his beard Orso worried he might tear his lower jaw off. “Can we be sure?”
bs: Brodova izdaja ostavila je prostoriju još zatečenijom nego Gloktin odlazak. Gorodets je toliko snažno čupao svoju bradu da se Orso zabrinuo kako će si otkinuti donju čeljust. — Možemo li biti sigurni?

en: “Brock is loved in Angland,” said Pike, in his emotionless drone. “We are despised. As long as he makes no move against us, he is beyond our reach.”
bs: — Broka vole u Englendu, reče Pajk svojim ravnim, bezizražajnim glasom. — Nas preziru. Sve dok ne poduzme nikakav korak protiv nas, izvan je našeg dohvata.

en: An uneasy muttering swept the table. Brint clenched his fist even tighter. The high consul glanced furtively at Gorst. Hoff dabbed at his sweaty forehead with the fur-trimmed sleeve of his gown. The whole stuffy little room reeked of panic and suspicion. By the Fates, any one of the old bastards could have been the traitor.
bs: Nemirno mumljanje prostrujalo je oko stola. Brint je još čvršće stisnuo šaku. Visoki konzul kradomice pogleda Gorsta. Hoff si je obrubljenim rukavom odore potrao znojno Šef. Cijela je zagušljiva prostorijica zaudarala po panici i sumnji. Tako mi Sudbine, bilo koji od tih starih kopiladi mogao je biti izdajnik.

en: “He’s gone altogether,” said Vick. “Retired. Didn’t the lord marshal tell you? I’m here on the king’s personal orders. So you can forget about appealing to a higher authority. There isn’t one.”
bs: — Otišao je posve, odvrati Vik. — U mirovinu. Zar vam lord maršal nije rekao? Ovdje sam po izričitim kraljevskim zapovijedima. Stoga možete zaboraviti na žalbu višoj vlasti. Više je nema.

en: Vick slapped him across the face, and not gently. He gasped as his head snapped sideways, turned slowly back to stare at her in stunned disbelief, one trembling hand raised to his pinking cheek. She wondered if it was the first time someone ever hit him hard. A life of luxury is poor preparation for a beating. Who’d know better than her, the pampered daughter of the Master of the Royal Mints, suddenly snatched away to the mines of Angland?
bs: Vik ga ošamari po licu, i to nimalo nježno. Zadihao se dok mu je Šef odskočila u stranu, polako se okrenuo natrag da je pogleda u zaprepaštenu nevjerici, s jednom drhtavom rukom podignutom prema zajapurenom obrazu. Zapitala se je li mu to prvi put da ga je netko snažno udario. Život u luksuzu loša je priprema za batine. Tko bi to znao bolje od nje, razmažene kćeri Majstora kraljevske kovnice novca, iznenada odvučene u rudnike Englenda?

en: “Names!” He gasped and gurgled, tried to curl up into a ball, and she leaned over and punched him in the arse, caught his fruits and made him howl.
bs: — Imena! Zadihao se i grgljao, pokušavajući se sklupčati u klupko, a ona se nagnula i udarila ga u stražnjicu, dohvatila mu mošnje i natjerala ga da zavija.

en: “Have to say I’m surprised it was you.” Vick frowned over at Lord Marshal Brint. “Always took you for an honourable man.”
bs: — Moram priznati da me iznenađuje što si to bio ti. Vik se namršti prema lordu maršalu Brintu. — uvijek sam te držala časnim čovjekom.

en: “Inquisitor Teufel.” Glokta smiled up, showing the yawning gap in his front teeth. “Thank you for coming.”
bs: — Inkvizitore Tojfel. Glokta se nasmiješio prema gore, otkrivajući zjapeću prazninu među prednjim zubima. — Hvala vam što ste došli.

en: “You think you know someone…” murmured Vick, rubbing absently at her bruised knuckles as she frowned out at the sunlight glittering on the lake. People were boating, laughing, lounging on the banks. You would never have thought a civil war was coming. But then the worst betrayals often happen in good weather. When there’s a blizzard blowing, people are too busy huddling together.
bs: — Čovjek misli da nekoga poznaje… progunđa Vik odsutno trljajući natučene zglobove prstiju dok je namršteno promatrala sunčevu svjetlost kako blista na jezeru. Folk su veslali, smijali se, izležavali se na obalama. Čovjek nikada ne bi pomislio da se sprema građanski rat. No, najgora izdaja ionako se često događa po lijepom vremenu. Kad puše mećava, Folk su previše zauzeti stiskanjem jednih uz druge.

en: “Well.” Glokta looked towards the summer revellers. So near to them, yet somehow in a different world. “I have often said that life is the misery we endure between disappointments. Whatever the reasons, you have never once disappointed me. I wish I had been so reliable in return, but I fear I have let you down. I know how much you want to be… need to be… loyal.”
bs: — Dobro. Glokta pogleda prema ljetnim veseljacima. Tako blizu njih, a opet nekako u posve drugom svijetu."Često sam govorio da je život jad što ga podnosimo između razočaranja. Kakvi god bili razlozi, ti me nikada nisi razočarala. Volio bih da sam ja zauzvrat bio toliko pouzdan, no bojim se da sam te iznevjerio. Znam koliko želiš biti… moraš biti… odana."

en: She remembered that last glimpse of his face. The shock and the hurt as they dragged him away. She remembered it as if it was happening now.
bs: Sjetila se posljednjeg prizora njegova lica. Šoka i bola dok su ga odvlačili. Pamtit će to kao da se događa sada.

en: Broad knelt there, in the dirt, in the darkness, axe in his fist, frowning across bare mud studded with tree stumps. Towards the road and the ruined sawmill just beyond.
bs: Brod je klečao ondje, u blatu, u tami, sjekirom u šaci, mršteći se preko ogoljenog tla posijanog panjevima. Prema cesti i uništenoj pilani tik iza nje.

en: Broad shifted back into the shadows as he heard the faint sound of hoofs, rattling harness, grind of carriage wheels.
bs: Brod se povukao natrag u sjenu kad je čuo slabašan zvuk kopita, zveckanje opreme i škripanje kočionih kotača.

en: Broad eased closer to Judge. “This right?” he whispered, hardly able to make the words for the tightness in his throat. “They can’t fit three-dozen prisoners in that one wagon.”
bs: Brod se pomaknuo bliže Džadž. — Je li ovo u redu?, prošaptao je, jedva uspijevajući izustiti riječi od stiska u grlu. — Ne mogu u ta jedna kola stati trideset i dva zatvorenika.

en: There was a flash like lightning, the great scar through the forest lit brighter than day, the broken teeth of the stumps casting strange shadows, the outline of men and horses frozen for an instant before they were flung tumbling in a spurt of fire. A crashing explosion clapped off the trees, a whizzing like angry wasps, flicking and pinging in the undergrowth. Something thudded into the trunk beside them in a spray of splinters.
bs: Bljesnulo je poput munje, velika brazda kroz šumu zasjala je svjetlije nego po danu, slomljeni zubi panjeva bacali su neobične sjene, obrisi Folk i konja zaledili su se na trenutak prije nego što su odbačeni u kovitlacu vatre i plamena. Zaglušujuća eksplozija odbila se od stabala, zazujalo je poput bijesnih osa, zvrjeći i zviždeći u raslinju. Nešto je udarilo u stablo pored njih uz prasak i rasprskavanje iverja.

en: Broad’s axe caught him right between the eyes, knocked his hat off and snapped his head back, arms flung wide as if he was offering a hug. He flopped into a puddle, blood flooding from the slice out of his forehead.
bs: Brodova ga je Hachette pogodila ravno među oči, izbila mu šešir i trgnula glavu unatrag, a ruke su mu se raširile kao da nekoga želi zagrliti. Survao se u lokvu, a iz rane na čelu šikljala je krv.

en: Someone was screaming. “No! No! Please!” And then they were just screaming. Was it him? No, he had his teeth clenched, moaning and snarling through them, not even words, just heaved breath and sprayed spit. Couldn’t think. Couldn’t see. Prickling with sweat under his new breastplate.
bs: Netko je vrištao. — Ne! Ne! Molim te!" A onda su samo vrištali. Je li to bio on? Ne, stisnuo je zube, stenjao i režao kroz njih, bez suvislih riječi, samo s izdahnutim dahom i ispljuvkom. Nije mogao misliti. Nije mogao vidjeti. Znoj mu je peckao kožu pod novim oklopom.

en: He could hear someone whimpering. Judge’s voice as well, dripping menace. “Open this fucking carriage or we’ll crack it open!”
bs: Čuo je kako netko cvili. Džadžov glas također, iz kojeg se cijedila prijetnja. — Otvorite ovu jebenu kočiju ili ćemo je razbiti!

en: “All right!” came a muffled voice from inside. “I’m coming out.” There was the squeaking of bolts being drawn and the carriage’s iron door clattered open. Judge’s men started forward, dragged someone out. A small man in neat clothes, balding hair all messed-up and a bleeding cut on his scalp, some sort of case in his hand. Or no, chained to his wrist with heavy manacles.
bs: — U redu! dopro je prigušen glas iznutra. — Izlazim. Začuo se škripavi zvuk povlačenja zasuna, i željezna vrata kočije uz prasak su se otvorila. Džadžovi su Folk krenuli naprijed, izvukli nekoga van. Sitnog čovjeka u urednoj odjeći, s raščupanom prorijeđenom kosom i krvavom posjekotinom na tjemenu, s nekakvim kovčežićem u ruci. Ili bolje rečeno, s okovima privezanim za zglob teškim verigama.

en: “This was about money?” Broad was having trouble thinking with the throbbing in the side of his head. Maybe he always had trouble thinking. He watched one of the Burners rooting through the pockets of a soldier’s mangled corpse. Must’ve been close to the cannon when it went off. He hardly had anything left you could even call a head. “What’s the bank got to do with anything?”
bs: — Ovdje je bila riječ o novcu? Brodu je bilo teško razmišljati s pulsiranjem u sljepoočnici. Možda mu je uvijek bilo teško razmišljati. Promatrao je kako jedan od Palitelja pretražuje džepove unakaženoga leša nekog vojnika. Mora da je bio blizu topa kad je opalio. Jedva da je išta ostalo od njega što bi se moglo nazvati glavom. — Kakve banka ima veze s išta od ovoga?

en: “I find you guilty of offences against the people,” said Judge. “Of usury, false dealing and profiting from misery. Of delaying the Great Change. And most of all, of selling your arse to those twin plagues Valint and Balk.”
bs: — Proglašavam te krivim za nedjela protiv naroda, reče Džadž. — Za lihvarenje, varanje i izvlačenje koristi iz bijede. Za odgađanje Velike Promjene. I povrh svega, za prodaju vlastite guzice onim dvjema napastima Valintu i Balku.

en: “Fuck!” snarled Broad, and his axe took the man’s arm off just above the wrist with a meaty thunk, spattering everyone around the stump with blood.
bs: — Jebote! prosikće Brod, i njegova Hachette odsječe čovjeku ruku neposredno iznad zapešća uz mesnati tup, poprskavši krvlju sve oko panja.

en: “Deeds and contracts and legal whatever-the-fuck.” She started to drop them into the flames, paper covered in swirling calligraphy blackening and curling as it caught light. “Won’t be worth shit when the Great Change comes, eh?” And she grinned up at Broad, letting the rest slide from her fingers into the fire. “Once our very good friends the Brocks throw down the king, we can decide afresh who owns what, who owes what.”
bs: — Tapije i ugovori i pravna sranja. Počela ih je bacati u plamen, papir prekriven nakinđurenim krasnopisom crnio se i uvijao hvatajući vatru. — Neće vrijediti pišljiva boba kad Velika Promjena dođe, zar ne? I nasmiješila se Brodu, puštajući ostatak da joj klizne iz prstiju u vatru. "Jednom kad naši jako dobri prijatelji Brocks svrgnu kralja, moći ćemo iznova odlučiti tko što posjeduje, tko što duguje."

en: Savine blinked at him. The truth was she had only loved one man, and he was the one they were going to war with. Love was unlucky. An encumbrance. She smiled, and pressed her hand against his, and felt their baby shift underneath it. “I love you, too,” she said, and shut him up with a kiss. There was plenty to like about Leo, after all. Especially at the head of an army. But there were some tasks he was not suited for.
bs: Savine trepnu. Istina je bila ta da je voljela samo jednog muškarca, a upravo su s njim išli u rat. Ljubav je donosila nesreću. Bila je teret. Nasmiješila se, pritisnula svoju ruku o njegovu i osjetila kako se beba pomaknula ispod njezinih prstiju. — I ja tebe volim, prošaptala je i ušutkala ga poljupcem. naposljetku, kod Lea se imalo što voljeti. Posebno kad se nalazio na čelu vojske. No postojali su zadaci za koje jednostavno nije bio stvoren.

en: The young lieutenant who’d been given the job of watching her hurried after, pink with embarrassment. “I tried to keep her out of the way, Your Grace, but—”
bs: Juvens poručnik koji je bio zadužen za Inspektorat nad njom požurio je za njom, crven od nelagode. — Pokušao sam je držati podalje, Vaša Milosti, ali — "

en: Savine felt a chill creeping up her back, then. As though, in spite of all her long preparations, because no one had actually said the words, she had not realised quite what they were about. That chill became colder yet as she recognised another familiar face. Yoru Sulfur, that humble representative of the Order of Magi, slipping through the crowds towards Lady Finree’s side.
bs: Tada je Savine osjetila kako joj studen puže niz leđa. Kao da usprkos svim svojim dugim pripremama, zato što nitko nije izgovorio prave riječi, nije sasvim shvaćala o čemu je riječ. Ta se studen još više sledila kad je prepoznala još jedno poznato lice. Joru Salfur, skromni predstavnik Reda magova, provlačio se kroz gomilu prema strani lady Finri.

en: “I seem to remember a battle at Red Hill!” he snapped, cheeks flushed red with anger. “I turned the tide there when no one else could!”
bs: — Čini mi se da se sjećam bitke kod Crvenog Brda! kresnuo je, obraza zajapurenih od bijesa. — Ondje sam preokrenuo tijek bitke kad nitko drugi nije mogao!

en: “People will be hurt.” Savine was disappointed to see there were tears in Finree’s eyes. She really was throwing away all the respect anyone used to have for her. “People will die!”
bs: — Folk će stradati. Savine se razočarala ugledavši suze u Finreeinim očima. Doista je odbacivala svako poštovanje koje je itko prije gajio prema njoj. — Folk će ginuti!

en: “I’m Corleth.” The girl frowned at Rikke, then Isern, then Shivers, like she was daring them to call her a liar. “And I want to fight.” She snarled the last word like a curse. Reminded Rikke of one o’ those mean little dogs that’ll take on anything, no matter how big.
bs: — Ja sam Corleth. Djevojka se mrsko pogleda na Rike, pa na Izern, pa na Šivers, kao da ih izaziva da je nazovu lažljivicom."A ja hoću boriti se." Posljednju riječ zagrknu kao prokletstvo. Podsjetila je Rike na jednog od onih zlih malih psića što će se baciti na sve, bez obzira na veličinu.

en: Rikke had called, half-expecting she’d be ignored, but folk had answered and then some. They’d come in a trickle, then a flow, then a flood, from every village, farmstead and woodsman’s hut in the Protectorate. The smiths and fletchers of Uffrith had worked their hands raw the past few weeks arming folk, then they’d stuck on helmets themselves and joined the throng. Some of the town’s women had even took a break from nattering at the well to stitch Rikke a standard of her own. A big eye, with ru
bs: Rike bijaše pozvala, pola očekujući da će je ignorirati, no Folk bijaše odazvao se i više nego to. Došli su kap po kap, pa u tok, pa u potop, iz svake vasi, seljačke kuće i drvnjače u Protectorateu. Kovači i streličari Afrita radili su rukama do krvi prošlih tjedana oružujući Folk, pa su sami natukli kacige i pridružili se gomili. Neke od gradskih žena maknuvši se čak od šepkanja bunarima da bi šile Rike svoj vlastiti stajer. Veliko Oko, s runama oko sebe onakvima kakve su joj utetovirane u lice

en: “Open your ears, you fucking maggots!” screamed Isern-i-Phail, so loud Rikke flinched at it. But silence fell, and everyone turned towards her. So many faces, choking the square and the streets about it. More of her people than she’d ever seen gathered in one place. More than she’d known she had. Made her heart swell, to see them come out on her say-so. She thought of how proud her father would’ve been as she clambered up on the wall beside Isern, and it gave her a lump in her throat. She pushed
bs: — Otvorite uši, jebeni crvi! vrisnula je Izern-i-Fejl tako glasno da se Rike trgnula. No nastupila je tišina i svi su se okrenuli prema njoj. Toliko lica koja su gušila Trg i okolne ulice. Više njezina naroda nego što ih je ikada vidjela na jednome mjestu. Više nego što je znala da ih ima. Srce joj je zaigralo kad ih je vidjela kako su došli na njezinu riječ. Pomislila je na to koliko bi njezin otac bio ponosan dok se pentrala na zid pored Izern, i stisnulo joj se grlo. Odbacila je kapuljaču koj

en: “Aye,” muttered Rikke, “but no one ever died from talking a good fight.” She rubbed at her own neck like she could rub away the nerves that had gathered there. “Fighting one’s another matter.”
bs: — Jest, prozbori Rike, ali nitko nikad nije umro od dobrog govorenja o borbi. Protrljala je vlastiti vrat kao da može izbrisati strepnju koja se tu nakupila. — Boriti se posve je druga stvar.

en: Clover shrugged. “I’ve seen a few, and by and large they were about like this one. Lots of men turning up with weapons. Sort of the point of the thing.”
bs: Klover slegnu ramenima. — Vidio sam ih nekoliko, i uglavnom su bili otprilike nalik ovome. Puno Folk koji se pojave s oružjem. Otprilike i jest u tome stvar.

en: “You’re set on this, then?” Black Calder stepped from the staircase and out onto the gatehouse roof, grey-streaked hair plastered to his pale frown by the rain. He looked sourer by the day. Like milk left out in the sun.
bs: — Znači, čvrsto si odlučio? Black Kalder zakorači sa stubišta na krov utvrde, a kosa prošarana sjedinama bila mu je od kiše zalijepljena za blijedo Šef. Iz dana u dan izgledao je sve kiselije. Poput mlijeka ostavljenog na suncu.

en: Stour seemed to guess the way Clover was thinking and gave one of those sly sideways winks of his, like they were all caught up together in the same funny secret. “But we never had Angland on our side before.”
bs: Staur kao da nasluti Kloverove misli te ga prostrijeli jednim od onih svojih lukavih namiga, kao da su oba upletena u istu smiješnu tajnu. — Ali dosad nikad nismo imali Englend na svojoj strani.

en: “Then I’ll fight ’em and I’ll win!” snarled Stour, showing his teeth. The sun came out then, peeping through a patch in the cloud, and brought a sparkle from the marching men. “Look at that!” There was a rainbow over the road south towards Ollensand. “A good omen, I reckon. An archway we’ll march through to victory!”
bs: — Onda ću se boriti protiv njih i pobijedit ću! odbrusi Staur, pokazujući zube. Sunce tada iziđe, provirujući kroz pukotinu u oblacima, te izmami iskru na marširajućim ljudima. — Pogledaj to! Nad cestom koja je vodila prema jugu prema Ollensandu stajala je duga. — Dobar znak, rekao bih. Slavoluk kroz koji ćemo umarširati u pobjedu!

en: “Mmmm.” Clover remembered the crunching as Bethod’s skull was smashed to mush. The thud as his body dropped in the Circle.
bs: — Mmmm. Klover se sjećao krckanja dok se Bethodova lubanja razbijala u kašu. Tupog udarca kad mu je tijelo palo u Round.

en: “If things turn sour over there, do whatever you have to, you understand? Bring him back alive. Do that, I’ll see you rewarded.”
bs: — Ako stvari tamo pođu po zlu, učini što god moraš, razumiješ? Vrati ga živog. Učini to, pobrinut ću se da budeš nagrađen.

en: “Out of the question,” said Orso. “Believe me, Lord Chamberlain, I would much prefer to be in my bed than my saddle, but this rebellion is like a fire in a distillery. If it is not stamped out at once it will spread. And I have to be seen to stamp it out.”
bs: — Nikakvog govora o tome, odvrati Orso."Vjerujte mi, lord-komornaru, radije bih bio u svom krevetu nego u sedlu, ali ova je pobuna poput vatre u destileriji. Ako se ne ugasi odmah, proširit će se. A Folk me mora vidjeti kako je gasim."

en: “No reliable sightings so far, Your Majesty,” said Pike, “but we have eyes on every beach, bay and wharf. If Lord Heugen told us the truth, we expect them to land tomorrow.”
bs: — Još nema pouzdanih dojava, Vaša Uzvišenosti, odvrati Pajk, "no motrimo svaku plažu, uvalu i pristanište. Ako nam je lord Heugen rekao istinu, očekujemo ih sutra.

en: “We need to prepare, Your Majesty,” said Hoff. “Tread carefully. Play for time. Gather all the troops we can.”
bs: — Moramo se pripremiti, Vaša Uzvišenosti, posavjetuje Hoff."Nastupati oprezno. Kupovati vrijeme. Sakupiti svu vojsku koju možemo.

en: Forest cleared his throat. “Your Majesty, if that’s all, we really should…” And he nodded towards the theoretical entrance to the tent, where Gorst was holding back a sweaty, panicky, impatient crush of messengers.
bs: Forest se prokašlja. — Vaša Uzvišenosti, ako je to sve, uistinu bismo trebali…" I kimnu glavom prema teoretskom ulazu u šator, gdje je Gorst zadržavao znojan, paničan i nestrpljiv metež glasnika.

en: “Organise some scouting parties, fan out, see if you can make contact with Isher and the rest of the Open Council’s troops. Where’s Stour due to land?”
bs: — Organizirajte izvidnice, raširite se, provjerite možete li stupiti u kontakt s Išerom i ostatkom postrojbi Otvorenog vijeća. Gdje bi Staur trebao pristati?

en: Orders were being called now, boots splashing in the surf and scraping in the shingle, a reassuring clamour of activity as the men of Angland began to pour from the boats and onto the beach.
bs: Sada su se čule vikane zapovijedi, pljuskanje čizama po plićaku i struganje po žalu, ohrabrujuća vreva posla dok su se Folk iz Englenda počeli iskrcavati iz čamaca na plažu.

en: Savine was so used to proving there was nothing she could not do, she rarely pondered whether there might be things better not attempted. Riding while heavily pregnant at the head of a military campaign mired by foul weather proved to be in that latter category.
bs: Savine je bila toliko naviknuta dokazivati da ne postoji ništa što ne može učiniti da je rijetko kad razmišljala postoje li stvari koje je bolje ne pokušavati. Jahanje u visokoj trudnoći na čelu vojnog pohoda zaglibljenog u lošem vremenu pokazalo se upravo tom drugom kategorijom.

en: There was a flash on the horizon, claws of trees caught black against the brightness. A moment later thunder crackled, and a horse reared and dumped one of Leo’s aides face first into a hedge. Savine’s own mount trembled, shuffled fearfully sideways, and she shushed in its ear, patted its neck, stroked her belly, trying to calm her struggling horse and her kicking baby and the rampaging storm all at once and wondering who the hell would calm her.
bs: Na obzoru bljesnu svjetlost, a siluete stabala ocrtavše se crno na blještavoj pozadini. Trenutak kasnije zagrme grom, konj se digao na stražnje noge i strmoglavio jednog od Leovih pobočnika naglavačke u živicu. Savinin vlastiti konj zatrese se, uplašeno uzmaknu u stranu, a ona ga je ušutkavala na uho, milovala po vratu, gladila trbuh, pokušavajući istodobno umiriti uznemirenu životinju, dijete koje ju je udaralo i divlju oluju, pitajući se tko će pobogu umiriti nju.

en: There was a collective gasp as men sagged in their saddles. “It’s the Young Lion!” called Leo, reassuring laughter in his voice. “No need to piss yourselves!”
bs: Prolomio se zajednički uzdah iznenađenja dok su se Folk opustili u sedlima. — To je Juvens Lav!" doviknuo je Leo, dok mu je u glasu podrhtavao umirujući smijeh. — Nema potrebe da se upišate u gaće!

en: “Most of ’em,” called Jin. “Stour’s somewhere to the east but half his boats drifted. In this weather, who knows where they’ll wash up?”
bs: — Većina njih, odvratio je Jin. — Staur je negdje na istoku, ali pola mu se čamaca odvagalo. U ovom vremenu, tko zna gdje će ih isprati?

en: “Damn it!” Leo held one up to the inadequate lamplight, set flickering as someone shoved the door wide and wind whipped through the room. “Can we get a decent light in here? Is this map accurate?”
bs: — Prokletstvo! Leo podigne jednu prema slabom svjetlu svjetiljke, koja zatreperi kad netko širom otvori vrata i vjetar prošiša prostorijom. — Možemo li dobiti pristojno svjetlo ovdje? Je li ova karta točna?

en: He looked about, realising all the soldiers had stopped their business to look at him, and nervously cleared his throat. “Nice evening for it.”
bs: Osvrne se oko sebe, shvativši da su svi vojnici prekinuli svoj posao kako bi ga promatrali, pa nervozno prokašlje. — Lijepa večer za ovo.

en: Zuri stood with hands on hips, looking down at a pair of empty milking pails, yoke still attached and propped on top.
bs: Zuri je stajala s rukama na bokovima, zagledana u par praznih kanti za mužnju, dok im je jaram još uvijek stajao prislonjen odozgo.

en: Savine shut her eyes, tears of gratitude prickling the lids. “What the hell would I do without your family? I’ve no idea how you can stay so calm.”
bs: Savine zatvori oči, a suze zahvalnosti zagreboše je pod vjeđama. — Što bih u ime svega svoga učinila bez vaše obitelji? Pojma nemam kako uspijevaš ostati tako smirena.

en: He did not look like a man with good news, it had to be said. Even in Valbeck, during the uprising, even when things got bad, he had always seemed hopeful, at least. Now he looked grim. Brows wrinkled, fists clenched. For a moment, the sight of him, scabbed head nearly brushing the low ceiling, gave Savine the slightest twinge of fear. An echo of the terror when she first saw his great silhouette on the barricade in Valbeck.
bs: Moglo se reći da nije izgledao kao čovjek s dobrim vijestima. Čak ni u Valbeku, za vrijeme pobune, čak ni kad bi stvari krenule po zlu, uvijek je djelovao barem donekle nadobudno. Sada je izgledao turobno. Obrve nabrane, šake stisnute. Na tren joj je taj prizor, s krastavom glavom koja je umalo doticala niski strop, utjerao u kosti blagi tračak straha. Odjek užasa koji je osjetila kad ga je prvi put ugledala u golemoj silueti na barikadi u Valbeku.

en: “Hope can’t hurt.” But Broad gave the strong impression that he did not think it would help much, either.
bs: — Nada ne može škoditi. No Brod odavaše snažan dojam da ne misli kako će od nje biti previše koristi.

en: Important news, for the important man. He puffed himself up, turned frowning to the busy yard. “Clear a path there! This woman needs to see the Lord Governor!”
bs: Važna vijest za važnog čovjeka. Naduo se od važnosti, okrenuvši se namrgođeno prema užurbanom dvorištu. — Raščistite put! Ova žena mora vidjeti lorda guvernera!

en: “Master Broad saved my life during the uprising in Valbeck,” said Savine. “And I shared the carriage there with Inquisitor Teufel.”
bs: — Majstor Brod spasio mi je život tijekom ustanka u Valbeku, reče Savine. — I dijelila sam kočiju ondje s inkvizitorom Tojfelom.

en: “Everyone’s loyalties are a touch tangled these days.” She hooked out the chair at the head of the table with her foot and dropped into it, meeting Savine’s eye. “I like to think I never let your father down. He got me out of the camps. I owed him. But he’s gone now.”
bs: — Svačija je odanost u ovo vrijeme pomalo zamršena. Izvukla je nogom stolicu s čela stola i srušila se u nju, susrevši Savinin Oko. — Volim misliti da nikad nisam iznevjerila tvog oca. Izbavio me iz logora. Bila sam mu dužna. No njega više nema.

en: “You’re right to be suspicious, though,” she said. “There’s a hell of a lot at stake. That’s why the lord marshal gave me this.” And she twisted Brint’s ring from her finger and tossed it into the dish with the sausages.
bs: — Ipak, u pravu si što sumnjaš, dometnu ona. — Mnogo je toga na kocki. Zbog toga mi je lord maršal Dow ovo. I skinula je Brintov prsten s prsta te ga ubacila u tanjur s kobasicama.

en: Worse than she’d feared. The rebels might outnumber the loyalists two to one. She smiled as though it was better than she’d hoped. “You might outnumber him four to one.”
bs: Gore nego što se pribojavala. Pobunjenici bi mogli nadmašiti lojaliste u omjeru dva naprema jedan. Nasmiješila se kao da je situacija bolja nego što se nadala. — Možda ih nadmašujete četiri naprema jedan.

en: “We just wanted the sheep!” One of ’em bleated from the pen, as if to lend support to that part of Dancer’s story if no other. “We even asked nicely.”
bs: — Mi smo htjeli samo ovce! zableja netko iz tora, kao da želi dati potporu tom dijelu Danserove priče, ako već nijednom drugom. — Čak smo lijepo zamolili.

en: “Then the woman set to screaming and, well…” Dancer winced down at the mud. “It went wrong, is all. You never had anything go wrong, Clover?”
bs: — Onda je žena počela vrištati i, pa… Danser se trgnuo gledajući u blato. — Pošlo je po zlu, eto. Zar se tebi nikad nije dogodilo da nešto pođe po zlu, Kloveru?

en: If there had been a time when Clover was impressed by wheedling, it was far in the past. “Not up to me, is it? If Stour lets it go, I guess it’s gone.”
bs: Ako je i postojalo vrijeme kad je Klovera impresioniralo cendravo umiljavanje, to je bilo davno u prošlosti. — Ne ovisi o meni, zar ne? Ako Staur prijeđe preko toga, pretpostavljam da je gotovo.

en: And who should burst from the trees but the Young Lion and a crowd of his bastards. They reined in so Stour and his lot were sneering bitter scorn from one side of the yard, Brock and his lot scowling righteous outrage on the other. Seemed the Young Lion hadn’t reached the point where tragedies became chores. If anything, he tended towards too much feeling.
bs: A tko je drugi izbio iz šume negoli Young Lion i gomila njegovih kopiladi. Zategnuli su uzde tako da su Staur i njegovi s jedne strane dvorišta sipali gorki prijezir, dok su se Brok i njegovi s druge mrštili u pravedničkom gnjevu. Činilo se kako Young Lion još nije dosegao točku u kojoj tragedije postaju obični poslovi. Ako išta, naginjao je tomu da osjeća previše.

en: “Last I checked, I was King o’ the Northmen.” Stour leaned towards Brock with that mad gleam in his wet eyes, catching hold of his chain and giving it a shake so the diamond he’d torn from his uncle’s cut throat danced. “These fuckers are Northmen. So I’ll say what’s done with ’em.”
bs: — Koliko se sjećam, ja sam kralj Sjevernjaka. Staur se nagnuo prema Broku s onim luđačkim sjajem u vlažnim očima, uhvativši mu lanac i prodrmavši ga tako da je dijamant otrgnut s ujakova prerezana grla zaigrao."Ovi su gadovi Sjevernjaci. Tako da ja odlučujem što će biti s njima."

en: His turn to wrench his horse around and ride off, showering everyone with dirt. Dancer stared at the ground. Prettyboy frowned bitterly at his bow. The fat one set to sobbing again. The corpses, naturally, were unmoved.
bs: Dođe red na nj da okrene konja i odjaše, zasuvši sve oko sebe zemljom. Danser zagleda u tlo. Lijepi se gorko namršti na svoj luk. Debeljko se ponovo dade u jecanje. Leševi, posve prirodno, ostadoše netaknuti.

en: A gentle green hill with a few trees at the crown overlooked the town on the right. Perhaps it would have been more military to say east. Or was it west? For some reason north and south were instinctive, but the other points of the compass always took a moment for Orso to work through. On the left of the town, across the river, there was a steeper hill studded with rocky outcrops. A bluff, might a surveyor have called it?
bs: Blagi zeleni brežuljak s nekoliko stabala na vrhu nadvijao se nad gradom s desne strane. Možda bi vojnički ispravnije bilo reći na istoku. Ili je to bio zapad? Iz nekog razloga Sjever i South dolazili su mu instinktivno, ali Orsu je uvijek trebalo malo vremena da odredi druge strane svijeta. S lijeve strane grada, preko rijeke, uzdizalo se strmije brdo načičkano golim stijenama. Bi li to geodet nazvao hridinom?

en: “Not at all, my dear sir, yours is a delightful burg.” Orso gestured towards the buildings about the square. Several fine old houses, a guildhall with a marble façade, a tavern with a half-timbered upper floor, a covered marketplace with its sagging roof held up on squat pillars. Progress had largely left this corner of the Union alone, it could barely have changed in two centuries. “The very quintessence of rural Midderland! In happier times I would delight in a tour, but I hope you will forgiv
bs: — Nipošto, dragi moj gospodine, vaš je gradić doista ugodan. Orso mahnu rukom prema građevinama oko trga. Nekoliko lijepih starih kuća, vijećnica s mramornim pročeljem, krčma s poludrvenim gornjim katom, natkrivena tržnica čiji se pognuti krov oslanjao na zdepaste stupove. Naprijed je uglavnom zaobišao ovaj kutak Unije, jedva da se ikakvo što promijenilo u posljednja dva stoljeća. — Prava esencija ruralnog Miderlanda! U sretnijim vremenima uživao bih u razgledavanju, no nadam se da ćete mi opros

en: Overseeing the work with the same total lack of emotion with which he had once overseen the hanging of two hundred Breakers, white clothes pristine in the afternoon sun, was Arch Lector Pike.
bs: Nadgledajući radove s onom istoznačnom, potpunom odsutnošću emocija s kojom je nekoć nadgledao vješanje dvjesto Lomljača, u snježnobijeloj odjeći koja je blistala na popodnevnom suncu, stajao je vrhovni Lektor Pajk.

en: “Their first scouts.” Forest rubbed at his grizzled jaw. “Even with the roads in the state they are, their main body should be with us before sunset.”
bs: — Njihove prve izvidnice. Forest protrlja svoju prosijedu čeljust. — Unatoč stanju u kakvom su ceste, glavnina njihovih snaga trebala bi nam se pridružiti prije zalaska sunca.

en: “Three loyal members of the Open Council are a few miles away to the west.” Pike pointed off beyond the orchards. “Lords Stenner, Crant and Ingenbeck, with perhaps a thousand men between them.”
bs: — Trojica vjernih članova Otvorenog vijeća nalaze se nekoliko milja zapadno. Pajk dade znak prema voćnjacima. — Lords Stenner, Crant i Ingenbeck, s možda tisuću Folk s njima.

en: “I told them a tale,” said Vick. “That you’re disorganised and short on men. That Brint has prevented any chance of reinforcements. The Lioness had her doubts, but her husband swallowed it whole, I think.”
bs: — Ispričala sam im priču, reče Vik. — Da ste neorganizirani i u manjku Folk. Da je Brint spriječio svaku mogućnost dolaska pojačanja. Lavica je imala sumnji, ali njezin je muž to progutao kao mamac, čini mi se.

en: Another ugly pause. From the concerned looks on the faces about him, Orso gathered that was more than they had hoped. “How many are we?” he asked, unable to keep a wheedling note from his voice.
bs: Još jedna mučna stanka. Prema zabrinutim izrazima lica oko sebe, Orso je zaključio da je to više nego što su se nadali. — Koliko nas je?" upita, ne uspijevajući suzbiti molbeni ton u glasu.

en: As luck would have it, the perfect man appeared to be within arm’s reach. “Arch Lector Pike?” asked Orso. “I believe you have experience on the battlefield?”
bs: Kakve li sreće, činilo se da je savršen čovjek nadohvat ruke. — Nadlektor Pajk?" upita Orso. — Vjerujem da imate iskustva s bojišta?

en: A breeze came up, and took the Steadfast Standard, and made the white horse against the gilded sun flap and ripple. The very flag under which Casamir had conquered Angland. Witness to so many military glories down the centuries. Orso wondered if there was any chance of it presiding over another.
bs: Zapuhnu povjetarac, prihvati Zastavu postojanosti te natjera bijelog konja pod pozlaćenim suncem da zatreperi i uzbiba se. Upravo onu zastavu pod kojom je Kazimir pokorio Englend. Svjedokinju tolikih vojnih slava kroz stoljeća. Orso se zapita postoji li ikakva šansa da ona presudi još jednoj.

en: “Hmmm.” Orso narrowed his eyes towards that tower house on the hill, wondering if the Young Lion was at that very moment considering the position through his eyeglass. “Colonel Gorst?”
bs: — Hm. Orso suzi oči motreći onaj utvrđeni dvorac na brežuljku te se zapita promatra li Juvens Lav u ovom točno trenutku taj položaj kroz durbin. — Pukovniče Gorst?

en: “Hard to say. In the centre, they look well dug in, but the hills are weaker held. I see some King’s Own standards. Some others I don’t recognise.”
bs: — Teško je reći. U središtu djeluju dobro utvrđeni, ali brda su slabije branjena. Vidim neke stjegove Kraljeve straže. Nekoliko ih ne prepoznajem.

en: Leo couldn’t have asked for a more splendid group around him: Lords Isher and Barezin and a good twenty other members of the Open Council, Lord Mustred and a dozen other noblemen of Angland, as well as Stour’s man Greenway and Rikke’s man Hardbread. And yet he felt very much alone as the king’s standard-bearer reined in his snorting mount on the hillside, the Steadfast Standard snapping majestically with the breeze and two dozen Knights of the Body in full battle armour clattering to a halt behi
bs: Leo nije mogao poželjeti sjajnije društvo oko sebe: lordove Išera i Barezina te dobrih dvadesetak drugih članova Otvorenog vijeća, lorda Mustreda i tucet drugih plemića iz Englenda, kao i Staurova čovjeka Grinveja te Rikina čovjeka Hardbreda. Pa ipak, osjećao se posve usamljeno kada je kraljevski stjegonoša zauzdao svoga konja koji je frktao na obronku, dok se nepokolebljivi stijeg veličanstveno presavijao na povjetarcu, a dvadesetak Vitezova tijela u punom bojnom oklopu uz tresak se zaustavilo

en: “I’ve dabbled with higher, my lords,” said Tunny, grinning, “but it never suited me. Carrying His Majesty’s standard is as much honour as I can manage.”
bs: — Okušao sam se i s višima, gospodo moja, reče Tani nasmiješeno, "ali to mi nikada nije odgovaralo. Nošenje stijega Njegova Veličanstva počast je preko koje mogu podnijeti.

en: “I’ll give the orders,” growled Leo, and Barezin sank grumpily into the roll of fat under his chin. “Please convey my thanks to His Majesty. He’ll have my answer within the hour.”
bs: — Ja ću izdati zapovijedi, prosikta Leo, a Barezin se mrzovoljno usiječe u nabore sala pod podbradkom. — Molim te, prenesi moju zahvalnost Vašem Veličanstvu. Dobit će moj odgovor unutar Straža vremena.

en: Leo winced. Maybe two could easily mean three. It wouldn’t be enough to push Orso back, he had to crush him. Could they do it in the lag end of an afternoon? He shaded his eyes, trying to work through the distances, the times, but there was so much to consider, his sight danced and his head buzzed with it all. He turned to ask Jurand’s opinion, then remembered, and felt the sting of disappointment and betrayal all over again. He was the only one of Leo’s friends who’d ever really had an opinion
bs: Leo se trgnu. Možda za dva lako je moglo značiti tri. Neće biti dovoljno samo potisnuti Orsa natrag, morao ga je smrviti. Mogu li to učiniti u samom smiraju popodneva? Zastrije oči dlanom pokušavajući proračunati udaljenosti i vrijeme, ali toliko je toga trebalo uzeti u obzir da mu se vid mutio, a u glavi mu je bumljao roj misli. Okrenu se pitati Džuranda za mišljenje, a onda se prisjeti te ponovno osjeti oštru bol razočaranja i izdaje. On bijaše jedini od Leovih prijatelja koji je ikad doista i

en: Had his mother been right? Was he no general? He caught himself wishing she was with him and forced the thought away. By the dead, he was the Young Lion! But courage and a loud roar wouldn’t be enough. Antaup was right, it was bad ground. Men would die taking those positions. Good men. Friends like Ritter and Barniva, killed by his recklessness.
bs: Je li mu majka bila u pravu? Zar on nije nikakav general? Uhvatio se kako priželjkuje da je s njim i otjerao tu pomisao. Tako mu mrtvih, on je Juvens Lav! No hrabrost i glasna Rike neće biti dovoljni. Antaup je bio u pravu, teren je bio loš. Folk će ginuti osvajajući te položaje. Dobri Folk. Prijatelji poput Rittera i Barnive, ubijeni zbog njegove nepromišljenosti.

en: Rikke squatted in the wet woods, fretting at the old dowel around her neck, going over and over her own tooth marks with her thumbtip.
bs: Rike je čučala u vlažnoj šumi, vrteći oko vrata stari drveni klin i vrhom palca prelazeći iznova i iznova preko tragova vlastitih zubi.

en: She fiddled at her dowel, fiddled, fiddled. Truth was she hadn’t needed it for months. Let alone a fit, she’d barely had a quiver since she came down from the forbidden lake with the runes on her face. She’d always hated having to wear the damn thing, but here she was hanging on to it. Some last shred of childhood. Some hint of a past where she didn’t have to make the hard choices.
bs: Vrtjela je onaj klin, vrtjela i vrtjela. Istina je bila da joj nije trebao mjesecima. A kamoli da je imala napadaj, jedva da je osjetila i podrhtavanje otkad se spustila s zabranjenog jezera s runama na licu. Oduvijek je mrzjela to što mora nositi prokletu stvar, ali sad se grčevito držala za nju. Nekakav posljednji ostatak djetinjstva. Nekakav nagovještaj prošlosti u kojoj nije morala donositi teške odluke.

en: His shout became a gurgle as the bald man stabbed him in the throat and shoved him back into the shadows of the tunnel. Proof once again that a little gold can succeed where a lot of steel might fail. He raised his lamp and stood politely out of the way as Shivers rushed past, leading a steady flood of armed men into Carleon.
bs: Vrisak mu se pretvorio u hropac kad ga je ćelavi čovjek ubo u grlo i gurnuo natrag u sjenu tunela. Još jedan dokaz da malo zlata može uspjeti tamo gdje gomila čelika možda podbaci. Podignuo je svjetiljku i učtivo se izmaknuo s puta dok je Šivers jurio pokraj njega, predvodeći neprekidnu bujicu naoružanih Folk u Carleon.

en: The Nail was leaning against a wall, using a dagger to carefully drill a hole in the pointy end of an egg. He’d a way of standing very still, nothing moving until it had to.
bs: Najl se naslanjao na zid, brižljivo bušeći rupicu bodežom na šiljastom vrhu jajeta. Znao je stajati posve mirno, a da se ništa ne pomakne sve dok ne mora.

en: “There’s always work.” The Nail kept on drilling at that egg with his dagger, patient as tree-roots. “The gates were shut when we got here. Whoever’s inside don’t feel like opening ’em. Keeps shooting arrows at us.”
bs: — Posla uvijek ima. Najl je i dalje reškao to jaje svojim bodežom, strpljiv poput drveća pod zemljom. — Vrata su bila zatvorena kad smo stigli. Tko god je unutra, ne namjerava ih otvarati. Samo pucaju na nas.

en: Rikke grinned all across her face. “Not one bit. The thought of Stour Nightfall’s face when he finds we stole his city is what’s been keeping me cheery these last few weeks.”
bs: Rike se široko osmijehnu. — Ni najmanje. Pomisao na lice Staura Najtfola kad shvati da smo mu ukrale grad držala me vedrom posljednjih nekoliko tjedana.

en: “Didn’t you fucking hear me?” He bared his teeth. “I said—” Isern grabbed him by the hair and stabbed him in the side of the neck, chopped his throat out with an easy flick of the wrist and sent black blood squirting, shoved him down into the gutter with her boot on his back.
bs: — Zar me, u pičku materinu, nisi čula? Ogoli zube. — Rekao sam… Izern ga grabljasto uhvati za kosu, zabode mu nož s bočne strane vrata, jednim ležernim trzajem zgloba mu prereže grkljan i pusti crnu krv da šiklja, pa ga s čizmom na leđima gurne u jarak.

en: “Pleasant-seeming personage, this one,” said Isern, tapping him on the shoulder with her dagger. “Family man, if I might take a guess?”
bs: — Ovaj odaje dojam ugodne pojave, dometnu Izern kucnuvši ga bodežom po ramenu. — Obiteljski čovjek, ako smijem nagađati?

en: “Maybe three dozen,” offered one of the others, shuffling forward on his knees. Here was a sad lesson. You can talk fine words till your tongue bleeds and never get a favour. Cut one throat and everyone’s falling over themselves to be helpful.
bs: — Možda tridesetak, ponudi se netko drugi, pužući na koljenima prema naprijed. Kakva li tužna lekcija. Možeš drobiti lijepe riječi dok ti jezik ne prokrvari, a da nikad ne dobiješ uslugu. Prerežeš li jedan grkljan, svi se otimaju tko će ti više pomoći.

en: Brock gestured to the two men he had brought with him, standing grimly against the wall. “These are my aides—Antaup…” Lean and handsome, with that slicked-back black hair which somehow always let a rakish lock or two drop over the forehead. “And Whitewater Jin.” A rugged, red-bearded Northman who looked to have been opening doors with his face most of his life.
bs: Brok pokaza na dvojicu Folk koje je dovio sa sobom, a koji su mrko stajali uza zid. — Ovo su moji pobočnici — Antaup…" Vitak i zgodan, s onom unatrag začešljanom crnom kosom kojoj bi se uvijek nekako omaknuo pokoji nestašni pramen preko čela. — I Whitewater Jin." Robustan Northman crvene brade koji je izgledao kao da je veći dio života otvarao vrata vlastitim licem.

en: “Please don’t ‘Majesty’ me, it’s faintly ridiculous at the best of times, but with armies in the field it’s positively absurd. Let’s talk like equals. Like friends. Just for tonight. I imagine tomorrow’s events will necessitate a whole new relationship between us, in any case.”
bs: — Molim te, nemoj me zvati "Vaša Uzvišenosti, to je pomalo smiješno u najboljim trenucima, ali s vojskama na terenu naprosto je apsurdno. Razgovarajmo kao ravnopravni. Kao prijatelji. Samo večeras. Pretpostavljam da će sutrašnji događaji ionako iziskivati potpuno nov odnos između nas.

en: Orso felt Gorst shift as the echoes faded and he held up a calming hand. The room was very still. He had to admit, he had never felt more respect for Leo dan Brock than at that moment. He was a man one could envy. A man for whom everything was simple. And he had a good claim to being the injured party. It was a shame it had come to this.
bs: Orso osjeti kako se Gorst pomaknuo kad su jeci utihnuli i podiže ruku u znak smirivanja. U sobi je vladala duboka tišina. Morao je priznati, nikad prije nije osjetio veće poštovanje prema Leu dan Broku nego u tom trenutku. Bio je čovjek kojemu se moglo zavidjeti. Čovjek kojemu je sve bilo jednostavno. A imao je i više nego opravdan razlog za ogorčenje. Šteta što je došlo do ovoga.

en: “But whether a man is a patriot, or for that matter of quality, all depends on who you ask, doesn’t it? Our current predicament makes that abundantly clear, if nothing else. As for principles, it was Bayaz who founded the Union, and he’s still on the Closed Council when it pleases him, in spite of my best efforts. You should spend some time in there. You’ll find your most proudly rigid principles turn shockingly flaccid. The First of the Magi can stretch them until they fit around any outrage, b
bs: — Ali je li netko domoljub ili, uostalom, čovjek od formata, sve ovisi o tome koga pitaš, zar ne? Naša trenutna nevolja to itekako jasno pokazuje, ako išta drugo. Što se tiče načela, Bajaz je utemeljio Unija, i on je još uvijek u Zatvorenom Vijeću kad god mu se to prohtije, unatoč svim mojim naporima. Trebao bi provesti malo vremena ondje. Vidjet ćeš kako tvoja najponosnija i najtvrđa načela postaju sablažnjivo mlohava. Prvi među Magi može ih rastegnuti tako da se prilagode svakoj gadosti, vjeru

en: “Oh, come on, I’m not going to poison you.” Orso leaned across, dipped his spoon in Brock’s soup and sucked it dry. “Now eat up, there’s a good fellow. There are excuses for High Treason but letting Bernille’s soup go cold is bloody unforgivable.”
bs: — Daj, molim te, neću te otrovati. Orso se nagnuo naprijed, zaronio žlicu u Brodovu juhu i posrknuo je do kraja. — Nego, jedi lijepo, budi dobar momak. Nađu se olakotne okolnosti za veleizdaju, ali dopustiti da se Bernillina juha ohladi krvavo je neoprostivo.

en: “I am sure your friend Lord Isher has thought it through. He’s not a man to under-plan, eh? We both know all that nonsense with Wetterlant was entirely his design.”
bs: — Siguran sam da je tvoj prijatelj lord Išer to promislio do kraja. Nije on čovjek koji propušta isplanirati stvari, zar ne? Oboje znamo da je ono sranje s Vetelantom potpuno njegova zamisao.

en: “I don’t know what story you’ve been told about reform, and freeing me from my chains and blah, blah, blah, but I’m quite certain Isher means to replace me entirely. Probably with you. Not sufficiently glorious to make a good puppet, is he? But I daresay he imagines he could pull the strings skilfully enough. And then, of course… there is your wife.”
bs: "Ne znam kakvu su ti priču ispričali o reformi, o oslobađanju mene iz mojih okova i bla, bla, bla, ali sasvim sam siguran da me Išer namjerava potpuno zamijeniti. Vjerojatno s tobom. Nisi dovoljno slavan da bi bio dobar lutak, zar ne? No usudio bih se reći da zamišlja kako bi mogao dovoljno vješto vući konce. I onda… tu je tvoja supruga."

en: Of course she was. How could she sleep with the endless kicking of her baby, the endless noise of soldiers on the move outside the window, the endless doubts, fears, hopes chasing each other around her mind like stray dogs after the butcher’s cart?
bs: D a je bila. Kako bi mogla spavati uz neprestano ritanje djeteta, uz neprekidnu larmu vojnika koji su se kretali pod prozorom, uz silne sumnje, strahove i nade što su se naganjale po njezinoj glavi poput lutajućih pasa za mesarskim kolima?

en: Savine would not have trusted him to carry her night-pot. “Of course you can, he’s bound to us, Leo, he has no—”
bs: Savine mu ne bi vjerovala ni da joj treba nositi noćnu posudu. " da možeš, vezan je uz nas, Leo, nema on…

en: She clapped a hand to his head, twisted her fingers in his hair and dragged his face towards her. “Stop. You’re not just a warrior, or a leader, or a general, you’re a hero.” Heroes are defined not by what they do, after all, or why, but by what people think they have done. “The cause is just.” She would be a wonderful queen. “We have strong allies beside us.” A circle of self-serving snakes. “We are going to win.” They had fucking better. “And the people of the Union will win with us. They need
bs: Prignula je ruku na njegovu glavu, uplela prste u kosu i povukla mu lice k sebi."Stani. Nisi samo ratnik, niti vođa, niti general — ti si heroj." Junaci se ne definiraju po onome što čine, u konačnici, niti po zašto, već po onome što Folk misle da su učinili. — Razlog je pravedan." Bila bi Vonderful kraljica. — Imamo snažne saveznike uz nas." Round samoljubivih zmija. — Mi ćemo pobijediti." Bolje im da pobijede, jebiga. "I Folk Unije pobijedit će uz nas. Oni nas trebaju. Oni trebaju tebe." Nije

en: When she gave birth to this bloody thing it would be heir to the throne of the Union. That decision was made already. She would never be caught defenceless again, as she had been in Valbeck. Never be scared, never be vulnerable. If Orso had to lose, and her father, and Rikke, so be it. She would be safe. She would be powerful. If the world had to lose so she could win, so be it. The dice were already rolling.
bs: Kad rodí ovo krvlju, bit će nasljednik prijestolja Unije. Ta je odluka već pala. Nikada više neće biti ugrabena bezbrana, kao u Valbeku. Nikada više strah, nikada ranjivost. Ako Orso mora izgubiti, i njezina otac, i Rike, neka bude. Ona će biti sigurna. Ona će biti moćna. Ako svijet mora izgubiti da ona pobijedi, neka bude. Kockice su već krenule.

en: “Not often you get seats like this at the show everyone’s talking about,” muttered Vick. “Imagine how much it cost to put on.”
bs: — Rijetko se kada dobiju ovakva mjesta za predstavu o kojoj svi pričaju, prozborila je Vik."Zamisli samo koliko je koštalo njezino postavljanje.

en: Two dark figures came across the hillside. One had a torch and a mask. The other was a boy, stumbling along with hands tied behind him. A Practical and a prisoner.
bs: Dvije tamne prilike prešle su preko padine. Jedna je nosila baklju i masku. Druga je bio dječak, teturajući s rukama svezanim na leđima. Praktik i zatvorenik.

en: Pike turned towards those thousands of pinprick lights, twinkling in the valley. “Faced with something on this scale, there could be no more rational response than to run away. But sometimes… we must do things that are not rational. Sometimes we must act on faith.” Pike stared at the lad and the lad stared back, the Practical looming dark over both. “Sometimes… even as the world goes mad… we must crouch next to Gert and load flatbows.”
bs: Pajk se okrenu prema onim tisućama svjetala poput iglenih ušica što su treperila u dolini. — Suočen s nečim u ovolikom obmjerju, čovjek ne može postupiti racionalnije nego pobjeći. No ponekad… moramo činiti stvari koje nisu racionalne. Ponekad moramo postupiti vođeni vjerom." Pajk je zurio u dječaka, a dječak je zurio u njega, dok se Praktik nadvijao u tami nad obojicom. — Ponekad… čak i dok svijet silazi s uma… moramo čučati pokraj Gerta i napinjati samostrijele.

en: “I understand cowards,” said Pike softly. “I used to be one. Who among us never had a weak moment, after all? It cannot all be darkness. We must have a little mercy.” He leaned sideways to whisper it. “As long as no one sees.”
bs: — Razumijem kukavice, prošaptao je Pajk. — I ja sam nekad bio jedna od njih. Tko među nama, na koncu, nikada nije imao trenutak slabosti? Nije sve u tami. Moramo imati malo milosti. Nagnuo se u stranu kako bi to izustio. — Sve dok nitko ne vidi.

en: “Laddermen prefer to go light.” Halder rubbed at the tattoo on the back of his hand. Same as Broad’s, but with just the one star. Some would say that was one too many. “Quicker you get to the top, the better your chances.”
bs: — Penjači ljestvama radije idu lagani. Halder protrlja tetovažu na nadlanici. Istu kao Brodova, ali sa samo jednom zvijezdom. Neki bi rekli da je i to jedna previše. — Što brže stigneš na Kruna, to su ti veće šanse.

en: “Sword’s a fine thing for riding down archers. Fighting armoured men face-to-face you can do better.” Halder nodded at Broad’s warhammer, laid out on an oilcloth, waiting for its own turn to be polished. “Hit a helmet hard with that, you can crack the skull inside without breaking the steel.”
bs: — Mač je divna stvar za gaženje strijelaca. Kad se boriš s oklopljenim ljudima licem u lice, možeš proći i bolje. Halder kimnu prema Brodovu ratnom čekiću, položenom na voštano platno, koji je čekao svoj red na glancanje. — Udariš li kacigu snažno njime, možeš razbiti lubanju unutra a da ne razbiješ čelik.

en: He placed an unhappy hand on his belly and tried his best to suck it in. One cannot suck in one’s hips, though. It was reaching the point where he was considering some form of corset. Savine always looked spectacular in them, after all, and exercise was out of the bloody question. He let it all sag again with horrifying results.
bs: Nezadovoljnu ruku položi na trbuh i dade sve od sebe da ga uvuče. Kukove se, međutim, nije moglo uvući. Bilo je došlo dotle da je razmatrao nekakav oblik korzeta. Savine je u njima naposljetku uvijek izgledala spektakularno, a o tjelovježbi nije bilo ni govora. Pustio je da se sve opet opusti s užasnim posljedicama.

en: Then he found himself wondering why he was still there, and slapped impatiently at the side of his head. “Damn it, Hildi, I think far too much to make a good general.”
bs: Zatim se upita zašto je on još uvijek ondje pa se nestrpljivo ošamari po glavi. — Dođavola, Hildi, previše razmišljam da bih bio dobar general.

en: “Big army to manage?” sneered the king, and he kicked out at a cookpot and sent it bouncing between the trees where it hit a Carl on the side of his knee and made him squeak with pain, though he kept smiling all the while, which was quite a feat.
bs: — Veliku vojsku teško voditi? podsmjehnu se kralj te ispalmi udarac prema loncu za kuhanje i otkotrlja ga kroz stabla gdje pogodi Carla u bočnu stranu koljena i natjera ga zacvili od boli, premda se cijelo vrijeme nastavio smiješiti, što je bio pravi pothvat.

en: “My king?” A wincing Carl was edging up, an eyeglass offered out to Stour like he was sticking his arm in a fire.
bs: — Moj kralju? Prikršeći se od bolova, Carls mu se približavao pružajući durbin prema Stauru, kao da ruku gura u vatru.

en: Shock turned to a reassuring fury that burned all the night’s doubts away. He was the Young Lion, damn it! He’d no business dithering when there was an enemy ahead.
bs: Šok se pretvorio u umirujući bijes koji je u trenu spalio sve noćne sumnje. Pa on je Juvens Lav, dođavola! Nije imao vremena za kolebanje kad mu je neprijatelj bio pred nosom.

en: Isher wiped sweat from his forehead and gave a stiff salute. “I do.” And he strode somewhat unsteadily to his horse.
bs: Išer obriše znoj s čela i ukočeno salutira. — Jest." I prilično nestabilnim korakom zaputi se prema svome konju.

en: “We could’ve beaten him last night.” He curled his fingers into a trembling fist. “But we’ll crush him today instead. Someone get my horse!”
bs: — Mogli smo ga srediti sinoć. Stisnu prste u drhtavu šaku. — Ali zato ćemo ga danas smrviti. Nek mi netko dovede konja!

en: Of Stour Nightfall’s Northmen there was no sign. Lurking in the woods, no doubt, waiting to pounce, as Northmen so loved to do. The Young Lion and the Great Wolf had been bitter enemies, fighting each other to the death but a few months before. Now Orso had achieved the apparently impossible and united them in mutual hatred for him.
bs: Sjevernjacima Staura Noćne Paljbe ni traga ni glasa. Vjerojatno su se skrivali po šumama i vrebali priliku za napad, kako to Sjevernjaci već vole činiti. Juvens Lav i Great Vuk do prije nekoliko su mjeseci bili ogorčeni neprijatelji koji su se borili na život i smrt. A sada je Orso postigao naizgled nemoguće i ujedinio ih u zajedničkoj mržnji prema njemu.

en: “Master Sulfur.” Orso was less than entirely delighted to see the magus step out onto the roof of the clock tower. “You always seem to arrive at moments of high drama.”
bs: — Majstore Salfur. Orso se i nije pretjerano obradovao ugledavši maga kako kroči na krov tornja sa satom. — Vi se uvijek nekako stvorite u trenucima najveće dramatičnosti.

en: “For which I am immensely grateful, of course.” Orso had seen Sulfur rip a man apart with his teeth. He knew Bayaz had made a wreck of half the Agriont and killed thousands. He was sure Valint and Balk had done even more damage in the years since, with far less spectacle. Truly, he had made a pact with devils. But a man lost in the desert, as the Gurkish say, must take such water as he is offered.
bs: — Na čemu sam neizmjerno zahvalan, dakako. Orso je svojim očima vidio kako Salfur zubima komada čovjeka. Znao je da je Bajaz pretvorio u ruševinu pola Agrionta i pobio tisuće. Bio je posve siguran da su Valint i Balk učinili još veću štetu u godinama koje su uslijedile, i to s daleko manje spektakla. Doista, sklopio je Unija s vragom. No čovjek izgubljen u pustinji, kako kažu Gurkish, mora piti kakvu mu vodu ponude.

en: There was something faintly horrifying about a tipple while men marched to their deaths. Epic disaster as light entertainment. “At a time like this?” asked Orso.
bs: Bilo je nečeg pomalo jezivog u ispijanju pića dok Folk marširaju u smrt. Epska katastrofa kao laka zabava. — U ovako nekom trenutku?" upita Orso.

en: “What are they doing?” muttered Savine, clenching her swollen fists so tight they trembled. “What the hell are they doing?”
bs: — Što to rade? progunđa Savine, stisnuvši natečene šake toliko čvrsto da su joj drhtale. — Što se to, u krasan kurac, događa?

en: Leo was not far away, dragging his horse impatiently back and forth, swarmed by a constantly shifting crowd of officers, messengers and panicked hangers-on. She wanted desperately to be down there with him. Being a powerless observer by no means suited her. But she knew no one would listen to her. No one was listening to anyone. Leo caught one man in the deep blue uniform of Isher’s soldiers and near dragged him from his saddle.
bs: Leo nije bio daleko, nemirno šetajući konja amo-tamo, okružen neprestanom mijenom časnika, glasnika i uplašenih priležnika. Silno je željela biti dolje s njim. Biti nemoćni promatrač nipošto joj nije odgovaralo. No znala je da je nitko ne bi poslušao. Nitko nije slušao nikoga. Leo zgrabi jednog čovjeka u tamnoplavoj odori Išerovih vojnika i zamalo ga svuče sa sedla.

en: She jumped at an almighty crash. Someone dived aside with a despairing cry as a cannon slid from its wagon and thudded to the turf, rolling down the hill and leaving a trail of wreckage, a tangle of ropes and pulleys dragged through a campfire after it.
bs: Trgne se na silan tresak. Netko odskoči u stranu s očajničkim krikom dok je top kliznuo s kola i tresnuo o tlo, kotrljajući se niz brdo i ostavljajući za sobom trag krša, klupko užadi i koturača koje je vukao kroz logorsku vatru.

en: Vick silently shook her head. From where they stood, she could just see the top of the clock tower. Hard to believe how little time had passed since the Open Council’s troops began to move. The trees on the far bank were swarming with soldiers now, their order entirely gone, columns crowding haphazardly in from behind to add their weight to the confusion. But the near bank still looked as peaceful as it had at dawn.
bs: Vik nijemo odvrgnu glavom. S mjesta na kojemu su stajali jedva je nazirala Kruna tornja sa satom. Nevjerojatno je kako je malo vremena prošlo otkad su se trupe Otvorenoga Vijeća počele micati. Stabla na suprotnoj obali sada su vrvjela vojnicima čiji se red posve raspao, a kolone su se zbijale sa stražnje strane kako bi svojim brojem pridodale metežu. No, obala bliže njima još je uvijek djelovala mirno kao u zoru.

en: The cannon jolted on its trestles, fire spurting from its mouth. There was a thunderous, barking explosion, as painfully loud as anything Vick ever heard. A moment later, the next cannon fired, and the next.
bs: Top poskoči na postolju, a iz cijevi suknu plamen. Uslijedi gromoglasna, hrapava eksplozija, bolno glasna poput svega što je Vik ikad čula. Trenutak kasnije opali idući top, pa potom sljedeći.

en: But Stour had slept through Osrung in his mother’s belly. His eyes shone as he watched the smoke puff out. “They call ’em cannons now,” he murmured, then turned about. “Get the men ready.”
bs: No Staur je Osrung prespavao u majčinu trbuhu. Oči su mu se caklile dok je promatrao dim kako suklja. — Zovu ih topovima sad, promrmlja, a potom se okrenu. — Pripremite ljude.

en: And there was a great clattering and hissing as swords were drawn and shields raised and spears hefted. A great growl and murmur of war curses and prayers to the dead, shouted orders echoing from further off as the call to arms spread down the long line. A great jingle and rustle as mailed warriors crunched through the brush to the very edge of the trees. Stour brushed Brock’s man out of his way and strode forward himself into the golden wheat, drawing his sword, and his gilded bastards crowded
bs: I začu se silan zveket i šuštanje dok su mačevi izlazili iz korica, štitovi se uzdizali, a koplja odmjeravala. Snažan hropac i mrmor ratnih kletvi i molitvi upućenih mrtvima, izvikane zapovijedi odjekivale su iz daljine dok se Poziv širio dugim redom. Silan zveket i šušanj dok su oklopljeni ratnici krčili put kroz grmlje sve do samog ruba šume. Staur pomaknu Brodova čovjeka s puta i sam zakorači naprijed u zlatnu pšenicu, izvlačeći mač, a njegova pozlaćena kopilad nagrnu za njim, tiskajući se i

en: “Damn it,” hissed Leo. If they waited for the Open Council to get across that river they’d be waiting till nightfall.
bs: — Prokletstvo, prosiktao je Leo. Ako budu čekali da Otvoreno vijeće prijeđe tu rijeku, čekat će sve do mraka.

en: Leo clapped the old lord on the shoulder. “We’ll have to outfight the bastards.” He turned in his saddle to roar at the men around him. “Lift the standard, lads! Beat the drums! It’s time!”
bs: Leo je udario starog lorda po ramenu. — Morat ćemo nadmašiti te kopiladi u borbi." Okrenuo se u sedlu kako bi zagrmio na vojnike oko sebe. — Podignite barjak, momci! Udrite u bubnjeve! Vrijeme je!

en: The air had a sharp smell. A tang of Gurkish Fire, and metal, and fear, and shit. Someone had dug a latrine pit way too close to camp and a couple of slumping wattle screens weren’t doing much to hide the sight of men’s waste, let alone the smell of it.
bs: Zrakom se širio Trdak miris. Aroma gurkishke vatre, metala, straha i govana. Netko je iskopao nužnik preblizu taboru, a nekoliko iskrivljenih pletenih pregrada nije odveć skrivalo prizor ljudskoga otpada, a kamoli njegov smrad.

en: Steebling squinted as Broad’s shadow cast him into darkness. “We Steeblings aren’t easily intimidated, you— Ah!” He squawked as Broad caught him by the ear and dragged him from his chair.
bs: Stibling je zaškiljio dok ga je Brodova sjena obavila tminom. — Mi Stiblingzi ne damo se tako lako zastrašiti, ti — Ah!" Vrisnuo je kad ga je Brod uhvatio za uho i odvukao sa stolice.

en: When he wept at his own front door, back in the loving embrace of his family, he’d thought he was done with blood. Thought nothing could ever get him back onto a battlefield. But it seemed Judge knew him better than he knew himself. Trouble was like hunger to him. Stuffing your face till you’re sick one day doesn’t mean you won’t want lunch the next. All you do is sharpen your appetite. And here he was, in spite of all his empty promises, back at the table again with his cutlery ready, clamourin
bs: Kad je jecao na vlastitom pragu, natrag u toplom zagrljaju svoje obitelji, mislio je da je završio s krvlju. Mislio je da ga ništa više nikad neće vratiti na bojno polje. No činilo se da Džadž poznaje njega bolje nego on samoga sebe. Trobli mu je bio poput gladi. To što se jedan dan prejedeš do mučnine ne znači da idući dan nećeš htjeti ručati. Time si samo iznova naoštrio apetit. I eto ga sad, unatoč svim praznim obećanjima, opet za stolom sa spremnim priborom, kako traži da ga se posluži.

en: The air was thick with the stink of Gurkish Fire, his mouth sticky with the tang of powder, his throat raw and his eyes smarting. At times, he could hardly see the next cannon along. Their crews were ghosts, crawling around their pieces, swabbing ’em, towelling ’em, loading ’em, feeding ’em powder, tending to their every screaming whim like a bunch of filth-smeared nannies to a nursery full of overgrown metal babies. Babies that spat death.
bs: Zrak je bio gust od smrada Gurkish Vatre, usta su mu bila ljepljiva od okusa baruta, grlo promuklo, a oči pekle. Ponekad jedva da je vidio idući top u nizu. Njihove posade bile su poput duhova; gmizale su oko oruđa, ispirale ih, brisale, punile, hranile barutom i udovoljavale svakom njihovom prodornom hiru poput gomile prljavih dadilja u rasadniku punom preraslih metalnih beba. Beba koje su bljuvale smrt.

en: He could see soldiers below them, through the drifting smoke. Lord Crant’s men, he thought. A ragged-looking regiment, stretched out crooked across the hillside. They’d tried to dig in but had about three good shovels between ’em and the rocky ground wasn’t offering much help. No one was. They were cowering now, at the thunder of the cannons behind them and the masses of enemy somewhere in front. Trapped betwixt hell and hail, as Peck’s granny used to say. They’d flung their weapons down to cove
bs: Kroz lebdeći dim mogao je vidjeti vojnike pod sobom. Folk lorda Cranta, pomislio je. Razbarušena pukovnija, razvučena poput krivudava ožiljka preko obronka. Pokušali su se ukopati, ali su imali otprilike tri dobra lopata za sve njih, a kamenito tlo nije im previše išlo na ruku. Nitko nije. Sada su se stiskali pred grmljavinom topova iza sebe i neprijateljskim masama negdje sprijeda. Stisnuti između pakla i tuče, kako je govorila Peckova baka. Odbacili su oružje da si zaklone uši, lica izobličena

en: There was a sound like a whip cracking in Suval’s ear, there was a great shower of stinging splinters and he cringed as something bounced off his back. A branch fell from a tree nearby and crashed down among the wreckage.
bs: Začuo se zvuk poput pucnja biča Suvalu u uhu, prosuo se silan pljusak oštrih i pekućih ivera, a on se skvrčio kad mu se nešto odbilo od leđa. Grana pade s obližnjeg drveta i s praskom se sruši među krhotine.

en: “God help us,” he whispered again. There were a lot of men praying. A lot of men crying. A lot of men screaming. One sat silent, in the dappled shade of the trees, looking exceedingly surprised, blood streaming down his face. Suval knew him a little. He had been a tailor in Ul-Khatif. No sense of humour. But senses of humour were not at a premium here.
bs: "Bože, pomozi nam, ponovno prošapće. Mnogi su se Folk molili. Mnogi su plakali. Mnogi su vrištali. Jedan je sjedio u tišini, u prošaranoj sjeni stabala, izgledajući krajnje zapanjeno, dok mu se krv slivala niz lice. Suval ga je površno poznavao. Bio je krojač u Ul-Khatifu. Bez trunke smisla za humor. No smisao za humor ovdje nije bio na cijeni.

en: Something spattered his face. Was it blood? Was he wounded? Oh, God, was this the end? He held his trembling fingertips up before his eyes.
bs: Nešto mu poprska lice. Je li to bila krv? Je li bio ranjen? O Bože, je li ovo bio kraj? Podignuo je svoje drhtave vrške prstiju pred oči.

en: He grabbed Barezin by a fistful of braid and hissed the words one at a time. “Just… get… them… across!” He pulled his horse around. “Now!”
bs: Grubo uhvati Barezina za šaku opleta i izgovori riječi sikćući jednu po jednu."Samo… ih… prevezi… preko!" Okrene konja. — Sad!

en: A nervous company had gathered at the side of a farmhouse. You could see their terror as they gazed across the body-speckled fields towards the burning orchards and the fuming hill beyond. An officer rode up and down in front of them, waving his sword, screaming himself hoarse. “Forward! For pity’s sake, forward!” But like a stubborn herd of goats refusing the shepherd’s commands, they wouldn’t be moved.
bs: Uznemirena satnija okupila se pokraj seoske kuće. Mogao si im vidjeti strah u očima dok su promatrali polja posuta tijelima prema zapaljenim voćnjacima i brdu iznad kojeg se dizao dim. Časnik je jahao gore-dolje Naprijed njih, mašući mačem i derući se do promuklosti. — Naprijed! Zaboga, naprijed!" No poput tvrdoglavog stada koza koje odbija pastirove zapovijedi, nisu se micali.

en: He was working up a new story. Something to really gild his reputation. A nobleman’s wife, this time. Lady something or other. Probably better not to think up a name, that could get him in trouble later. I’ll take it to my grave and all that. Mysterious older woman. Terribly wealthy. Frisson of danger. Husband couldn’t get it hard any more. They’d swallow it whole. Antaup, you dog! How do you do it? Easy when you made it up. And a lot more fun than having to actually persuade women to take you t
bs: Radio je na novoj priči. Nečemu čime će doista učvrstiti svoju reputaciju. Plemićkoj ženi, ovaj put. Lady toj-i-toj. Vjerojatno je bolje ne smišljati ime, to bi ga kasnije moglo uvaliti u nevolju. Odnijet ću je u grob i tako to. Tajanstvena starija žena. Užasno bogata. Dašak opasnosti. Mužu se više nije dizao. Progutat će to u komadu. Antaupe, stari pseto! Kako ti to polazi za rukom? Lako kad sve izmisliš. I mnogo zabavnije nego se doista truditi nagovoriti žene da te odvedu u krevet. Nije uopće

en: He noticed bolts poking from the stubbled fields to either side now. All pointing at the same angle. Within flatbow range, then. Leo would be where the danger was, of course. It was one of the things you had to admire about the—
bs: Sada je primijetio strijele iz samostrela kako vire iz strništa s obje strane. Sve okrenute pod istim kutom. Dakle, u dometu ravnog Utočište. Leo će biti tamo gdje je opasnost. To je bila jedna od onih stvari kojima se čovjek mora diviti kod —

en: The string was cranked all the way now and he hefted the bow, plucked up a bolt, slotted it home, all smooth and practised. He paused a moment, wondering how many bolts he’d shot in his life. But his job wasn’t to count ’em, just to put ’em in the air, calmly and carefully and quickly as possible.
bs: Tetiva je sada bila potpuno navijena, pa on podiže luk, dohvati projektil, umetnu ga na mjesto, sve glatko i uigrano. Zastade na trenutak pitajući se koliko je projektila ispalio u životu. No njegov posao nije bio brojati ih, nego ih slati u zrak, mirno, pažljivo i što je brže moguće.

en: A man fell, screaming. As he looked around, Starling saw he had a bolt in his face. A horrible red flash of it before he went down under the stumbling men, and someone near tripped over his pike as he dropped it, everyone wobbling and clanking into each other.
bs: Čovjek pade uz vrisak. Dok se osvrtao, Starling opazi strijelu zabodenu u njegovu licu. Užasan crveni bljesak prije nego što je potonuo pod gomilom Folk koja se saplitala, a netko se u blizini spotaknuo o njegov kopljište dok ga je ispuštao, dok su se svi teturali i zveckali sudarajući se jedni o druge.

en: Wished he was in the front rank, so he could see where he was going. Then he caught sight of where they were going. That drystone wall, and men standing there, lowering their own pikes, and bloody hell was he glad he wasn’t in the front rank. Everyone packed in so tight. No room, no room at all. Sort of a comfort, sort of a fear. Men protecting you, brothers at your shoulder, but how could you get out? You couldn’t. That was the whole point.
bs: Poželio je biti u prvoj borbenoj liniji kako bi vidio kamo ide. Onda je ugledala kamo zapravo idu. Onaj suhozid i ljude kako stoje ondje, spuštaju svoja koplja, i u kvragu je bio sretan što nije prvenstveno. Svi stisnuti tako tijesno. Mjesta ni za lijek, nema mjesta ni za što. Nekako utješno, a nekako zastrašujuće. Folk te štite, suborci su ti uz rame, ali kako pobogu pobjeći? Nikako. U tome i jest cijela poanta.

en: Bloody hell, the noise. The growling and spitting and swearing, the squeal and grind of tortured metal and wood, now and again a scream or a whimper or a begging gurgle.
