bs: U kvragu, ta buka. Režanje, pljuvanje i psovanje, škripa i mljevenje izmučenog metala i drveta, a povremeno vrisak, jecaj ili molitveni hropac.

en: “Fuck!” he snarled. “Shit! Fuck!” He twisted and kicked ever more desperately, and the bright point of the blade scraped sideways across his breastplate, caught on the metal lip near his armpit. He stared down at it, hardly daring to breathe, begging it to somehow hold there. He let go of his pike, tried desperately to twist around but couldn’t even pull his right hand free, could only get the faintest, useless grip on the shaft between finger and thumb of his left.
bs: — Jebote! prosiktao je. — Sranje! Jebo te! Zakovrčio se i ritnuo još očajnije, a sjajni Kruna sječiva kliznuo je u stranu preko njegova naprsnika i zapeo za metalni rub blizu pazuha. Zagledao se dolje u nj, jedva se usuđujući udahnuti, moleći ga da nekako izdrži. Ispustio je svoju piku, očajnički se pokušao okrenuti, ali nije mogao osloboditi ni desnu ruku, već je lijevom mogao uhvatiti držak samo vrhovima prstiju, jedva i beskorisno.

en: Be a man, he’d said, with his big calloused hand heavy on Lake’s shoulder, and his bottom lip stuck right out as if he was saying something weighty.
bs: Budi muškarac, rekao je, s velikom žuljevitom šakom teškom na Lakeovu ramenu, dok mu je donja usna bila isturena kao da govori nešto važno.

en: He clutched at the mud, dragged himself back. Through the boots, through the legs. Something thudded into his ribs, rolled him over, a boot caught the side of his face as it came down and he shoved at it, punched at it, dragged himself on through the feet and the mud and the corpses.
bs: Stisnuo je blato šakama, odvukao se natrag. Kroz čizme, kroz noge. Nešto ga je tupo udarilo u rebra, prevrnulo ga na leđa, čizma ga je zakačila po strani lica dok se spuštala, a on ju je odgurnuo, udario šakom, nastavio se vući kroz stopala, blato i leševe.

en: Ariss had wanted to do something before she married. Wanted to do something real. Something to be proud of. Her uncle had fought in Gurkhul, long ago. He’d tried to warn her.
bs: Ariss je htjela učiniti nešto prije nego što se uda. Htjela je učiniti nešto stvarno. Nešto čime bi se ponosila. Ujak joj se davno borio u Gurkhulu. Pokušao ju je upozoriti.

en: Ariss wearily nodded. “I suppose.” She lurched up, stumbled as someone crashed into her. A boy who went sprawling next to the corpses, cap falling off to show a shock of blonde curls.
bs: Ariss umorno kimnu. — Pretpostavljam." Posrnuvši ustade, spotaknuvši se kad se netko zabio u nju. Dječak se prostro pokraj leševa, a Hat mu spade i otkrije čuperak plavih kovrča.

en: She paused on the hillside to catch her breath. Paused, and prised her eyes away from the grass. Made herself turn to stare out across the valley.
bs: Zastade na padini kako bi uhvatila dah. Zastade i odvoji Oko s trave. Natjera se okrenuti i zagledati preko doline.

en: She ran past a man snarling, “Damn it!” again and again as he fiddled with the jammed crank of his flatbow, fussing with the bolt, trying to turn the handle, fussing with the bolt, trying to turn the handle, fussing with the bolt, over and over. “Damn it! Damn it! Damn it!”
bs: Protrčala je pokraj čovjeka koji je neprekidno režeći ponavljao: — Prokletstvo!" dok se mučio sa zaglavljenom ručicom svog plošnog Utočište, namještajući strelu, pokušavajući okrenuti ručicu, namještajući strelu, pokušavajući okrenuti ručicu, namještajući strelu, iznova i iznova. — Prokletstvo! Prokletstvo! Prokletstvo!

en: She stumbled up, holding the message out to him, realised it was crumpled to a smudged mess in her sweaty fist. “The Anglanders… are pushing us back… towards Stoffenbeck.” She was breathing so hard, she was nearly sick. “His Majesty… needs support.”
bs: Posrnula je ustajući i pružila mu poruku, a onda shvatila da se u njezinoj znojnoj šaci smrvila u nečitku kašu. — Anglanđani… potiskuju nas… prema Štopenbeku." Teško je disala, zamalo povrativši od napora. — Vaša Uzvišenosti… treba pojačanje.

en: The best you could do was play a long con and act as if you had them. Never show fear. Never show doubt. Command was a trick. You had to spread the illusion that you knew what you were doing as deep and as wide through your men as you could. Spread the illusion and hope for the best.
bs: Najviše što si mogao učiniti bilo je igrati dugu igru i ponašati se kao da ih imaš. Nikad ne pokazati strah. Nikad ne pokazati sumnju. Zapovijedanje je bilo varka. Morao si širiti iluziju da znaš što radiš, i to što dublje i šire među svojim ljudima. Širiti iluziju i nadati se najboljem.

en: “Lord Marshal!” he stared with wide, wet eyes. “I was… I was…” Running for it, obviously. Forest hardly blamed him. But he had to stop him.
bs: — Gospodine maršale! — zagledao se u njeg širokim, suznim očima. — Ja sam… ja sam… Bježi glavom bez obzira, očito. Trdak mu to jedva bijaše uzeo za zlo. No morao ga je zaustaviti.

en: He stared about him at the men he was supposed to command. Everything was a muddle now. He’d no idea where his company ended and the next began. Didn’t know half the faces. Or maybe it was the mad expressions that made them strangers. The filth and the blood and the bared teeth. Animals. Savages.
bs: Zagleda se u ljude kojima je trebao zapovijedati. Sve se pretvorilo u zbrku. Nije imao pojma gdje njegova satnija završava, a sljedeća počinje. Nije poznavao ni pola lica. Ili su mu možda ta lica strancima činili mahniti izrazi. Prljavština, krv i ogoljeni zubi. Životinje. Divljaci.

en: A man stood, teeth gritted, one hand clapped to his bloody side while he gripped his spear with the other. There was bravery.
bs: Neki je čovjek stajao sa stisnutim zubima, pritisnuvši jednu ruku na krvavi bok, dok je drugom stezao Pajk. E to je bila hrabrost.

en: Arrows fluttered down. Gentle, almost. One stuck into the ground near him. Another bounced from a man’s shoulder and spun away.
bs: Strijele su lepršale spuštajući se. Nježno, gotovo. Jedna se zabola u tlo blizu njega. Druga se odbila od čovjekova ramena i otkotrljala.

en: No game. No story. They meant to kill him. They meant to rip him open and spill his guts down the hillside. They meant to dash his brains out like they’d dashed out Corporal Bland’s brains, and him a very nice man with a sister in Holsthorm who’d just had a daughter.
bs: Nikakva igra. Nikakva priča. Namjeravali su ga ubiti. Namjeravali su ga raskomadati i prosuti mu utrobu niz padinu. Namjeravali su mu razbiti lubanju kao što su razbili lubanju kaplaru Blandu, a on je bio tako dobar čovjek sa sestrom u Holsthornu koja je upravo rodila kćer.

en: Something crashed into his shoulder, knocked him sideways and he slid on the wet grass, fell, reeled up, almost smashed a man over the head before he realised it was a Northman, turned the other way, screaming, charging, rammed into someone and knocked him down. He squealed something before Downside drove the rim of his shield into his throat, and again.
bs: Nešto ga je udarilo u rame, ponijelo u stranu i on je kliznuo po mokroj travi, pao, teturajući ustao, zamalo razbio glavu nekom čovjeku prije nego što je shvatio da je to Northman, okrenuo se na drugu stranu, vrišteći, jurišajući, zabio se u nekoga i oborio ga. Onaj je nešto zacvilio prije nego što mu je Dausaid zabio rub štita u grlo, pa još jednom.

en: He blinked stupidly as he realised his hand was empty. Loop must’ve broken, axe flown off who knew where. He fumbled a dagger from his belt with numb fingers and straight away dropped it as a man blundered into him, caught him, wrestled with him, the two of them staggering about, slipping on the wet grass, over the wet corpses, the fallen weapons, the fallen shields, the bits of men.
bs: Tupo je treptao shvativši da mu je ruka prazna. Petlja se morala potrgati, Hachette odletjeti tko zna kamo. Utrnulim je prstima napipao bodež za pojasom i odmah ga ispustio kad se čovjek zaletio u njega, uhvatio ga, hrvao se s njim, obojica su posrtala, kližući se po mokroj travi, preko mokrih leševa, paloga oružja, palih štitova, komada Folk.

en: A ridiculous affectation, of course, things had gone beyond horrifying some time ago and did not look like coming back. But why attend a battle at all if you’re not going to say at least one heroically imperturbable thing?
bs: Smiješna taština, dakako; situacija je već odavno prerasla u užas i nije se činilo da će se to promijeniti. Ali čemu uopće dolaziti u bitku ako čovjek ne namjerava izreći barem jednu herojski staloženu rečenicu?

en: Quite possibly his last, the way things were going. The thought almost brought up a snort of laughter. The Fates help him, he was enjoying himself. Was he mad?
bs: Vrlo vjerojatno i posljednjim, s obzirom na to kako su se stvari odvijale. Ta mu je pomisao gotovo izmamila smijeh. Neka mu Sudbine pomognu, uživao je. Je li poludio?

en: “Protect the king!” squealed Gorst, stepping in front of Orso with his shield up. He was astonished to see Tunny flinging himself into the path of danger on the other side, Steadfast Standard in one hand and sword in the other. Horsemen were indeed moving through the murk. Orso inflated his chest indignantly, exactly the way his mother might have when faced with an impudent maid.
bs: — Zaštitite kralja! zacvili Gorst, stajući Naprijed Orsa s podignutim štitom. Bio je zapanjen vidjevši Tunnyja kako se baca u smjeru opasnosti nasuprot tome, sa zastavom Steadfasta u jednoj i mačem u drugoj ruci. Maršali su se doista kretali kroz izmaglicu. Orso je ogorčeno napuhao prsa, baš onako kako bi to učinila njegova majka suočena s drskom sluškinjom.

en: “My leg! My leg!” A man was carried past, arms over the shoulders of two others, his leg most clearly missing below the knee. A cannon-stone struck a roof on the other side of the square and sent an avalanche of broken slates raining down, people diving for cover in all directions.
bs: — Noga! Moja noga! Prolazio je čovjek držeći ruke preko ramena dvojice drugih, a noga mu je očito nedostajala ispod koljena. Topovska kugla udarila je u krov nasuprot tome Trga i poslala lavinu razbijenog crijepa da se sruši u kiši, dok su se Folk razbježali u potrazi za zaklonom na sve strane.

en: That footman was still following him, his purple livery thoroughly besmirched, cringing at the occasional impacts, his tray sheltered under one arm rather than balanced on his fingertips.
bs: Onaj ga je poslužitelj još uvijek pratio, s purpurnom livrejom potpuno uprljanom, zgrčen od povremenih udara, držeći pladanj pod rukom umjesto da ga balansira na vršcima prstiju.

en: Vick looked down towards Stoffenbeck, fires burning in the rubble-strewn streets, wounded trickling towards the rear. “The king will be left with his arse in the breeze.”
bs: Vik je pogledala prema Štopenbeku, gdje su vatre gorjele u ulicama zatrpanima ruševinama, a ranjenici su se vukli prema pozadini. – Kralju će ostati gola guzica na vjetru.

en: “Good timing, Lord Marshal Rucksted!” called Pike. Vick wasn’t usually slow on the uptake, but it took her a moment to make sense of things.
bs: — Dobar tajming, lord-maršale Ruckstede! – pozvao je Pajk. Vik inače nije bila spore pameti, ali trebalo joj je malo vremena da pohvata konce.

en: The fierce smile had spread across her face. With that bluff in their hands, the town could not be held. The centre would give, Stour would break through on the left, the day would be theirs.
bs: Divlji osmijeh razvukao joj se licem. S tom liticom u njihovim rukama, grad se nije mogao održati. Sredina će popustiti, Staur će probiti lijevo, dan će biti njihov.

en: “No,” whispered Savine. A moment ago, she had tasted victory. Now nothing was certain. She wanted to sink to her knees. She wanted to lie down in the grass. But someone had to do something.
bs: — Ne, prošaptala je Savine. Do prije trenutka okusila je pobjedu. Sada ništa nije bilo Sejf. Poželjela je klonuti na koljena. Poželjela je leći u travu. No netko je morao nešto poduzeti.

en: “By the dead,” he growled. The army of Angland had done their part. Fought for every inch of ground, forced Orso’s men from their positions, bent their crescent in the centre until it touched the outskirts of Stoffenbeck. They were still fighting, through the smoke and spitting rain, the melee broken up into a dozen ugly little struggles among the buildings.
bs: — Tako mi mrtvih — zaurla on. Vojska Englenda dala je svoj obol. Borila se za svaku stopu tla, potisnula Orsove ljude s položaja, savila njihov polumjesec u središtu sve dok nije dotakao predgrađa Štopenbeka. I dalje su se borili kroz dim i sitnu kišu, dok se meč pretvorio u tuce ružnih, malih borbi među zgradama.

en: Now Leo was smiling. How could he help it when his friends were laughing at death? He had to stop himself turning to ask Jurand what he thought. He wished him and Glaward were there now. He looked up towards the king’s standard. The Steadfast Standard, flapping free above the smoke and ruin on the high clock tower, the golden sun glinting as the real thing slipped through the spitting clouds overhead.
bs: Sada se i Leo smješkao. Kako i ne bi kad mu se prijatelji smiju smrti? Morao se suzdržati da se ne okrene i upita Džuranda što misli. Želio je da su on i Glavard sada ovdje. Podignuo je Oko prema kraljevskoj zastavi. Stalan barjak slobodno je lepršao iznad dima i ruševina na visokom tornju sa satom, dok je zlatno sunce blistalo dok se pravo sunce probijalo kroz prozirne oblake iznad njih.

en: Few of them could’ve heard the words but they got the gist, shoving their lances at the spitting heavens, letting go a rousing cheer.
bs: Malo tko od njih mogao je čuti te riječi, ali shvatili su poantu, gurnuvši koplja prema nabusitom nebu i prolativši gromoglasan poklič.

en: Now at a trot, the buildings ahead growing clearer through the rain and the smoke, bodies scattered where they’d fallen as the fighting ground towards Stoffenbeck, the tangle of weapons and limp banners where the battle was still hot, all jolting with the movement of Leo’s horse.
bs: Sada u kas, dok su se građevine pred njim primicale i postajale jasnije kroz kišu i dim, s tijelima razasutim ondje gdje su pala dok se borba vukla prema Štopenbeku, spletom oružja i ološnih zastava ondje gdje je bitka još uvijek bjesnjela, a sve se to treslo u ritmu kretanja Leova konja.

en: Everything was pounding hooves, flying mud and billowing smoke, rushing noise and rushing wind, thudding along with his own thumping heartbeat, rattling teeth, booming breath, all seen through a slot you could hardly get a letter through.
bs: Sve se svelo na tutnjavu kopita, leteće blato i sukljajući dim, hučnu buku i nahrupjeli vjetar, uz udaranje vlastitoga srca u grudima, klokotanje zuba, hropac, a sve to promatrano kroz prorez kroz koji jedva da bi se moglo ugurati pismo.

en: He froze, crouching in a trampled flower bed by the wreckage of a fence. Any man with half his sense would’ve run the other way. But Broad had proved a dozen times he had no sense at all once the fighting started, and he was in the thick of the fighting now. His head throbbed with the noise of it, the smell of it. There was no resisting its pull any more than a floating cork resists a wave.
bs: Ukočio se, čučnuvši u izgaženoj gredici cvijeća pokraj ostataka ograde. Svatko imalo razuman pobjegao bi glavom bez obzira. No Brod je već desetak puta dokazao da nema ni trunke razuma jednom kad borba počne, a sada se nalazio u samom njezinu žarištu. Sljepoočnice su mu bubnjale od buke i smrada borbe. Otpor njezinoj privlačnosti bio je uzaludan poput otpora plutajućeg čepa morskom valu.

en: He squirmed in the dirt, back arched, and Broad stepped over him, looking for more, snorting breath steam-hot, teeth locked vice-tight, muscles coiled-spring tense.
bs: Koprcao se u blatu, leđa savijenih u luku, a Brod je zakoračio preko njega, tražeći još, frkćući dahom vrelim poput pare, zuba stisnutih poput škripca, mišića napetih poput opruga.

en: There were dead men everywhere. Broad could hardly move without stepping on ’em. Dead men and dead horses, tangled and torn apart. Even the stonework was scarred and pockmarked. Cannons’ work, he reckoned. Cannons filled with smiths’ oddments. A storm of hot metal no armour, no shield and for damn sure no courage could stop. The place stank of smoke and blood, of broken men and smashed-open horses and everything they hold.
bs: Mrtvih je Folk bilo posvuda. Brod se jedva mogao pomaknuti a da ne nagazi na nekoga. Mrtvi Folk i mrtvi konji, zapetljani i raskomadani. Čak je i kamenje bilo izbrazdano i izrovano. Topovski rad, procijenio je. Topovi napunjeni kovačkim otpacima. Oluja užarenog metala koju nijedan oklop, nijedan štit i, bogami, nijedna hrabrost nisu mogli zaustaviti. Mjesto je zaudaralo po dimu i krvi, po slomljenim ljudima, raskomadanim konjima i svemu što su sa sobom nosili.

en: He caught a flicker of movement, lurched back as a blade hissed past his nose. Lurched back again as the sword came at him the other way, caught it clumsily on the steel haft of his hammer.
bs: Spazio je djelić pokreta, trgnuo se natrag dok mu je oštrica prozujala pokraj nosa. Trgnuo se ponovno kad je mač poletio prema njemu nasuprot tome, nespretno ga dočekavši na čeličnu držalicu malja.

en: Broad staggered up, spitting, gasping for breath. Battle was done here for now, but it’d be back, like waves up a beach. Waves of blood that left bodies as flotsam. He could hear it coming. Screams and clashes. Mad honking, squealing, like pigs rutting.
bs: Brod se uspravio teturajući, pljujući i hvatajući zrak. Bitka je za sada ovdje završila, ali vratit će se, poput valova koji zapljuskuju obalu. Valovi krvi koji su za sobom ostavljali tijela kao olupine. Čuo je kako dolazi. Vriskovi i zveket. Ludo glasanje i cika, poput svinja u divljem zanosu.

en: Broad could see that. He could see that very clearly. He looked up at Jin, and the Northman looked back, and no words were any use.
bs: Brod je to vidio. Vidio je to posve jasno. Pogledao je gore u Džina, a Northman mu uzvrati Oko i svake su riječi bile suvišne.

en: “Best I can tell, the Young Lion’s glorious charge came to grief. Let that be a lesson for you in the value of glorious charges.”
bs: — Koliko vidim, slavni juriš Mladića Lava završio je neslavno. Neka ti to bude lekcija o vrijednosti slavnih juriša.

en: Some arrows fell fluttering and Clover dropped down, hunching his shoulders. Like hunching your shoulders would do any good. Who was shooting anyway? In all this, there was just as much chance of killing your side as theirs. Maybe it got so you didn’t care any more. So any killing seemed a sensible notion. Everyone else was at it, why be the one fool left out?
bs: Neke su strijele padale lepršajući, a Klover se srušio i sagnuo ramena. Kao da bi ti saginjanje ramena pomoglo. Tko je uopće pucao? U svemu ovome postojala je podjednaka šansa da ubiješ svoje ljude kao i njihove. Možda bi došlo do toga da te više nije briga. Pa se svako ubijanje činilo smislenom idejom. Svi su drugi to radili, zašto biti jedina budala koja zaostaje?

en: He’d taken the approach to battle Clover might’ve when his name was still Steepfield, which was to say running for wherever the fight was wildest, raging and flailing and spilling every drop of blood he could without a thought for shield or helm or consequences. He was so red-spattered, he might as well have gone swimming in a sea of corpses, doing his best imitation of the Bloody-Nine, the mad fucker.
bs: Bitci je pristupio onako kako bi to Klover možda učinio u vrijeme kad se još zvao Stipfild — trčeći onamo gdje je tuča bila najdivlja, bijesneći, mlateći i prolijevajući svaku kap krvi koju je mogao, bez ijedne pomisli na štit, kacigu ili posljedice. Bio je toliko poprskan krvlju da je komotno mogao poći zaplivati u moru leševa, dajući sve od sebe da oponaša Nine, tog luđaka.

en: Clover bent down to one of the corpses, some Union man huddled on his side like a child on a cold night. He took a quick peek about but everyone was bent to their own tragedies, so he stuck his hand in the man’s ripped-open jacket and flicked blood on his face, smeared it down his mail, rubbed his sword along the corpse’s side to get a bit of red on it.
bs: Klover se nagnuo nad jedno truplo, nekog vojnika Unije zgrčenog na bok poput djeteta u hladnoj noći. Letimično baci Oko oko sebe, ali svi bijahu zaokupljeni vlastitim tragedijama, pa zavuče ruku u čovjekovu rasparanu jaknu, poprska mu lice krvlju, razmaže je po njegovu oklopu i protrlja svoj mač uz leš kako bi na njuh uhvatio malo crvenila.

en: “There’s nothing more to prove up here, my king,” Clover shouted over the racket. “Time to bend with the breeze. Save what we can.”
bs: — Ovdje se više nema što dokazivati, moj kralju, doviknu Klover preko graje. — Vrijeme je da se savijemo s vjetrom. Da spasimo što se da spasiti.

en: Stour worked his red mouth a moment, frowning up towards the summit of the hill. Then he bared his teeth, and spat red, and turned away. “We fucking pull back.”
bs: Staur je nakratko pomaknuo Red usta, namrštivši se prema vrhu brda. Zatim je ogolio zube, pljunuo krv i okrenuo se. — Povlačimo se, u pičku materinu.

en: “No,” hissed Leo, forcing the one leg that worked underneath him, hooking his elbow around the saddle horn of a dead horse and hauling himself to a wobbling crouch.
bs: — Ne, prosiktao je Leo, oslanjajući se na jedinu nogu koja ga je služila, zakačivši lakat oko sedlarske kuke mrtva konja i podižući se u teturavi čučanj.

en: Something in his total lack of feeling made Leo utterly furious. He screamed as he lurched forward, lifting his sword for a clumsy thrust.
bs: Nešto u tom njegovom potpunom manjku osjećaja razbjesnilo je Lea do kraja. Vrisnuo je posrnuvši prema naprijed i podigavši mač za nespretan ubod.

en: Still, good teeth were one of Rikke’s few natural blessings that hadn’t been covered with tattoos or blinded with a needle, so she made the best use of ’em and smiled up wide enough to compensate for all the funereal faces.
bs: Ipak, zdravi zubi bili su jedan od rijetkih Rikkinih prirodnih darova koji joj nisu bili prekriveni tetovažama niti oslijepljeni iglom, pa ih je najbolje iskoristila i široko se nasmiješila gore, nadoknađujući sva ta pogrebnička lica.

en: “A Gurkish coin, how about that? All the way from the sunny South!” She stood, brushing her knees off. “Anyway, this is for whoever opens the gates. How you split it is up to you. If Master Silent wants to open ’em, he can share it out, I guess.” She left a meaningful pause. “Or the rest of you could. Have yourselves a wrestling match over the Gurkish one. Your business. Long as someone lets us in.”
bs: — Gurkijski novčić, što kažete na to? Sve tamo iz sunčanog Southa! Uspostane se, otresajući koljena. — u svakom slučaju, ovo je za tko god otvori vrata. Kako ćete ga podijeliti, vaša je stvar. Ako Majstor Silent želi otvoriti ta vrata, pretpostavljam da ga može raspodijeliti. Ostavila je rječitu stanku."Ili biste vi ostali mogli. Potucite se međusobno oko tog gurkijskog. Vaša stvar. Dok god nas netko ne pusti unutra."

en: The Nail didn’t shift a hair. He was one of those rare men goes beyond bravery to a kind of madness where there’s no regard for danger at all. He just watched whatever it was plummet down, hands on hips, and didn’t even flinch as it crashed into the cobbles a stride or two in front, spotting him with blood.
bs: Najl nije trepnuo. Bio je jedan od onih rijetkih Folk koji prelaze granicu hrabrosti i dospijevaju u vrstu ludila u kojoj opasnost uopće ne postoji. Samo je promatrao što god je to već bilo kako strmoglavo pada, s rukama na bokovima, i nije se čak ni pomaknuo kad se tresnulo o kaldrmu korak-dva Naprijed njega, poprskavši mu lice krvlju.

en: “Someone get a fire lit, eh?” she called out as the Named Men tramped into the hall. “Before I shiver my tits off.”
bs: — Neka netko naloži vatru, ha? povikala je dok su se Imenovani Folk teturajući uvaljivali u dvoranu. — Prije nego što se ovdje smrznem do kostiju.

en: The Nail turned on her, holding one fist up under her nose, close enough she had to look at it a little cross-eyed. “My father died in this fucking cage!”
bs: Najl se okrenu prema njoj, podigavši stisnutu pesnicu pod sam joj nos, toliko blizu da je morala pomalo razrokih očiju gledati u nju. — Otac mi je poginuo u ovom jebenom kavezu!

en: “Was there a cushion in your vision?” asked Isern. “You might think of finding one if you plan to perch there long.”
bs: — Je li u tvojoj viziji bio jastuk? upita Izern. — Mogla bi razmisliti o tome da ga pronađeš namjeravaš li ondje dugo čučati.

en: “So…” The Nail narrowed his eyes, counting off the points on his fingers. “You promised the Young Lion you were going with him, then not only did you not go, you stole his ally’s land while he was gone, and warned his enemies he was coming.”
bs: — Dakle… Najl suzi oči, brojeći točke na prstima."Obećala si Mlađem Lavu da ćeš poći s njim, a onda ne samo da nisi pošla, nego si mu dok je bio odsutan ukrala zemlju saveznika, i još upozorila njegove neprijatelje da dolazi."

en: Isern nodded. “He spent a lot of effort winkling his son onto that chair, d’you see? Won’t be overjoyed to hear you’ve wedged your skinny arse into his place.”
bs: Izern kimnu. — Uložio je silan trud da ugura svog sina na tu stolicu, razumiješ? Neće biti presretan kad čuje da si zabila svoju mršavu stražnjicu na njegovo mjesto.

en: The Nail nodded along in sympathy. “There are times I wish folk had never heard o’ me. Look small, look foolish, got no name, well… that’s when you’re given chances.”
bs: Najl je suosjećajno kimnuo glavom. — Ponekad bih poželio da Folk nikad nije čuo za mene. Djelovati sitno, ispasti glup, nemati ime, pa… to su trenuci kad ti se pružaju prilike.

en: The corpse-gatherers had been labouring from before first light. Whole companies of them, dragging cadavers by hand, by stretcher and by cart into orderly piles at the corners of fields. There prisoners made unwilling gravediggers chopped away with pick and shovel in an effort to make holes big enough to hold them all. Flies, crows and human scavengers had meanwhile appeared from nowhere, flitting busily among the bumper crop of bodies while there were still pickings to be had.
bs: Skupljači leševa radili su od prije zore. Čitave čete njih vukle su trupla rukama, na nosilima i kolima u uredne hrpe na rubovima polja. Ondje su zatvorenici, prisiljeni kopati rake, udarali pijukom i lopatom nastojeći iskopati rupe dovoljno velike da sve prime. Muhe, vrane i ljudski strvinari u međuvremenu su se niotkuda stvorili, žurno prelijećući bogatu žetvu tijela dok se još moglo štogod ugrabiti.

en: “Marvellous,” murmured Orso. “I have engineered a quantity of death to satisfy even the First of the Magi.” His eyes could hardly comprehend the carnage. He kept looking to one side, then scanning across, in an effort to take it all in. “How many people do you think died here?”
bs: — Divno, prošapta Orso. — Smislio sam dovoljno smrti da zadovoljim čak i Prvog od Magi. Oči su mu jedva uspijevale obuhvatiti pokolj. Neprestano je gledao u jednu stranu, pa prelazio pogledom unaokolo, pokušavajući sve to sagledati. — Koliko je Folk, po vašem mišljenju, ovdje poginulo?

en: “When it comes to the rank and file, I tend towards mercy,” said Orso. “We have enough Union men to bury.”
bs: — Što se tiče običnih vojnika, skloniji sam milosti, reče Orso. — Imamo dovoljno Folk iz Unije koje moramo pokopati.

en: “We can put down the Great Wolf another day.” Orso paused a moment, frowning. “There was no trouble from the Breakers in Keln?”
bs: — Možemo srediti Velikog Vuka drugog dana. Orso zastade na trenutak, mršteći se. — Nije bilo nikakvih neprilika s Lomljačima u Kelnu?

en: The door squealed open to reveal a dim chamber, walls glistening with damp, cut in half by rust-speckled gratings. Beyond, the wretched occupants of cells stuffed to bursting squinted into the light, shrank into the shadows, pressed themselves against the bars.
bs: Vrata su zaškripala i otkrila zamračenu prostoriju čiji su zidovi blistali od vlage, a napola ju je dijelila rešetka prošarana hrđom. Iza nje su bijedni stanovnici ćelija krcatih do pucanja škiljili prema svjetlu, povlačili se u sjenu i pribijali se uz rešetke.

en: Orso had hoped to feel some satisfaction at the sight of his sneering adversaries from the benches of the Open Council ruined. But he felt mostly hollow, irritable and slightly disappointed that he felt nothing more. As if all meaningful emotion for the year had been used up during the battle in one profligate splurge.
bs: Orso se nadao osjetiti barem malo zadovoljstva ugledavši propast svojih podrugljivih protivnika s klupa Otvorenog Vijeća. No osjećao je ponajprije prazninu, razdražljivost i blago razočaranje što ne osjeća išta više. Kao da su sve smislene emocije za tu godinu bile istrošene tijekom bitke u jednom rastrošnom izljevu.

en: “Your Majesty.” Pike leaned close to murmur. “I suggest they all be hanged as soon as is practicable.”
bs: — Vaša Uzvišenosti, prišapnu Pajk nagnuvši se blizu. — Predlažem da ih sve objesimo čim prije bude moguće.

en: Gorst lowered his eyes and trudged from the room, pulling the door shut. When Orso turned back, Brock had a pained grimace on his face.
bs: Gorst obori Oko i teškim korakom iziđe iz prostorije, privukavši vrata za sobom. Kad se Orso okrenuo natrag, Broku se na licu ocrtavala bolna grimasa.

en: Orso barked out a joyless laugh. “Please. As if she ever went into anything without her eyes wide open. I’ve no doubt she’s every bit as guilty as you are, if not more so. She doesn’t even have youth, stupidity and a massively bloated sense of her own importance as excuses.”
bs: Orso se nasmijao bez trunke radosti. — Molim te. Kao da je ikad išta započela a da nije širom otvorila oči. Nemam nimalo sumnje da je jednako kriva kao i ti, ako ne i više. Ona barem nema izgovore poput mladosti, gluposti i silno napuhanog osjećaja vlastite važnosti.

en: “My scripture teacher used to tell me…” murmured Zuri, eyes narrowed with concentration as she stitched, “that pain is a blessing.”
bs: —— Moj učitelj vjeronauka običavao mi je govoriti… promrmljala je Zuri, očiju suženih od koncentracije dok je šivala, da je bol blagoslov.

en: A cannon had burst, that’s what Zuri told her. A splinter of metal had grazed her head, ripped her wig off and knocked her flat. A little lower and it would have sprayed her brains across the hillside. She had missed the chaos of the rout, bouncing unconscious in the back of a wagon. A lady of taste should appear to make no effort. The right things simply happen around her. She woke here in the woods, with the worst headache she’d ever had.
bs: Topovska granata je pukla, to joj je Zuri rekla. Krhotina metala okrznula joj je glavu, otkinula periku i bacila je ničice. Malo niže i raznijela bi joj mozak po obronku. Promakao joj je kaos paničnog bijega dok je u nesvijesti odskakivala na stražnjem dijelu kola. Dama s ukusom trebala bi djelovati kao da se uopće ne trudi. Prave se stvari jednostavno događaju oko nje. Probudila se ovdje u šumi, s najgorom glavoboljom koju je ikada osjetila.

en: “Done?” asked Broad, standing over them. He offered one big hand. The one with the tattoo on its back. Savine noticed the knuckles were all scratched and scabbed. “Lady Savine?”
bs: — Gotovo? upita Brod stojeći nad njima. Pruži jednu veliku šaku. Onu s tetovažom na nadlanici. Savine primijeti da su joj zglobovi bili izgrebani i prekriveni krastama. — Lady Savine?

en: “It’s my only chance to save myself. We have no supplies. The king’s forces are everywhere. My entourage is down to two and it’s two more than I deserve. We’ll never make it to the coast. Not with me the size of a house.”
bs: — To mi je jedina prilika da spasim samu sebe. Nemamo zaliha. Kraljeve su snage svugdje. Moja se pratnja svela na dvoje, a i to je dvoje više nego što zaslužujem. Nikada nećemo stići do obale. Ne s trbuhom do zuba.

en: Perhaps those searching for her were far to the North, watching the coast for her escape. Perhaps they were looking for someone fleeing her crimes, not limping meekly back through their very scene. Perhaps—bald, bloody and bedraggled—she bore little resemblance to anyone’s idea of the famous beauty Savine dan Glokta, and her own least of all.
bs: Možda su oni koji su je tražili bili daleko na sjeveru, motreći obalu ne bi li spriječili njezin bijeg. Možda su tražili nekoga tko bježi pred svojim zločinima, a ne nekoga tko se skrušeno i šepajući vraća na samo mjesto zločina. Možda je — ćelava, krvava i dronjava — najmanje od svih nalikovala na bilo čiju predodžbu o slavnoj ljepotici Savine dan Glokta, a ponajmanje na vlastitu.

en: If she had really tried, if she had truly wanted to, she could have found a way to stop this. There were a thousand moments when she could have found a way to stop this.
bs: Da se zaista potrudila, da je to doista htjela, mogla je pronaći način da ovo zaustavi. Postojalo je tisuću trenutaka u kojima je mogla pronaći način da ovo zaustavi.

en: Savine felt Broad’s heavy hand on her other shoulder. “No one makes a thing like this happen alone. We all had our hand in it.”
bs: Savine osjeti Brodovu tešku ruku na svom drugom ramenu. — Nitko ovakve stvari ne čini sam. Svi smo mi umiješali prste u to.

en: From time to time, she heard guards outside the door. Muffled voices. Even laughter. She was a prisoner, then. Something she had better get used to, she supposed. Along with being universally reviled, all she had built ruined, her name used as a cheap joke or a warning lecture—
bs: Povremeno čula je stražare pred vratima. Prigušene glasove. Čak i smijeh. Dakle, bila je zatvorenica. Nešto na što će se morati naviknuti, pretpostavila je. Uz to što je bila općenito omražena, sve što je izgradila uništeno, a njezino ime korišteno kao jeftina šala ili upozoravajuća lekcija —

en: “I was surprised to hear you had given yourself up. I felt sure you’d be slithering away somewhere to hatch some new scheme.” The room was warm, but his voice was cold enough to make the hairs on her arms bristle.
bs: — Iznenadilo me čuti da si se predala. Bio sam siguran da ćeš negdje gmizati kako bi skovala neki novi plan. U sobi je bilo toplo, ali njegov je glas bio dovoljno hladan da joj se naježe dlačice na rukama.

en: “I would’ve been amazed if you hadn’t. But somehow I kept hoping.” Orso bared his teeth. “I received a letter, some time ago, warning me of a conspiracy to steal my throne. A plot by members of the Open Council. With friends in the North.”
bs: — Čudio bih se da nisi. No, nekako sam se nadao. Orso ogoli zube. "Primio sam pismo prije nekog vremena, koje me upozoravalo na urotu da mi se otme prijestolje. Urotu članova Vijeća. S prijateljima na Sjeveru."

en: She did, and it was pounding now. She felt as if her battered skull was going to split. He gripped the arms of her chair with white knuckles and she shrank back, turning her face away as he leaned down over her, snarling, spitting, stabbing at his chest with a finger.
bs: Imala ga je, i sada je mahnito udaralo. Osjećala se kao da će joj se razbijena lubanja raspući. On dohvati naslone njezine stolice bijelih zglobova te se ona trznu unatrag, odmaknuvši lice dok se nadvio nad nju, režeći, pljujući, udarajući prstom po vlastitim prsima.

en: “I lost my way after that!” She struggled up somehow, took a wobbling step towards him. “I lost all my judgement. I was just… pretending… to be me. I was still trapped in Valbeck, somehow! I couldn’t see… past my own ambitions… I didn’t have anything else!” Pathetic excuses, mangled in her dry mouth. “Leo… he’s a good man. He could be… but he’s so easily led. Isher and the rest brought him to this.” She closed her eyes, tears welling down her face. “I brought him to this. Blame me. I wanted… I d
bs: — Nakon toga sam izgubila kompas! Jedva se uspravila, napravila kolebljiv korak prema njemu."Izgubila sam svaku prosudbu. Samo sam… glumila… da sam ja. Bila sam još uvijek zarobljena u Valbeku, nekako! Nisam mogla vidjeti… dalje od vlastitih ambicija… nisam imala ništa drugo!" Jadne isprike, skučene u suhim ustima. — Leo… on je dobar čovjek. Mogao bi biti… ali njime je tako lako upravljati. Išer i ostali doveli su ga do ovoga. Sklopila je oči, a suze su joj se slivale niz lice. — Ja sam ga dovel

en: They’d scratched together a crew half his men, half Stour’s young bastards who’d lived through the battle. One had a wound in his back and died after a night of groaning on the water. They’d rolled him over the side, the only ceremony Clover’s observation that not everyone goes back to the mud after all. Some get the big drink instead. Greenway had looked green the whole way, and especially green at that, Rikke’s prediction that he’d die on water no doubt weighing on his mind.
bs: Skrpili su posadu napola od njegovih Folk, napola od Staurovih mladih kopiladi koja su preživjela bitku. Jedan je imao ranu na leđima i preminuo nakon noći stenjanja na vodi. Prevalili su ga preko palube, a jedini ispraćaj bila je Kloverova opaska kako naposljetku ipak ne završavaju svi u blatu. Neki umjesto toga dobiju veliko piće. Grinvej je cijelim putem izgledao zeleno u licu, a osobito zeleno u tom trenutku, dok mu se Rikino proročanstvo da će skončati na vodi nedvojbeno motalo po glavi.

en: “In my experience o’ the Great Wolf,” mused Clover, “and I have about as much these days as any man alive, he’s not prone to look on the sunny side. I’d best try and calm the bastard, eh?” He heaved out a sigh as he stood. “Doubt anyone else will.” And he pulled the damp blanket off and tossed it over Sholla’s head.
bs: — Prema mojem iskustvu s Velikim Vukom, razmišljao je Klover, a imam ga otprilike koliko i bilo koji čovjek koji je još živ, on nije sklon gledati na vedriju stranu života. Bit će najbolje da pokušam umiriti tog kopilana, zar ne? Teško je uzdahnuo dok se uspravljao. — Sumnjam da će itko drugi. Potom je skinuo vlažnu deku i prebacio joj je preko glave.

en: Stour glared at him. Seemed he found that a touch too philosophical when he was still licking his wounds in the shadow of disappointment.
bs: Staur ga prostrijeli pogledom. Činilo se kako mu je to mrvicu previše filozofski s obzirom na to da je još lizao rane u sjeni razočaranja.

en: Then, quick as the weather shifts in autumn, he grinned. “You’ve been loyal to me, Clover. I know I’m not always the easiest. No, no, don’t deny it.” No one had thought about denying it. “But if any man can talk me into looking on the sunny side, it’s you.” He reached out and gave Clover a slap on the shoulder. “You’ll get your reward, don’t worry about that.”
bs: Zatim se, naglo poput promjene vremena u jesen, nasmiješi. — Bio si mi odan, Klovere. Znam da mi nije uvijek lako ugoditi. Ne, ne, nemoj poricati." Nitko nije ni pomišljao poricati. — Ali ako me ikatko može nagovoriti da sagledam stvari s vedrije strane, onda si to ti." Pruži ruku i ošamari Klovera po ramenu. — Dobit ćeš svoju nagradu, ne brini se zbog toga.

en: “Traitor, did he say?” Clover raised a brow at Downside. Downside shrugged and set to wiping Greenway’s brains off his axe. “Traitor, did you say?” Clover shoved Stour down again and smiled. After so long under this little shit’s boot, felt awfully nice to have their positions swapped about.
bs: — Izdajica, reče li on? Klover je uzdigao obrvu prema Dausaidu. Dausaid je slegnuo ramenima i prionuo brisati Grinvejov mozak sa sjekire. — Izdajica, reče li ti? Klover je ponovno gurnuo Staura dolje i nasmiješio se. Nakon toliko vremena provedenog pod čizmom ovoga malog govna, bilo je strahovito ugodno zamijeniti im mjesta.

en: There were men waiting in the light of the fake beacon, just as they’d arranged. Hard-bitten men with weapons, scars and scowls in abundance. Clover knew a few faces. Named Men of Uffrith and the West Valleys, the Nail standing among ’em in that crookback slouch of his with thumbs in his sword-belt. At their front, arms folded, metal eye glinting through his long hair, stood Caul Shivers.
bs: U svjetlu lažnog svjetionika čekali su Folk, baš kako su se i dogovorili. Prekaljeni Folk, naoružani, izbrazdanih lica i mrkih pogleda. Klover je poznavao neka lica. Imenovani Folk Afrita i Zapadnih dolina, a među njima stoji Najl, onako pognutih leđa, s palčevima zadenutim za mačev pojas. Na čelu im, prekriženih ruku, dok mu metalno oko sjaji kroz dugu kosu, stajao je Caul Šivers.

en: “She’s got that cage ready for you. You remember? The one in Skarling’s Hall? The one you kept my da in?”
bs: — Pripremila ti je onaj kavez. Sjećaš se? Onaj u Skarlingovoj dvorani? U koji si zatvorio mog starog?

en: The Nail gave a high little titter. “Can’t see it. To be a swordsman you have to be able to stand up.” And he bent down, grabbed hold of two fistfuls of Stour’s trouser legs and yanked them down hard. Yanked them right down to his ankles.
bs: Najl otpusti sitan, visok smijuljak. — Ne vidim to. Da bi bio mačevalac, moraš moći stajati na nogama." I sagnuvši se, dograbi dvije pregršti Staurovih nogavica te ih snažno trgnu prema dolje. Trgnu ih skroz do gležnjeva.

en: There was a silent pause, like it took a moment for Stour to realise what had happened, then his eyes bulged and he gave a great sobbing shriek, wriggling and twisting, blood running in streaks down his calf. Sholla winced and looked the other way. Downside frowned, and held Stour tight, careless as a shepherd holding a sheep for shearing. The Nail grinned like he’d never heard such a joke.
bs: Nastade tiha stanka, kao da je Stauru trebalo trenutka da shvati što se dogodilo, a onda mu oči iskočiše iz duplji te on pusti silan, grcan vrisak, meškoljeći se i savijajući, dok mu je krv u mlazovima curila niz listove. Šola se zgrozi i odvrati Oko. Dausaid se namršti i čvrsto držaše Staura, ležerno poput pastira koji drži ovcu za striženje. Najl se iskesi kao da nikada u životu nije čuo bolju šalu.

en: Climbing the steps to the platform might’ve been the hardest thing Leo had ever done, but he was determined to get there on his own. Determined to salvage that much pride though, the dead knew, pride had done him no favours. Pride had put him here in the first place.
bs: Penjanje uz stepenice na podest možda je bilo najteže što je Leo ikada učinio, ali bio je odlučan stići ondje sam. Odlučan sačuvati barem toliko ponosa — premda je, bogami, ponos malo toga učinio za njega. Ponos ga je uopće i dovio ovamo.

en: He worked himself up with his good arm, teeth gritted, managed to ease his right leg under him, groaning as his weight went onto the stump of his left. But once he’d made it to hands and knees—or hand and knee, at any rate—how to get further? He couldn’t reach for the crutch without falling, and even if he could, how would he push himself up? There’d been a time when achieving the impossible for Leo dan Brock had meant besting the greatest swordsman of the age, or breaking an enemy’s line single
bs: Podignuo se oslanjajući se na zdravu ruku, stisnutih zubi, uspio namjestiti desnu nogu ispod sebe i zajaukao kad mu se težina prebacila na bataljak lijeve. No kad se jednom domogao četveronožnog položaja — ili bolje rečeno, položaja na jednoj ruci i jednoj nozi — kako dalje? Nije mogao posegnuti za šakom a da ne padne, a sve i da je mogao, kako bi se odgurnuo gore? Bilo je vrijeme kada je postizanje nemogućeg za Lea dâ Broka značilo nadmašiti najvećeg mačevaoca tog doba, ili sam probiti neprijat

en: It all felt strangely bland. Strangely banal. He’d hardly known what to expect. Yet another irony. The first hanging he’d ever attended would be his own.
bs: Sve se činilo neobično bljutavim. Neobično banalnim. Jedva da je znao što očekivati. Još jedna ironija. Prvo vješanje kojem je ikada prisustvovao bit će njegovo vlastito.

en: It was better to imagine that Leo dan Brock died on the battlefield. It was true, in every way that mattered. He’d been a great fire, burning brightly. Why cry at the snuffing out of the feeble ember that remained?
bs: Bilo je bolje zamrijeti u mislima da je Leo dan Brok poginuo na bojnom polju. Bila je to istina, u svakom smislu koji je bio važan. Bio je velika Palioc koja je sjajno gorjela. Zašto plakati nad gasnućem tog slabašnog žara što je preostao?

en: He could hardly bear to look at her. Even though hers was the only sympathetic face in the whole ruined square. Because hers was the only sympathetic face. At the sight of her, he might realise all he was about to lose.
bs: Jedva ju je mogao gledati. Premda je njezino lice bilo jedino sućutno u cijelome razorenom Trgu. Upravo zato što je njezino lice bilo jedino sućutno. Ugledavši je, mogao je shvatiti sve što će izgubiti.

en: There were a dozen other people who’d brought them to this. A hundred. Isher, nowhere now to be seen, had sown the seed. Heugen and Barezin himself had eagerly watered the sprouts. Savine and Stour had their parts in tending the crop. Even Rikke and the Breakers, by going back on their word, had helped bring in this harvest of hangings.
bs: Bilo je tu tucet drugih Folk koji su ih doveli do ovoga. A stotinu. Išer, kojemu se sada nije vidio trag, posijao je sjeme. Heugen i sam Barezin željno su zalijevali klice. Savine i Staur imali su svoje uloge u njegovanju usjeva. Čak su i Rike i Lomljači, pogazivši svoju riječ, pomogli požnjeti ovu žetvu vješanja.

en: The whole while, as he listened to the others rage, blurt, weep, reason, all to no purpose, he’d wondered what he’d say. Now the moment came, the last moment, he found he had nothing.
bs: Sve dok je slušao druge kako bjesne, blebeću, plaču i razumno argumentiraju, i to sve uzalud, pitao se što će reći. Sada kada je taj trenutak došao, posljednji trenutak, shvatio je da nema ništa.

en: Leo’s life was measured in moments now. In breaths. In heartbeats. He didn’t want to look, couldn’t look away, winced as the executioner pulled Lady Wetterlant’s lever—
bs: Leo se život sada mjerio u trenucima. U udasima. U otkucajima srca. Nije želio gledati, a nije mogao odgledati, i trgnuo se kad je krvnik povukao polugu gospođe Wetterlant —

en: “Fuck yourselves, you bastards!” Lady Wetterlant had worked free of her gag and now started screaming insults again. “Damn you all, you vultures! You worms!”
bs: — Jebite se, kopiladi! Gospođa Vetelant uspjela se osloboditi poveza na ustima te je ponovno počela vikati uvrede. — Prokletstvo svima vama, strvinarima! Crvima jednim!

en: He dropped under the platform and with a snap his rope jerked tight. So it seemed great lords of the Open Council meet the long drop just like other men.
bs: Propao je ispod platforme i uže mu se uz prasak zategnulo. Činilo se, dakle, da i moćni Lords s Open Councila pronalaze dugi Dausaid jednako kao i svi drugi Folk.

en: Then Orso slumped back in his chair and gave a sharp wave of his hand. “Leo dan Brock, I commute your sentence to life imprisonment.”
bs: Tada se Orso zavalio u stolicu i oštro mahnuo rukom. — Leo dan Brok, preinačujem tvoju kaznu u doživotni zatvor.

en: It was a bright autumn day when Vick rode back into Valbeck. The place looked nothing like the last time she was there, in the final chaotic days of the uprising. No rubbish choking the streets, no burned-out shells of buildings, no sounds of distant violence, no unattended corpses. Only a few pink smears showing through the hastily applied whitewash, reminding the careful observer that these buildings were once daubed with Burners’ slogans. There was even a pleasant breeze, carrying the smog of
bs: Bilo je to vedro jesensko jutro kad je Vik jahala natrag u Valbek. Mjesto nije nimalo nalikovalo na ono otprije, na dane kaotičnog finala ustanka. Nije bilo smeća koje bi gušilo ulice, ni izgorjelih kostura zgrada, ni odjeka dalekog nasilja, ni nepočišćenih leševa. Tek bi pokoja ružičasta mrlja probijala kroz na brzinu navučeni vapnac, podsjećajući opreznog promatrača da su te zgrade nekoć bile išarane parolama Palitelja. Puhao je čak i ugodan povjetarac, noseći smog obnovljenih manufaktura u un

en: “The Breakers are traitors,” said Vick. Stick to the official line. He could only judge her on what she said, not what she thought. “Enemies of the king. There’s nothing to sympathise with.”
bs: — Lomljači su izdajnici, reče Vik. Drži se službene linije. Mogao ju je suditi samo po onome što je rekla, ne po onome što je mislila. — Neprijatelji kralja. Tu se nema za čime simpatizirati.

en: “It was Colonel West who pulled me from the camps,” he mused, “without the slightest idea that we had known each other years before. In his company I even held a shield in a duel, if you can believe that. When the Bloody-Nine beat the Feared and made himself King of the Northmen! Life is… such a cobweb of coincidences, isn’t it? West was a man one could admire.” He gave a sorry sigh. “But the truly good men never seem to last. He died, and I began to work with Arch Lector Glokta. Even though I k
bs: — Pukovnik West bio je taj koji me izvukao iz logora, zamisli se on, — ne imajući ni najmanje predodžbe da smo se poznavali još od ranije. U njegovoj sam četi čak držao štit u dvoboju, ako to možeš vjerovati. Kada je Krvavi Nine potukao Strašenog i proglasio se kraljem Sjevernjaka! Život je… tolika paučina slučajnosti, zar ne? West je bio čovjek kojemu se moglo diviti. Teško uzdahnu. — No izgleda da istinski dobri Folk nikada ne opstaju. On je umro, a ja sam počeo surađivati s nadlektorom Glokto

en: “Who are these?” muttered Vick. Some private militia, hired to keep the peace with the king’s soldiers gone? But something didn’t fit. Rough-looking men, all standing their own way. Clean armour, maybe, but unshaven faces.
bs: — Tko su ovi? promrmlja Vik. Nekakva privatna milicija, unajmljena da održava mir nakon što su kraljevi vojnici otišli? No nešto se nije uklapalo. Grubi Folk, svaki na svoj način. Očišćen oklop, možda, ali neobrijana lica.

en: Like every puzzle, once Vick knew the answer, she couldn’t understand how she hadn’t seen it right away. She was the one who’d fallen into the trap. She alone.
bs: Poput svake zagonetke, jednom kad je Vik saznala odgovor, nije mogla shvatiti kako ga nije odmah prozrela. Ona je bila ta koja je upala u klopku. Ona sama.

en: “I called the like-minded people I gathered the Breakers,” said Pike, watching Judge set her torch to oil-soaked wood at the bank’s doors. “Not because we would break machines, though we have, but because we would break the Union. Break it, and rebuild it in a new way. A better way.” Pike watched the flames lick at Valint and Balk’s fine new stonework and the armed Breakers gathered in the square gave a great cheer. “The banks have twisted about the nation like ivy about a tree, choking all life
bs: — Ljude istomišljenike koje sam okupio nazvao sam Lomljačima, reče Pajk, promatrajući kako Džadž prislanja baklju na drvo natopljeno uljem pred vratima banke. — Ne zato što bismo lomili strojeve, premda jesmo, već zato što bismo slomili Unija. Slomiti ga i izgraditi na nov način. Na bolji način. Pajk je gledao kako plamenovi ližu fino klesani kamen Valinta i Balka, a naoružani Lomljači okupljeni na trgu gromoglasno su zapljeskali. — Banke su se ovile oko nacije poput bršljana oko stabla, gušeći

en: “You served Glokta faithfully,” said Pike. “Admirably, even. Because he was the one man who ever gave you anything. Even if it was only the chance to wear the boot, rather than having it ground into your face.” He did understand her, damn it. Maybe not better than she understood herself, but well enough. “I would like to offer you something more.”
bs: — Vjerno si služila Glokti, reče Pajk. — Čak i hvalevrijedno. Jer on je bio jedini čovjek koji ti je ikada išta pružio. Čak i ako je to bila samo prilika da nosiš čizmu, umjesto da ti njome melju lice. Razumio ju je, kvragu. Možda ne bolje nego što je ona razumjela samu sebe, ali dovoljno dobro. — Želio bih ti ponuditi nešto više.

en: “Leave. Go back to King Orso. Serve his corrupt regime in its dying days. Or run to distant Thond, for that matter, where they worship the sun. Go with our blessing.”
bs: — Odlazi. Vrati se kralju Orsou. Služi njegovu korumpiranom režimu u njegovim posljednjim danima. Ili bježi u daleki Thond, što se toga tiče, gdje štuju sunce. Idi s našim blagoslovom.

en: To the artists responsible for somehow continuing to make me look classy: Didier Graffet, Dave Senior, Laura Brett, Lauren Panepinto, Raymond Swanland, Tomás Almeida, Sam Weber.
bs: Umjetnicima zaslužnima što nekako i dalje čine da izgledam uglađeno: Didieru Graffetu, Daveu Senioru, Lauri Brett, Lauren Panepinto, Raymondu Swanlandu, Tomásu Almeidi, Samu Weberu.

en: Arch Lector Sand dan Glokta—“Old Sticks,” the most feared man in the Union, Head of the Closed Council and His Majesty’s Inquisition.
bs: Vrhovni lektor Sand dan Glokta — "Stari Sticks, najstrašniji čovjek u Uniji, šef Zatvorenog vijeća i Inkvizicije Njegova Veličanstva.

en: Grand Duchess Monzcarro Murcatto—“The Serpent of Talins,” mother of King Jappo, a feared general and ruthless politician, responsible for the unification of Styria.
bs: Velika vojvotkinja Monzcarro Murkato — "Zmija s Talinsa, majka kralja Džapa, strašna generalica i nemilosrdna političarka, zaslužna za ujedinjenje Stirije.

en: The Prophet Khalul—former Second of the Magi, now arch-enemy of Bayaz. Rumoured to have been killed by a demon, plunging the South into chaos.
bs: Prorok Khalul — bivši Drugi među magovima, sada Bajazov smrtni neprijatelj. Šuška se da ga je ubio demon, gurnuvši South u kaos.

en: “I did, didn’t I.” An unforced smile was creeping across Orso’s face, all by itself. He could hardly remember the last time that happened. “The Young Lion, beaten bloody by the Young Lamb.” His clothes just seemed to fit him better than they had before the battle. He rubbed at his jaw, left unshaven for a few days in all the excitement. “Should I grow a beard?”
bs: — Jesam, zar ne? Izazvan ničim, iskren osmijeh sam od sebe se širio Orsovim licem. Jedva se mogao sjetiti se kada mu se to posljednji put dogodilo. — Juvens Lav, krvavo pretučen od Mlađeg Janjeta. Odjeća mu je naprosto pristajala bolje nego prije bitke. Protrlja bradu, neobrijanu već nekoliko dana u silnom uzbuđenju. — Trebao bih pustiti bradu?

en: “Doubtless.” Orso could not help glancing towards the rear of the column yet again. The wounded Lord Governor of Angland was not their only significant captive. Behind the Young Lion’s prison wagon rattled the heavily guarded carriage containing his heavily pregnant wife. Was that Savine’s pale hand gripping the windowsill? The mere thought of her name made Orso wince. When the only woman he had ever loved married another man, then betrayed him, he had fondly imagined he could feel no worse. The
bs: — nesumnjivo. Orso nije mogao odoljeti a da još jednom ne pogleda prema začelju kolone. Ranjeni guverner Englend nije bio njihov jedini važan zarobljenik. Iza zatvorskih kola Mladića Lava kloparala je strogo čuvana kočija u kojoj se nalazila njegova trudna supruga. Je li to bila Savinina blijeda ruka na prozorskom okviru? Sama pomisao na njezino ime natjerala je Orsa da se strese. Kad se jedina žena koju je ikada volio udala za drugoga, a potom ga izdala, naivno je vjerovao da se ne može osjećat

en: The wagon grew even gloomier. Its clattering wheels began to echo. Beyond the barred window Leo saw cut stone rush past, knew they must be riding through one of Adua’s gates. He’d dreamed of entering the capital at the head of a triumphant parade. Instead he came locked in a prison wagon stinking of stale straw, wounds and shame.
bs: U kolima je postajalo sve mračnije. Njihovi su kotači počeli odjekivati. Iza rešetaka na prozoru Leo je vidio kako klesani kamen promiče pokraj njega; znao je da moraju prolaziti kroz jedna od vrata Adua. Sanjao je o ulasku u prijestolnicu na čelu pobjedničke povorke. Umjesto toga, stigao je zaključan u zatvorskim kolima koja su zaudarala na ustajalu slamu, rane i sramotu.

en: He should’ve sent his reply to Orso’s dinner invitation on the end of a lance, attacked with every man before sunset and swept the lying bastard from the high ground, torn up his reinforcements as they arrived.
bs: Odgovor na Orsov poziv na večeru trebao je poslati na vrhu koplja, napasti sa svim ljudima prije zalaska sunca i pomesti lažljivo kopile s uzvisine, rasturiti njegova pojačanja čim pristignu.

en: “By the dead,” he whispered. A warehouse had been burned out, its charred rafters like the ribs of a picked-over carcass. A slogan was daubed across its blackened front in letters three strides high.
bs: — Tako mi mrtvih, prošaptao je. Skladište je izgorjelo do temelja, a njegove ugljenisane grede izgledale su poput rebara očišćene strvine. Preko pocrnjelog pročelja bio je ispisan slogan slovima visokim tri koraka.

en: It had probably begun as a strike. Savine knew every manufactory in Adua, and this was Foss dan Harber’s paper mill, a concern she had twice declined to invest in. The profits were tempting, but Harber’s reputation stank. He was the kind of brutal, exploitative owner who made it hard for everyone else to properly exploit their workers. It had probably begun as a strike then turned, as strikes quickly can, into something altogether uglier.
bs: Vjerojatno je sve počelo kao štrajk. Savine je poznavala svaku manufakturu u Adui, a ovo je bila papirna utvrda Fossa dan Harbera, posjed u koji je dvaput odbila ulagati. Zarada je bila primamljiva, ali Harberov je glas smrdio. Bio je onaj tip okrutnog, izrabljivačkog vlasnika zbog kojega je svima drugima bilo teško propisno iscrpljivati radnike. Vjerojatno je sve počelo kao štrajk, a onda se pretvorilo, kao što štrajkovi brzo i znaju, u nešto posve ružnije.

en: “Traitor!” someone screamed. At her? At Leo? An arm hooked through, a dirty hand fishing for the catch. Savine smashed at it clumsily with the side of her fist, not sure whether it would be worse to be dragged from the carriage by the mob or dragged to the House of Questions by the Inquisition.
bs: — Izdajnik!, netko je vrisnuo. Njoj? Leo? Ruka se uvukla unutra, prljavi prsti opipavali su bravu. Savine ju je nespretno udarila bočnom stranom šake, ne znajući je li gore da je svjetina izvuče iz kočije ili da je Inkvizicija odvuče u Kuću pitanja.

en: Gorst spurred past, teeth bared as he hacked savagely on one side then the other, bodies dropping. “The king!” he squealed. “The king!”
bs: Gorst prostruji pokraj njih s ogoljenim zubima, divljački sijekući čas na jednu, čas na drugu stranu, dok su tijela padala. — Kralj!, zacvilio je. — Kralj!

en: Outside the window she saw Lord Chamberlain Hoff clinging to his reins, chain of office tangled tight around his red throat. She saw the king’s old, grey-haired standard-bearer gripping his flagstaff, the sun of the Union streaming overhead, an oily smear across the cloth of gold.
bs: Kroz prozor je ugledala lorda komornika Hoff kako se grčevito drži za uzde, s lancem službe čvrsto omotanim oko svog crvenog grla. Ugledala je kraljeva starog, sijedog stjegonošu kako steže stijeg, dok je sunce Unije lebdjelo nad njima, poput masne mrlje na zlatnoj tkanini.

en: After they brought him down from the gallows, she had changed the dressing on his leg. It seemed the sort of thing a wife should do for her wounded husband. Especially when his wounds were in large part her doing. She had thought she could be strong. She was notorious for cool ruthlessness, after all. But as she unwound the bandages in an obscene striptease they had gone from spotted brown, to pink, to black. The stump revealed. The dressmaker’s nightmare of clumsy stitching. The weeping purple-
bs: Nakon što su ga skinuli s vješala, promijenila mu je zavoj na nozi. Činilo se to kao nešto što bi supruga trebala učiniti za svog ranjenog muža. Posebno kada su njegove rane u velikoj mjeri bile njezino djelo. Mislila je da može biti jaka. Uostalom, bila je ozloglašena po svojoj hladnoj bezobzirnosti. No dok je odmotavala zavoje u opscenom striptizu, oni su prelazili iz smeđih mrlja u ružičaste, pa u crne. Ukazao se batrljak. Krojačeva noćna mora smetenih šavova. Suzeće grimizno Red nazubljenih

en: Orso strode across the Square of Marshals in the rough direction of the palace, fists clenched. The sight of her still somehow took his breath away. But there were more pressing concerns than the smouldering ruins of his love life.
bs: Orso je koračao preko Trga maršala u grubom smjeru palače, stisnutih šaka. Prizor nje još mu je nekako oduzimao dah. No, postojale su preče brige od tinjajućih ruševina njegova ljubavnog života.

en: “That feels a very long time ago,” said Orso, stalking on. He was concerned that if he did not keep moving, he might collapse like a child’s tower of bricks. “I have already received the congratulations of a considerable crowd of rioters on the Kingsway.” And he frowned up at the looming statue of Casamir the Steadfast, wondering whether he had ever been obliged to flee from his own people through the streets of his own capital. The history books made no mention of it.
bs: — To se čini kao vrlo davno, rekao je Orso, nastavljajući žurno hodati. Zabrinulo ga je da bi se, ako ne nastavi kretati, mogao srušiti poput dječje kule od kocaka. — Već sam primio čestitke poprilične gomile izgrednika na Kingswayu. I namrštio se gledajući uvis prema prijetećem kipu Kazimira Postojanog, pitajući se je li on ikada bio prisiljen bježati od vlastitog naroda ulicama vlastite prijestolnice. Povijest o tome nije zabilježila ništa.

en: “I hope so, Your Grace,” said the knight herald. “Groups of Breakers have taken over some of the manufactories. They march openly in the Three Farms, calling for… well, the resignation of His Majesty’s Closed Council.” Orso did not care for the way he said resignation. It felt like a euphemism for something considerably more final. “People are stirred up, Your Majesty. People want blood.”
bs: — Nadam se, Vaša Milosti, reče Ritter glasnik. "Skupine Lomljača preuzele su neke od manufaktura. Otvoreno marširaju kroz Tri Farme, pozivajući na… pa, ostavku Vijeća Vašeg Veličanstva." Orso nije mario za način na koji je izgovorio ostavku. Zvučalo je kao eufemizam za nešto znatno konačnije. — Folk su uzburkani, Vaša Uzvišenosti. Folk žele krv.

en: “Bloody streets indeed,” murmured Orso, wiping his cheek with his fingertips and seeing them come away lightly smeared with red. Gorst’s handiwork had left him speckled all over. “Any news from Arch Lector Pike?”
bs: — Krvavim ulicama, uistinu, promrmljao je Orso, brišući obraz vršcima prstiju i gledajući kako se na njima pojavljuju blijedi tragovi crvene boje. Gorstov ga je rad ostavio išaranog po cijelom tijelu. — Ima li vijesti od Lektora Pajka?

en: “A bloody plague of treason,” breathed Hoff, eyes fixed on the empty chair at the bottom of the table. “Can we get a message to Lord Bayaz?”
bs: "Krvava kuga izdaje", izdahnuo je Hoff, očiju prikovanih za praznu stolicu na dnu stola. — Možemo li poslati poruku lordu Bajazu?

en: Vick had half-expected, half-hoped that they’d melt away as they slogged across the muddy country in worsening weather, but their numbers had quickly swelled. In came labourers, smallholders and farmers with scythes and pitchforks—which caused some concern—and with flour and hams—which caused some celebration. In came gangs of beggars and gangs of orphans. In came soldiers, deserted from who knew what lost battalions. In came dealers, whores and demagogues, dishing up husk, fucks and political t
bs: Vik je napola očekivala, napola se nadala da će se osuti dok budu gazili kroz blatnjavi Country po sve gorem vremenu, ali njihov se broj brzo povećao. Pridružili su se nadničari, sitni posjednici i seljaci s kosama i vilama – što je izazvalo određenu zabrinutost – te s brašnom i šunkama – što je izazvalo slavlje. Stizale su bande prosjaka i skupine siročadi. Stizali su vojnici, dezerteri iz tko zna kojih izgubljenih bojni. Stizali su trgovci, kurve i demagozi, servirajući prazne priče, jebačinu

en: Now she had that feeling again, but she knew the quake had only just begun. How long would the world shiver? What would still be standing when it stopped?
bs: Sada ju je taj osjećaj ponovno obuzeo, no znala je da je potres tek počeo. Koliko će dugo svijet drhtati? Što će ostati uspravno kada sve stane?

en: Risinau worried Vick. The one-time Superior of Valbeck was considered a deep thinker, but far as she could tell he was an idiot’s notion of a genius, his ideas a maze with nothing at the centre, heavy on the righteous society to come but light as air on the route they’d take to get there. The pockets of his jacket bulged with papers. Scrawled theories, manifestos, proclamations. Speeches he whined out to eager throngs whenever the People’s Army halted. Vick didn’t like the way the crowd greeted
bs: Risinau je zabrinjavao Vik. Bivšeg Superiora iz Valbeka smatrali su dubokoumnim misliocem, no koliko je ona mogla procijeniti, on je bio idiotova predodžba genija; njegove su ideje bile labirint bez središta, pun teških riječi o pravednom društvu koje dolazi, ali posve isprazne o puta kojim će do njega stići. Džepovi njegova kaputa bili su izbočeni od papira. Naškrabane teorije, manifesti, proglasi. Govori koje je cvilio pred nestrpljivim masama kad god bi se Narodna vojska zaustavila. Vik se ni

en: “The world doesn’t need changing,” grunted Judge, black eyes fixed on the capital. “It needs burning.”
bs: — Svijetu ne treba promjena, otpuhne Džadž, s crnim očima prikovanim za prijestolnicu. — Treba mu Veliko Gorenje.

en: But Risinau and Judge continued to tolerate each other and the King’s Own made no appearance. Even now, as the rain slacked off and they marched into the ill-planned, ill-drained, ill-smelling maze of shacks outside the walls of the capital, water spattering from the broken gutters and into the muddy lanes below. Maybe Orso’s forces had been fought out against Leo dan Brock. Maybe there were other uprisings to deal with. Maybe these strange times had stretched their loyalties in so many directio
bs: No, Risinau i Džadž nastavili su tolerirati jedno drugo, a Kraljevi se nisu pojavili. Čak i sada, dok je kiša jenjavala, marširali su u loše isplaniran, slabo dreniran i smrdljiv labirint baraka izvan zidina prijestolnice, dok je voda prskala iz polomljenih oluka u blatnjave prolaze ispod njih. Možda su Orsove snage bile iscrpljene u borbi protiv Lea dan Broka. Možda je bilo drugih ustanaka s kojima se trebalo nositi. Možda su ova čudna vremena toliko rastegnula njihovu odanost da više nisu znal

en: Her horse shied, and she ripped at the reins and dragged it around in a tight circle, that finger still extended, while the thunder of thousands upon thousands of tramping feet grew steadily louder.
bs: Njezin se konj propne, a ona grubo povuče uzde i okrene ga u uskom krugu, ne spuštajući taj prst, dok je tutnjava tisuća i tisuća marširajućih koraka postajala sve glasnija.

en: The High King’s banner, which had flown over the walls of Adua for centuries. The golden sun of the Union, given to Harod the Great as his emblem by Bayaz himself. The flag folk had knelt to, prayed to, sworn their loyalty to… came fluttering down to lie in the puddle-pocked road before the gate.
bs: Zastava Visokog kralja, koja je stoljećima vijorila iznad zidina Adua. Zlatno sunce Unije, koje je sam Bajaz darovao Harodu Velikom kao njegov amblem. Zastava pred kojom su Folk klečali, molili se, zaklinjali na vjernost… pala je i spustila se u cestu išaranu lokvama pred vratima.

en: When he grabbed his coat he sent pamphlets scattering off the table. Wasn’t as if he’d read them. Wasn’t as if he could read, really. But having ’em felt like a fine step towards freedom. And who needed pamphlets, when the Breakers were come in person?
bs: Kada je zgrabio kaput, razbacao je letke sa stola. Nije da ih je čitao. Nije da je, zapravo, znao čitati. Ali imati ih činilo se kao lijep korak prema slobodi. A tko je trebao letke kada su Lomljači stigli osobno?

en: He’d been ready to fight. Ready to charge ranks of royalist spears, freedom and equality as his armour. Petree had not cared for that idea, and honestly, he’d been having some doubts of his own as the day grew closer. But he only saw a few soldiers, and they had smiles on their faces and jackets hanging open, cheering and jumping and celebrating like everyone else.
bs: Bio je spreman za borbu. Spreman jurnuti na redove kraljevskih kopalja, sa slobodom i jednakošću kao svojim oklopom. Petree nije mario za tu zamisao, a iskreno, i sam je osjećao sumnju kako se dan primicao. No vidio je tek nekolicinu vojnika; lica su im bila ozarena, jakne raskopčane, klicali su, poskakivali i slavili kao i svi ostali.

en: “Brothers! Sisters! To the Agriont!” And she pointed up the road towards freedom. “I’ve a fancy to greet His August fucking Majesty!”
bs: — Braćo! Sestre! Prema Agriontu! I pokazala je cestom prema slobodi. — Imam želju pozdraviti Njegovo August jebeno Vaša Uzvišenosti!

en: His colonel had assured him help was coming. From the King’s Own. Then from Westport. Then from Starikland. From ever less likely directions. But no help appeared to have arrived at all.
bs: Pukovnik ga je uvjeravao da stiže pomoć. Od kraljevske garde. Zatim iz Vestporta. Pa iz Stariklanda. Iz sve manje izglednih pravaca. No činilo se da pomoć uopće ne stiže.

en: “Steady,” said Leeb, but it came out a squeak that couldn’t have steadied anyone. It might have unsteadied those already steady, indeed. It was painfully obvious that his brittle little line had no chance of stopping that boiling tide. No chance at all.
bs: — Mirno, reče Leeb, no zvučalo je poput piskutanja koje ne bi moglo smiriti nikoga. Štoviše, moglo je uznemiriti i one koji su već bili smireni. Bilo je bolno očito da njegova krhka linija nema nikakve šanse zaustaviti tu kipuću plimu. Baš nikakve.

en: “Raise bows!” roared Corporal Grey, veins bulging from his thick neck. At the same time, he looked at Leeb with a vaguely desperate expression. The pilot of a foundering vessel, perhaps, looking to his captain, silently asking if they really did intend to go down with the ship. Perhaps that’s why captains do go down with their ships. No better ideas.
bs: — Podignite lukove! zagrmio je kaplar Grey, dok su mu žile iskakale na debelom vratu. Istodobno je pogledao Leeba izrazom blage očajničke nade. Poput kormilara broda koji tone, koji nijemo gleda kapetana pitajući se namjeravaju li doista potonuti zajedno s brodom. Možda zato kapetani i tonu sa svojim brodovima. Nema boljih ideja.

en: “Bloody hell.” He stared down at his officer’s jacket. Bright red. How could it be redder? The whole purpose was to make him stand out. Like a bullseye on a target.
bs: — Prokleto pakao. Zagledao se u svoju časničku jaknu. Jarko crvenu. Kako je mogla biti još crvenija? Čitava joj je svrha bila da ga učini uočljivim. Poput mete na streljani.

en: Then they were all on him, kicking, swearing. Slavering madmen. Furious animals. Leeb curled up as best he could, whimpering at each blow. Something hit him so hard in the back he was sick. To his horror, he saw one of them take out a knife.
bs: Onda su se svi sručili na njega, udarajući nogama, psujući. Zaluđeni manijaci. Bjesomučne životinje. Leeb se sklupčao najbolje što je mogao, cvileći pri svakom udarcu. Nešto ga je tako snažno pogodilo u leđa da je povratio. Na užas, primijetio je kako jedan od njih izvlači nož.

en: “They’re here.” Shawley watched a set run down the alley below, footsteps clapping from the fronts of the narrow buildings, and he tossed back the last of his wine and swung his legs from the window seat.
bs: — Eno ih. Shawley je promatrao skupinu kako trči niz uličicu ispod; koraci su odzvanjali s pročelja uskih zgrada, a on je ispio ostatak vina do dna, prebacio noge preko prozorske klupice i skočio.

en: He could hear the violence, further on. The mad noise, spreading through the richer districts inside Arnault’s Wall. They might call it the People’s Army, and there might be a few high principles tossed about, but if you wanted his opinion, there were plenty of thugs with pretty excuses mixed in, and no small number who weren’t even bothering with the excuses, just turning a quick profit from the chaos. Evidence of their handiwork all over. Shawley stopped to filch a nice ring off a corpse that
bs: Čuo je nasilje u daljini. Pomahnitalu buku koja se širila imućnijim četvrtima unutar Arnaultovih zidina. Mogli su to zvati Narodnom vojskom i razbacivati se uzvišenim načelima, ali ako ste htjeli njegovo mišljenje, ondje se motalo pregršt razbojnika s lijepim izlikama, uz nemali broj onih koji se nisu ni trudili tražiti izlike, već su samo zgrtali brzu dobit u nastalom kaosu. Dokazi njihova rada posvuda. Shawley zastade kako bi ukrao lijep prsten s leša koji je netko ostavio da leži. Oduvijek ga

en: And Shawley realised the girl must be Furnevelt’s daughter. That was how long he’d been waiting. Should’ve just killed the old bastard where he sat, but Shawley wanted him to know. So he stepped around the door frame and tipped his hat.
bs: I Shawley shvati da ta djevojka mora biti Furneveltova kći. Eto koliko je dugo čekao. Trebao je naprosto ubiti starog gadca ondje gdje je sjedio, ali Shawley je htio znati. Stoga zakorači preko dovratka i napola skine šešir.

en: One of the dressmakers screamed, pins falling from her open mouth. Furnevelt’s daughter stared, the tendons starting from her pale bare feet.
bs: Jedna od krojačica vrisne, a igle joj ispadnu iz otvorenih usta. Furneveltova kći ukočeno je zurila, a tetive su joj se napinjale na blijedim, bosim stopalima.

en: She once listened to one of them give a speech. Hidden at the back of a meeting in a shawl she borrowed from her maid. She had thought it such a daring thing to do, had been expecting fire and fury and, well… danger. But it had all sounded so reasonable. Fair pay. Equitable hours. Decent treatment. She had hardly been able to understand why everyone was so afraid of them. Later, flushed and eager, she had repeated all the arguments to her father. He had told her she had no notion of the complexi
bs: Jednom je slušala jednog od njih kako drži govor. Skrivena u stražnjem dijelu dvorane, ogrnuta šalom koji je posudila od sluškinje. Mislila je da je to odvažan potez, očekivala je vatru, bijes i, pa… opasnost. No, sve je zvučalo tako razumno. Poštena plaća. Pravedno radno vrijeme. Pristojan tretman. Jedva je mogao razumjeti zašto ih se svi toliko boje. Kasnije, zajapurena i puna poleta, ponovila je sve argumente ocu. Rekao joj je da nema pojma o složenosti upravljanja tržištem rada, da ono što n

en: Only that morning it had felt so important that all the right guests should accept their invitations. That the words of their vows be perfect. That the hem of her dress was stitched just so. Now the hem of her dress was black with road-filth and, Fates help her, speckled brown with her father’s blood, and all the world was turned upside down and inside out.
bs: Samo tog jutra činilo se tako važnim da svi pravi uzvanici prihvate pozivnice. Da riječi njihovih zavjeta budu savršene. Da porub njezine haljine bude baš kako treba. Sada je porub njezine haljine bio crn od ulične prljavštine i, neka joj Sudbine pomognu, poprskan smeđim mrljama očeve krvi, a cijeli se svijet okrenuo naglavce i izvrnuo naopako.

en: “Oh no,” she whispered. She could not run any more. There was nowhere left to run to. A house was on fire, smoke rolling from the upstairs windows into the spitting sky.
bs: — O, ne, prošaptala je. Više nije mogla trčati. Nije bilo mjesta na koje bi pobjegla. Jedna je kuća gorjela, a dim je sukljao iz prozora na katu u nebo koje je sipalo kišu.

en: The People’s Army was coming. Wasn’t she the people, too? When had she become their enemy? She squeezed her eyes shut, shivering in the icy water, and gave up trying to smother her own sobs. No one could have heard them over the deafening noise of the mob above. Tramping boots, clashing metal, breaking glass, rumbling wagon wheels. A demon with many voices.
bs: Narodna vojska je dolazila. Zar i sama nije bila Folk? Kada je postala njihov neprijatelj? Stisnula je oči, drhteći u ledenoj vodi, i odustala od pokušaja ugušiti svoje jecaje. Nitko ih nije mogao čuti od oglušujuće buke gomile iznad. Topot čizama, zvek metala, lomljenje stakla, grmljavina kola. Demon s mnogo glasova.

en: So she shouldered through the crowd, skirts gathered up and tucked into her belt the way she did when there was work to do. She jostled her way to the front, which one way or another she’d been doing all her life, using her elbows and her fixed jaw and her great loud voice. “Out o’ my way!” Forced a path through the big men, the armed men, the armoured men, still loitering. They might be hard on the outside, but they were soft where it counted. Mother Mostly hadn’t been born with much softness i
bs: Stoga se probila kroz gomilu, podignutih suknji zadenutih za opasač onako kako je činila kad je trebalo zapeti. Prokrčila si je put naprijed, što je činila cijeloga svog života na ovaj ili onaj način, služeći se laktovima, stisnutom čeljusti i svojim snažnim, glasnim glasom. — S puta mi!" Prokrčila je stazu među divovima, naoružanim ljudima, oklopljenim ljudima koji su se još motali okolo. Izvana su možda bili čvrsti, ali ondje gdje je najvažnije bili su mekani. Majka Mostly nije rođena s previš

en: He leaned back to survey the results. Those words had always worked magic before, conjuring obedience from thin air. But now, suddenly, the spell had no effect. “I order you to bloody halt!” He doubted the crowd could even hear him over their own clamour. He could hardly hear himself over his own thudding heart.
bs: Odmaknuo se kako bi provjerio učinak. Te su riječi dotad uvijek činile čuda, izazivajući poslušnost ni iz čega. No sad, iznenada, čarolija nije imala nikakva učinka. "Zapovijedam vam da prokleti stojite!" Posumnjao je da ga gomila uopće može čuti od vlastite vike. Jedva je čuo samoga sebe od tutnjave vlastita srca.

en: Captain Rithinghorm came close to point through the arrow-loop. Close enough that Parry could hear his breath echoing in the narrow chain room. Close enough that he could smell him. He must wear some kind of perfume. Hint of lavender. He pointed down, white with anger. Down towards that laundry-woman.
bs: Kapetan Rithinghorm primaknuo se dovoljno blizu da pokaže kroz strijelnicu. Dovoljno blizu da Parry čuje kako mu dah odjekuje u uskoj prostoriji s lancima. Dovoljno blizu da ga osjeti. Mora da nosi nekakav parfem. Trag lavande. Pokazao je dolje, bijel od bijesa. Dolje prema onoj pralji.

en: Rithinghorm threw him back against the wall, jaw muscles squirming on the sides of his taut face. “Sergeant Hope!”
bs: Rithinghorm ga baci natrag na zid, dok su mu se mišići čeljusti grčili na stranama napetog lica. — Naredniče Hope!

en: He turned to the men. They were staring at him. Parry and all the rest. So young, they were. Good lads. Could he ever have looked that young, when he first joined? They didn’t know what to say. What to do. Hope didn’t know, either, but they had to do something.
bs: Okrenuo se prema ljudima. Zurili su u njega. Parry i svi ostali. Bili su tako Juvens. Dobri momci. Je li on ikada izgledao tako mlado kad se prvi put pridružio? Nisu znali što reći. Što učiniti. Hope također nije znao, ali morali su nešto poduzeti.

en: The Breakers charged. Didn’t need an order. They couldn’t have stopped even if they’d wanted to, there was so much shoving from behind. The whole People’s Army at their backs. Every ground-down worker in the Union. But Smiler didn’t want to stop. He wanted to smash this whole corrupt place. These grasping bastards who’d sent his friends to die in Styria, to die in the mills, to die in the cellars. He wanted to burn away the rot and make a country for its people.
