en: His mount was restless and he reined it savagely around, keeping his frown fixed on her all the while. “Rikke o’ the Long Eye!”
bs: Konj mu se nemirno meškoljio, a on ga je divljački trgnuo uzdom, ne skidajući mrki Oko s nje. — Rike od Dugog Oka!

en: “He tells me you’re willing to make a trade,” called Calder. “My son for half the North. That true?”
bs: — Kaže mi da si voljna sklopiti pogodbu, doviknu Kalder. — Mog sina za pola Sjevera. Je li to istina?

en: And she thrust out an arm towards the ill-smelling cripple who was once the terror of the North. There was a pause while those below took in the state of him and wondered if it could truly be the same man.
bs: I pružila je ruku prema smrdljivom bogalju koji je nekada bio strah i trepet Sjevera. Nastala je stanka dok su oni dolje proučavali njegovo stanje i pitali se je li to doista isti čovjek.

en: “You can never have too many.” He pulled one out, the work-polished handle towards her. Not a big one. But a small blade can do the job, more often than not. “Sure you don’t want me to do it?” he asked, in that husky whisper.
bs: — Čovjek ih nikad nema previše. Izvadio ga je, s drškom uglačanom od rada okrenutom prema njoj. Ne velik. Ali mala oštrica češće nego rijetko obavi posao. — Sigurna si da ne želiš da ja to obavim? upitao je onim hrapavim šapatom.

en: He flinched, first, with a little gasp, like he’d been bee-stung. He stared at her, wet eyes wide, slack face all red-speckled from the bubbling wound.
bs: Najprije se trgnuo uz tihi uzdah, kao da ga je ubodla pčela. Zureći u nju vlažnim, razrogačenim očima, s mlitavim licem posutim kapljicama krvi iz rane koja je ključala.

en: If anyone had asked him, Clover would’ve said there was less than no chance this’d be settled with talk. But you never realise how much hope you’re holding till it gets knifed and thrown off a roof.
bs: Da ga je tko pitao, Klover bi rekao da nema ni najmanje šanse da se ovo riješi razgovorom. No čovjek nikada nije svjestan koliko se nada drži sve dok joj netko ne zabode nož u leđa i baci je s krovova.

en: “What happened is…” Clover narrowed his eyes towards the walls of Carleon, like a man wincing into a storm. “I was hoping I’d never have to fight in another battle.” Black Calder’s men had started forwards. Not the most eager of charges, after all the shit they’d waded through to get here. But they’d started forwards even so. Clover gave a sigh, right from his guts. “But there’s hopes for you.”
bs: — Dogodilo se to da… Klover je suzio oči prema zidinama Carleona, poput čovjeka koji se mršti na oluju. — Nadao se jesam da se više nikad neću morati boriti u bitci. Folk Blacka kretali su naprijed. Nisu to bili najvatreniji juriši, nakon svega kroz što su se morali probiti da stignu ovamo. Ali svejedno su krenuli naprijed. Klover je uzdahnuo duboko iz utrobe. — No, čovjek se uvijek može nadati.

en: “Isern-i-Phail’s a suspicious sort. Maybe that’s what happens when you’ve a madman for a father and no mother but the moon. She took against you right off. So she set some folk to watch your granny and, phew.” Rikke puffed out her cheeks. “They’re in and out of her house like it’s a brothel.”
bs: — Izern-i-Fejl je prilično sumnjičava. Možda to biva kad ti je otac luđak, a majka ti gola mjesečina. Okomila se na tebe odmah u startu. Pa je postavila neke ljude da motre na tvoju baku i, fiju. Rike napuha obraze. — Ulaze joj u kuću i izlaze kao da je bordel.

en: Corleth’s body was tensed to run, but there was nowhere to go. They were setting ladders, outside the walls. She could see a couple swung up against the parapet, men struggling to shove ’em back down.
bs: Corlethino tijelo napelo se za bijeg, ali nije bilo kamo. Namještali su ljestve, izvan zidina. Vidjela je par komada prislonjenih uz grudobran, dok su se Folk mučili gurnuti ih natrag dolje.

en: By the dead, not far away down the wall some of Calder’s men had made it to the top, blades twinkling as they struggled. Couldn’t be long, now, till the city fell. Too long for Corleth, though, maybe.
bs: Tako mi mrtvih, nedaleko odatle niz bedem neki su Kalderovi Folk uspjeli se domognuti vrha, a sječiva su im bljeskala dok su se borili. Neće proći dugo, sad već, dok grad ne padne. Predugo za Corleth, ipak, možda.

en: “I’ve heard that before, too! But mad’s just a different way of seeing things. Shivers, you reckon it’s time for a toot on that horn o’ yours?”
bs: — I to sam već čula! Ali ludilo je samo drukčiji način gledanja na stvari. Šivers, misliš li da je vrijeme za malo trube?

en: But that didn’t mean he wasn’t nervous. Stomach churning away. He smothered a burp, rubbed at his breastbone where the sore fire seemed to burn up his throat. By the dead, if they waited much longer he’d need to shit again. That’d be just his luck, to get the call while he was squatting in the brush, trousers down.
bs: No to nije značilo da nije nervozan. Želudac mu se vrzao. Suzbio je podrigivanje, protrljao prsnu kost gdje ga je žarka Palioc navodno pekla uz grlo. Tako mu mrtvih, ako potraju još malo, morat će opet kenjati. To bi bila baš njegova sreća, da dobije Poziv dok čuči u grmlju spuštenih hlača.

en: “There we go!” And he set to running again. More of a jog, being honest, it was tough through the trees. Broken ground and fallen branches and tree roots ready to trip you. He was wheezing as he burst from the woods and heard the noise, far louder, far closer, far harsher.
bs: — Idemo! I ponovo je potrčao. Iskreno rečeno, više je to bio kas, teren među stablima bio je nezgodan. Neravno tlo, polegnute grane i korijenje drveća samo što ga nisu sapleli. Teško hvatanje zraka izbilo ga je iz šume te je čuo graju, mnogo glasniju, mnogo bližu, mnogo oštriju.

en: “All right, Chief?” asked Brandal, thumping Hardbread’s standard into the turf beside him. “You want some water?” And he offered out a flask.
bs: — Je li sve u redu, šefe? upitao je Brandal, zaboživši Hardbredov stijeg u travu pokraj sebe. — Hoćeš li malo vode? Ponudio mu je plosku.

en: He heard a scream as someone fell from the next ladder down. He took no notice. Nothing to be done. He fixed on the stones in front of his face, kept ’em moving past.
bs: Zasluša vrisak dok je netko padao s idućih ljestvi niže. Nije obraćao pozornost. Tu se nije moglo ništa učiniti. Usredotočio se na kamenje pred svojim licem, nastavio ih pomicati mimo sebe.

en: “Fucking what?” Flatstone bellowed, spinning about, and saw straight away what. A great mass of men were pouring down the long slope to the south of town. Towards the walls Flatstone and his men had just climbed. A tide of coloured shields and twinkling mail. Reinforcements! Come to help him storm the city! He felt a rare smile crack his lips.
bs: "Jebeni što?" zaurlao je Flatstone, okrenuvši se u Round, i odmah vidio što. Velika masa Folk hrlila je niz dugu padinu južno od grada. Prema zidinama na koje su se Flatstone i njegovi Folk upravo popeli. Plima obojenih štita i blistave brne. Pojačanja! Došli su mu pomoći u jurišu na grad! Osjetio je rijedak osmijeh kako mu kida usne.

en: They were fighting, up on the wall. Ignet could see ’em, peeking around the corner of her house. Something was burning. She could smell it. Like burned cakes.
bs: Borili su se gore na zidinama. Ignet ih je mogla vidjeti provirujući iza ugla svoje kuće. Nešto je gorjelo. Osjetio je miris. Poput zagorjelih kolača.

en: She stared at the bolts, her shoulders up around her ears, waiting for them to jump and rattle in the brackets.
bs: Zurila je u zasune, s ramenima podignutima uz same uši, iščekujući da oni poskoče i zveckaju u ležištima.

en: So Rikke’s plan had worked. Seemed a mad plan, when she whispered it to him, her eyes in the darkness, the one that saw nothing and the one that saw too much, her breath hot on his face and smelling pleasantly of ale. Seemed a mad plan, but such a bold one he couldn’t say no. Never even thought of saying no. Didn’t know how he’d ever say no to her.
bs: Dakle, Rikin je plan uspio. Činio se suludim planom kad mu ga je šapnula, dok su joj oči u tami — ona koja nije vidjela ništa i ona koja je vidjela previše — sjajile, a dah joj je bio vruć na licu i ugodno mirisao po pivu. Činio se kao sulud plan, ali toliko odvažan da joj nije mogao reći ne. Nije mu palo na pamet reći ne. Nije znao kako bi joj ikada mogao reći ne.

en: He was up and sprinting before the echoes of Shivers’ second blast even faded, flying down the sedge-patched hillside.
bs: Bio je na nogama i jurio prije nego što su odjeci Šiversova drugog roga uopće utihnuli, leteći niz padinu obraslu šašom.

en: There were a few guards, but most were already running. He could hear their desperate cries, tugging him on. Women, too, shrieking and wailing. There was a fighter at the front, in bright mail with a bright spear, trying to turn his men, to form a wobbly shield-wall, but they weren’t halfway there. Far too late and far too few. The Nail ran right for him, faster’n ever, wind in his face. He always went at the hardest-looking bastard he could find. Bring down their toughest, break the rest.
bs: Bilo je tu nekoliko stražara, no većina je već bježala. Čuo je njihove očajničke vapaje koji su ga vukli naprijed. I žene, kako vrište i nariču. Pred sobom je ugledao borca u sjajnom oklopu sa sjajnim kopljem, koji je pokušavao okrenuti svoje ljude, složiti klimav zid od štitova, ali nisu bili ni na pola puta. Daleko prekasno i daleko premalo. Najl potrči ravno na njega, brže nego ikad, vjetar mu je puhao u lice. Uvijek bi navalio na najopasnijeg kophića kojega je mogao pronaći. Srušiti njihova

en: “Hello,” said the Nail, already swinging as the man twisted about, wet eyes staring. Caught his neck just right and took his head spinning off and it clonked against the side of the cart. Blood sprayed the horse half-harnessed in the traces and it bucked, kicked out and set off at a wild, straining canter, dragging the cart jolting after on one wheel, barrels and boxes bouncing from the back, catching a tent and ripping it up, dragging it after like the train on a bride’s dress, torn clothes and
bs: — Zdravo – reče Najl, već u zavoju, dok se muškarac vija, mokre oči upregnute. Uhvatio ga je za vrat upravo kako treba i otrgnuo mu glavu, koja se zaletjela u bočicu kolica. Krv proždirala konja, pola upregnutog u uže, a on zabukao, zabijačio kopitima i počeo divlji, napregnuti trčak, vučući kolica kako su se ljuljala na jednom kotaču, bare i kutije su skakutale s krila, hvatajući šator i trgajući ga, vučući za sobom kao šlep na nevjestinoj haljini, potrgano odijelo, naduveni lonci i isavijene ž

en: There were enemies everywhere. Trapper wasn’t sure who they were. Where they’d come from. That witch Rikke must’ve witched ’em up out o’ hell. They’d laughed at the Long Eye, back in Currahome. No one was laughing now.
bs: Neprijatelja je bilo posvuda. Zamkač nije bio siguran tko su oni, odakle su došli. Ona vještica Rike Sejf ih je dozvala iz pakla. Svi su se smijali Dugom Oku onomad u Currahomeu. Sav smijeh je zamro.

en: She’d watched Calder’s men and the Crinna bastards move forwards, set their ladders, start to climb. Then everything had fallen apart. First what looked like men of Uffrith had come pouring down from the far hills to the south, then what looked like men of the West Valleys had swept in from the west, ripping through the baggage, splitting Calder’s forces in half. Some of ’em were pressing in not too far from where Sholla and Flick were standing.
bs: Gledala je kako se Kalderovi Folk i Crinnini gadovi kreću naprijed, postavljaju ljestve, počinju se penjati. Onda se sve srušilo. Prvo su se Folk iz Afrita sručili s udaljenih brda na jugu, a zatim su Folk iz Zapadnih Dolina nahrupili sa zapada, probijajući se kroz prtljagu i prepolovivši Kalderove snage. Neki od njih tiskali su se nedaleko od mjesta gdje su stajale Šola i Flik.

en: “The West Valleys, I reckon. The Nail and his boys. Seems he didn’t fall out with Rikke after all.” Clover rubbed his jaw with something close to admiration. “Reckon she laid a smart trap and we’ve all blundered into it. Knew I should’ve stuck with her.” He put a hand on Sholla’s shoulder, leaning close. “Might be a good move for you and Flick to head into the woods.” There were a lot of other folk heading into the woods. Heading as fast as their legs’d carry ’em. Most of Clover’s boys had alrea
bs: — Iz Zapadnih dolina, tako mi svega. Najl i njegovi momci. Izgleda da se ipak nije posvađao s Rike. Klover je protrljao čeljust s primjesom divljenja. "Rekao bih da nam je postavila mudru klopku i da smo svi uletjeli u nju. Znao sam da sam trebao ostati uz nju." Položio je ruku Šoli na rame, prislonivši se blizu. — Možda bi za tebe i Flika bilo pametno da se uputite u šumu. Mnogi su drugi Folk hrlili u šumu. Hrlili su onoliko brzo koliko su ih noge mogle nositi. Većina Kloverovih momaka već se r

en: ’Twas a vast battle. Ten battles put together. Biggest he ever saw by far. Bigger’n any his father saw, in spite of all his bloated boasting, which had been one o’ the man’s many failings. His father once claimed he killed two hundred men at Yarnvost and Scenn later learned there’d only been a hundred with both sides put together. Thinking of his father made him smile. He’d hated that fat bastard, but he’d been quite the laugh in the right mood. Beloved of the moon, he’d been. Beloved of the moo
bs: Bila je to golema bitka. Deset bitaka spojenih u jednu. Udaleko najveća koju je ikad vidio. Veća od išta što je njegov otac vidio, unatoč svim onim njegovim napuhanim hvalisanjima, što je bila tek jedna od mnogih mana tog čovjeka. Otac mu se jednom hvalisao da je posjekao dvjesta Folk kod Yarnvosta, a Skenn je kasnije doznao kako ih je ondje bilo jedva stotinu kad se zbroje obje strane. Sjećanje na oca izmamilo mu je osmijeh. Mrzio je tog debelog kopilana, ali bio je urnebesan kad bi ga ulovila

en: “Likewise the axe. Might as well say his spear’s sleepy.” And Isern gave it a shake. “Load o’ nonsense. They’re wood and metal and have no feelings.”
bs: — Također i Hachette. Mnogi bi kazali da mu je i Pajk pospano. I Izern ga protrese. — Gomila gluposti. To su drvo i metal i nemaju osjećaje.

en: The Crinna bastards were spread out ahead in a spiked and painted line. Horrible savages, they were, all pierced and puckered and covered in bloody bones. They’d seen what had happened to their friends. Had time to shift away from the city, wheel to face the Nail and his boys as they poured down from the west. But they had no idea Crummock-i-Phail’s children were coming on ’em from the north, and the ones at the near end spun about white-eyed, scattered wailing and head-clutching as the hillmen
bs: Crinna bastardi bili su raštrkani pred njima u šiljastoj i obojenoj liniji. Užasni divljaci, svi izbušeni i naborani te prekriveni krvavim kostima. Vidjeli su što se dogodilo njihovim prijateljima. Imali su vremena odmaknuti se od grada, okrenuti se i suprotstaviti Najlu i njegovim momcima dok su se spuštali sa zapada. Ali nisu imali pojma da djeca Crummocka-i-Fejla naviru na njih s Sjevera, a oni na bližem kraju okrenuli su se izbuljenih očiju, razbježali se jaučući i hvatajući se za glave dok

en: There was death smeared all over and the good grass watered with good blood and the moon could not but smile on this day’s work. Rikke-o’-the-Long-Eye in particular, who’d looked but a pale and stringy streak when she was carried into the hills but had seen this come, made this come, laid out the good gifts so they could all take their fill.
bs: Smrt je bila razmazana posvuda, dobra trava natopljena dobrom krvlju, a Mjesec se nije mogao nego nasmiješiti današnjem poslu. Rike-o"-the-Long-Eye ponajviše, koja je izgledala tek kao blijeda i žilava crta kad su je unijeli u brda, ali vidjela je da će ovo doći, prouzročila je da ovo dođe, pripremila dobre darove kako bi se svi mogli zasititi.

en: He frowned over at a set of great pots, man high, fires banked underneath ’em, steam pouring from inside.
bs: Namršteno je pogledao u smjeru nekoliko golemih kotlova, visokih poput čovjeka, ispod kojih su tavorile vatre, dok je iz njih kuljala para.

en: Calder’s men weren’t ready. Panicked by the attacks from behind, now panicked by an attack from in front. They wavered, spears wobbling, but Rance didn’t fancy running at ’em. Didn’t fancy it at all. It came to him, of a sudden, how hard and unforgiving is a spearhead, and how soft and easily torn is a man’s belly.
bs: Kalderovi Folk nisu bili spremni. Prestrašeni napadima s leđa, sada su paničarili i zbog napada sprijeda. Kolebali su se, koplja su im podrhtavala, ali Ranceu nije bilo ni na kraj pameti da juriša na njih. Baš nimalo. Iznenada mu je sinulo koliko je Kruna koplja Trdak i nemilosrdan, a koliko je čovjekov trbuh mehak i lako rješiv rana.

en: The hillmen chased after them a way, but fell to picking over the dead for trinkets and were left behind. They sent arrows flitting after, whistling farewells, twittering into the greenwood, clicking into the trunks with their feathers fluttering. Stand-i’-the-Barrows kept up a fast pace on his long shanks and the sound of battle soon faded.
bs: Brđani su ih progonili još neko vrijeme, ali su stali prebirati po mrtvima tražeći dragocjenosti pa su zaostali. Odaslali su strijele za njima, fijukale su poput oproštajnih pozdrava, cvrkutale dok su letjele u šumarak, udarale u debla s perjem što je lepršalo. Stand-i’-the-Grobovi održavao je žestok tempo svojim dugim nogama i jeka bitke ubrzo utihnu.

en: “Whence comes this mist?” hissed Stand-i’-the-Barrows, creeping forwards slowly, and it was true it seemed a thing alive, twisting between the black trunks, sticking to men in tatters.
bs: — Odakle ova magla? prosiktao je Stand-i’-the-Grobovi, polako se prikradajući naprijed, i doista, činilo se kao da je živa, uvijajući se između crnih debala i hvatajući se za ljude u prnjama.

en: Like water from a broken bowl, the mist drained from the clearing, but Scunlich felt no joy at its passing. He saw figures among the trees at its edge. Ghosts at first, all around, but turning more horribly real with every moment, and Scunlich found he was wishing that the mist would come again.
bs: Poput vode iz razbijene zdjele, magla je iscurila s čistine, ali Skunlik nije osjetio radost zbog njezina nestanka. Ugledao je prilike među stablima na njezinu rubu. Najprije utvare, posvuda, ali sa svakim su trenom postajale sve užasnije stvarne, i Skunlik se uhvati kako priželjkuje da se magla vrati.

en: Not far off one of those great dogs bounced and rolled and barked, its side somehow on fire, frisking madly across the grass, trying to escape from itself. Something Clover had been trying to do for years, with as little success.
bs: Nedaleko odatle jedan je od onih velikih pasa poskakivao, valjao se i lajao, a bok mu je bio nekako u plamenu, ludujući i preskačući preko trave, pokušavajući pobjeći sam od sebe. Nešto od čega je Klover godinama pokušavao pobjeći, s jednako malo uspjeha.

en: “But he’s done!” Clover waved with his free hand towards the battle, which was hard not to wave at, since it was all around ’em, pressing in closer on Calder’s guards with every breath they took. “Anyone can see he’s fucking done! He’s saying he’s done himself!”
bs: — Ali gotov je! Klover mahnu slobodnom rukom prema bitki, u koju je bilo teško ne mahnuti jer se širila svuda oko njih, sa svakim udahom stežući obruč sve tješnje oko Kalderovih stražara. — Svatko vidi da je u kurcu! I sam govori da je gotov!

en: Downside looked big when he was on your side. He looked a lot bigger on the other, with his scarred shield up, heavy mail from neck to knees and a steel cap on. A hard bastard to put down with a sword. Faster than Clover was, and stronger, and better armed. But it’s a man’s wits that set him apart from the beasts. Or so he told himself. Downside stepped forwards again and Clover slipped sideways, trying to keep the flat rock between them and hoping some opportunity might present itself. The figh
bs: Dausaid je djelovao velik kad ti je bio na strani. Djelovao je mnogo veći kad je bio na suprotnoj, s podignutim izbrazdanim štitom, teškom oklopnom košuljom od vrata do koljena i čeličnom kacigom na glavi. Trdak kojeg je mačem bilo teško položiti na zemlju. Brži od Klovera, jači i bolje naoružan. No čovjeka od zvijeri razlikuje njegova pamet. Barem je to govorio sam sebi. Dausaid ponovno zakorači naprijed, a Klover se izmače u stranu, nastojeći zadržati ravno kamenje između njih i nadajući se da

en: An arrow came looping from the trees and stuck into Downside’s shoulder. It didn’t stick deep. Just lodged in his mail. Probably didn’t even draw blood. But it was enough to make him turn his head, for an instant.
bs: Strelica je u luku izletjela iz stabala i zabila se Dausaidu u rame. Nije se zabila duboko. Tek se zaglavila u njegovu oklopu. Vjerojatno nije potekla ni krv. Ali bila je dovoljna da mu odvrati glavu na tren.

en: Metal scraped as the point slid through Downside’s mail and into his belly. Clover might never draw the thing in anger, but he kept it sharp even so.
bs: Metal zaškripa kad šiljak skliznu kroz Dausaidovu brnjastu košulju ravno u trbuh. Klover možda nikada ne bi potegnuo to sječivo iz gnjeva, ali ga je svejedno držao oštrim.

en: She’d often heard it said that there’s no sweeter sight than dead enemies. Usually by folk who’d never really had an enemy, let alone killed one. The truth was she felt no satisfaction, seeing the Great Wolf back to the mud. But she felt no regret, either. It had needed doing. For her father. For her people. For herself. It had been long overdue.
bs: Često je slušala kako nema slađeg prizora od mrtvih neprijatelja. Obično su to govorili Folk koji zapravo nikada nisu imali neprijatelja, a kamoli ubili nekog. Istina je bila da ne osjeća nikakvo zadovoljstvo gledajući Velikog Vuka vraćenog u blato. No nije osjećala ni žaljenje. To se moralo učiniti. Za njezina oca. Za njezin Folk. Za nju samu. To je odavno trebalo biti obavljeno.

en: With marvellous dexterity, Isern flicked it into her mouth before Rikke’s fingers could close on it. “If your faults aren’t spread clearly before you, how can you improve on the bastards?”
bs: Uz čudesnu spretnost, Izern je ubaci u usta prije nego što su je Rikini prsti uspjeli uhvatiti. — Ako ti tvoje mane nisu jasno iznesene pred oči, kako se pobogu misliš popraviti?

en: “I thought it all felt too easy,” mused Calder, frowning off towards Carleon, across the corpse-scattered fields where even now the last of his army were being driven off or taken prisoner.
bs: — Mislila sam da je sve djelovalo prelagano, razmišljao je Kalder, bacajući Oko prema Carleonu, preko polja posijanih leševima gdje su se čak i sada posljednji ostaci njegove vojske razbježali ili bili zarobljeni.

en: “Ah.” For some reason, Calder had the ghost of a smile at the last. He leaned forwards and spoke so softly only she could hear. “So you don’t see everything.”
bs: — Aha. Tko zna zašto, Kalder se na samom kraju nakratko blago osmjehnuo. Nato se nagne naprijed i progovori toliko tiho da ga je samo ona mogla čuti. — Znači, ipak ne vidiš sve.

en: “And I!” roared the Nail, before Rikke could get a word in, stepping up out of the crowd, so spattered head to toe with blood it looked like he’d gone swimming in it. “I stand with Black Rikke!”
bs: — A i ja!, zagrmi Najl prije nego što je Rike stigla prozboriti i riječ, istupivši iz gomile toliko obliven krvlju od glave do pete da je izgledalo kao da se kupao u njoj. — Ja stajem uz Black Rike!

en: Rikke looked from that little hill across the churned-up battlefield, then down at Calder’s corpse. She felt no satisfaction in it.
bs: Rike je pogledala s onog brežuljka preko izorana bojišta, a zatim dolje, u Kalderov leš. Nije osjećala nikakvo zadovoljstvo zbog toga.

en: Savine closed her eyes and took a shuddering breath. She had charges of her own to answer. Some almost as insane and laughable as those against Zuri and her brothers. Others all too horribly true. She had to fight for herself first. If they found her guilty, she could help no one.
bs: Savine je sklopila oči i udahnula s drhtavim grčem u prsima. I sama se imala za što braniti. Neke su optužbe bile gotovo jednako sulude i smiješne kao one protiv Zurija i njezine braće. Druge su bile previše užasno istinite. Najprije se morala izboriti za samu sebe. Ako je proglase krivom, nikome neće moći pomoći.

en: There was a crash outside and Savine spun towards the door, took a lurching step for the children, one hand pressed to her churning stomach, the other reaching for the cribs.
bs: Vani je odjeknuo prasak i Savine se naglo okrenula prema vratima, napravila teturav korak prema djeci, pritisnuvši jednu ruku na uzburkani želudac, dok je drugom posegnula za kolijevkama.

en: “There is nothing to forgive,” she said, with an effort. “Perhaps it could have been a good thing. Should have been. And I am not a lady any more. Just plain Citizeness. That is what I need people to see.”
bs: — Nema se tu što oprostiti, rekla je uz napor. — Možda je i mogla biti dobra stvar. Trebala je biti. I ja više nisam plemkinja. Samo obična građanka. To je ono što želim da Folk vide.

en: Broad’s jaw worked, his bloodshot eyes fixed on the letter, his hand halfway towards it. “What does it say?”
bs: Brodova se čeljust ukoči, zakrvavljene oči prikovaše mu se za pismo, a ruka pođe prema njemu. — Što piše?

en: “If you can call it marching.” The drums were beating double time but the demoralised remains of the People’s Army and the exhausted remnants of the Crown Prince’s Division moved at a trudge, their ranks dissolved into a shambling mass, flags limp and polearms drooping, a trail of mud and rubbish in their wake. A giant military slug, squirming spent across the damp country. “They hardly look ready for a fight.”
bs: — Ako se to uopće može nazvati marširanjem. Bubnjevi su udarali dvostrukim tempom, ali demoralizirani ostaci Narodne vojske i iscrpljeni ostatci Divizije prijestolonasljednika kretali su se vukući se, razbijenih redova svedenih u trome gomile, opuštenih zastava i oborenih koplja, ostavljajući za sobom trag blata i smeća. Divovski vojni puž koji se iscrpljeno migoljio preko vlažnog Countryja. — Teško da izgledaju spremni za borbu.

en: “They believe we’re killing each other miles away,” said Leo. “And Inspector Teufel is making sure the People’s Inspectorate won’t be putting anyone straight on that score.”
bs: — Vjeruju da se međusobno ubijamo miljama daleko, reče Leo. — A inspektorica Tojfel se brine da Narodni inspektorat nikoga ne razuvjeri po tom pitanju.

en: “They’ve arrested her. Judge is putting her on trial for profiteering and treason and… er…” Yolk swallowed. “Well, incest got a mention.”
bs: — Uhapsili su je. Džadž joj sudi za profiteering i izdaju i… ovaj… Žumanj proguta knedlu. — Pa, spominjao se i incest.

en: “If I learned one thing at Stoffenbeck,” said Leo, “it’s that you’ll do no good with bad men. Lord Marshal, I suggest you pick out two hundred men you fully trust, the best armed and mounted. Your most loyal. When we make it through Arnault’s Wall—”
bs: — Ako sam išta naučio u Štopenbeku, prozbori Leo, to je da od loših Folk nema nikakve koristi. Lorde maršale, predlažem da odaberete dvjesto Folk kojima potpuno vjerujete, najbolje naoružanih i opremljenih. Svoje najlojalnije. Kad se probijemo kroz Arnaultov zid —

en: “You and me. I spin the guards a story about worries over their loyalty, try to get at least a couple out, then… we deal with the rest. We bar the door. We hold it till the Young Lion’s cavalry arrives.”
bs: — Ti i ja. Ja ću stražarima prodati priču o brizi za njihovu odanost, pokušati izvući van barem dvojicu, a onda… pobrinut ćemo se za ostale. Zabarikadirat ćemo vrata. Držat ćemo ih dok ne stigne konjica Mlada Lava.

en: The fact was, with only the two of them, this wouldn’t be easy. She could’ve asked Tallow along, but she told herself he’d only get in the way. She could’ve hired men, but there was no one she trusted.
bs: Činjenica je bila da im, s obzirom na to da su bile samo njih dvije, ovo neće biti lako. Mogla je povesti Taloua, ali sama bi sebi rekla da bi joj samo smetao. Mogla je unajmiti ljude, ali nikome nije vjerovala.

en: Over the past few weeks, the audiences had thinned out and grown ever more jaded. He had seen trials in which the observers were outnumbered by the accused. He had seen crumbs shower down from people enjoying a quick pastry in the gallery while blood-curdling accusations were made. He had seen elderly Representatives nod off on their benches as young mothers pleaded for their lives.
bs: Tijekom proteklih nekoliko tjedana gledališta su se ispraznila i postala sve ravnodušnija. Gledao je suđenja na kojima je bilo više optuženih nego promatrača. Gledao je kako mrvice sipaju s galerija gdje su Folk uživali u brzom pecivu dok su se iznosile zastrašujuće optužbe. Gledao je ostarjele Zastupnike kako drijemaju na klupama dok mladolike majke mole za svoje živote.

en: “What if they don’t get here in time?” He was all too keenly aware how quickly the Court of the People could produce a verdict. “What if Savine’s… convicted?”
bs: — Što ako ne stignu na vrijeme? Previše je dobro znao kojom se brzinom u palači Narodni sud može donijeti presuda. — Što ako Savine… bude osuđena?

en: He wanted to call out some encouragement. Be strong! or You’ll beat the bastards! or I love you! but she did not meet his eye. She glided across the tiled floor with her hands clasped and her head high, a member of some more virtuous species than the sweaty mass gathered on the benches and in the galleries. Two maids followed, each carrying what looked like a little bundle of blankets.
bs: Htiot je htio viknuti kakvu ohrabrujuću riječ. Budi jaka! ili Pobijedit ćeš, kopiladi! ili Volim te!, ali ona nije uzvratila njegov Oko. Kliznula je po popločanom podu skrštenih ruku i visoko uzdignute glave, pripadnica neke vrlije vrste nego što je bila znojna masa skupljena na klupama i galerijama. Dvije su je sluškinje slijedile, svaka noseći ono što je izgledalo poput malog smotuljka deka.

en: Usually insults would shower on the accused, sometimes bits of food, coins and broken glass, on one memorable occasion a bucket of piss, but the mood was different today. The murmur from above was of approval. Support, even. It seemed there was almost as much admiration for Savine’s quiet dignity in the public galleries as there was in Orso’s cage. He could not suppress the slightest smile, the slightest shake of his fist. In the Court of the People, one had to celebrate small victories.
bs: Obično bi na optuženicu kišile uvrede, ponekad komadi hrane, kovanice i razbijeno staklo, u jednoj nezaboravnoj prilici i kanta mokraće, no raspoloženje je danas bilo drugačije. Šapat odozgo bio je ispunjen odobrenjem. Čak i podrškom. Činilo se da je u javnim galerijama bilo gotovo toliko divljenja za Savinino tiho dostojanstvo koliko i u Orsinom kavezu. Nije mogao suzbiti ni najmanji osmijeh, ni najmanji trzaj šake. Na Narodnom se sudu trebalo radovati malim pobjedama.

en: “Citizeness Brock!” Sworbreck swaggered towards Savine in his absurd scarlet coat, a sheaf of papers flapping in one hand. It appeared the pompous dolt had duped himself with his own play-acting and come to believe he really was the great legal mind of the age.
bs: — Građanko Brok! Svorbrik se domunđavši uputio prema Savine u svom apsurdnom grimiznom kaputu, dok mu je snop papira lepršao u jednoj ruci. Činilo se da je taj umišljeni idiot nasamario samog sebe svojim glumatanjem i povjerovao da je doista velik pravni um toga doba.

en: “More than your share, some would say! You pretend to be a humble Citizeness of the Union like any other. You hide your infamous history behind your husband’s celebrated name.” He appealed again to the galleries. “But we know who you are! You are none other than Savine dan Glokta, the notorious… the notorious… whatever are you doing?”
bs: "Više nego vlastitim udjelom, rekao bi netko! Pretvarate se da ste skromna građanka Unije kao i svaka druga. Svoju zloglasnu povijest krijete iza slavnoga imena svoga supruga." Ponovno se obratio galerijama."Ali mi znamo tko ste vi! Vi niste nitko drugi doli Savine dan Glokta, ozloglašena… ozloglašena… što se to zaboga trudite učiniti?"

en: “Of course, Citizeness Judge, of course.” Sworbreck rifled through his papers, which Savine would not have been surprised to find were blank, trying to recover his lost rhythm. “To the, er… to the specific charges, then! You were a leading light and founding member of that coven of profiteers, the Solar Society!”
bs: —, građanice Džadž. Svorbrik je listao svoje papire – za koje se Savine ne bi iznenadila da su bili prazni – pokušavajući vratiti izgubljeni ritam. — Na… ovaj… na specifične optužbe, dakle! Bili ste vodeća osoba i osnivačica onoga kluba profitera, Sunčanog društva!

en: Sworbreck gave an ungainly cough, staring down at his notes as she settled Ardee again. The girl could have fed through an earthquake. “You have participated in usury on a grand scale! Squeezed outrageous rents from the desperate! Lived like an empress while your tenants squatted in filth! You have conspired with the Banking House of Valint and Balk—”
bs: Svorbrik se nespretno zakašljucnu, zagledavši se u svoje bilješke dok je Savine ponovno namještala Ardi. Cura je mogla sisati i za vrijeme potresa. — Sudjelovali ste u lihvarenju golemih razmjera! Iscijedili ste astronomske najamnine od očajnika! Živjeli ste poput carice dok su vam stanari prebivali u blatu! Urotili ste se s Bankarskom kućom Valint i Balk — "

en: Broad would’ve been shocked if she hadn’t. He’d warned Judge it was a mistake to give Savine a chance to speak. But she’d been fixed on a big display. On humbling her as well as punishing her. Wasn’t quite turning out that way. But all he cared about was the letter. It felt heavy in his sweaty hand. Like a square of hot iron.
bs: Brod bi se šokirao da ona to već nije učinila. Upozorio je Džadža da je pogreška dati Savine priliku da progovori. No on je zapeo za veliku predstavu. Za ponižavanje jednako koliko i za kažnjavanje. Nije sve išlo baš glatko. Ali njega je zanimalo samo pismo. Činilo se teško u njegovoj znojavoj šaci. Poput komada užarenog željeza.

en: “And now,” Sworbreck was screeching, “you would have us believe that you have turned all your undoubted cunning towards charitable projects? That the great exploiter has become a great philanthropist!”
bs: — A sada, pištao je Svorbrik, "htio bi nam uvaliti priču da si svu svoju neupitnu lukavost usmjerio na dobrotvorne projekte? Da je Great izrabljivač postao Great filantrop!"

en: Broad remembered the day that pamphlet was written, out in the Three Farms, and he gave a disbelieving snort. You had to admire the gall of it.
bs: Brod se sjeti dana kad je taj letak nastao, tamo u Tri Farme, te ispušta nevjernički frktaj. Morao im se diviti na drskosti.

en: Other riders were bursting through the archway, surging around him and into the city. Teufel’s gold had done most of the job, but there was still work to do with steel. Still some Breakers and Burners fixed on fighting.
bs: Drugi su jahači provaljivali kroz luk, navirući oko njega u grad. Tojfelovo zlato obavilo je veći dio posla, ali s čelikom je još trebalo raditi. Još je bilo Lomljača i Palitelja odlučnih u borbi.

en: Glaward swallowed. “I understand.” He was a good man, too, in his way, but too soft-hearted to ever really be in the foreground.
bs: Glavard proguta knedlu. — Shvaćam." Na svoj je način bio dobar čovjek, ali previše blag da bi se ikad istinski probio u prvi plan.

en: end of the square, where the outline of the House of the Maker showed above the rooftops. “If they don’t know we’re coming already, they soon will.”
bs: — Misliš li da ćemo imati problema kod Agrionta? Forest se namrgodio prema dalekom kraju trga, gdje se obris Zidareve Kuće nazirao iznad krovova. — Ako već ne znaju da dolazimo, uskoro će saznati.

en: He glanced at the others, nervously licking his lips, but found no way out. “Corporal Smiler?” he muttered, as if he wasn’t completely sure.
bs: Osvrnu se prema drugima, živčano oblizujući usne, ali ne nađe izlaz. — Desetnik Smiler?" procijedi, kao da ni sam nije posve siguran.

en: “Sergeant Hambeck!” No doubts now he was naming someone else. If there was one thing everybody knew how to do these days, it was denounce.
bs: — Narednik Hambeck! Sada više nije bilo sumnje da nekoga cinkari. Ako je u ovo doba postojalo nešto što su svi znali raditi, bilo je to cinkarenje.

en: The mace made a meaty crunch as Vick smashed him across the back of the head. He crumpled over the windlass, blood squirting from a ragged gash across his scalp, sprinkling across the chains, the gears, the floor.
bs: Buzdovan je proizveo tupi, mesnati prasak kad ga je Vik udarila po potiljku. Sklupčao se preko vitla, a krv je šikljala iz razderane pukotine na njegovu tjemenu, prskajući po lancima, zupčanicima i podu.

en: Vick rocked back on her haunches. “Shit,” she whispered. She should’ve known limiting the violence would be a forlorn hope. But it looked like their luck had held. They had the chain room, and that was the part that had worried her most. The place was designed to be held even if the walls around it were taken. Now they just had to lock themselves in—
bs: Vik se zaljuljala na petama. — Tojfel odnio sve, prošaputala je. Mogla je i znati da će suzbijanje nasilja biti uzaludna nada. No činilo se da ih je sreća poslužila. Osvojili su prostoriju s lancima, a upravo ju je to najviše brinulo. Mjesto je bilo projektirano tako da se može obraniti čak i ako okolni zidovi padnu. Sada su se samo trebali zaključati unutra…

en: “That’s it!” screamed Judge, springing up and smashing at the wounded table so savagely she put a great split in it. “Fucking stop!”
bs: —"To je to!" vrisne Džadž, skočivši na noge i tako divljački udarivši po već izmučenom stolu da ga je propisno rascjepkala."Jebeno prestanite!"

en: “Sit the shit down, you posturing dunce!” she snarled back at him. “’Fore I send you to the Tower ahead!”
bs: "Sjedi s tim sranjem, ti uobraženi tumpane!" odbrusila mu je. — Prije nego što te pošaljem u Toranj po kratkom postupku!

en: fucking to one side. Put all the rest in the best baby-nurturing, orphan-housing, loaf-giving light you’ve got. Truth is you are a profiteer. You did exploit the working man, and woman, and child. You have built your palaces from their bones. You’re the worst o’ the old regime, squeezed into the shape of a woman. You’re fucking guilty, girl, guilty as Glustrod, and I know it, and you know it, and we all damn well know it.”
bs: — Poštedi me svog crvenjenja. Džadž ležerno mahnu rukom."Ostavi to jebanje s bratom po strani. Prikvači sve ostalo u najljepšem mogućem svjetlu dadiljanja, zbrinjavanja siročadi i dijeljenja kruha. Istina je da jesi ratna profiterka. Jesi iskorištavala radnog čovjeka, i ženu, i dijete. Svoje si palače sagradila na njihovim kostima. Ti si najgore od starog režima, sabijeno u ženski oblik. Ti si jebeno kriva, curice, kriva poput Glustroda, i ja to znam, i ti to znaš, i svi mi to, u pičku materinu,

en: No one called out in Savine’s defence now, paid or not, and who could blame them? There was only accusation in the rings of tight-packed faces at the balconies above. She leaned over the dock to lay Ardee in the crook of Freid’s arm, next to her brother. The blanket had come loose and she tucked it gently around her again, laid one hand upon her, the other on Harod. He squirmed and snivelled. She wanted to hold him so badly, one last time. But that would only put them in danger. She had to do th
bs: Nitko se više nije javljao u Savininu obranu, bilo plaćen, bilo besplatno, a tko bi im mogao zamjeriti? U nabijenim krugovima s balkona iznad visjele su same optužbe. Nagnula se preko optuženičke klupe kako bi položila Ardi u naručje Freid, pokraj svog brata. Dekica se bila otpustila pa ju je nježno ponovno ušuškala oko nje, spustivši jednu ruku na nju, a drugu na Haroda. On se vrpoljio i šmrcao. Toliko ga je željela zagrliti, još samo jedan posljednji put. No to bi ih samo dovelo u opasnost. Mo

en: “Yes, good Citizens and Citizenesses, His Eminence Arch Lector Glokta was a specimen as morally as he was physically repugnant. But he did not ruin the Union alone! He did not bring us to the dire pass in which we now find ourselves without a willing patsy to warm the throne while he worked. Pray allow me to make an introduction to my noble father, King Jezal the First!”
bs: — Da, dobri građani i građanke, Eminencija vrhovni Lektor Glokta bio je uzor moralno jednako odvratan kao i tjelesno. Ali nije Unija upropastio sam! Nije nas dovio u groznu situaciju u kojoj se sada nalazimo bez voljne marionete koja će grijati prijestolje dok on radi. Molim vas da mi dopustite predstaviti vam mog plemenitog oca, kralja Džezal Prvog!

en: “All this is common—if horrible—knowledge, but do you know how he profited from it all? Profited beyond the dreams of avarice? You want usurers? Hoarders? Speculators? Bayaz is the grandfather of them all. A magus more taken with money than magic!” Secrets did not seem so very important now, nor immortal wizards so very frightening. “He is both Valint and Balk! The loans that broke the state were all taken from him, the interest all paid to him. He was the one who made a Great Change inevitable.
bs: — Sve je to opće – premda užasno – znanje, ali znate li kako je od svega toga profitirao? Profitirao preko svih granica gramzivosti? Želite li lihvare? Skupljače blaga? Spekulante? Bajaz im je svima djed. Mag više opčinjen novcem nego magijom! Tajne se u tom trenutku nisu činile osobito važnima, niti besmrtni Magi pretjerano zastrašujućima. — On je i Valint i Balk! Zajmovi koji su slomili državu svi su uzeti od njega, a kamate su se plaćale njemu. On je učinio Veliku Promjenu neizbježnom. Čak i

en: For a moment, even she was lost for words. Everyone was. And as Orso looked across the staring faces on the Representatives’ benches, from Citizens Heugen and Isher to a surprisingly popular beggar elected from the Three Farms, he knew they were all working desperately at this strange new sum, trying to tally up where their best interests lay, and therefore what mixture of emotion to put on display. He suspected loyalties shifted quicker in that moment than at any time since his father was unexp
bs: Na tren je i njoj ponestalo riječi. Svima je. I dok je Orso prelazio pogledom po ukočenim licima na klupama Zastupnika, od građana Heugena i Išera do iznenađujuće popularnog prosjaka izabranog iz Tri Farme, znao je da svi očajnički rješavaju tu čudnu novu jednadžbu, pokušavajući zbrojiti gdje im leže najbolji interesi, a samim time i kakvu mješavinu emocija izložiti. Slutio je da su se lojalnosti u tom trenu promijenile brže nego ikada otkad je njegov otac neočekivano izabran na prijestolje.

en: Halder looked like he’d much rather have slipped out of a side door, but the habit of obedience was hard to break. He and one of his fellows pulled Orso’s arms behind him and the cord painfully tight about his wrists, while Broad brought Savine down from the dock and bound her hands, his heavy jaw fixed, his red eyes staring.
bs: Halder je izgledao kao da bi radije neopaženo klisnuo kroz sporedna vrata, ali naviku poslušnosti bilo je teško slomiti. On i jedan suborac povukoše Orsove ruke iza leđa, a uže mu se bolno zategnu oko zapešća, dok Brod skide Savine s optuženičke klupe i sveza joj ruke, ukočene teške čeljusti i upregnutih crvenih očiju.

en: She’d wedged pieces of a broken spear into the brackets where the bar would’ve gone, but they didn’t fit, jumping and flexing. She could hear them outside, one voice calling the rhythm. “Shove! Shove! Shove!”
bs: Zaglavila je komade slomljenog koplja u držače kamo je trebala ući prečka, ali nisu pristajali, skakali su i savijali se. Čula ih je vani, jedan je glas diktirao ritam. — Gurni! Gurni! Gurni!

en: The door jerked open another finger’s breadth. Something slid through, so close to Vick she had to twist her face away, staring at it cross-eyed. The blade of a spear. Someone was using it as a lever, working the door open.
bs: Vrata su se trznuvši otvorila još za širinu prsta. Nešto se provuklo, toliko blizu Vik da je morala okrenuti lice i prekrižiti oči zuriti u to. Oštrica koplja. Netko ju je rabio kao polugu, pokušavajući otvoriti vrata.

en: Which is how one could come straight at Vick, screaming at the top of his voice. She caught a glimpse of him as he pounded through a shaft of light, lips curled back, a smear of Burner’s red paint across his cheek.
bs: Zbog čega je netko mogao krenuti ravno na Vik, urličući iz sveg glasa. Ugledala ga je na tren dok je u trku prolazio kroz snop svjetlosti, usana uvučenih unatrag, s tragom crvene boje Burnera razmazanom po obrazu.

en: He gave a surprised ooof as Vick charged into him, drove him crashing into the wall, the axe bouncing off her back and onto the floor. She went at him with everything she had. Tried for his balls with a clumsy jab of the mace but only hit his hip, dug her other fist into his stomach but barely got a wheeze from him. She straightened up so she could swing at his throat.
bs: Otme mu se iznenađeno uf kad Vik uleti u nj, silovito ga zabaci u zid, a Hachette joj se odbije od leđa i tresne na pod. Navalila je na nj svim snagama. Nespretno ga pokuša buzdovanom sunuti u jaja, ali pogodi ga samo u kuk, drugom šakom udari ga u trbuh, no iz njega izmami jedva nekakav hropac. Uspravi se kako bi mogla zamahnuti po grlu.

en: She managed to work her heel up the wall behind her. He twisted her head up, back, as if he was killing a chicken. Wringing her neck. She wriggled, squirmed, till her fishing hand found the grip of the knife in her boot. Felt like he was going to twist her head off, felt like her skull was going to burst. Couldn’t breathe.
bs: Uspjela je petu potisnuti uza zid iza sebe. Zabacio joj je glavu gore, unatrag, kao da kolje kokoš. Lomeći joj vrat. Koprcala se i vrpoljila sve dok joj ruka u potrazi nije napipala dršku noža u čizmi. Činilo joj se da će joj otkinuti glavu, činilo se da će joj lubanja puknuti. Nije mogla udahnuti.

en: Vick could certainly have used Gorst’s help. But if he let go and that portcullis dropped, all their plans were fucked.
bs: Vik bi zasigurno mogao iskoristiti Gorstovu pomoć. No ako on pusti i te se rešetke spuste, svi će im planovi pasti u vodu.

en: Gorst let go of the windlass. There was a whirr of gears as the portcullis dropped, then a clank as one of the steel bars caught on the axe haft and was held there, loose chains faintly rattling.
bs: Gorst je pustio vitlo. Mehanizam zupčanika zazujao je dok su se rešetke spuštale, a onda je odjeknuo prasak kad se jedna od čeličnih šipki zakvačila za držak sjekire i ostala visjeti, uz slabašno zveketanje labavih lanaca.

en: She saw the bridge. The slogan-daubed buildings beyond. The wide street that led into the city. And coming up it, at a clattering canter, a great mass of horsemen. Armed and armoured, bristling with steel. Leo dan Brock’s lion standard flew at the head, the sun of the Union beside it.
bs: Ugleda most. Zgrade išarane parolama u pozadini. Široku ulicu koja je vodila u grad. A njome su, u kloparajućem trku, nadirale silne gomile konjanika. Naoružani i oklopljeni, nakinđureni čelikom. Lavlji barjak Lea dan Broka vijorio se na čelu, a sunce Unije stajalo mu je uz bok.

en: People scattered from the gateway. Shocked faces as they dived aside. Could’ve been Breakers, Burners, fools come to gawp at Savine’s trial or fools running for their lives. All Leo was sure of was that they were in his way.
bs: Folk se razbježaše s ulaza. Šokirana lica dok su ustrčali u stranu. Mogli su to biti Lomljači, Palioci, budale koje su došle zjakati na Savinino suđenje ili budale koje su bježale glavom bez obzira. Leo je bio siguran samo u jedno: stajali su mu na putu.

en: He had to drop his reins to free his sword. You’d think with one arm you could still swing a blade well enough, but without his leg to grip his horse or his other arm to give him balance, he wobbled in the saddle, flailed uselessly, struck someone with the flat and nearly fumbled the grip. His own clumsiness filled him with fury and he clenched his teeth, hacking about him, finally landing a decent blow on the other side, blood spattering yellow hair.
bs: Morao je pustiti uzde da oslobodi mač. Čovjek bi pomislio kako s jednom rukom još uvijek može sasvim pristojno zamahnuti oštricom, ali bez noge kojom bi obgrlio konja i druge ruke da mu drži ravnotežu, ljuljao se u sedlu, nemoćno mlatarao, udario nekoga ravnim dijelom oštrice i umalo ispustio dršku. Vlastita ga je nespretnost ispunila bijesom te je stisnuo zube, mlateći oko sebe, dok napokon nije zadao pošten udarac nasuprot tome, pri čemu je krv poprskala plavu kosu.

en: Leo pushed it angrily away. She was his wife. The mother of his children. He was duty-bound to do everything he could to save her. The Young Lion might not be swept away by every feeling any more, but he still took his duty very seriously.
bs: Leo je gnjevno otjerao tu misao. Ona mu je bila žena. Majka njegove djece. Bio je dužan učiniti sve što je u njegovoj moći da je spasi. Juvens Lav možda više nije bespogovorno robovao svakom osjećaju, ali je svoju dužnost i dalje shvaćao vrlo ozbiljno.

en: Judge glowered back up the rubbish-strewn steps towards the Lords’ Round. The Commons’ Round. The Court of the People. The heart of the Union, whichever version of the Union you subscribed to, rebuilt even more grandly on the grand ruins of the one Bayaz had laid waste to, its stonework pocked and scarred and daubed with the slogans of the Great Change.
bs: Džadž je mrko pogledala natrag uz smećem zatrpane stepenice prema Lords’ Roundu. Kružoku pučana. Sudu naroda. Srcu Unije, ma kojoj god verziji Unije da ste pripadali, iznova sagrađenom još velebnije na veličanstvenim ruševinama onoga što je Bajaz sravnio sa zemljom, čije su kamene Tell bile izrovane, izbrazdane i išarane parolama Velike Promjene.

en: She stumbled, would have fallen if Broad hadn’t caught her arm. Candles sent skittering. Set up as a little shrine beside one of the names carved in the flagstones. The names of those killed to keep the old regime in power, half-glimpsed under her shuffling feet, blurred through the wet in her eyes. The names of those her father had beaten, tortured, hanged so that she could be rich.
bs: Spotaknula se, pala bi da joj Brod nije uhvatio ruku. Svijeće su se rasprskale. Namještene kao mali oltar pored jednog od imena uklesanih u kamene ploče. Imena onih ubijenih da bi se održao stari režim, napola viđenih pod njenim posrtajućim stopalima, zamagljenih od suza u očima. Imena onih koje je njezin otac tukao, mučio, vješao kako bi ona mogla biti bogata.

en: The sounds of fighting were growing louder. Closer. Leo might be just beyond the edge of the square. Might be cutting his way through to her, even now. A surge went through the Burners and she was shouldered sideways, caught her shoe on something, bit her tongue as she nearly fell. The outstretched arm of a limp body, bloody hair spread across the cracked flagstones.
bs: Zvukovi borbe postajali su glasniji. Bliži. Leo je možda bio tik iza ruba Trga. Možda se probijao prema njoj, čak i sada. Val prostruji kroz Palitelje i ona bi gurnuta u stranu, zapela cipelom za nešto, grizući jezik dok je umalo pala. Ispružena ruka beživotnog tijela, krvava kosa rasuta po ispucalim kamenim pločama.

en: A few more Burners were finally showing some doubts, but not Judge. “That’s your thing, not mine. No one’ll be deal-making their way out o’ this. You lot, hold the line here! Nobody comes through, you understand? Sarlby, Halder, let’s go.”
bs: Još nekoliko Palitelja napokon je pokazivalo određene sumnje, ali ne i Džadž. — To je tvoja furka, a ne moja. Nitko se odavde neće izvući nikakvim pogodbama. Vi tu, držite liniju! Nitko ne prolazi, jeste li razumjeli? Sarlbi, Halder, idemo.

en: “Think I am crying,” said Sarlby, “but maybe it’s the smoke.” There was a tickle of it on the air now, as the flames licked ever higher up the Court of the People. Or was it the Lords’ Round again, just while it burned?
bs: — Mislim da ja doista plačem, reče Sarlbi, ali možda je to od dima. Osjećao se blagi miris dima u zraku dok su plamenovi lizali sve više uz Narodni sud. Ili je to opet bio Round gospode, barem dok gori?

en: “Save the king!” Gorst hacked someone down with his long steel, sent them bouncing from a pedestal, smearing blood across the stained marble. He kicked, shoved, screeched his way through the mob and Vick limped after him, her face one enormous throb, a watchful eye on his steels in case he took her head off with a backswing, wondering what her chances were of finding someone out here who could set a broken nose.
bs: — Spasite kralja! Gorst je oborio nekoga svojim dugim čelikom, odbacivši ga od postolja i razmazujući krv po uprljanom mramoru. Udarao je nogama, gurao, pištao probijajući se kroz rulju, a Vik je hramala za njim, lice joj je pulsiralo u jednoj golemoj boli, dok je budnim okom pratila njegove čelike ako joj zamahom odvali glavu, pitajući se kakve su joj šanse da ovdje pronađe nekoga tko joj zna namjestiti slomljeni nos.

en: There were Burners there. A curved line of them, weapons ready, sharpened steel gleaming with the colours of fire. A last line of defence around their place of execution.
bs: Tamo su bili Palioci. Zakrivljen stroj njih, s oružjem u pripravnosti, naoštreni čelik blistao je u bojama vatre. Posljednja linija obrane oko njihovog stratišta.

en: Vick stood staring, breathing hard through her sore mouth, still gripping the mace so tight her hand ached.
bs: Vik je stajala zurivši, teško dišući kroz bolna usta, i dalje držeći buzdovan tako čvrsto da ju je ruka boljelo.

en: Broad stepped onto the roof of the Tower of Chains. It had turned out a fine day. Crisp and sunny, with a cool breeze carrying off the vapours so you could see across the city. That same mad view he’d witnessed a hundred times, but every time it somehow took him by surprise.
bs: Brod zakorači na krov Tornja Chains. Bio se razvedrio lijep dan. Svjež i sunčan, uz blagi povjetarac što je rastjerivao isparavanja tako da se vidio cijeli grad. Bio je to isti onaj suludi prizor kojem je svjedočio stotinu puta, ali svaki bi ga put iznova nekako zatekao.

en: “Don’t worry,” said Judge, her wild red hair whipped and slashed by the wind, and behind her flames flickered, smoke rolling into the sky from the burning Court of the People. She put a hand on Broad’s cheek. “I know this isn’t easy. Sarlby?”
bs: — Ne brini, reče Džadž, dok joj je divlja Red kosa vijorila i šibala na vjetru, a iza nje su plamsale vatre, dok se dim valjao u nebo iz spaljenog Narodni sud. Stavi ruku Brodu na obraz. — Znam da ovo nije lako. Sarlbi?

en: “Ready, Your Majesty?” Broad stepped up close, cutting the cord between his wrists with a sharp jerk of his knife, then pressing it into his palm.
bs: — Spremni, Vaša Uzvišenosti? Brod mu priđe posve blizu, oštrim trzajem noža prereza konop oko njegovih zapešća, pa mu gurnu sječivo u dlan.

en: One of the other Burners was coming at Broad with a mace. Luvonte was his name. A Styrian. Strange, that he’d be a Burner. But then who’d have thought Broad would ever be one, either?
bs: Jedan od ostalih Palitelja krenuo je na Broda s buzdovanom. Zvao se Luvonte. Stirijac. Čudno da je bio Palioc. No tko bi uopće pomislio da će i sam Brod ikada postati jedan od njih?

en: He saw Halder sat against the parapet, hand clutched to his throat, blood squirting between his fingers, black as tar.
bs: Vidio je Haldera kako sjedi naslonjen na grudobran, rukom stisnutom za grlo, dok mu je krv šikljala među prstima, Black poput katrana.

en: They staggered to one side, wrestling over an axe, leaving Savine and Judge to stare at each other across the flat roof of the Tower of Chains.
bs: Zatečeni su se oteturali na stranu, rveći se oko sjekire, ostavljajući Savine i Džadž da se promatraju preko ravnog krova Tornja lanaca.

en: Judge bared bloody teeth, almost a smile, shot out a hand. Nails sank into Savine’s neck, ripping at her. She gave a shriek, cut off in a gulp as Judge kneed her in the gut, shoved her staggering off the lift and back across the tower’s roof.
bs: Džadž ogoli krvave zube, gotovo se osmjehnuvši, i ispruži ruku. Nokti joj se zabodeše u Savininu šiju, trgajući je. Ona vrisnu, a vrisak joj se presiječe u grlu kad je Džadž udari koljenom u trbuh, gurnuvši je posrćuću s dizala natrag preko krova tornja.

en: She spun about, axe held clumsily in her tied hands, just as Judge rammed her into the parapet with a shoulder, driving her breath out in an agonised rasp. They wrestled, tangled, clawed, elbowed. Savine got the axe in the way, snarling as she pressed it into the side of Judge’s face, but there wasn’t enough force behind it to stop her, only to slowly peel a flap of flesh from her cheek.
bs: Okrenula se, držeći sjekiru nespretno u svezanim rukama, upravo u trenutku kad ju je Džadž ramenom pribila uz grudobran, istisnuvši joj zrak u mučnom hropcu. Hrvale su se, zaplitanje, grebanje, laktarenje. Savine je uspjela postaviti sjekiru između njih, režeći dok ju je pritiskala uz stranu Judgeina lica, no u tome nije bilo dovoljno snage da je zaustavi, već samo da joj polako oguli komad mesa s obraza.

en: She saw Judge drop. Just a glimpse of her bloody snarl before she was gone in a mass of clawing limbs and flapping cloth.
bs: Vidjela je kako Džadž propada. Samo letimičan Oko na njezinu krvavu grimasu prije nego što je nestala u masi udova koji su mlatarali i tkanine koja je lepršala.

en: There were lots of soldiers at the bottom. Lots of Anglanders in dark uniforms. There were Burners, too, but on their knees, or having their wrists bound, or lying still, daubed with red, and not just paint. Figures of terror no more.
bs: Dolje je bilo mnogo vojnika. Mnogo Anglanđana u tamnim odorama. Bilo je tu i Palitelja, ali na koljenima, s vezanim zapešćima ili kako leže nepomično, premazani crvenilom, i to ne samo bojom. Više nisu bili figure strave i užasa.

en: They did not kiss, or fall into each others’ arms, but then Savine had never been one for displays of affection. “Where are the children?” she asked.
bs: Nisu se poljubili niti pali jedno drugome u zagrljaj, no Savine ionako nikada nije bila sklona javnim izljevima nježnosti. — Gdje su djeca?, upita.

en: He looked across those eager faces. Some of them were even starting to smile. “No more riots,” he called, “no more trials, no more executions. No vengeance and no settling of scores. No Court of the People!” He caught Savine’s eye, her chin up, her eyes shining. If she believed in him, he knew it could be done. “But there can be no more Closed Council, either. No corruption and injustice. No dead grip of Valint and Balk around the throat of the nation. This time… I mean to govern for the many, n
bs: Pogledao je preko tih ozarenih lica. Neka su se čak počinjala smiješiti. — Nema više nereda, povikao je, nema više suđenja, nema više pogubljenja. Nema osvete ni raščišćavanja računa. Nema Narodnog suda!" Uhvatio je Savinin Oko; brada joj bijaše uzdignuta, a oči su joj sjajale. Ako je ona vjerovala u njega, znao je da se to može ostvariti. "Ali isto tako više nema ni Zatvorenog vijeća. Nema korupcije ni nepravde. Nema više mrtvačkog stiska Valinta i Balka za vratom nacije. Ovog puta… namjeravam

en: Orso turned to the Young Lion—pale, gaunt and ungainly on his false leg, blond hair darkened with sweat and that sickly smile still on his face. For various reasons, several of them good ones, Orso had grown to dislike the ex-Lord Governor of Angland quite intensely. But his father once said you can measure a man by how he treats those he dislikes. He had said he would be a king for everyone, and he meant it. The lowest as well as the highest, his enemies as well as his friends. And Brock had co
bs: Orso se okrenuo Mlađem Lavu — blijedu, mršavu i nespretna hoda na umjetnoj nozi, plave kose zatamnjene od znoja i s onim bolećivim osmijehom još uvijek na licu. Iz raznoraznih razloga, od kojih su neki bili posve opravdani, Orso je prilično snažno zamrzio bivšega lorda upravitelja Englenda. No otac mu je jednom rekao da se čovjeka može procijeniti po tomu kako se ophodi prema onima koje ne podnosi. Rekao je da će biti kralj za svakoga, i to je mislio ozbiljno. Za one najniže jednako kao i za naj

en: “You fucking bathtard,” breathed Vick, but with an air of wounded resignation. Orso could only watch with a familiar sinking feeling. He should have known, the moment things started looking up, that something like this would happen.
bs: — Ti jastarsko kopile, prosikta Vik, ali s prizvukom ranjene pomirenosti sa sudbinom. Orso je mogao samo promatrati uz dobro poznat osjećaj propadanja u utrobi. Morao je znati, čim bi stvari krenule nabolje, da će se dogoditi ovako nešto.

en: “What have you done?” whispered Savine, back of one hand to her mouth. “Let them go, Leo, please, let them go!”
bs: — Što si učinio? prošapta Savine, prislonivši nadlanicu na usta. — Pusti ih, Leo, molim te, pusti ih!

en: “Aye.” Rikke tweaked that fine fur about her shoulders and wriggled her back as straight as she could. “Those, too.” Shivers gave the guards a nod, and there was a mighty creaking as the doors of Skarling’s Hall were swung wide.
bs: — Tako je. Rike popravi ono fino krzno oko ramena i ispravi leđa koliko je god mogla. — I njih. Šivers kimnu stražarima, a vrata Skarlingove dvorane otvoriše se uz snažan škrip.

en: “I’ve a little trip to take before I can sit here secure.” Rikke found she was fussing with the emeralds around her neck and let them drop. “I hear tell my old friends the Young Lion and his wife—”
bs: — Imam jedan mali put pred sobom prije nego što ovdje budem mogla sjediti spokojno. Rike primijeti da se igra smaragdima oko vrata pa ih pusti da klonu. — Čujem da su moji stari prijatelji, Juvens Lav i njegova žena –

en: “Patch up the knife holes, then, before Leo gets it in his head to put a few in us. The North never does well out of wars with the Union. What we need is peace, and smiles, and trade—”
bs: — Onda zakrpaj te rane od noža prije nego što Leo umisli da bi i nama mogao utisnuti koju. Sjever se nikada ne provede dobro u ratovima s Unijom. Ono što nam treba jest mir, osmijesi i trgovina —

en: “Right y’are.” The Nail loitered a moment, like he had something more to say. She could guess what was on his mind. What happened between the two of them before he went away. It was on her mind, too. She’d have liked to say stay. Even if it was just for a night. Even if it was just for a quick fumble behind the kitchen. But a leader has to be careful who she lets in. Who she’s seen to let in. Specially a she.
bs: — Kako ti kažeš. Najl se zadrža još tren, kao da ima još što reći. Mogla je naslutiti što joj se muva po glavi. Ono što se dogodilo između njih dvoje prije nego što je otišao. I njoj je to bilo na pameti. Bilo bi joj drago da ga je zamolila da ostane. Čak i da je bilo samo na jednu noć. Čak i da je bilo samo radi brzog dodirivanja iza kuhinje. No vođa mora paziti koga pušta blizu. Koga drugi vide da pušta blizu. A pogotovo žena.

en: “There’s been bad blood between the clans of the North and the people of the hills for far too long,” said Rikke. “Since the time of Crummock-i-Phail and Bethod and since times long before. But that’s all washed away. You were there when I needed you, and I’ll be there if you need me, that’s my promise. But since promises are cheap, you can take the land we discussed as well.”
bs: — Predugo je zla krv gorjela između klanova Sjevera i brđana, reče Rike. — Još od vremena Crummock-i-Fejla i Bethod te davno prije toga. Ali sve je to isprano. Bili ste uz mene kad ste mi trebali, i ja ću biti uz vas zatrebate li me, to vam obećavam. No budući da su obećanja jeftina, možete uzeti i zemlju o kojoj smo razgovarali.

en: “Ah, enemies and profits.” Scofen’s eyes lit up. “Things our father loved almost as much as the moon.” And there was laughter, and back-slapping, and trading of well-meaning insults and overblown tales of the battle.
bs: — Aha, neprijatelji i dobit. Skofenove oči zasjaše. — Stvari koje je naš otac volio gotovo jednako kao i mjesec. I prolomio se smijeh, i pljeskanje po leđima, i razmjena dobronamjernih uvreda i pretjeranih priča o bitci.

en: “Oh. Right.” And with a pained grunt, hands still bound behind him, Flatstone wobbled down to one knee.
bs: — Oh. Da. I uz bolan uzdah, ruku još uvijek svezanih iza leđa, Flatstone se nespretno spustio na jedno koljeno.

en: “It is.” The girl didn’t look much chastened, her jaw jutting. As much fight in her as when she first came to Uffrith.
bs: — Jest. Djevojka nije izgledala odviše pokajnički, isturene čeljusti. Borbenosti je u njoj bilo jednako kao onda kad je prvi put došla u Afrit.

en: A miserable crowd came next, kicked and bundled into Skarling’s Hall, forced down on the pitiless stones before her, chains rattling. Stand-
bs: Zatim stiže jadna gomila, izudarana i ugurana u Skarlingovu dvoranu, prisiljena na nemilosrdno kamenje pred njom, uz zveckanje lanaca. Stani —

en: “I like to think so.” She nodded to Shivers. “Kill ’em first, then boil ’em down to the bones, then get Flatstone to send the bones back across the Crinna. Maybe that’ll teach their kind to stay on their side of the water.”
bs: — Volim tako misliti. Klimnu Šiversu. — Prvo ih ubij, onda ih skuhaj do kostiju, pa reci neka Flatstone pošalje kosti natrag preko Crinna. Možda će to naučiti njihovu vrstu da ostane na svojoj strani vode.

en: Clover had seen ’em rise and fall. The leaders, the chiefs, the kings. He’d taken a hand in a few of those ups and downs himself, indeed. Bethod, and the Bloody-Nine, and Black Dow, and Scale Ironhand, and Stour Nightfall, an ever-lengthening list o’ glory and disaster. Those who served ’em, too, the fortunes of the little men rising and falling with the big men they chose to follow, like boats lifted by the tide, or dropped stranded on the sands. He glanced over at Sholla and Flick. Hoped they
bs: Klover je vidio mnoge kako se uzdižu i padaju. Vođe, poglavarice, kraljeve. Doista, i sam je umiješao prste u neka od tih uzdignuća i strmoglavljivanja. Bethod, pa Krvava Devetka, i Black Dow, te Ljuska Željezna Ruka, i Staur Najtfol – poduži i sve duži popis slave i propasti. I one koji su im služili, sudbine malih Folk što su rasle i gubile se prateći velike za koje su se odlučili vezati, poput čamaca koje plima podigne ili ostavi nasukane na pijesku. Pogledao je prema Šoli i Fliku. Nadao se d

en: “Jonas Clover,” she said, tapping a thoughtful fingernail against the arm of Skarling’s Chair as he traipsed up nervously to stand before her. “Here’s a riddle.”
bs: — Jonas Klover, reče, kuckajući zamišljeno noktom o naslon Skarlingove stolice dok se on nervozno vukao da stane pred nju. — Evo ti jedne zagonetke.

en: “When you let Stour live, then tossed all your friends away, I started worrying you might not have the bones for the task. In my defence, you did act the part o’ someone shitting themselves very nicely.”
bs: — Kad si pustila Staura da živi, a onda odbacila sve svoje prijatelje, zabrinuo sam se da možda nemaš petlje za taj zadatak. U svoju obranu, mora se priznati da si odglumila strah i trepet sasvim uvjerljivo.

en: Rikke raised the brow over her blind eye at Sholla. “If I’ve one regret it’s that my cheese never quite carves thin enough.”
bs: Rike izdiže obrvu nad svojim slijepim okom prema Šoli. — Ako zbog nečega žalim, to je što moj sir nikako da se nareže dovoljno tanko.

en: “Don’t we get a say?” muttered Sholla, following him out with Flick. The sun was getting low now, and the yard was half in bright light, half in deep shadow. Rarely all one way or the other, like he’d told Rikke.
bs: — Zar se mi ništa ne pitamo? promrmlja Šola prateći ga van s Flikom. Sunce se već primicalo obzoru, a dvorište je bilo napola obasjano jasnom svjetlošću, napola uronjeno u duboku sjenu. Rijetko kad posve jednako na ovu ili onu stranu, baš kao što je bio rekao Rike.

en: Clover grinned. “Something usually comes up.” And he turned and started walking, sword over his shoulder.
bs: Klover se nasmiješi. — uvijek nešto iskrsne." I okrenuvši se, zaputi se dalje, noseći mač preko ramena.

en: Savine looked sideways at him, and hardly with the proper affection a wife should have for her husband. “From you, I suppose?”
bs: Savine ga pogleda poprijeko, i to jedva s onom prikladnom naklonošću koju bi supruga trebala gajiti prema mužu. — Od tebe, pretpostavljam?

en: Still, the only alternative was Zuri, and Leo trusted her less than ever these days. Even though Savine loved her so much. Because Savine loved her so much, maybe. It was a bad message to send, having brown faces around the royal children.
bs: Ipak, jedina alternativa bila je Zuri, a Leo joj je ovih dana vjerovao manje nego ikada. Čak i usprkos tome što ju je Savine toliko voljela. Možda upravo zato što ju je Savine toliko voljela. Bila je to loša poruka, imati tamnoputa lica oko kraljevske djece.

en: “She has proved herself effective. My father is gone and Pike was never apprehended. We must have someone competent in charge of the Inquisition. There are hundreds of Breakers and Burners still at large. Thousands, maybe. We have to root them out.” Her grazed cheek tightened as she clenched her jaw. “We have to make sure nothing like the Great Change can ever happen again.”
bs: "Pokazala se učinkovitom. Moj otac je otišao, a Pajk nikada nije uhvaćen. Na čelu Inkvizicije moramo imati nekoga sposobnog. Stotine Lomljača i Palitelja još su na slobodi. Možda tisuće. Moramo ih korijenito istrijebiti." Njezin izgrebani obraz napeto se zatekao dok je stiskala čeljust."Moramo se pobrinuti da se nešto poput Velike promjene nikada više ne ponovi."

en: Savine had not set foot in that building during Risinau’s reign, but even she could tell the balance of the Representatives had greatly changed since then. Less than half this crowd had been voted for, and those were mostly from the richer towns and districts. Landowners, merchants, men of business. The rest had all once been nobles. Members of the Open Council lucky and unprincipled enough to slip from one body to another. Now Leo had made them nobles again. There were even a few women, taking
bs: Savine nije kročila u tu zgradu tijekom Risinauove vladavine, no čak je i ona mogla primijetiti da se ravnoteža snaga među predstavnicima otad uvelike promijenila. Manje od polovice ove gomile bila je izabrana, a i ti su većinom dolazili iz bogatijih gradova i okruga. Vlasnici zemljišta, trgovci, poslovni Folk. Svi ostali nekoć bijahu plemići. Članovi Otvorenog vijeća dovoljno sretni i beznačajni da se provuku iz jednog tijela u drugo. Sada ih je Leo ponovno učinio plemićima. Bilo je tu čak i ne

en: “My friends!” called Leo as the clapping faded. “My peers! Noblemen and commoners! Representatives of the people of the Union! The Great Change… is behind us!”
bs: — Prijatelji moji! povika Leo dok je pljesak jenjavao. — Moji vršnjaci! Plemići i pučani! Predstavnici naroda Unije! Velika promjena… iza nas je!

en: More applause. Savine had to admit she was impressed. She had always been more comfortable with small rooms, intimate groups, hushed whispers. But Leo knew how to fill a hall. “He speaks well,” she murmured.
bs: Još pljeska. Savine je morala priznati da je impresionirana. Oduvijek se bolje snalazila u malim prostorijama, intimnim skupovima i prigušenim šaptima. No Leo je znao ispuniti dvoranu. — Dobro govori, prošaptala je.

en: “We must return to our principles,” said Leo, sternly. “And as the first step, we must elect a new king.”
bs: "Moramo se vratiti svojim načelima", rekao je Leo strogo. — A kao prvi korak, moramo izabrati novog kralja.

en: “I’d like a show of hands!” he told the Hall of Mirrors. “Nothing hidden. Nothing suspect. Each man makes his loyalty clear. Now. An open vote for our new king.” A vote observed by him, who had all the armed men in the city, not to mention at least a hundred in this room, firmly under his command. Only a fool calls for a vote when he hasn’t made sure of the outcome, after all.
bs: — Želim vidjeti podignute ruke! obrati se Dvorani zrcala. — Ništa skriveno. Ništa sumnjivo. Neka svaki čovjek jasno pokaže svoju odanost. Sad. Javno glasanje za našega novoga kralja. Glasanje koje će nadzirati on, čovjek koji je pod svojim čvrstim zapovjedništvom držao sve naoružane ljude u gradu, da i ne spominjemo barem stotinu njih u ovoj prostoriji. Naposljetku, samo budala poziva na glasanje ako se nije uvjerila u ishod.

en: He didn’t look much like a king, as Leo glanced around. He looked like a white bundle in the arms of his mother, who with her unerring instinct for the centre of attention appeared to have swapped babies while the voting was underway. But King Harod the Second was raised to the throne, as his grandfather King Jezal the First had been, by near-unanimous accord.
bs: Nije previše nalikovao kralju, dok je Leo bacio Oko oko sebe. Izgledao je poput bijelog smotuljka u naručju majke, koja je s nepogrešivim instinktom za privlačenje pozornosti očito zamijenila bebe dok je glasovanje još trajalo. No kralj Harod Drugi uzdignut je na prijestolje, baš kao i njegov djed, kralj Džezal Prvi, gotovo jednodušnim pristankom.

en: “My thanks! I humbly accept this great honour, this great responsibility. I’m a soldier first, but now is the time for healing wounds. For reforging what’s been broken, stronger than ever. For making us a Union again!” He thumped his fist on the table. “We’ll have a new age, my friends! Not the corruption of the old regime. Not the folly of the Breakers or the madness of the Burners. The best of both worlds! Justice and good government for all!”
bs: "Moja hvala! Ponizno prihvaćam ovu veliku čast, ovu veliku odgovornost. Ja sam ponajprije vojnik, no sada je vrijeme za zacijeljivanje rana. Za ponovno kovanje onoga što je slomljeno, jače nego ikad. Za stvaranje novog Unije!" udari šakom o stol. — Imat ćemo novo doba, prijatelji moji! Ne korupciju starog režima. Ne Ludilo Lomljača ni mahnito bjesnilo Palitelja. Najbolje od oba svijeta! Pravdu i dobru vladavinu za sve!

en: “Not much need to refresh our memories as to your crimes, is there?” she asked. “You’ve been up to your eyes in the Great Change, right back to Valbeck. You were at Judge’s side in the Court of the People. You herded dozens off the Tower of Chains.”
bs: — Nema prevelike potrebe da obnavljamo gradivo o tvojim zločinima, zar ne? upitala je. — Do guše si ogrezao u Veliku Promjenu, sve tamo od Valbeka. Bio si uz Džadža u Sudu Naroda. S Kule lanaca otjerao si desetine Folk.

en: She sat forwards with a grunt. Damn, she was aching. “Truth is—and take it from someone who spent a dozen years in prison—in the end, people don’t really care much about being free. They want to be warm and well fed and to not have to worry. In particular, they want to not have to worry about being thrown off a tower for wearing the wrong shoes.”
bs: Nagnula se naprijed uz tihi stenjaj. Prokletstvo, sve ju je boljelo. — Istina je — a poslušaj to od nekoga tko je proveo desetak godina u zatvoru — što na kraju ljude zapravo nije previše briga za slobodu. Žele biti na toplom, dobro jesti i nemati briga. Ponajviše žele ne brinuti se hoće li biti bačeni s kule zato što nose pogrešne cipele.

en: “That’s what the Breakers said. And the Arch Lector before them, for that matter. A couple of enemies to cross out. Just get to the bottom of the list. Except the list kept getting longer.” She ventured a little sniff, a squeak of barely moving air in her swollen face, a hint of salty snot at the back of her throat which she could never quite manage to swallow. “We must have enemies, Tallow. Always.”
bs: — Tako su govorili Lomljači. A i vrhovni Lektor prije njih, kad smo već kod toga. Nekoliko neprijatelja za prekrižiti. Samo doći do dna popisa. Osim što je popis postajao sve duži. Ona se laktaški potegnu, jedva čujnim šumom zraka u svom natečenom licu, s primjesom slane sline u dnu grla koju nikako nije uspijevala progutati. — Moramo imati neprijatelja, Talou. Uvijek.

en: Vick raised her brows. Even that felt like an effort. “I spent years working for your father—your adopted father, not the other one—so I learned how to take a hint. I got the strong feeling your husband’s offer was to swear the oath and stay in the Inquisitor’s chair or refuse and go in the prisoner’s one. But then I’ve always been a traitor and a liar so… wasn’t difficult to do.” She gave a hopeless shrug. “Far be it from me to stand in the way of the new Union. Or the new new Union, is it?”
bs: Vik podiže obrve. Čak je i to iziskivalo napor. — Provela sam godine radeći za tvog oca — tvog posvojitelja, ne onog drugog — tako da sam naučila kako prepoznati nagovještaj. Stekla sam snažan dojam da je muževa ponuda bila ili položiti prisegu i ostati u Inkvizitorovoj stolici ili odbiti i završiti u zatvoreničkoj. No, ionako sam oduvijek bila izdajica i lažljivica pa… nije mi bilo teško to učiniti." Beznadno slegnu ramenima. — Daleko od toga da bih stajala na putu novoj Unija. Ili onoj dvaput

en: “Good.” Vick cleared her throat. “Good.” She turned away, trying to swallow that lump in her throat, wiping her eyelids with a knuckle. Tallow stood against the wall, staring at her like he’d seen Euz rise from the grave. “What?” Vick snarled at him.
bs: — Dobro. Vik pročisti grlo. — Dobro. Okrenu se, pokušavajući progutati tu knedlu u grlu, brišući vjeđe zglobom prsta. Talou je stajao uz zid, zírajući u nju kao da je vidio Euz kako ustaje iz groba. — Što je? zaciča Vik na njega.

en: “No point asking my forgiveness,” said Vick. “I’m not allowed any. You might have more luck with her.” She nodded towards the door. “But I wouldn’t bet on it.”
bs: — Nema smisla tražiti moje oproštenje, reče Vik. — Meni nije dopušteno dijeliti ga. Možda budeš imao više sreće s njom. Kimnula je prema vratima. — Ali ne bih se kladila na to.

en: “Please! All you got carried away with, Sworbreck, was your own power, and cruelty, and self-importance.”
bs: — Molim te! Jedino što te ponijelo, Svorbriku, bila je tvoja vlastita moć, okrutnost i samodopadnost.

en: The Lady Regent considered her carefully. “You spent years working for my father. You should have learned not to hang what you can use.” She narrowed her eyes at Sworbreck. “I suggest you get to your press and keep it hot. You live now to make me loved. And you will live precisely as long as you are useful to me.” Savine stood, looking down her nose at the sobbing ex-prosecutor. “Not an instant longer.”
bs: Gospa Regentica odmjerila ju je pomno. — Provela si godine radeći za mog oca. Trebala si naučiti da se ne vješa ono što se može iskoristiti." Suzi oko na Svorbrika. — Predlažem ti da požuriš do svoje tiskare i dobro je zagrijanom držiš. Od sada živiš zato da učiniš da me vole. I živjet ćeš točno onoliko dugo koliko mi budeš od koristi." Savine ustane, gledajući s visoka na jecajućeg bivšeg tužitelja. "Niti trenutak duže."

en: Rowdy cheering. While attention was elsewhere, Savine slipped behind her fan and took the tiniest pinch of pearl dust, eyelashes fluttering at that delicious, invigorating burning in her face. Thank the Fates, trade of all kinds was flowing once again, at least for those with the money. She liked to think she had changed, but the Mother of the King, like any mother, needs a little something from time to time.
bs: Bučno navijanje.
